pmaxhogan/bsaber-mods.readme:
# MaxTweaks

Personal quality-of-life mod for Beat Saber PC (BSIPA), built for game version **1.40.8**.
Open source, but designed for one player's setup.

## Features

Every feature has its own on/off switch in **Mod Settings > MaxTweaks** and in the MaxTweaks tab
under the song preview.

- **Hide OSTs** - one-click icon next to the solo song list's category tabs hides every official
  song (OST, Extras, DLC) from the packs, the All list, search and playlists.
- **Auto-reload maps** - watches the custom map folders (native Windows file notifications) and
  reloads added, edited or deleted maps in place without Ctrl+R, keeping your place in the list.
  Never reloads mid-song; shows a toast if the map you are playing changed on disk.
- **Blink** - in long note-free, wall-free stretches, a soft vignette and closed-eye icon remind you
  to rest your eyes (at most once every 5 minutes of play; all thresholds configurable).
- **Chapters** - a `chapters.json` next to a map's `Info.dat` defines labelled (possibly
  overlapping) sections, shown above the notes with progress bars. In practice mode, point at
  `<` / `>` and press A to jump to a chapter's start or end. See [docs/chapters.md](docs/chapters.md);
  `tools/ChaptersFromBookmarks` generates a starter file from a map's editor bookmarks.
- **Difficulty switch (practice mode)** - hold Y to show the difficulty list, flick the right
  stick to pick, release Y to switch. The notes are swapped in place without stopping the music;
  maps that need Noodle/Mapping Extensions/360 fall back to a restart at the same time. Flick the
  stick left/right instead to pick a note jump speed (your difficulty's own is underlined) and
  release Y to change only the NJS, in place, until the song ends or restarts.
- **Active pause (practice mode)** - press X to freeze the song in place without the pause menu;
  notes turn ghostly and twelve buttons (-1m ... -.25b / +.25b ... +1m, b = beats, snapped to the
  beat grid) let you step through the map with a saber and A or the trigger. Press X again to play
  on from there. Point at frozen notes to select them and press Flag to save feedback (labels like
  "Too dense", the selected notes, a screenshot) to `flags.json` next to the map - see
  [docs/flags.md](docs/flags.md).
- **Heart rate bridge** (off by default) - starts [tools/hr-osc-bridge](tools/hr-osc-bridge) with
  the game and keeps it running: your Bluetooth chest strap (Wahoo TICKR, Polar, Garmin...) is read
  through the PC's own Bluetooth and fed to the [HRCounter](https://github.com/qe201020335/HRCounter)
  mod over OSC. No phone app. Needs HRCounter on its "OSC Protocol" source and
  [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed.

## Install

Requires BSIPA, SiraUtil, BeatSaberMarkupLanguage and SongCore (all standard). Download the zip
from the latest [GitHub Release](https://github.com/pmaxhogan/bsaber-mods/releases) and extract it
into the game folder (it adds `Plugins/MaxTweaks.dll` and `UserData/MaxTweaks/hr_osc_bridge.py`).

## Development

See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for commands and layout, [docs/maxtweaks-spec.md](docs/maxtweaks-spec.md)
for the feature spec, [docs/qa.md](docs/qa.md) for the desktop-mode (FPFC) QA harness and
[docs/qa-checklist.md](docs/qa-checklist.md) for the VR playtest checklist.

## License

MIT

# halo-2-universal

Descompilación en curso de **Halo 2 para Xbox** (build `02.09.27.09809`,
`halo2ship.exe`, SHA-256 del `default.xbe`
`92746c937cd3d41e247cef7c9aea7d0dd1f3d09066b8f445c7665efaa0c6d17c`).

El objetivo a largo plazo es un port nativo del juego, como el que
[halo-ce-universal](https://github.com/cybersecurity/halo-ce-universal) hizo
con Halo: Combat Evolved.

**Estado: muy temprano.** El juego no arranca ni está cerca de hacerlo. Hoy
el proyecto abre los mapas del juego, lista su contenido y exporta los
niveles y los modelos con su textura principal. Del código del ejecutable
hay descompiladas 3074 funciones de las 11.265 que lista Ghidra (el 27,29 %), y
3397 en total contando las que Ghidra no separa de otras; todas
comprobadas contra el original. Consulta
[ESTADO.md](ESTADO.md) para la lista de lo hecho y lo que falta, y
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) para el detalle de cada paso.

## En qué se basa

Este proyecto sigue el método y la organización de
[cybersecurity/halo-ce-universal](https://github.com/cybersecurity/halo-ce-universal),
el port de la descompilación de Halo: Combat Evolved a Linux, Windows y
Android. Ese proyecto parte a su vez de
[bnunu/halo-1](https://github.com/bnunu/halo-1), que es un fork de
[punpckhdq/halo](https://github.com/punpckhdq/halo).

De halo-ce-universal se toma:

- La estructura de carpetas (`source/` por sistemas del motor, `tools/`).
- El estilo del código C.
- El código de Halo 1 como referencia: Halo 2 hereda parte de ese motor, y
  comparar funciones ayuda a identificarlas.
- A futuro, su capa de plataforma (`port/`), que sustituye a la consola Xbox
  (Direct3D 8, sonido, entrada, red). Halo 2 corre en la misma consola.

Este repositorio **no** es un fork de halo-ce-universal ni contiene su
código. Todo el código de aquí se escribe a partir del ejecutable de Halo 2.

## Datos del juego

El repositorio no incluye el juego ni nada sacado de él. Necesitas tu propia
copia de Halo 2 para Xbox, con `default.xbe` y la carpeta `maps/`.

- Copia `default.xbe` a `disc/`.
- Los mapas se pueden leer desde donde estén; no hace falta copiarlos.

`disc/` y `ghidra/` están en `.gitignore` y no se suben nunca.

## Herramientas

| Herramienta | Uso |
| --- | --- |
| [Ghidra](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra) 12.0.3 con [ghidra-xbe](https://github.com/XboxDev/ghidra-xbe) | Análisis del ejecutable |
| JDK 21 | Lo necesita Ghidra |
| clang y ld.lld ([llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw), o el componente Clang de Visual Studio Build Tools, firmado por Microsoft, si Smart App Control bloquea el otro) y [ninja](https://ninja-build.org/) | Compilar |
| Python 3 | Scripts de `tools/` |
| [Unicorn](https://www.unicorn-engine.org/) y [Capstone](https://www.capstone-engine.org/) (`pip install unicorn capstone`) | Emulador de procesador para probar las funciones, y desensamblador |

## Compilar y probar

```
ninja
python tools/test_functions.py
python tools/test_maps.py "<carpeta maps del juego>"
```

`ninja` comprueba los tamaños de las estructuras de `source/`. No genera
ningún programa: todas las herramientas son scripts de Python.

`test_functions.py` comprueba el código descompilado: ejecuta en un emulador
cada función de `source/` y la función del ejecutable de la que salió, con
los casos de `tests/`, y compara los resultados. Necesita `disc/default.xbe`.
Al final dice qué parte del código del juego está descompilada.

`test_maps.py` comprueba las herramientas de datos: abre todos los mapas,
comprueba que cada tag está donde el cargador lo espera y exporta la
geometría de cada nivel a `build/obj/`.

### Descompilar una función

1. Elegirla con `python tools/function_index.py leaves` (las más llamadas) y
   leerla con `function_index.py show <dirección>` (pseudocódigo) y
   `python tools/disassemble.py <dirección>` (instrucciones). El pseudocódigo
   de todas está en `ghidra/decompiled/all/`.
2. Buscar su equivalente de Halo 1 en `source/` de halo-ce-universal, para
   el nombre y como referencia de lo que hace.
3. Escribirla en `source/`, en el archivo del sistema al que pertenece, con
   su dirección en un comentario.
4. Añadirla a `symbols/functions.csv`, con el lugar de cada argumento en la
   función original (un registro o `stack`).
5. Si usa una variable global, definirla en `source/` y añadirla a
   `symbols/globals.csv` con su dirección.
6. Si llama a una función del juego que aún no está descompilada, añadir
   esa función a `symbols/functions.csv` sin archivo de origen. La prueba
   da entonces la misma función simulada a los dos lados
   (`externals={"nombre": función}`) y compara también las llamadas que
   recibe. Así se puede sustituir también una función ya descompilada,
   para probar solo la que la llama. Para un puntero a función dentro de
   una estructura se usa `Mock`. Si una variable global tiene punteros a
   sí misma (una tabla con sus entradas enlazadas en una lista), se le da
   un `GlobalData`; un puntero a ella como argumento es un `GlobalPointer`.
   Una función que nunca retorna se prueba cortándola desde una función
   simulada, con `raise StopCall`.
7. Añadir sus casos a `tests/` y ejecutar `test_functions.py`.

Listar el contenido de un mapa:

```
python tools/mapinfo.py "<carpeta maps>\zanzibar.map" --tags
```

```
python tools/bsp2obj.py "<carpeta maps>\zanzibar.map" zanzibar.obj

```

coloca (escenografía, máquinas, cajas, vehículos), con un material por
shader y su textura principal como PNG en una carpeta al lado. Con
`--collision` lleva la geometría que usa la física.

Sacar un modelo o una textura sueltos (el nombre puede ser el final del
nombre del tag):

```
# rickroll
An open-source Rickroll that's never gonna give you up.

commits.msg:
Merge pull request #24 from retracdev/feat/lms-variation

Add /lms/ LMS Max variation

Add /lms/ "LMS Max" fake-install variation

New entry page: LMS Max landing page with an Install button, a scrollable
features section, a fake installer (waits for the shared warm-up), a
browser-style "extension installed" notice at ~85%, then a Start button
that begins the Rickroll.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #23 from retracdev/feat/always-warmup

Always run the warm-up, starting at page load

Always run the warm-up, starting at page load

Filter detection never triggered on a real school filter, so drop it
(and probe.html) and give every visitor the same hidden, paused
standby player plus a 3.63s hold that starts as soon as the page loads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #22 from retracdev/feat/crazygames-probe

Use docs.crazygames.com as the filter probe site

Use docs.crazygames.com as the filter probe site

Google Sites refuses to be framed, so probe a game-site docs page that
allows embeds and answers 200 without redirects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #21 from retracdev/feat/iframe-filter-probe

Detect school filters with a hidden Google Sites iframe

Detect school filters with a hidden Google Sites iframe

A hidden probe page frames sites.google.com under a frame-src CSP; a
redirect to another domain raises a securitypolicyviolation that is
reported to the page, which then starts the warm-up. The plain fetch
check stays as a second signal (and no longer counts timeouts).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #20 from retracdev/feat/filter-warmup

Pre-load the video behind the intro on filtered networks

Pre-load the video behind the intro on filtered networks

If a fetch to Google Sites fails (a sign of a school web filter), create
the player early in a hidden, paused standby state and hold the fake
check / games loader for 3.63s. Normal networks are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #19 from retracdev/fix/games-inter-font

Keep the Rickroll in Inter on /games/

Keep the Rickroll in Inter on /games/

Fredoka was set on body, so the video section inherited it. Scope it to
the GamerNow intro (.gn-stage) only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #18 from retracdev/feat/games-variation

Add /games/ GamerNow variation

Add /games/ "GamerNow" variation with Play Now button

New entry page: candy-pink fake games site with the GamerNow logo, a
loading bar, then a "Play Now!" logo-button that starts the Rickroll.
The video player, reveal section and falling-photo layer now live in
script.js so every entry page shares them; the root page is unchanged
in behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #17 from retracdev/chore/remove-thanks-pill

Remove the green thanks pill

Remove the green "thanks" pill under the counter

Reverts the pill added in #16; the counter itself is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #16 from retracdev/feat/thanks-pill

Add green thanks pill under the counter

Add green "thanks" pill under the counter

A pill with a pulsing green dot says "Thanks for making the counter just
a little bit higher!" and stays for 10s after the reveal, then fades out.
Skipped if the counter request failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #15 from retracdev/feat/live-counter

Add live Rickroll counter

Add live Rickroll counter backed by Abacus

Every page load hits the free Abacus counter service and shows the
returned total in the counter card. The count lives outside the repo, so
it survives deploys and updates without a redeploy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #14 from retracdev/feat/release-pile

Drop the remaining pile through the screen 2.77s after falling ends

Drop the remaining pile through the screen 2.77s after falling ends

At MAYHEM_END_MS + 2770ms (~9.37s after playback starts), the settled photos
fall off the bottom of the screen with a little stagger and tumble, then are

# VAD для Android (APK)

Приложение: вставляете ссылку (или нажимаете «Поделиться» в браузере и выбираете VAD),
выбираете качество или формат, жмёте «Скачать». Файлы падают в `Загрузки/VAD`.
Движок: yt-dlp + ffmpeg (библиотека youtubedl-android), поддерживает большинство сайтов.

Возможности: авто-режим (FHD / HD / максимум), выбор видео- и аудиоформата вручную,
MP3, плейлисты, обновление yt-dlp кнопкой, свой прокси (socks5://… от ByeDPI/VPN), отмена.

## Как получить APK (без Android Studio)

1. Создайте на github.com пустой репозиторий (можно приватный).
2. Загрузите в него всё содержимое этой папки (Add file → Upload files; папка `.github` тоже!).
3. Откройте вкладку **Actions** → «Build APK» → дождитесь зелёной галочки (5-10 минут).
4. Внутри запуска, раздел **Artifacts** → `VAD-apk` → скачайте ZIP, внутри `app-debug.apk`.
5. Перекиньте APK на телефон и установите (разрешите установку из неизвестных источников).

## Сборка вручную (Android Studio / командная строка)
`gradle assembleDebug`: APK появится в `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/`.
Нужны JDK 17 и Android SDK 34.

# snes-recomp

Recompilador estático de ROMs de SNES (CPU 65816) escrito en Rust desde cero. Traduce la ROM a C, que se compila junto a un runtime propio (bus, DMA/HDMA, PPU, SPC700 y DSP, entrada y partidas guardadas) para obtener un ejecutable nativo.

> **Aviso legal.** Este repositorio no contiene ninguna ROM ni recurso de ningún juego, ni lo tendrá. Cada usuario debe aportar su propia copia obtenida legalmente. El C generado deriva de la ROM, así que va a `out/` (ignorado por git) y no debe subirse ni distribuirse. Proyecto independiente, sin relación con Nintendo ni con ningún titular de derechos de los juegos.

Este repositorio es el **motor**: recompilador, runtime y `snes-port`. No incrusta ningún juego; cada juego es un *perfil* (`games/<id>.toml` y, si lo necesita, C propio) que vive en su propio repositorio. El primero es *The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past* (USA, CRC32 `777AAC2F`): [`alttp-recomp`](https://github.com/AlexPerez7/alttp-recomp), que ya se juega en una ventana con imagen, sonido, teclado/mando y partidas guardadas.

Licencia: [MIT](LICENSE) (solo el código de este repositorio; no da derechos sobre ningún juego). Para contribuir, mira [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Cómo funciona

```
ROM ──► carga y cabecera ──► descubrimiento de código ──► grafo de funciones y bloques ──► generador de C
                              (descenso recursivo,         (aristas, tail calls,           (una función por función,
                               tablas de saltos,            diagnósticos)                   una etiqueta por bloque)
                               anchos M/X)                                                          │
                                                                                                    ▼
                                         runtime (C): bus LoROM · DMA/HDMA · PPU · SPC700+DSP · entrada · SRAM ──► ejecutable
```

- **Descubrimiento:** sigue el código desde los vectores y las entradas del perfil del juego (`games/<id>.toml`), resuelve saltos indirectos con tablas comprobadas a mano contra la ROM y sigue los anchos de los registros M/X por contexto de función.
- **Generación:** cada función del grafo es una función C; un bloque alcanzado con anchos distintos se emite una vez por combinación. Los retornos no locales (descartar una dirección con `PLA`/`PLA` antes de `RTS`) funcionan porque cada llamada comprueba la pila y la dirección de retorno al volver.
- **Runtime:** el C generado habla con el runtime a través de `runtime/snes_rt.h`. El runtime se reparte en un núcleo de hardware, la PPU, el sonido y dos frontales (uno sin vídeo para pruebas y otro interactivo con SDL2).

## Estado

| Área | Estado |
|---|---|
| Carga de ROM (LoROM, cabecera de copiador, CRC32, vectores) | hecho |
| Decodificador 65816 y desensamblador, con seguimiento de M/X | hecho |
| Descubrimiento de código y tablas de saltos | hecho (ALttP: 0 saltos sin resolver) |
| Grafo de funciones y bloques | hecho |
| Generador de C de toda la ROM | hecho: con el perfil de ALttP genera 4 176 de 4 178 funciones; 2 quedan como *stub* (`01:CA17`, `08:A8E3`) y no se ejecutan |
| Bus, DMA y HDMA | hecho |
| PPU por línea | hecho: modos 0 a 7, sprites, ventanas, mosaico, color math, HDMA, modo 7 |
| SPC700 y DSP | hecho: 256 instrucciones, temporizadores, ROM de arranque, voces BRR, ADSR/GAIN, ruido, eco |
| Frontal interactivo (SDL2) | hecho: ventana, pantalla completa, teclado y mandos, audio, `.srm` |
| Constructor de port desde la ROM del usuario (`snes-port`) | hecho: caché por CRC32, MSVC/gcc/clang o TinyCC descargado con consentimiento |
| Opciones de port (menú F1, `config.ini`, filtros) | hecho |
| Perfiles de juego (entradas, tablas, ganchos y C propio) | hecho: viven en el repositorio de cada juego |
| Pantalla ancha (`wide`, hasta 96 px por lado) | hecho en el motor, con API para el C del juego; el relleno específico de ALttP (franjas negras donde no hay mapa) está en curso en el cambio `alttp-wide-fill` y la precarga real del exterior queda como trabajo futuro |

Validación: más de 200 pruebas (algunas compilan y ejecutan el C generado; las que necesitan compilador, SDL2 o la ROM se omiten solas si faltan) y suites de *fuzz* de 30 000 fotogramas por mazmorras, overworld y Mundo Oscuro sin paradas ni *stubs* ejecutados.

Limitaciones conocidas: la interpolación del DSP usa un núcleo en forma de campana, cercano a la gaussiana del hardware pero no su tabla exacta; la PPU no emula el entrelazado; los comportamientos dependientes de ciclos exactos no se reproducen (el reloj es proporcional por bloques).

## Requisitos

- Rust estable (`cargo`).
- Un compilador de C: `gcc`, `clang` o Visual Studio Build Tools (en Windows, desde "x64 Native Tools" o tras `vcvars64.bat`).
- Para el frontal interactivo: el paquete de desarrollo de SDL2 para Visual C++ (`SDL2-devel-x.y.z-VC.zip`), descomprimido en `out/sdl2` o apuntado por `SDL2_DIR`.
- Tu ROM en `roms/` (ignorada por git), por ejemplo `roms/alttp_usa.sfc`.
- El **perfil del juego**, que sale del repositorio de ese juego (para ALttP, `alttp-recomp`): su carpeta `games/` va junto a `snes-port.exe` o en el directorio desde el que lo ejecutas, o se pasa con `--game <perfil.toml>`. Sin perfil, `snes-port` dice dónde busca y no construye nada.

## Uso

En los ejemplos, `games/alttp_usa.toml` es el perfil del repositorio `alttp-recomp`; si lo tienes en `games/` no hace falta `--game`.

### Análisis

```
cargo run --release -- info roms/alttp_usa.sfc                 # cabecera, CRC y vectores
cargo run --release -- disasm roms/alttp_usa.sfc 00:8000 40
cargo run --release -- discover roms/alttp_usa.sfc --game games/alttp_usa.toml   # --unresolved, --widths
cargo run --release -- graph roms/alttp_usa.sfc [00:8000] --game games/alttp_usa.toml   # resumen, o la función que contiene la dirección
cargo run --release -- codegen roms/alttp_usa.sfc 00:8000 --depth 1 -o out/reset.c --game games/alttp_usa.toml
cargo run --re

Ptalati015/Stumps_Ahead.readme:
# Stumps Ahead

A short-format cricket game for mobile browsers, inspired by EA Sports Cricket and Real Cricket 20 but much simpler. You play one T20-style match against the computer.

**Play it:** https://ptalati015.github.io/Stumps_Ahead/

## What's in the game

- Seven nations: India, England, Australia, New Zealand, West Indies, South Africa and Sri Lanka.
- Squads are generated fresh every session. All player names are fictional.
- Real home grounds for each nation (two per team), shown by their plain names without sponsors.
- Batting with shot buttons (including Loft), a direction pad to pick where to hit, moving across the crease, and right- and left-handed batters.
- Bowling where you drag a landing ring to pick where the ball pitches. You also choose a variation (swing, slower ball or spin), and whether to bowl over or around the wicket.
- Red, white or pink ball. A pink ball makes it a night match under floodlights.
- Ball-by-ball commentary, with lines and banners for milestones such as fifties, hundreds and hat-tricks.
- A pause button with the full scorecard, a short how-to-play and Quit to menu.
- 2, 5, 10 or 20 overs, with a super over if the match is tied, at Easy, Normal or Hard difficulty.

There is no backend, no account and no saved data. Refreshing the page starts a new session.

## Run it locally

You need any static file server, because ES modules don't load from `file://`.

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open http://localhost:8000.

## Tests

Tests use Node's built-in runner (Node 22 or later). There are no dependencies to install.

```sh
node --test
```

QA scripts live in `qa/` (see `qa/QA_CHECKLIST.md`). `node qa/check-names.mjs` checks that no generated name matches a real cricketer. `node qa/smoke.mjs` runs a headless mobile smoke test and needs Playwright.

## Project layout

```
index.html        App shell
css/              Styles
js/main.js        Screen router; holds the current match
js/engine/        Match rules, outcomes, AI, seeded RNG (pure, no DOM)
js/data/          Nations, name generator, venues
js/ui/            Screens, scoreboard, match scene, input
js/version.js     Current version
tests/            Node tests
qa/               QA checklist and scripts
dev/              Developer test page for the play screen
```

## How the project works

- **SPEC.md** is the product spec and the contract between the engine and UI code, including who owns which file.
- **ROADMAP.md** tracks what's done and what could come next.
- **CHANGELOG.md** lists every release. Versions use semantic versioning: new features bump the minor version and fixes bump the patch. The version in `js/version.js` is changed only in release PRs.
- Changes go through pull requests. Merging to `main` needs the owner's approval. GitHub Pages deploys from `main`.

The team works in named roles: Karen (product and spec), Ayush (match engine and play screen), Joel (teams, names and UI screens), Mark (security), Violet (QA), Researcher (ideas for what to build next) and Julie (docs, bug triage and release checks).

BirkleyG/Extraction.readme:
# Extraction Tycoon

**[Play the development sandbox](https://birkleyg.github.io/Extraction/play/)** · [Original prototype](https://birkleyg.github.io/Extraction/prototype/)

Mine ore, open shafts, upgrade your machines, and ship to published NPC buyers. Sales pay at departure. The animated mine runs immediately; no Firebase project, account or API key is needed to try it.

The default Pages game is a **single-player development sandbox with browser-local saves**. New mines use a provisional three-line Pick/Lift/Hauler economy: ten miners per shaft, punchier upgrades and short early shipping trips. Existing sandbox mines retain their previous economy; open **Tools → Try new economy** to back up the old mine and start fresh. It is not the authoritative multiplayer release. The original prototype and its separate browser saves remain available at `/prototype/`.

The scene reuses the original game's pixel sprites and look. Each planet is built around one central theme (for example a candy world, a haunted bone-yard, a dead neon city) and picks its own sky, moons, rock layers, ore names/colours and a ring of 5-7 regions. There are 39 region landscapes: 27 earthlike (mesa, dunes, glacier, volcanic, swamp, canyon, salt flats, temperate forest, jungle, savanna, tundra, taiga, prairie, alpine peaks, island chain, sea cliffs, lake country, hoodoo badlands, moor, autumn woodland, scrubland, red-rock arches, waterfall cliffs, geyser basin, palm oasis, rice terraces, redwoods) and 12 alien or sci-fi (crystal spires, fungal forest, floating islands, bone forest, neon ruins, tendril jungle, mirror desert, hive towers, black monoliths, reality rifts, scrap titans, watcher fields).

AI is the default way to make a planet: under **Tools** add your own Claude or OpenAI key, then **Planet → Ask the Maker**. The prompt makes the AI choose a theme first and read a summary of earlier planets (kept in this browser) so each one is new. With no key the Maker improvises from one of twelve built-in themes instead, avoiding recently used ones. Planets are presentation only in this sandbox; they do not change rates, prices or the ledger.

Controls: mouse wheel or pinch to zoom, drag to pan, `+` `-` `0` keys or the corner buttons to zoom and fit, and the top-left thumbnail (or `M`) flips between your mine and the whole-planet map, where you can click a region and move your mine there. Upgrades are named machines (Hand Winch → Rope Hoist → Steam Lift ...) that change how the lift, pick, yard and hauler look as you tier up.

Mining follows the rulebook (section 04): each region's site has one endless common ore, and shafts hide finite rare veins (and, in tough regions, a mythic one). Tunnels are dug out as the crew mines, veins sit in the rock ahead, and a vein only yields once the tunnel reaches it *and* the pick is hard enough. Opening a mine in a different region, or building a new planet, starts a fresh mine because ore and veins belong to the site.

Open **Tools** to fast-forward, adjust sound/motion, download your save or recovery backup, add explicit test coins, or reset only the sandbox. Older detailed history is summarized in Records while accounting totals are preserved. Prices, buyer budgets, starting coin and incomplete upgrade lines in this build are test fixtures, not certified game balance. No month competition is active.

## Run locally

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Visit http://localhost:8000/play/ for the sandbox or http://localhost:8000/prototype/ for the original prototype. Serve the repository root so the shared production ES module can load.

## Development and tests

Node 24.19.0 is pinned in `.nvmrc`.

```sh
npm --prefix play test
npm --prefix backend ci
npm --prefix backend test
npm --prefix backend run test:integration
```

The Firebase emulator tests additionally require Java 21. See [backend setup](backend/README.md) for the authenticated local API/demo and [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) for the original prototype's Firebase guide. Production Firebase deployment and its spending ceiling remain separate decisions.

## Specification and progress

- [Maintained rulebook](docs/rulebook/Extraction-Rulebook-v1.2.md)
- [Buildout plan](docs/development/Buildout-Plan.md)
- [Questions for the Boss](docs/development/Questions-for-the-Boss.md)
- [Production calibration evidence](docs/development/calibration/Production-Calibration.md)

GitHub Pages publishes `main`, root directory. Publishing changes must reach `main`; merging into a development/specification branch alone does not update the playable site. Future playable changes should target that published integration branch and pass the model/backend checks before deployment.

## Online play and latest evidence

Use **Play online** in the same pixel interface (or [open online mode](https://birkleyg.github.io/Extraction/play/?mode=online)), sign in and enter your private invite code. Online accounts and balances belong to the trusted server; sandbox saves and tuning do not transfer. [Deployment guide](docs/development/Deploy-Guide.md) explains setup. Backend source updates need a separate Cloud Run deployment; merging a PR only publishes browser changes through Pages.

[Sandbox economy studies](play/sim/README.md) include the supplied fluid approximation, the adopted experimental tuning and reproducible actual-engine pacing. The actual scripted first hour earns 130,010 gross with no grants; full-month balance remains provisional. [Latest progress and verification](docs/development/Overnight-Progress.md).

## Industry and colony preview

The new-economy sandbox now includes **Industry** and **Colony** tabs. Build a refinery (25K local test coin), route raw ore into it, refine and sell to NPC stations. Choose an output policy to sell automatically or fill your own station every 30 simulated seconds. Build a station (250K), stock refined goods and complete published spot orders. Hourly simulated market quotes react to supply. Ho

# PoE2 Builder

A Path of Exile 2 build optimizer driven by a headless Path of Building (PoB) engine. The spec
and roadmap are in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md). The old Rust attempt lives untracked in `legacy/`.

## Setup

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and git. Windows only for now: the engine runs on
PoB's bundled 64-bit LuaJIT DLL.

```
uv sync
uv run python scripts/fetch_pob.py
```

## Use

Double-click **`PoE2 Builder.bat`** in the project folder: it starts the local server and opens
the page in your browser (keep its window open while you use it; close it to stop). From a
terminal:

```
uv run python -m builder.data dump     # export game data from the pinned PoB (after setup or a pin change)
uv run python -m builder.data prices   # refresh the poe.ninja price cache
uv run python -m builder.web           # open the local web page
uv run python -m builder.search tests/fixtures/requests/ice_shot_gemling.json --seconds 300
uv run pytest                          # request, constraint and search tests
```

The web page holds the request form and saved requests. **Optimize** runs the search on the
request in the form (progress streams into the page) and shows the result: Requested vs
Delivered, a PoB code verified by reloading it, a shopping list (every item with its target affixes,
tiers and roll ranges, an estimated price with its confidence, and the total against the budget),
skills, a test-in-game checklist for every number marked * or not modeled, the conditions the build
sustains and its campaign reward choices. Each shopping-list line has a **Trade** button that makes
an official trade-site search for it when clicked (never automatically) and opens it. For a unique
whose version the optimizer chose (Megalomaniac's notables, From Nothing's keystone, a ring size),
that click also prices the exact version, which poe.ninja can't, and the list keeps that price. Results are
also saved under `data/results/`. The page
also checks any PoB code or poe.ninja / pobb.in share link against the current request. Optional:
set `POE2_BUILDER_CONTACT` to add a contact to the User-Agent sent to poe.ninja and the trade
site, as their API docs ask.

Beside the request form (below it on a narrow screen) is the **passive tree**: scroll to zoom, drag to
move, search for a passive by name or effect, left click a notable or keystone to require it and right
click to ban it. It edits the same Passives lists as the form and follows them (small passives share
names, so only notables and keystones can be picked). It is drawn with the game's own node art, cut
once from the sprite sheets PoB ships and cached under `data/` (Grinding Gear Games' art, for local use
only; without PoB's sheets the nodes are plain dots). Ticking an ascendancy sets the class to match
(Any class when the ticked ones span classes), and changing the class or ascendancy drops required or
banned ascendancy passives that no longer fit, saying which. A few nodes beside the class starts are a
different passive for some classes (Vile Wounds is Eagle Eye for a Huntress; PoB applies that when the
class is selected): they are marked ⇄, the tree shows the version of the chosen class (or whichever you
pick), and requiring or banning one sets the class to match. A result shows the same tree read-only,
with the passives the build allocated. While a run is going, edits to the form reach it about a second and a half
after you stop typing: the search stops, keeps its best build, and continues from that build's PoB code
with the new settings for the time left (an edit with errors is reported and changes nothing). Under the
progress, a summary of the best build found so far updates each time a search round ends.

**Calibrate rare prices** (top of the page) prices about 24 representative rares on the official
trade site, paced by its rate limits (a few minutes), and fits the rare price model to them; the
next optimizer run uses it. Slots with too little data stay labelled as estimates.

**Price unique versions** (also at the top) prices every version of From Nothing (one per keystone)
and Controlled Metamorphosis (one per ring size) on the trade site, about 7 minutes. poe.ninja has
one price for all of a unique's versions; after this, the optimizer budgets each version at its own
trade price and doesn't offer versions nobody sells. A Megalomaniac's notables are chosen at
poe.ninja's price: its Trade button in the shopping list prices that exact version.

Gear is normal bases, affordable uniques and rares built affix by affix, with runes, Soul Cores
and Idols in their sockets and jewels in the tree's sockets. Rare prices come from the calibrated
model (uncalibrated estimates until you calibrate), and flasks and charms aren't modeled yet. Any skill can be the main skill;
where PoB doesn't model a skill's trigger (e.g. Explosive Transmutation's Remnant pickups), the
result marks the assumed rate with an asterisk.

## Engine checks

```
uv run python benchmarks/make_test_builds.py   # regenerate benchmarks/builds/*.xml
uv run python benchmarks/run_gates.py          # fidelity, delta agreement, round trip, timings
uv run python benchmarks/bench_pool.py         # parallel what-if throughput by worker count
uv run python benchmarks/compare_versions.py   # dev snapshot vs PoB release, per build
uv run python benchmarks/run_optimizer.py      # optimizer vs naive baselines on four skeletons
uv run python benchmarks/fuzz_constraints.py   # gate 5: random requests, every result rechecked
```

`scripts/fetch_pob.py` checks out both the pinned dev snapshot (what the optimizer calculates
with) and the matching PoB release (what the PoB app runs, used for cross-checks).

To check fidelity against real builds, save PoB codes exported from the PoB app as
`benchmarks/reference/<name>.txt`. `run_gates.py --pob-dir vendor/PathOfBuilding-PoE2-<release>`
compares them with the release the app runs; `compare_versions.py` explains what the snapshot
changes.

socketed non-unique Time-Lost jewel gets the node set of its radius made 40% longer, by PoB's own

enchantments there; From Nothing's keystone and the ring size are option stats), then all but one
line for versions of several. Only the exact search prices the version (median of the five
cheapest asks); it is kept per (unique, variants) in data/prices/<league>/unique_versions.json,
and the shopping list uses it with its date, or says the version isn't listed.

- Unique corrections keep the line's variant tags and rolled ranges
- Bridge re-adds corrections when PoB re-parses ascendancy nodes, which had
  silently dropped them; parseLines reports the parsed modifiers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Ledger for PoB's gaps: find what PoB ignores, correct it, show the rest

- The bridge asks PoB which passive and unique lines its parser can't
  read (885 passive lines on 304 notables/keystones, 454 lines on 217
  uniques); the data dump saves the list as gaps.json.
- Ledger entries (ledger/entries/*.yaml) translate an ignored line into
  modifier text PoB does calculate, with confidence and sources. Passive
  corrections are added to the tree nodes' own modifier lists in the
  engine, so allocations and what-ifs see them; unique corrections are
  appended to the item text. Lines with no effect on boss DPS or the
  checked defences are recorded as such.
- Every result lists its own blind spots: lines on its passives and items
  that PoB ignores, and which of them the ledger covers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Abyssal Lich, and required skills that only an item or passive grants

- Abyssal Lich has no passives of its own in PoB's tree: it switches the
  Lich's 19 nodes to its own stats. An ascendancy without nodes now uses
  the nodes of the one sharing its start node, so it's no longer rejected
  with "no allowed ascendancy has passives to allocate".
- A required skill no gem gives (e.g. Cast on Block, from Svalinn) brings
  its source along as a requirement, and only weapon setups that can hold
  that source are searched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Phase 3: rares, sockets, jewels, budget, and gate 4

- Rares built affix by affix from PoB's modifier pool (spawn weights by
  base tags, one per group, 3 prefixes + 3 suffixes), with item level,
  best tier and roll capped by the gear tier; priced by an uncalibrated
  estimate that still counts against the budget.
- Budget weight lambda: every gear choice pays for its price once spending
  presses on the cap; the cap still holds at the source.
- Runes, Soul Cores and Idols in sockets, priced from poe.ninja, with
  per-character augment limits enforced.
- Rare and unique jewels in the tree's sockets; one new socket tried per
  full round.
- Normal bases now carry their implicits (PoB doesn't add them).
- Skill-cost sustain: recovery under 10% of the per-second cost is a
  requirement-style shortfall (a gate 4 Ice Nova "did 2.4M" paying 3,263
  Mana/s against 114 regeneration). The bar is set below the user's own
  endgame builds (19-71%) since flasks aren't modeled.
- benchmarks/gate4.py: each reference build re-optimized at its own
  defences; 3 of 4 beaten (x4.4 to x24), the Ritualist (dual wield,
  item-granted keystone) not.

The user's 4,000-Mana Gemling request is met (4,006 Mana, 77% all
resistances, 314k DPS); Little Minions meets its 1.5M gate (1.92M).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Every skill can be a main skill, Explosive Transmutation included

- Skills only a passive or a unique grants (Elemental Storm, Demon Form,
  Wildwood's Gifts, ...) get skeletons that require their source; the
  granted group becomes the main group.
- The skill screen no longer filters by skill type; PoB's numbers decide.
- Assumptions for what PoB doesn't model, injected as modifiers and shown
  with an asterisk: Explosive Transmutation explodes at min(Remnants per
  second from the build's sources, its cooldown cap), with the source rates
  from the user's 0.5.4 audit; other triggered main skills with a cooldown
  and no modeled trigger fire whenever the cooldown allows (low confidence).
  Remnant-source gems and ascendancy nodes get real trials, since their
  worth only shows once the assumption updates.
- The main skill's stat set (e.g. Fire vs Cold storm) is chosen by score.
- Required ascendancy passives are always allocated, even before the main
  skill deals damage.

Explosive Transmutation (Acolyte): 0 -> 100k DPS; Elemental Storm 41k.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Requirements first, and a double-click launcher

A first real test (Gemling Glacial Lance, MoM, pure Armour, 75% all
resistances, 4,000 Mana) stopped at 2,165 Mana and called it infeasible.
Fixed weights never paid for the several DPS-losing moves a big gap
needs. Now a requirement still short after a pass gets its weight raised
(x4, up to x64), the tree is regrown on the second raise, and results are
ranked by shortfall before damage. The same request reaches 3,560 Mana
with everything else met; experiments put the uniques-only ceiling near
there, so the rest needs rare gear (Phase 3), and the result says so.

Also: one-handed weapons get both Shield and Focus skeletons; stats come
back as an object even when empty (the condition resolver crashed on an
empty list); "PoE2 Builder.bat" starts the page with a double-click,
reusing a running copy or picking a free port.

Benchmarks still beat the naive baselines (x3.2 to x9.7), gate 5 passes
30/30 over three seeds, gates 1-3 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Phase 2: optimizer core, wired into the web page

The search (builder/search/): every legal skeleton (ascendancy, main skill,
weapon) probed across the worker pool with successive halving, then block
coordinate ascent with kicks on the best few. Supports are scored with PoB's
accelerated gem path, persistent skills fill spare Spirit, the passive tree
grows by path value per point (lazy greedy, Steiner pairs, prune and regrow,
attribute choices, exact ascendancy enumeration), and gear is uniques plus
normal bases with the budget enforced at the source. A condition resolver
turns PoB conditions on only with real evidence, and quest rewards are
chosen. Finalists are polished on Full DPS, exported, and the code is
reloaded to verify it. The web page runs requests, streams progress and
shows the result; `python -m builder.search` does the same from a shell.

Engine fixes found on the way: PoB's copyTableSafe wrote into the objects it
copied, growing the shared passive tree on every build load until a worker
ran out of memory (corrected in the bridge at runtime, gates still exact);
gem what-ifs now recompute gem requirements; Full DPS no longer counts
on-death damage like Fiery Death for bosses; unpayable skill costs are hard
limits. The pool has a watchdog for runaway workers.

Results: beats naive baselines x3.2 to x10.5 on four skeletons in two
minutes; gate 5 passes 20/20 random requests; gates 1-3 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- builder.data: dump gems, passive tree, bases, uniques, mods and runes

refaustria/daisychess.desc: DaisyChess — free, ad-free, open-source chess analysis, training and play. Web app: play.daisychess.org
refaustria/daisychess.readme:
# DaisyChess — Browser & Server Chess Analysis

A modern, minimal chess analysis web app. Play a game yourself or import a PGN, and let Stockfish (or other UCI engines) evaluate every position with a live evaluation bar, best-move suggestions and full-game analysis.

Two analysis backends are offered and can be switched at runtime:

- **Browser mode** — Stockfish compiled to WebAssembly runs in a Web Worker on the user's machine. No server required.
- **Server mode** — native Stockfish (and optionally other engines) runs on a dedicated machine and streams results over WebSocket. Stronger, faster, multi-threaded.

> **License:** GPL-3.0-or-later (see [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE), third-party components in [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)).
> **Live instance:** <https://play.daisychess.org> (formerly c.referee.at, which now redirects) · **Community site:** <https://daisychess.org> · **Source:** <https://github.com/refaustria/daisychess>
> **Run your own:** a single host with nginx and systemd is described in [`deploy/README.md`](./deploy/README.md); a Docker Compose setup (web + engine server) is in [`docker/`](./docker/). Want to contribute? See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

> **For Claude Code:** this repository is run by an orchestrating Claude Code session that acts as project manager only. It does not implement features itself; it plans, delegates to sub-agents, reviews and integrates. See [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md) and the section *Working Model for Claude Code* below.

## Status

All milestones M0–M10 are implemented (play, browser and server analysis, game review, play vs engine, online import, theming, hardening); the live app is https://play.daisychess.org (moved from c.referee.at in ADR-021; the old address hands browser settings over once and redirects). Task-level status is in [`docs/PLAN.md`](./docs/PLAN.md), design decisions in [`docs/DECISIONS.md`](./docs/DECISIONS.md) (ADR-001..), the threat model in [`docs/SECURITY.md`](./docs/SECURITY.md), deployment in [`deploy/README.md`](./deploy/README.md) and `docker/`.

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Play (board, move list, undo, flip, FEN/PGN import, keyboard navigation) | done |
| Browser engine (Stockfish 19 WASM, MultiPV, eval bar, arrows, line preview) | done |
| Server engine (native Stockfish 19, WebSocket, limits, Origin check) | done |
| Game review (accuracy, eval graph, key moments, annotated PGN export) | done |
| Engine registry and multi-engine comparison | done (Stockfish; other UCI engines are configurable on the server) |
| Human-like engine: Lc0 + Maia 1100–1900 on the server (`style: human`, 1-node policy move, move probabilities) | server done (ADR-019, M23-1); web (play vs Maia, review hints) in progress (M23-2/3) |
| Theming (board colours, piece sets Cburnett/Letters, coordinates, highlights, sounds, dark/light) | done |
| Accessibility / performance pass | done (axe e2e checks, keyboard-operable tabs; the board itself is mouse/touch only) |
| Play a friend via link (rooms on the server: nickname, time control, colour; reconnect, draw/resign/abort/claim, spectators) | server done (ADR-013); web UI in progress (M16-2) |
| Opening database, accounts | not built (non-goals for v1) |

---

## 1. Goals

| Goal | Description |
|---|---|
| Play | Drag-and-drop board, legal-move highlighting, undo, flip, move list with SAN notation |
| Import | Load PGN (file upload or paste), FEN input, navigate with keyboard arrows |
| Analyze | Live engine evaluation of the current position, top-N lines (MultiPV), best-move arrows |
| Eval bar | Vertical bar next to the board, centipawn → win-probability mapping, mate display (M3) |
| Game review | Analyze all moves of a game, classify (best / good / inaccuracy / mistake / blunder), accuracy per side |
| Engines | Pluggable engine registry; enable/disable engines, run several in parallel for comparison |
| Backends | Switch between browser (WASM) and server (native) analysis at any time |
| Look & feel | Clean, modern board (Lichess-like default: brown/beige squares, cburnett pieces); themes for colors, pieces, coordinates, dark/light UI |

Non-goals (for v1): online multiplayer, user accounts, opening database, cloud storage.

---

## 2. Architecture

```
daisychess/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/                 # Vite + React + TypeScript frontend
│   └── server/              # Node.js (TypeScript) engine server, WebSocket API
├── packages/
│   ├── engine-core/         # Shared: UCI parser, Engine interface, eval types, cp→% mapping
│   └── ui-theme/            # Board/piece themes (CSS + assets)
├── engines/                 # Native engine binaries / NNUE files for the server (git-ignored, fetched by script)
├── docker/                  # Dockerfiles + compose for server mode
├── .claude/                 # Claude Code agent definitions and project memory
├── CLAUDE.md
└── README.md
```

### 2.1 Frontend (`apps/web`)

- **Vite + React 18 + TypeScript**, state via Zustand.
- **Board:** `chessground` (the Lichess board library). Pure CSS theming → easy customization.
- **Rules / notation:** `chess.js` for move generation, FEN, PGN parsing, SAN.
- **Engine access:** a single `EngineClient` interface with two implementations:
  - `WasmEngineClient` — loads a WASM engine inside a Web Worker.
  - `RemoteEngineClient` — talks to the server over WebSocket.
- **Layout:** a single page (`/`): board + eval bar, engine panel, and tabs for Moves, Play, Openings, Live, Friend, Import, Review, Explorer and Settings (all but Moves and Import are lazy-loaded). There is no router.
- Structure and dev hooks: [`apps/web/README.md`](./apps/web/README.md).

| `lite` (multi-thread) | small | yes | if headers available |

crazy0codes/hospital-escape.readme:
# St. Aldric: Night Shift Never Ended

First-person 3D horror in the browser. You wake in a closed hospital at night. One stalker hunts you. Find 3 keys, unlock the exit, get out. About 10 to 15 minutes.

## Run

Needs Node 18+.

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

Open the URL it prints (http://localhost:5173), click **Click to begin**.

To play the production build instead: `npm run play` (opens on http://localhost:4173).

Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox with headphones. Sounds are `.ogg`; browsers without Ogg Vorbis support (older Safari) will run the game silently.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| W A S D | Move |
| Mouse | Look |
| Shift | Run (loud, 5 s of stamina) |
| F | Flashlight |
| E | Interact (take, read, unlock) |
| Esc | Pause |
| R | Restart (after death or win) |

## How it plays

- Keys are in Ward A (north), the Pharmacy (north east) and the Boiler Room (south west). The exit is at the south end.
- The torch drains. Spare cells (green cans) give +35%.
- The Patient hears running (12 m) and walking (5 m), and sees you in its view cone (14 m, or 8 m if you stand still with the torch off).
- Holding the torch beam on it for about a second makes it flinch for a few seconds. It then comes back, so use it to get away, not to win.
- Each key makes the hospital worse: key 1 wakes it, key 2 kills corridor lights and speeds it up, key 3 starts an alarm and it hunts you.

## Stack

three.js (rendering, GLTF, animation, positional audio), Rapier (collisions and character controller), recast-navigation (navmesh and pathfinding), postprocessing (bloom, vignette, grain, grade), Vite. Custom code is only the level layout, enemy rules and game flow in `src/`.

## Assets

All CC0. Sources and file list are in `CREDITS.md`. Design notes are in `GAME_SCRIPT.md`.

## What was and wasn't tested

Tested automatically in headless Chromium (software WebGL), against both dev and production builds: loads with no console errors or warnings; every key, battery, note, waypoint and the exit is reachable on the navmesh; the player capsule collides with walls and furniture and passes through doorways; enemy patrol, hear, chase, stun and kill; key pickup, locked and unlocked exit, win, death, restart and pause; keyboard and mouse input.

Not tested (no way to here): real GPU frame rate, how the sound mix and scare pacing feel, pointer lock in a real browser window (the tests used a no-lock mode), Safari. Software rendering ran at only a few frames per second, so performance on a laptop is unmeasured. The scene is light (about 130 meshes, 43k triangles, one shadow-casting light) but treat smoothness as unconfirmed.

Known limits: the models are low-poly and flat coloured, so the look comes from darkness, fog and grain. The stalker is a user-supplied wendigo model. Its walk, run, stun and attack are posed in code (`src/creature.js`) over a single idle clip; this was checked in a model viewer only, not yet in a full playthrough.

Optional test scripts are in `tools/tests/` (they need `@sparticuz/chromium` and `puppeteer-core`).

k-chary/kulki.readme:
# Kulki

A Lines-style ball puzzle for the desktop, in Polish. Tauri + React + TypeScript, SQLite for highscores and the saved game.

- Spec: [docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md) — the single source for game rules, behavior and tech decisions.
- Visual design: [Kulki visual design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/Rg7LMfMFpU8usuiQCrqQF4). Reference copies of its tokens and component CSS are in [docs/design/](docs/design/).
- Work is tracked as GitHub issues under the `v1` milestone; one PR per issue, reviewed and merged by @k-chary.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 26 (see `.nvmrc`; 22 or newer works) and npm
- Rust (stable) and the [Tauri 2 system dependencies](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) for your OS. On Debian/Ubuntu:
  `sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential libssl-dev librsvg2-dev`

Then install the JavaScript dependencies:

```sh
npm install
```

## Commands

| Command                   | What it does                                                         |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run tauri dev`       | Runs the desktop app with hot reload (starts Vite on port 1420)      |
| `npm run tauri build`     | Builds the installer for the current OS into `src-tauri/target/`     |
| `npm run dev`             | Runs only the web frontend in a browser at http://localhost:1420     |
| `npm run build`           | Typechecks and builds the web frontend into `dist/`                  |
| `npm run build:e2e`       | Builds the web frontend with the e2e test hook (`?seed=`, `?board=`) |
| `npm run e2e`             | Playwright end-to-end tests against that build (builds it first)     |
| `npm run lint`            | ESLint, Stylelint and Prettier check                                 |
| `npm run format`          | Formats every file with Prettier                                     |
| `npm run typecheck`       | TypeScript in strict mode, no emit                                   |
| `npm test`                | Vitest once (`npm run test:watch` to keep it running)                |
| `npm run storybook`       | Storybook at http://localhost:6006 with the Tokens page              |
| `npm run build-storybook` | Builds Storybook into `storybook-static/`                            |

Pull requests run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `.github/workflows/pr.yml`. The full suite (Vitest, component tests and Playwright) runs on demand from the Actions tab (`.github/workflows/full-suite.yml`) and for releases. Run `npx playwright install chromium` once before `npm run e2e`.

The e2e build reads `?seed=7` (seeded random generator) and `?board=rrrr...../...&preview=bbb` (nine rows split by `/`; r o y g b p for a ball, `.` for empty) from the URL. The hook exists only in `--mode e2e` and dev builds.

## Releasing

The version lives in git tags. Agents never push tags by hand; CI does.

1. **Every PR gets a suggested version** in a comment (`.github/workflows/version-suggestion.yml`), from the PR title: `feat:` is a minor bump, `feat!:` or `fix!:` a breaking one (a minor bump while the app is below 1.0), and anything else a patch. A label overrides the title: `release:major`, `release:minor`, `release:patch` or `release:none` (no tag). Merging is the approval.
2. **Every merge to `main`** runs the full suite (`full-suite.yml`: lint, typecheck, Vitest and component tests, Playwright, `cargo test`) in `.github/workflows/main.yml`. If it passes, the job tags the commit with the next version, taking the largest bump of the PRs merged since the last tag. A failing suite means no tag; the next merge covers it.
3. **The merge also creates a draft GitHub Release** with generated notes, and asks for your approval. The `release` environment (Settings › Environments) has you as a required reviewer, so GitHub sends a push notification to the mobile app: open the run and tap **Review deployments › Approve and deploy**. Ignoring the request skips that version; it expires after 30 days.
4. **After the approval** `release.yml` stamps the tag's version into `package.json`, `Cargo.toml` and `tauri.conf.json` for that build only (the copies on `main` are not updated and can look stale), builds installers for Windows, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux, attaches them to the draft release and publishes it. The in-app update banner appears for installed copies once the release is published. If an installer build fails, the release stays a draft.

To build a tag by hand (for example one made before the approval step existed), open **Release** in the Actions tab, press "Run workflow" and type the tag; an empty field means the latest tag.

One-time setup: create the environment `release` under Settings › Environments, tick "Required reviewers" and add yourself. Without it the `gate` job fails and nothing is built.

`node scripts/release.ts next v0.3.0 < prs.tsv` (lines of `title<TAB>labels`) shows what version a set of PRs would produce.

The installers are not code-signed yet, so the first launch shows a warning:

- **Windows:** SmartScreen says “Windows protected your PC”. Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
- **macOS:** Gatekeeper refuses an app from an unidentified developer. Right-click Kulki in Applications, choose “Open” and confirm, or allow it under System Settings › Privacy & Security. If macOS says the app is damaged, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Kulki.app`.
- **Linux:** no warning; make the AppImage executable with `chmod +x`.

## Updates

The installed app looks for a newer **published** release at launch and every 6 hours. When it finds one, a bar at the top of the window shows „Dostępna nowa wersja X.Y.Z” with „Zainstaluj i uruchom ponownie” (the game is saved after every move, so restarting loses nothing) and „Później”. A failed check (offline, no release yet) shows nothing. The code is in `src/update/` and `src/components/UpdateBanner/`; the Tauri updater plugin read

tkFX-0/ironfield.desc: Cooperative factory-automation game for iPhone and desktop browsers
tkFX-0/ironfield.readme:
# Ironfield

A cooperative factory-automation game for the browser, built for iPhone Safari and desktop.
Mine, smelt, belt, research, refine oil and launch a rocket together.

**Play:** https://tkfx-0.github.io/ironfield/

- One big world cut into 47 equal plots, one per prefecture, laid out like a tile map of Japan (`src/plots.js`). You build in your own prefecture's plot together with the other players from that prefecture. Each plot is an open room (`plotRoom(p)` in `src/net/session.js`): whoever is inside hosts it; when the host leaves, a remaining player takes over automatically, and a retained copy on the broker (plus a copy on every player's device) lets the next visitor resume it when nobody is inside.
- There is no single player, no self-hosted world and no room codes: every factory lives in a plot.
- Multiplayer is deterministic lockstep over public MQTT brokers: only player commands travel; every peer runs the same simulation.
- All art and sound are generated procedurally at load time. No build step: plain ES modules.
- Prefecture territory battle (陣取り, design in `docs/陣取り設計.md`): flags made in the factory are placed on a 10 km grid of Japan, 3 per day. For now the map and the other prefectures are simulated on the device (`src/jintori/`).

## Run locally

```
npx http-server . -p 8140 -c-1
```

Then open http://localhost:8140/. Headless checks: `node tools/simtest.mjs`, `node tools/stress.mjs`, `node tools/jintori-test.mjs`.

## Layout

- `src/sim/` deterministic simulation (belts, inserters, machines, power and fluid networks, research)
- `src/render/` WebGL2 renderer, procedural sprite atlas, terrain shader
- `src/ui/`, `src/input.js` touch-first HUD and panels
- `src/net/session.js` lockstep multiplayer over MQTT
- `src/audio.js` synthesized sound

Big world: each prefecture's own scenery (snowy north, southern beaches)

Prefectures get a snow and a warmth amount (plots.js CLIMATE) that blend
smoothly across plot borders. Snow lies in patches that join up further
north, trees turn into snowy firs, rocks and dead trees get snow, the sea
goes cold and ices over on Hokkaido's coast. The south gets wider bright
beaches, turquoise shallows, palms and lusher green. The minimap follows.

A plot's newest saved copy runs on this device only (ViewSession), refreshed
every minute. Reached from the title screen, the menu's 47-plot picker, or by
tapping a neighbouring plot's name at the border. Building, removing and
saving are off while looking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Big world: show the neighbouring plots' buildings past the border

After you enter a plot, the 8 plots around it are read in the background
from their saved copies (the broker's retained copy or this device's,
whichever is newer; sides first, then corners; again every 5 minutes) and
drawn 64 tiles deep around yours with the same scene code, dimmed. Plots
without a copy still show the land they were generated with.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Big world: land runs on across plot borders, neighbouring plots visible past the edge

Terrain is now one landscape in world coordinates; only sides with no plot in
the tile map become coast. The renderer draws 64 tiles of the neighbouring
plots' land and trees around yours, dimmed, with a border line and the
neighbours' names. Plot rooms move to KENY* (and local copies to plot2-*)
because the old plots' land no longer matches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Big world: 47 prefecture plots replace single player, self-hosting and the shared world

The title screen now shows the 47 prefectures as equal plots on a tile map
shaped like Japan. Each plot is an open room (plotRoom in net/session.js)
with the same host takeover as the old shared world. Your prefecture on the
territory map is your plot; changing it moves your factory there.
Single player, hosting, room codes, the lobby list and saved worlds are gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Territory battle: factory-made flags and a local Japan map

Steps 1 and 2 of docs/陣取り設計.md. A new flag item (hand-craftable;
the "flag-improved" research unlocks a cheaper machine-only recipe) is
spent on a 10 km grid of Japan (4,223 squares built from Natural Earth
admin-1, public domain). Three flags a day, refilled at 05:00 JST,
carrying over up to nine. Flags take empty squares next to your
prefecture, wear down a rival square's defence, or raise your own;
prefectural offices cannot be taken. Until the server exists, the map
lives in localStorage and the other prefectures are simulated.

live in src/jintori/. Checks: node tools/jintori-test.mjs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Shared open world anyone can enter, with automatic host takeover

A fixed room (PLAZA2) holds one world for everybody. Entering probes
the broker for a live host; with nobody inside, the device opens the
newest copy (the broker's retained copy or its own). When the host
leaves, remaining players take over in join order. Hosts carry an
epoch: a stale host (e.g. a phone waking up) yields to the newer one,
and clients ignore frames from hosts they do not follow.

Mxeaez/mxeaez-dps.readme:
# mxeaez-dps

A fork of the [OSRS Wiki DPS calculator](https://github.com/weirdgloop/osrs-dps-calc) (by Weird Gloop, GPL-3.0),
live at **https://dps.mxeaez.com**.

What this fork adds on top of upstream:

* **The Fractured Archive (raid 4) bosses**: Archive Guardian, The Smorks + Bork, Ezekiel, Dreadnoth the Jellied,
  Moia, Xarth, the Dagon'hai Elder + Monks and Ocellus (all phases), with party size, defence floors and boss-specific
  rules, plus the raid's reward items (Obligator, Zorya's tome, Ascension crossbows, Zeal, elemental fragments).
* **Best setup** (`/best-setup`) with four raid tabs — **Fractured Archive, Tombs of Amascut, Chambers of Xeric,
  Theatre of Blood** — each with the same three tabs, run in a web worker:
  * **Search**: a gear search per boss / phase over a pool of end-game items (the presets seed it);
  * **Plan**: the worn set + switch items that minimise the raid's DPS time within 28 inventory slots (items always
    brought, comfort supplies; the combat potions are chosen from the kit; one camped ring by default, or camp
    Lightbearer / allow ring switches), with its per-encounter times and the route comparison (Fractured Archive: 8
    routes; the old Routes / Encounters tab was merged into it in phase 23);
  * **Summary**: the top search result for every boss / phase.
* **Items I don't own**: cross off items you don't have (kept in your browser). Search still shows the true best and
  greys rows that use them (or "Only items I own"); Plan never uses them.
* A simple view with the rarely changed inputs under **Advanced**, a "?" glossary, and drains shown as weapon icons ×
  count with each spec's chance to land.
* **Drain states** None / Solo / Team: Solo = your own spec weapons within your spec energy, Team = the carriers' first
  round of specs; both rank at the Defence floor when P(floor) ≥ 95%, else at the expected Defence.
* **The planner picks the spec weapons** (Plan tab): Solo tries every set of Elder maul / DWH / BGS / Tonalztics / Eye
  of Ayak with the kit ("Bring: …", with what dropping / adding each changes); Team picks the team's carriers (each must
  save ≥ 1 s of route time; FA 6-man: 2 Elder maul + 2 Tonalztics) and your share ("assign me"). Headline plans
  (defaults, Team; phase 31: nothing pinned by default, the Saturated heart is magic's kit potion, Dizana's quiver holds a
  second arrow / bolt type for free; phase 32: no zero-value switch items, a loadout without ammo keeps the kit's ammo
  in its slot; phase 35: adds such as Kephri's scarabs or the CoX Mystics get no specs; phase 36: one spec budget per
  encounter, damage specs and the surge potion; its review: one spec bar per party member): see *Headline plans* below.
* **Damage specs and the surge potion** (phase 36): Voidwaker, Dragon / Burning claws, Zaryte crossbow and Crimson
  kisten specs compete with the drains for one spec budget per encounter (100% at each boss, regen on the fight's
  clock); the planner brings a damage spec weapon or a Surge potion when it saves ≥ 1 s per slot and says where to drink
  the doses; the Search tab lists every damage spec's value on the selected boss ("Specs (damage)": average damage, gain
  over normal hits, time saved, cost, best gain per 100% energy first).
* **Plans in under a minute** (phase 37): exact memos of the planner's encounter times and passes, and the camp-one ring
  runs spread over parallel workers (FA ~19 s, ToA ~17 s, ToB ~21 s, CoX ~38 s on a 20-thread machine), same results.
* **Times assume N players at your DPS** (the "Players assumed at your DPS" input under Advanced; the page says "times assume N players at your DPS"):
  N defaults to the party size in ToA / CoX / ToB, where upstream scales boss hp with it, and to 1 in the Fractured
  Archive, whose hp scaling is unknown.
* Images served from this repo's `cdn/` folder, so new monsters have images.

u11028/mu_sky.readme:
# MU Sky

เกม RPG ออนไลน์ 3 มิติ ตัวละครชิบิน่ารัก เล่นได้ทั้งบนเว็บและมือถือ ผจญภัยใน 6 ภาคของไทย ตีมอนสเตอร์ ล่าบอส สู้กับผู้เล่นอื่น สะสมฉายา และทำภารกิจประจำวัน

## ต้องมี

- Node.js 22 ขึ้นไป

## เริ่มเล่น

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm start
```

เปิด http://localhost:2567 ในเบราว์เซอร์ มือถือที่ต่อ Wi-Fi เดียวกันเข้าได้ที่ `http://<IP ของคอม>:2567`
(ครั้งแรก Windows อาจถามเรื่อง Firewall ให้กดอนุญาต)

## ระหว่างพัฒนา

```bash
npm run dev
```

เปิด http://localhost:5173 แก้โค้ดแล้วหน้าเกมโหลดใหม่เอง ส่วนเซิร์ฟเวอร์ (พอร์ต 2567) รีสตาร์ทเอง

## วิธีเล่น

| | คอม | มือถือ |
|---|---|---|
| เดิน | WASD หรือลูกศร หรือคลิกพื้น | จอยสติ๊กซ้ายล่าง หรือแตะพื้น |
| ซูมกล้อง | ลูกกลิ้งเมาส์ | ใช้สองนิ้วถ่างหรือหุบ |
| โจมตี | Space หรือ J | ปุ่มแดง ⚔ |
| ฟันพายุหมุน (ตีรอบตัว) | Q หรือ 1 | ปุ่ม 🌀 |
| พุ่งทะยาน | E หรือ 2 | ปุ่ม 💨 |
| ฟาดสายฟ้า (ตีหนักข้างหน้า) | R หรือ 3 | ปุ่ม ⚡ |
| พรแห่งชีวิต (ฮีลตัวเอง) | F หรือ 4 | ปุ่ม 💚 |
| แชท | Enter พิมพ์ แล้ว Enter ส่ง | แตะช่องพิมพ์ |
| ภารกิจและฉายา | ปุ่ม 📜 มุมซ้ายบน | เหมือนกัน |

- **6 ภาค** เดินเข้าประตูวาร์ปเพื่อเดินทาง แต่ละภาคมีมอนสเตอร์ของตัวเองและบอส 1 ตัว ยิ่งไกลจากภาคกลางยิ่งเก่ง
- **ต่อสู้** ตีได้ทั้งมอนสเตอร์และผู้เล่นอื่น ล้มแล้วได้ XP เลเวลอัพแล้วเลือดและพลังโจมตีเพิ่ม ถูกล้มแล้วฟื้นใน 5 วินาที
- **ภารกิจประจำวัน** 5 ข้อ เปลี่ยนใหม่ทุกเที่ยงคืนเวลาไทย
- **ฉายา** 26 แบบ ตั้งแต่ธรรมดาจนถึงระดับเพี้ยนระดับตำนาน แสดงบนหัวและเปลี่ยนกรอบแชต
- **ห้อง** เลือกได้ในหน้าเข้าเกม: 🌏 ห้องรวม (เจอทุกคน) · 🔒 สร้างห้องส่วนตัว (ได้รหัส 6 ตัว กด "ชวนเพื่อน" เพื่อส่งลิงก์) · 🔑 เข้าห้องเพื่อนด้วยรหัส ห้องส่วนตัวมีมอนสเตอร์และบอสของตัวเอง เดินข้ามภาคก็ยังอยู่ด้วยกัน
- **อาชีพ** แต่ละตัวละครสู้ต่างกัน: อัศวินเลือดเยอะ นักรบเถื่อนตีแรง โจรตีไว พรานป่ายิงธนู นักฆ่าคลุมหน้ายิงหน้าไม้ จอมเวทยิงลูกเวท กดโจมตีแล้วจะหันหามอนสเตอร์ใกล้สุดเอง
- **ทองและร้านค้า 🛒** มอนสเตอร์ดรอปทอง (บอสให้เยอะ) ซื้อยาเลือด อาวุธ 5 ขั้น (เรืองแสงตามขั้น) และเกราะ 5 ขั้น
- **ยาเลือด 🧪** ปุ่มเหนือสกิล หรือกด G / 5 ฟื้นเลือด 50%
- **ปีก 🪽** 6 แบบในร้านค้า: นางฟ้า ปีศาจ ผีเสื้อแสงจันทร์ ฟีนิกซ์เพลิง มังกรมรกต เทพจักรวาล กระพือตามจังหวะ เพิ่มพลังโจมตีสูงสุด ×1.3
- **สัตว์ขี่ 🐎** 6 ตัวในร้านค้า: ม้า กวาง หมาป่า ม้าขาว แร็พเตอร์ มังกร (บินได้) กดปุ่ม 🐎 ข้างจอยสติ๊ก หรือกด V เพื่อขึ้นลง วิ่งเร็วสูงสุด ×1.85 โจมตีเมื่อไหร่จะลงจากหลังเอง
- **ทีม 👥** ชวนผู้เล่นในภาคเดียวกันเข้าทีม (สูงสุด 4 คน) แบ่ง XP และทอง ตีกันเองไม่โดน เห็นเลือดเพื่อนที่มุมจอ
- **ตั้งค่า ⚙** เปิดปิดเพลงและเสียง ปรับคุณภาพกราฟิก (เครื่องกระตุกให้เลือก "ประหยัด") แต่ละภาคมีเพลงของตัวเอง ใกล้บอสเปลี่ยนเป็นเพลงต่อสู้
- **บัญชี** สมัครในหน้าเข้าเกม (หัวข้อ "บัญชี") แล้วเข้าสู่ระบบจากเครื่องไหนก็ได้ เลเวล ฉายา และภารกิจจะตามไปด้วย

## เปิดให้เล่นออนไลน์ผ่าน GitHub Codespaces (ฟรีตามโควตา GitHub)

1. ในหน้า repo บน GitHub กดปุ่มเขียว **Code → Codespaces → Create codespace on master**
2. รอสักครู่ เกมจะ build และเปิดเซิร์ฟเวอร์เอง
3. ไปที่แท็บ **Ports** คลิกขวาที่พอร์ต 2567 → **Port Visibility → Public**
4. คัดลอกลิงก์ในช่อง Forwarded Address ส่งให้เพื่อน

Codespace จะหยุดเองเมื่อไม่มีการใช้งานสักพัก (ค่าเริ่มต้น 30 นาที) และข้อมูลผู้เล่นอยู่ในตัว codespace นั้น

## เปิดให้เล่นออนไลน์ (Render)

ไฟล์ `render.yaml` เตรียมไว้แล้ว ทำครั้งเดียว:

1. สมัคร https://render.com ด้วยบัญชี GitHub
2. กด **New → Blueprint** แล้วเลือก repo `mu_sky`
3. ใส่ `GM_KEY` (รหัส GM ที่จะใช้พิมพ์ `/gm <รหัส>` ในเกม) แล้วกด **Apply**
4. รอ build เสร็จ จะได้ลิงก์ `https://mu-sky-xxxx.onrender.com` ส่งให้เพื่อนเล่นได้เลย

ตอนนี้ตั้งเป็นแผน `free` (ไม่ต้องผูกบัตร) ข้อเสียคือเซิร์ฟเวอร์จะหลับเมื่อไม่มีคนเล่นสักพัก และข้อมูลผู้เล่นจะเริ่มใหม่ทุกครั้งที่เซิร์ฟเวอร์รีสตาร์ท
ถ้าอยากเก็บข้อมูลถาวร เปลี่ยนเป็นแผน `starter` พร้อมดิสก์ตามที่เขียนไว้ใน `render.yaml` (ต้องผูกบัตร มีค่าบริการรายเดือน)
ทุกครั้งที่ push ขึ้น GitHub Render จะอัปเดตเกมให้เอง

## GM (ผู้ดูแลเกม)

ครั้งแรกที่รันเซิร์ฟเวอร์ จะสร้างรหัส GM แบบสุ่มไว้ที่ `server/data/gm-key.txt` (ไม่ถูกส่งขึ้น Git)
ในเกม พิมพ์ในแชทว่า `/gm <รหัส>` ครั้งเดียว ผู้เล่นนั้นจะเป็น GM ตลอด แล้วกดปุ่ม 🛡 GM เพื่อเปิดแผงควบคุม:
ฆ่า ฟื้นพลัง อมตะ ฆ่าทีเดียวตาย เพิ่มหรือลดเลเวล มอบฉายา วาร์ปไปหา ดึงมาหา เตะออก แบน (กี่วันหรือถาวร) ปลดแบน และประกาศถึงทุกภาค

จะตั้งรหัสเองก็ได้ด้วยตัวแปร `GM_KEY` ตอนรันเซิร์ฟเวอร์

## ข้อมูลที่เซิร์ฟเวอร์เก็บ

อยู่ใน `server/data/` (ไม่ถูกส่งขึ้น Git) หรือในโฟลเดอร์ที่ตั้งด้วยตัวแปร `DATA_DIR` สำรองโฟลเดอร์นี้ไว้ถ้าย้ายเครื่อง

| ไฟล์ | มีอะไร |
|---|---|
| `progress.json` | เลเวล ภารกิจ ฉายา สถานะ GM และการแบนของผู้เล่นทุกคน |
| `accounts.json` | ชื่อบัญชีและรหัสผ่าน (เก็บเป็นค่าแฮช scrypt ไม่ใช่รหัสจริง) |
| `gm-key.txt` | รหัส GM |

## โครงสร้าง

| โฟลเดอร์ | มีอะไร |
|---|---|
| `server/` | เซิร์ฟเวอร์ Colyseus: ห้องละภาค คุมการเดิน การต่อสู้ มอนสเตอร์ แชท ภารกิจ GM และบัญชี |
| `client/` | ตัวเกม 3 มิติ (Three.js) + หน้าจอ HTML (แชท ภารกิจ แผง GM ปุ่มต่อสู้) |
| `shared/` | กติกาที่ทั้งสองฝั่งต้องตรงกัน: ภาค แผนผังฉาก มอนสเตอร์ สกิล ฉายา ภารกิจ |

เซิร์ฟเวอร์เป็นตัวตัดสินทุกอย่าง ทั้งตำแหน่ง ดาเมจ และรางวัล ตัวเกมส่งแค่ปุ่มที่กด จึงโกงไม่ได้

โมเดล 3 มิติจาก KayKit และ Quaternius เสียงจาก Ninja Adventure ทั้งหมดเป็น CC0 ดูรายละเอียดที่ `client/public/assets/CREDITS.md`

commits.msg:
fix: a round of bugs found by testing every feature again

- Memory: since the renderer is shared between regions, the canvas kept every left region's touch
  listeners, and with them the whole region; textures made for a region (ground, sea, glows) were
  never freed either. Both now go when a region is left.
- Teams: the invite list only showed players whose model had loaded and never refreshed, so a
  newcomer could not be invited; it now follows the server's players. A new team shows at once.
- Voice: the listening side could drop a good link when it heard of the talker's microphone a
  moment after the offer, leaving both silent for half a minute; only the offering side now decides
  when to remake a link. Routes that arrive before the offer is taken in are kept, not lost.
- Messages up to 16 KB: the default 4 KB was below some phones' voice offers, cutting them off.
- A direction of Infinity made a player's position NaN; directions are clamped.
- Wrong GM keys are counted by address and player across visits (5, then 15 minutes locked),
  not reset by rejoining; bans can't overflow; names can't pose as the system or a GM.
- The world boss ends for everyone when its region closes; GM "all mounts" rides at once; the
  tutorial no longer shows over the start screen when leaving early.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: leaving a team, and the music switch on iPhones

- Leaving a team did nothing on screen: the team status each second only goes to players in a
  team, so the one who left (and a teammate left alone) kept the frames and the leave button. The
  server now tells them at once; the invite list refreshes, and listening voice links close too.
- Music off still played on iPhones, which ignore an audio element's volume: loudness now goes
  through Web Audio, and the switch pauses every tune at once instead of fading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(voice): hear teammates without turning one's own microphone on

A voice link was only made between two teammates who both had their microphone on, so a teammate
who only listened heard nothing. Now every teammate hears whoever talks; 🎤 is only for talking.
A voice the browser refuses to play before a touch is played on the next one (with a note asking
for it), and a link that finds no route says so instead of staying silent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: walk only with the joystick or keys; a button to leave or log out

Touching the world no longer sends the player walking (a stray thumb did); pinching still zooms.
Settings get a leave button, pressed twice: it goes back to the start screen at once (no hold for a
reconnection), and signs out of the account if there is one; a guest keeps their progress here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(store): keep a daily backup of player data for a week

The first save of each Thai day also copies the records to "<name>@<date>" in MongoDB, keeping the
last seven; the free Atlas tier has no backups of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: team voice chat

A 🎤 button, shown while in a team, turns the microphone on; teammates with theirs on hear each
other wherever they are, the sound going straight between browsers (WebRTC, Google's public STUN).
The server only passes the set-up messages between teammates, who know each other by a random
voice tag rather than their player id. Team frames show who has a microphone on and light up when
someone speaks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: reconnect after a dropped connection

A phone switching networks or a locked screen used to throw the player back to the join screen.
Now the server keeps them where they stood for 45 seconds, out of harm's way and marked 📶, while
the game reconnects on its own; kicked and banned players are not kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: safe zones in the middle of each region and at every portal

Inside a blue circle nobody can be hurt, by players or monsters (monsters give up the chase, shots
fly past), nobody can attack (so archers can't shoot out at monsters that can't reach them), and
health comes back three times as fast without waiting. A badge shows while inside and the attack
buttons dim; monsters now live further from the middle and the portals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: faster trips between regions

- The loading screen shows the moment the player steps into a portal, and the next region's
  models download while its room is joined, instead of after.
- While playing, the models of the regions the portals lead to are fetched in the background, so
  stepping through needs no download at all.
- New shaders are compiled off the main thread where the browser can, before the region shows.
- The server tells browsers to keep models, music and pictures for a day and the built code for
  good, instead of asking about every file across the ocean each time the game opens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(hud): menu no longer overlaps the attack buttons

The column of menu buttons grew to six and ran into the potion and attack buttons on short and
landscape screens. Below 720 px of height it folds into one ☰ button that opens as a row (with a
dot when the bag or a team invite has news); landscape phones also get a smaller stick and attack
buttons, with the menu beside the stats panel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: loot, world boss, daily gifts, leaderboards, title screen and tutorial

- Saving: progress and accounts go to MongoDB when MONGODB_URI is set (the free host wipes its
