# amade-hover-cab-game

**amade-hover-cab-game** is the flying cab of the [amadeOS](https://github.com/datazuul/amadeos) desktop: steer a cab with a main jet, side jets and a roof jet against gravity and wind, land gently on numbered pads, pick up the passengers who hail you and fly them to the pad they ask for. Twelve shifts, from the rooftops of a city to a mine, a canyon, a factory with a lift, an orbit station and a storm at sea. The passengers call out in voices made by the engine's speech synthesizer. Built on [amade-game-engine](https://github.com/datazuul/amade-game-engine); runs on other operating systems as well.

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-EUPL--1.2-blue)
![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-25-orange)

![Hover Cab](docs/screenshots/amade-hover-cab-game.png)

## Playing

- **Enter**, **Space** or **Start** on a gamepad starts the first shift from the title, where the autopilot flies.
- **Up** (or **W**) fires the main jet under the cab, **left** and **right** (or **A** and **D**) the side jets, **down** (or **S**) the roof jet, which pushes the cab down. Jets burn fuel.
- **Space** (or **G**) moves the landing gear out or in. The cab starts with it out.
- Land only with the gear out, slowly, and with both legs on the deck of a pad. Anything else is a crash: a wall, a roof, a moving van, the sea, a closed gate, coming down too fast, or landing with the gear in. A firm landing is allowed but costs the passenger's tip a dollar.
- A passenger appears on a pad and calls "Hey, cab!". Land on their pad: they walk to the cab, get in and say where to, "Pad 3, please!". Land there and they pay the **fare** (two dollars and one for every hundred units of distance) and the **tip**, which starts at five dollars and melts during the ride.
- The **fuel pad** (green) fills the tank while the cab stands on it, for money from the till.
- The last passenger of a shift says "Up, please!": the gate in the ceiling opens, and flying out through it ends the shift.
- Three spare cabs at the start, and another for every hundred dollars earned. The best earnings enter the high score table.
- **P** or **Esc** pauses, and so does leaving the window; **Esc** in the pause leaves the game.
- Gamepads: d-pad or left stick to steer, **A** or **Up** for the main jet, **B** or **Down** for the roof jet, **X** or **Y** for the gear, **Start** to pause.
- **F11** switches to full screen and back. *Game → Graphics* chooses how the shift reaches the screen: **Direct** (at the screen's full size) or **Pixels** (640 × 400, enlarged by whole factors). **F12** shows how long each frame takes.
- Sound effects, voices and music can be switched off under *Game → Sound*.

The keys can be changed in `~/.config/amadeos/hovercab/hovercab.properties`, with the names Java gives them, several separated by spaces:

```properties
keys.left=LEFT A
keys.right=RIGHT D
keys.up=UP W
keys.down=DOWN S
keys.gear=SPACE G
keys.pause=P ESCAPE
```

Texts and voices in English, Deutsch, Français, Español and Italiano.

## Gamepads

Plugged in before or while the game runs; any of them plays. *Help → About* shows how many are connected.

- **Linux**: the game reads `/dev/input/js0` to `js3`, which needs read access to them (on most desktops the user at the screen has it). The buttons follow the Xbox layout of the `xpad` driver.
- **Windows**: XInput, so Xbox and compatible controllers.
- Elsewhere the game runs without gamepads.

## Files

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Settings (graphics, sound, keys) | `~/.config/amadeos/hovercab/hovercab.properties` |
| Best earnings | `~/.local/share/amadeos/games/hovercab/` |

## Making shifts

The shifts are text files, `src/main/resources/eu/amadeos/games/hovercab/shifts/shift1.txt` to `shift12.txt`, one thing per line, `#` starts a comment. The screen is 640 × 400 units; the top bar takes 22, the ceiling with the gate reaches down to 36.

```text
name Harbour Heights         # the shift's English name; the translations are in messages_*.properties
theme dusk                   # day, dusk, night, cave, canyon, snow, space, factory, storm
gravity 1                    # optional: a factor of the normal gravity
air 0.2                      # optional: how much the air slows the cab per second
wind 0 30 5                  # optional: a steady push, gusts up to so much on top, a gust every so many seconds
sea 372                      # optional: water from this height down
gate 300 380                 # where the gate in the ceiling is, from x to x
start 2                      # the pad the cab starts on
block brick 0 150 120 250    # a solid: look x y width height
poly rock 0 300 60 280 90 320 0 320   # a solid polygon: look and its corners
beam 100 36 100 150          # a solid steel strut from a point to a point
sign pink 160 60 70 22 NOODLES   # a solid neon sign on chains from the ceiling: colour x y width height text
deco lamp 120 360            # a decoration that does not collide
pad 1 10 150 90              # a pad: number x y width; y is the top of its deck
fuel 334 270 70              # the fuel pad
lift 6 300 200 60 320 8      # a pad that moves: number x y width, down to y2, there and back in so many seconds
mover van 150 62 40 14 140 0 6 0   # a moving block (also van or drone): look x y w h, by dx dy, in seconds, starting late by
riders 2>4 1>3 5>2 4>up      # the passengers in order, from pad to pad; the last one wants up
```

The looks are `brick`, `glass`, `concrete`, `steel`, `rock`, `ice`, `hull`, `wood`, `sand` and `plain`; the decorations `tank`, `antenna`, `tree`, `pine`, `lamp`, `crane`, `chimney`, `dish`, `pipe`, `cactus`, `crystal` and `flag`. A mistake is reported with the file and the line.

`AutopilotTest` flies every shift with the autopilot, through all passengers and out through the gate without a crash, so a shift that cannot be flown fails the build.

## Building

```bash
./gradlew test          # the window test needs a display (xvfb-run on servers)
./

BartJanCoppens/GameStudio.readme:
# Game Studio

Gamified learning platform for Deloitte: a creator describes a game, answers the AI's questions, approves a design shown on screen and watches the AI build it; after a check against the admin's house rules, players play it in a sealed-off frame.

Implemented from the Claude Design prototype `Game Studio.dc.html` with the TaxConnect design system. Any kind of game can be made: the AI proposes the game's shape, writes its content, screens and logic, and can play a role in it (a game master or an opponent). Games can be grounded in the Belgian VAT source document (*Invoice mandatory mentions.md*). Sign-in, users, roles, games, runs and AI keys are on Supabase. See [docs/pitch-demo.md](docs/pitch-demo.md) for the pitch walkthrough and [the design](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-any-game-studio-design.md) for how it works.

## How a game is made

1. **Questions** (`game-architect`, fast model): up to six questions with clickable choices.
2. **Design** (`game-architect`): a concept card and a static mock-up of the main screen; revise by chatting, change the look, approve.
3. **Code** (`game-builder`, streamed): the content and the screens are written side by side, then the logic. Each step is scanned before it is accepted; a failed step can be retried on its own.
4. **Test & publish**: play-test (never counted), **Check house rules** (`game-check`), **Publish to players** (the database's `publish_game` refuses any version whose fingerprint didn't pass the check), **Export code** for platform admins. The first publish names the game's **game admin**; the game then starts closed.

**Looking after a game** (Game administration). Each game has one game admin, named by its creator at first publish; only they (and platform admins, who can hand a game to another game admin) see and look after it:
- **Online / offline:** one switch stops the game for every player, runs in progress included; bringing it back keeps who may play.
- **Access:** everyone, or selected groups and people; nobody until the game admin chooses. The database enforces it on live content, runs, leaderboards and the in-game AI. Groups are kept by platform admins under **Admin › Groups**.
- **Content:** describe what to add; the AI writes it in the game's own shape (nothing existing may be dropped or retyped). It then gets the same house-rules review, and goes live with `publish_live_content`. A creator whose draft has fallen behind takes the live content in before republishing. The AI sees the AI role's hidden knowledge so additions fit the character; its output is checked for echoes of it and never streamed as text, but that check is best effort: a game admin who asks for a paraphrase can learn the hidden knowledge (players can't reach this step).
- **Players & results** and **AI services** as before.

**Turn-taking games between two colleagues** (play mode chosen in the Studio questions):
- **Starting:** a player invites a colleague who may also play the game (**Invite a colleague** on the game's page). *Your games with colleagues*, at the top of the library, lists invitations and games with their status (Invites you, Your turn, Their turn, Finished…) and keeps itself up to date.
- **Ways to play**, as the creator chose: **live** (both online, a timer per turn; a turn that runs out passes to the other player) and/or **turn by turn**. The invited colleague moves first.
- **The platform keeps the game:** `game-match` is the only writer of `matches`; it checks access and whose turn it is, and refuses a second move for the same turn. Each player has **private state** the other never receives (database, function and bridge), so games with hidden information (ships, hands) are fair. A game in progress keeps the version it started on (`game_versions`). Games get `getMatch`, `makeMove` and `onMatchChange` on the bridge; the platform doesn't check whether a move is legal.
- **Notifications** (invitation, answer, your turn), as the creator chose: a **phone notification** (Web Push; players turn it on in *Profile details*, on iPhone after adding Game Studio to the home screen) and/or **email**. They never contain game content. Email needs a sending service: set the function secrets `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` (a verified sender address); until then email is skipped. Push uses the `VAPID_*` function secrets and `VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` at build time.
- **Endings:** a pg_cron job every 5 minutes expires unanswered invitations (live 1 hour, turn by turn 7 days) and cancels games without a move for longer than the game admin's limit (*Players & results*: defaults 3 days and 10 minutes). Finished games count for a wins/draws/losses leaderboard and the game admin's results when the creator chose so. Turn-taking games have no AI role yet; a secret shared by neither player (a deck both draw from) isn't supported yet.

Players play in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` with a strict content security policy: no network, storage, forms or outside resources. A game reaches the platform only through `window.GameStudio` (data, score, leaderboard, common goal, AI role), and the app validates every message. A game that navigates away is stopped. Known limits: a game can still send data out by navigating (the frame is then closed), and WebRTC isn't covered by the content security policy (the bridge removes it before game code runs, best effort), so games only get first names with an initial.

## Run

```sh
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # then fill in the Supabase URL and publishable key
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run build    # typecheck + production build
npm run lint
npm test         # unit tests: bridge protocol, page builder, code scan, concept checks, export, leaderboard
npm run test:sql # database checks (publish gate, secrets, contributions) in a rolled-back block
npm run check:functions   # type-checks the Edge Functions with Deno
npm run e2e      # Playwright, against the Supabase project in .en

xXCrusaderXx/DartPilot.desc: Open-source automatic dart scoring engine for three USB cameras, backed by a millimetre benchmark
xXCrusaderXx/DartPilot.readme:
# DartPilot

[![CI](https://github.com/xXCrusaderXx/DartPilot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xXCrusaderXx/DartPilot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: GPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

An open-source **automatic dart scoring engine for three USB cameras**. Its goal is a more precise impact position than existing camera-based systems, backed by a reproducible millimetre benchmark instead of claims.

DartPilot treats scoring as a measurement problem: every throw yields a board point in millimetres with its uncertainty and diagnostics, and the engine may abstain instead of forcing a wrong score. The full reasoning is in the [technical plan](docs/technical_plan.md).

> **Status: early development.** The repository contains the project structure; the engine modules are still empty. Work starts with [phase 1 – Measurability](ROADMAP.md).

> DartPilot is an independent project. It is not affiliated with any manufacturer of dartboards or dart scoring systems. See [LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md).

## How it works

```text
3 USB cameras ─► capture (timestamps, frame IDs, ring buffers)
              ─► event_detection (throw window, difference masks)
              ─► tip_candidates (tip candidates per camera, with covariance)
              ─► geometry (board projection / triangulation)
              ─► fusion (temporal association, robust estimate, abstention)
              ─► scoring (board point in mm ─► sector and ring)
              ─► score + confidence + diagnostics
```

Detection, geometry and scoring are separate modules. Every result can be traced back to its source frames, and every recorded throw can be replayed with identical results.

The core metrics are the radial position error in mm (median, P95), segment and multiplier accuracy, and false acceptance and abstention rates, which are always reported together. See [section 6 of the technical plan](docs/technical_plan.md#6-metrics-and-preliminary-targets).

## Repository layout

| Path | Content |
| ---- | ------- |
| [`engine/`](engine) | C++20 engine: one library per module, plus `apps/dartpilot_cli` and the developer GUI `apps/dartpilot_setup` (Qt 6, optional) |
| [`tests/`](tests) | C++ tests (GoogleTest, run with `ctest`) |
| [`ui/`](ui) | Flutter player app (Linux, Windows, web, Android), see [ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-user-interface.md) |
| [`tools/`](tools) | Python tools for benchmark evaluation and annotation |
| [`docs/`](docs) | [Technical plan](docs/technical_plan.md), [reference hardware](docs/hardware.md), [session format](docs/replay-format.md), [engine API](docs/engine-api.md) and [architecture decisions](docs/adr) |
| `data/` | Local recordings and datasets; never committed |

## Building from source

Requirements: CMake 3.20 or newer, a C++20 compiler and OpenCV 4 or 5. GoogleTest is downloaded automatically when the tests are enabled.

```sh
# Arch Linux
sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel cmake ninja opencv
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build libopencv-dev
# Fedora
sudo dnf install gcc-c++ cmake ninja-build opencv-devel

cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
./build/engine/apps/dartpilot_cli/dartpilot --version
```

### Tests

```sh
cmake -B build -G Ninja -DDARTPILOT_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

The tests need no cameras and no internet connection (apart from the first GoogleTest download).

### Checking and recording the cameras

```sh
./build/engine/apps/dartpilot_cli/dartpilot capture-check 30     # frame rate, losses and timestamp quality
./build/engine/apps/dartpilot_cli/dartpilot record --seconds 60  # session in ~/.local/share/dartpilot/sessions
python -m dartpilot_tools.capture_report ~/.local/share/dartpilot/sessions/<session>   # capture health of a recording
```

A recording of three cameras takes about 200–360 MB per minute, depending on the scene; the format is described in [docs/replay-format.md](docs/replay-format.md). Recordings stay on your computer and are never committed (see [LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md)).

### Python tools

```sh
cd tools
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e '.[dev]'
pytest
```

### Player app

The Flutter app in [`ui/`](ui) needs the [Flutter SDK](https://docs.flutter.dev/get-started/install) (3.47 or newer). Until the engine API exists, darts are entered on the screen.

```sh
cd ui
flutter run -d linux
flutter test
```

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. Development happens on `dev`; `main` only receives merges from `dev` at release points. Every commit needs a DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`). Pull requests go against `dev` and are checked by CI; a maintainer reviews and merges them. Changes to detection report their effect on the benchmark.

- Security problems: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)
- Code of conduct: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- Legal notes, recordings and datasets: [LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md)
- Plans and milestones: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)

## License

DartPilot is licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 or later](LICENSE). Datasets and recordings may have their own licenses (see [LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md)).

DeepanshuCFI/righttowalk.desc: Right to Walk: a citizen footpath check for Gurugram (Crashfree India prototype)
DeepanshuCFI/righttowalk.readme:
# Right to Walk · Footpath Check (Phase 0 + Phase 1)

Crashfree India's citizen "right to walk" street check. One stretch of road, eleven plain questions, the stretch drawn live as you answer, a result in the Supreme Court's own audit vocabulary, and a notice to the owning agency.

Design direction "kerb and chalk": the street's own materials (concrete pavers, black-and-yellow kerb paint, tactile yellow, chalk marks, the pedestrian signal). Khand + Mukta, both Latin and Devanagari. Deliberately not the Crashfree India design system (Deep, 23 Oct 2026: citizen and crowdsourcing products match their audience).

## Files
- `src/head.html` metas, title, font link
- `src/style.css` tokens (light and dark) and components
- `src/body.html` markup for the learn, check and saved views
- `src/data.js` strings (EN/HI), the eleven items with Court heading, IRC standard and ask text, the Gurugram owner list
- `src/learn.js` the Hindi learn page. The English learn copy is written in `body.html` and read into `S.en` at boot from the `data-s` / `data-sh` elements; `learn.js` holds the Hindi for the same keys (court quotes stay in English with a Hindi gloss line; agency names, IRC numbers and case names stay in Latin script; status tags are short Hindi labels)
- `src/obs.js` the footpath problem types and their SVG glyphs, reconciled on 23 Oct 2026 against `research_notes/Right to walk auditor India/footpath_problem_taxonomy.md` (21-row taxonomy, 91 sources): twelve first-screen types (parked vehicles; vendor cart, kiosk or tin shed; shop or house spilling onto it; private ramp or fence; electric pole, box or transformer; tree or bushes; open manhole or drain; broken or missing tiles; dug up and left; malba or garbage; signboard, bus stop or furniture; waterlogged) plus three behind "More kinds" (two-wheelers riding on it, stray cattle or dogs, shrine or statue). Absence, discontinuity, height and darkness are audit items, not tiles. Hindi names follow MCG's own posts and Gurugram press; each type carries the clause (IRC:103-2012 numbering, Rules of the Road, Street Vendors Act, HMC Act s.408, IS 1726/12592, SC 2009 shrines order) and the usual Gurugram agency. Old ids from earlier saved checks are migrated on load.
- `src/app.js` state, scoring, the street-strip and signal drawings, notice builder, routing
- `src/config.js` the Phase 1 connection (project URL, public anon key, tile URL) and `src/sectors.json` the Gurugram sector list
- `src/rtw.js` the shared Phase 1 client (plain fetch against PostgREST, Storage and GoTrue; no SDK), `src/share.js` the WhatsApp share card (canvas), `src/cards.js` the four awareness cards on the learn page ("Share the right": the right, the 36,526 number, the 100 m test, the vendor nuance; 1080×1350 PNG each, drawn on the device in the page language, Web Share or download)
- `src/map.html` + `map.js`, `src/report.html` + `report.js`, `src/dataset.html` + `dataset.js`, `src/moderate.html` + `moderate.js`, `src/pages.css` the secondary pages
- `src/roads.json` the sampling frame: Haryana's own road list (the "30-day challenge", 100 Gurugram roads by 7 Nov 2026) with each road's agency, kind, source and an approximate OpenStreetMap line baked in; built once by `tools/roads_geocode.py` (Nominatim, Overpass and the OSRM demo router, cached in `tools/.roads-cache/`; the pages themselves call none of these). `src/frame.js` matches published checks to the roads in the browser (a check belongs to the nearest road within 60 m). `src/roads.html` + `roads.js` + `roads.css` the printable assignment sheet (two volunteers per road, 500 m stretches). # LOOP LINE（ループライン）

路線をつないで、環状線を完成させろ。色の合う曲がった線路札をつなぎ、2つの駅を両方通る輪を作る1人用パズル。

- 盤は7×7。2行2列目と6行6列目に駅（L字）が最初から置いてある。
- 手札5枚から1枚ずつ、のびている線の先に置く。隣り合う線は同じ色でつなぐ。
- お助けカード（リセット・トラッシュ・ワイルド）はどれも1回だけ。
- 札はすべて L字（隣り合う辺をつなぐ曲がった線）。
- レベルは3段階（4色・5色・6色）。人がよく考えて遊んだときの勝率の目安は 約9割・約8割・約3割（`docs/balance.md`）。

```sh
npm install
npm run dev     # 開発サーバー（ゲーム集の入口からは 5183 番で開く）
npm test        # ルールのテスト
npm run sim     # 自動プレイで勝率を測る（-- 1000 lv2 でレベル指定、-- 100 deep で先読みするプレイヤー）
npm run build
```

仕様は `要件定義書.md`。SNS 共有用の画像 `public/og.png` は、ゲーム集（GameHub）の `scripts/render-images.sh` で作る。

mjaffry01/ai-word-bank.readme:
# AI Concepts

AI Concepts is an AI course site: a learning web of about 660 terms arranged in rings from the core outward, a ring-by-ring learning path, a glossary, flashcards and multiple-choice ring quizzes.

Students sign in with Google. The teacher approves them and sees every score and answer in a Google Sheet. Everything runs on free services.

| Part | Service | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Website | GitHub Pages | `docs/` → https://mjaffry01.github.io/ai-word-bank/ |
| Student sign-in | Sign in with Google | Google Cloud project `ai-word-bank-login` |
| Server | Google Apps Script web app | `apps-script/Code.gs` |
| Admin panel and data | Google Sheet | "AI Word Bank - Students and Results" in the teacher's Drive |

## For the teacher

Everything is managed in the Google Sheet.

- **Students:** every student who signs in appears here as `pending`. Change the **Status** dropdown to `approved` to let them in, or to `rejected` to keep them out. A waiting student's page checks every 30 seconds and opens by itself.
- **Attempts:** one row per finished quiz, with the date, student, ring, score and percent.
- **Answers:** one row per question, showing the question, the student's answer, the right answer and whether it was correct. Use **Data → Create a filter** to look at one student or one ring.
- **Summary:** each student's best score per ring. It updates by itself.
- **Module quizzes:** one row per finished quiz from Module 2 onward, with a **Level** column (Beginner, Intermediate or Advanced). Each answer is also in **Answers**, with the module and level in the Ring column.
- **Module summary:** each student's best score per module and level. It updates by itself.
- **Submissions:** practice tasks students hand in, showing the task, the AI tool used, their final prompt and what they changed. The tab appears after the first hand-in.

## Modules

1. **Vocabulary:** learning web, learning path, glossary, flashcards and ring quizzes (`docs/index.html`).
2. **Prompting & AI tools:** a lesson, a prompt builder, eight technique cards, a hallucination hunt, five practice tasks to hand in, and a 15-question quiz (`docs/module2.js`, `docs/module2.css`).
3. **How machines learn:** a lesson (data → features & labels → training → model → prediction → testing), the three ways machines learn with a sorting check, a spam-filter lab students label, train and test themselves (with a confusion matrix), an overfitting lab, four real case studies, a Teachable Machine hand-in, and a 15-question quiz (`docs/module3.js`, `docs/module3.css`).

4. **How LLMs work:** a lesson (next-token prediction, the six steps of an answer, pre-training → instruction tuning → RLHF), a tokenizer lab using the real GPT-4 tokenizer (loaded from jsDelivr only when the tab opens), a next-word game with a temperature slider, an attention explorer, a hallucination demo, a context-window lab, a hand-in and a three-level quiz (`docs/module4.js`, `docs/module4.css`).

Modules 2, 3 and 4 save quizzes to **Module quizzes** and hand-ins to **Submissions**, labelled with the module name. To add another module, add a `data-module` button, a `lede` paragraph and an `m<n>` container in `index.html`, and register its render function in `window.WB_MODULES`.

## How it fits together

1. The site shows Google's **Sign in with Google** button. Google gives the browser a signed ID token for the student.
2. The site sends that token to the Apps Script web app. The script checks the token with Google, and checks that it was issued for this site's Client ID. Only then does it read or write the Sheet.
3. New students are added as `pending`. Only `approved` students can save quiz results, and the script rejects impossible scores.

The Apps Script web app is set to **Execute as: Me** and **Who has access: Anyone**. Students' browsers need that access to reach it. It doesn't open your data: every request must carry a valid Google sign-in, and the Sheet itself stays private.

## Settings

- `docs/config.js` holds the Client ID and the Apps Script web app URL. Neither is a secret.
- `apps-script/Code.gs` holds `CLIENT_ID` and `SHEET_ID`. It is a copy of the script in the Apps Script editor. After changing it, paste it into the editor, save, then go to **Deploy → Manage deployments → Edit → Version: New version → Deploy**. The URL stays the same.

## Changing the words

The terms are in `docs/index.html` inside `<script type="text/plain" id="data">`, one `Term|topic|meaning` per line. The connecting words are in `<script type="text/plain" id="web">`, one `Word > words that build on it` per line. Commit and push, and GitHub Pages updates within a minute or two. Each term also has an **In depth** explanation and an **Example** in `docs/deep.txt` (one `Term|In depth|Example` per line, using exactly the same term names). They show in the learning-web panel, the glossary and on the back of flashcards, and the search box searches them too.

## Limits

- **Sign-in lasts 48 hours.** A Google sign-in starts a 48-hour session, signed by the Apps Script with a secret kept in its Script Properties. Students stay signed in on that device, even after closing the browser, until the 48 hours end or they click **Sign out**. If it ends mid-quiz, the site asks them to sign in again and then saves the result. To sign everyone out at once, delete `SESSION_SECRET` under **Project Settings → Script Properties**. Approval is still checked on every request, so setting a student to `rejected` locks them out straight away.
- **The word list is public.** It is part of the page, so anyone with the address can read it. The sign-in gate protects the quizzes and results.
- **Scores can be faked.** They are worked out in the student's browser, so a technically skilled student could fake one.
- **Free quotas.** Apps Script's free quotas (about 20,000 URL checks and 90 minutes of run time a day) are plenty for a class.

Anaraa010907/Voice-game.readme:
# Voice-game

Найзуудтайгаа дуугаар тоглох парти тоглоомууд: **Мафи**, **Who's the Imposter?**, **Хэн вэ?** (онлайн өрөө + voice) болон нэг утсаар тоглох **Kings Cup**.
React + Vite + TypeScript, Supabase (өгөгдөл + realtime), LiveKit (voice).

| Тоглоом | Төлөв |
| --- | --- |
| Мафи (Мафи / Эмч / Мөрдөгч / Иргэн) | ✅ эхний хувилбар |
| Who's the Imposter? | ✅ эхний хувилбар |
| Хэн вэ? | ✅ эхний хувилбар |
| Кодын нэр, Truth or Dare, Хоёр үнэн нэг худал, Дүр таах, Хориотой үг | ⏳ удахгүй |

**Нэг утсаар тоглох (онлайн шаардахгүй):** 👑 Kings Cup (Ring of Fire) ✅

## Тохируулах

1. `npm install`
2. `.env.example`-ийг `.env` болгож хуулаад Supabase URL / anon key-ээ бөглөнө.
3. Supabase төсөл дээр:
   - **Authentication → Providers → Anonymous sign-ins**-ийг идэвхжүүлнэ.
   - `supabase/migrations/` доторх файлуудыг дарааллаар нь (`0001_init.sql`, `0002_imposter.sql`, `0003_game_types.sql`, `0004_whoisit.sql`) ажиллуулна (SQL editor эсвэл `supabase db push`).
   - Edge function байршуулна: `supabase functions deploy livekit-token`
   - Secrets: `supabase secrets set LIVEKIT_URL=wss://... LIVEKIT_API_KEY=... LIVEKIT_API_SECRET=...`
4. `npm run dev`

## Бүтэц

- `supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql` — хүснэгт, RLS, бүх тоглоомын логик (RPC). Үүрэг нууц хадгалагдана, зөвхөн өөрийн үүргийг уншиж чадна.
- `supabase/functions/livekit-token` — өрөөний гишүүнд LiveKit token олгоно.
- `src/games/registry.ts` — тоглоомуудын жагсаалт + voice дүрэм (хэн хэнийг сонсох).
- `src/games/mafia/`, `src/games/imposter/` — тоглоом бүрийн UI.
- `supabase/migrations/0002_imposter.sql` — Imposter-ийн үгсийн сан (`imposter_words`), нууц үг (`game_secrets`), RPC-ууд.

## Kings Cup

- Нэг утсыг дамжуулж тоглоно. Supabase, LiveKit шаардахгүй (`src/games/kingscup/`).
- Оноо, ялагч байхгүй. Ээлжээр карт татахад карт дээр асуулт эсвэл даалгавар шууд гарна. Уух нь сонголт, хүсэхгүй бол "Шийтгэл сонгох" эсвэл "Алгасах".
- 5 төрөл, нийт 26 карт: Дуурайж үзүүл (2), Үнэн эсвэл зориг (5), Хэн нь хамгийн… (10), Хань татаж уух (5), Хааны аяга (4).
- Бүх карт, төрөл, шийтгэл `src/games/kingscup/cards.ts`-д байна. Шинэ карт нэмэх бол `CARDS`-д нэг бичлэг нэмнэ. Шинэ төрөл бол `KINDS`-д нэмнэ.
- Ангилал (Энгийн, Үдэшлэг, +18, Хосууд): карт дээр `categories: ["adult"]` гэж зааж өгвөл зөвхөн тэр ангилалд орно. Ангиллын тусгай карт байхгүй байхад тохиргоонд ангилал харагдахгүй. 18+ ангилалд 18-аас дээш гэдгээ баталгаажуулна.

## Хэн вэ? дүрэм

- 3–12 тоглогч, 8 асуулт ("Хэн хамгийн нинжин сэтгэлтэй вэ?" гэх мэт эерэг асуултууд).
- Асуулт бүрт 30 секундэд нууцаар санал өгнө (өөрийгөө сонгохгүй). Бүгд санал өгвөл шууд үр дүн гарна.
- Хэн хэнд санал өгсөн нь хаана ч хадгалагдаж харагддаггүй, зөвхөн нийлбэр тоо ил болно.
- Төгсгөлд хамгийн олон асуултад ялсан хүмүүсийн шагналын самбар гарна.

## Who's the Imposter? дүрэм

- 3–12 тоглогч. Нэг хүн imposter болно; бусад нь нэг үгийг (жишээ нь "бууз") авна, imposter зөвхөн ангиллыг ("Хоол") мэднэ.
- Үе: үг харах (20с) → хэлэлцүүлэг (150с) → санал хураалт (45с) → imposter баригдвал үг таах (30с).
- Imposter баригдаж, үгийг зөв таавал ялна. Буруу хүн хөөгдвөл эсвэл санал тэнцвэл imposter ялна.

## Мафи дүрэм

- Шөнө (45с): мафи хохирогч сонгоно, эмч аврана, мөрдөгч шалгана.
- Өдөр (120с): хэлэлцэж санал хураана, хамгийн их санал авсан хүн хөөгдөнө (тэнцвэл хэн ч үгүй).
- Voice: шөнө зөвхөн мафи хоорондоо ярина, өдөр амьд хүмүүс ярина, хасагдсан хүмүүс үзэгч болж бие биетэйгээ ярина.
- 4–12 тоглогч. Мафийн тоо = тоглогч / 4 (дор хаяж 1).

> Анхаар: voice-ийн дүрмийг одоогоор клиент талд хэрэгжүүлсэн (сонсохгүй/ярихгүй болгодог). Хатуу хамгаалалт хэрэгтэй бол LiveKit token-ий эрхийг үе бүрт шинэчилдэг болгоно.

apaton93/siro.readme:
# Siro

Football away-day platform: plan your away day, find your fellow fans, know what to do when you get there.

Everything revolves around a **fixture** and the fans travelling to it.

## Status
MVP in development. Work is tracked in Jira (project **SIRO**).

## Repo layout
| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `shared/` | `@siro/shared` – API response types used by both api and app |
| `app/` | Frontend – React + Vite + TypeScript (mobile-first) |
| `api/` | Backend – Azure Functions (Node + TypeScript) |
| `db/` | `@siro/db` – Drizzle ORM schema, migrations and seed data |
| `docs/` | Data model, architecture, user journeys and decision records (`docs/adr`) |

## Tech stack
React · TypeScript · Vite · Azure Static Web Apps · Azure Functions · PostgreSQL + PostGIS · Drizzle ORM · Static Web Apps auth (GitHub, Microsoft) · Leaflet + OpenStreetMap

## Getting started (Windows)

### Prerequisites (one-off)
- Git
- Node.js 22 LTS with **npm 11** (`npm install -g npm@11.16.0`, check: `npm -v`)
- Docker Desktop (WSL2 backend), running
- Azure Functions Core Tools v4: `winget install Microsoft.Azure.FunctionsCoreTools` (check: `func --version`)
- VS Code (accept the recommended extensions prompt)

### First run
```powershell
git clone https://github.com/apaton93/siro.git
cd siro
npm install          # installs db + app + api (npm workspaces)
npm run setup        # creates api/local.settings.json from the example
npm run db:up        # starts Postgres + PostGIS in Docker
npm run db:migrate   # creates the tables
npm run db:seed      # loads the example Barcelona v Dundee United data
npm run dev          # starts app + api behind the SWA CLI
```
Open **http://localhost:4280** – you should see the example fixture. `/status` checks the API, database and PostGIS.

Signing in locally shows the SWA CLI's mock login form: type any username to simulate a GitHub or Microsoft user.

### Everyday commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | App, API and SWA proxy together (labelled app/api/swa output) at http://localhost:4280 |
| `npm run db:up` / `db:down` | Start / stop the local database |
| `npm run db:reset` | Wipe and recreate the local database (then `db:migrate` + `db:seed`) |
| `npm run db:migrate` | Apply database migrations |
| `npm run db:seed` | Wipe tables and reload dev seed data |
| `npm run db:studio` | Browse the database in Drizzle Studio |
| `npm run db:generate` | Generate a migration after changing `db/src/schema.ts` |
| `npm run build` | Production build of db, app and API |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript checks for db, app and API |
| `npm test` | API tests (in-memory Postgres + PostGIS, no Docker needed) |

### Local URLs
| URL | Service |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:4280 | Site (use this one) |
| http://127.0.0.1:5173 | Vite dev server (frontend only) |
| http://localhost:7071/api/health | Functions host directly |
| `127.0.0.1:5433` | Postgres in Docker (user/password/db: `siro`). Port 5433 avoids clashing with any local Postgres install on 5432. |

## Docs
- [Data model](docs/data-model.md)
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md)
- [User journeys](docs/user-journeys.md)
- [Decision records](docs/adr/)

## Deployment
GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/azure-static-web-apps.yml`) deploys to Azure Static Web Apps:
- **Pull request** → typecheck, lint, test, build, then a **preview site** (URL posted as a PR comment). Removed when the PR closes.
- **Merge to main** → same checks, then **production** deploy.

Requires the `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN` repo secret. Runtime settings (`DATABASE_URL`, `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING`) live in the Static Web App's environment variables, never in the repo.

Database migrations against Azure are run manually for now (`DATABASE_URL=... npm run db:migrate`).

## Admin
Fixtures, teams, stadiums, cities, airports and guides are managed at `/admin` (signed-in admins only), backed by `/api/manage/*` – Azure Functions reserves routes starting with `admin`.
To make yourself an admin, sign in once, then from PowerShell:
```powershell
$env:DATABASE_URL = '<connection string>'   # leave unset for local
npm run db:make-admin -- "Your Display Name"
Remove-Item Env:DATABASE_URL
```

### Champions League 2026/27 data
`npm run db:import-ucl` adds the league phase (36 clubs, 144 matches, venues, airports) from `db/src/ucl/ucl-2026-27.ts` and removes the example fixture. It only adds what's missing, so it's safe to re-run and won't overwrite edits made in `/admin`. Run a migration first (`db:migrate`), then the import, with `DATABASE_URL` set for production.

### City photos
`npm run db:import-photos` adds Wikimedia Commons photos (with credits) to cities that don't have one. It never replaces a photo set in `/admin`. To choose or change a photo, edit the city in `/admin` and use **Find a photo on Wikimedia Commons**.

Andersonfrfilho/zombiada.readme:
# ZombiAdA — site das equipes

Portal das equipes e documentação offline do jogo, publicados em https://zombiada.adatechnology.com.br.
Tudo abre sem internet: three.js e fontes vêm de `vendor/`, e nenhuma página aponta para o Claude.

## Pastas

| Pasta | O que guarda |
|---|---|
| `site/pages/<seção>/` | Páginas do jogo, uma pasta por seção. Publicadas em `/docs/offline/<seção>/` |
| `site/portal/` | Portal das equipes. Publicado em `/` e `/portal/portal-equipes.html` |
| `site/kit/` | Kit de peças (template). As peças vêm da Galeria do Vale Cinzento a cada build |
| `site/templates/` | Índice da documentação offline, montado a partir do `site.config.json` |
| `tools/build/` | Pipeline: gera `dist/`, troca links de artefato por páginas locais, embute libs, checa offline |
| `vendor/` | three.js r128 e fontes (Barlow Condensed, IBM Plex, JetBrains Mono) |
| `deploy/` | Configuração do Caddy |
| `dist/` | Saída gerada. Fora do git |

`site.config.json` define seções, páginas, descrições e tags do índice e, em `artifacts`, o mapa
de cada artefato publicado para a página local que o substitui.

## Comandos

```bash
make site    # gera dist/ e roda a checagem offline
make serve   # gera e serve em http://localhost:4800
make image   # build da mesma imagem que o Railway usa
```

## Página nova

1. Salve o `.html` em `site/pages/<seção>/`.
2. Acrescente a página na seção certa de `site.config.json`. Se ela veio de um artefato do Claude,
   acrescente o id em `artifacts`.
3. `make site`. O build avisa se a página ficou fora do índice; a checagem falha se ela carregar algo
   da internet ou apontar para `claude.ai`.

## Publicação

Fluxo: branch `staging` → PR → `main`. O Railway (projeto `zombiada`, serviço `site`, workspace
AdA Technology) faz o build do `Dockerfile` a cada push na `main`. O próprio build roda a checagem
offline, então uma página que dependa da internet impede o deploy.

Fomiller/fantasy-rpg.desc: Multiplayer 2D fantasy cave-crawl loot extractor. Godot client, Go servers, homelab Kubernetes.
Fomiller/fantasy-rpg.readme:
# fantasy-rpg

Multiplayer 2D fantasy cave-crawl loot extractor. Godot client, Go authoritative servers, homelab Kubernetes.

Managed by [flake-hub](https://github.com/Fomiller/flake-hub). Run `nix run .#generate`
after changing `repo.nix`.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
| --- | --- |
| `client/godot/` | The 2D Godot client, in GDScript. |
| `src/cmd/<binary>/` | One Go main package per server: `world-server`, `instance-server`, `instance-manager` and `inventory`. |
| `src/internal/` | Shared Go game code: world, combat, AI, inventory, loot. |
| `proto/game/v1/` | Protobuf messages shared by the client and the servers. |
| `deploy/` | Docker Compose for local runs, Kubernetes manifests for the homelab. |
| `tests/load/` | Headless bot clients and load test scenarios. |
| `docs/` | The mdbook: game design, architecture, decisions. |

The other paths get created by the ticket that needs them.

## Development

Enter the dev shell first. It has Go, buf, protoc, just, docker, kubectl, k3d, kind and helm.

```sh
nix develop
```

Godot is not in the dev shell. Install Godot 4 yourself. Docker must be running.

There are three ways to run the stack, from fastest to most realistic.

**1. Local process.** Postgres and Redpanda run in Compose. Each server runs as a normal Go process, so a restart is a few seconds.

```sh
just dev                     # migrate, then run world-server on :8080
just instance instance-0 8081 # an instance-server, in a second terminal
just instance instance-1 8082 # another, in a third
just deps                    # only postgres + redpanda, with the topics
just migrate                 # apply database migrations to the Compose postgres
just inventory               # the inventory service on :8070
```

The client connects to the world server on :8080 by default. The player walks around the hub town there, uses the stash chest, and walks into the cave entrance to get a ticket. The client then moves to that instance server for the run. When the run ends the client goes back to the town. All three processes share the Compose database and the dev join key. To go through the inventory service as the cluster does, run `just inventory` and start the others with `INVENTORY_URL=http://localhost:8070`. A server with neither `INVENTORY_URL` nor `DATABASE_URL` exits, unless `STORE=memory` is set. Then it keeps characters in memory and loses them on restart.

**2. Full Compose.** Every server runs as a container.

```sh
just up      # world-server :8080, instance-0 :8081, instance-1 :8082, postgres :5432, redpanda :19092
just down
```

**3. Local Kubernetes.** A k3d cluster called `fantasy-rpg`. Recipes always use the `k3d-fantasy-rpg` context, and creating the cluster does not change your current kubectl context. It runs the world server only. Instances need Agones, which this cluster does not install, so use the local process or Compose to play.

```sh
just deploy-local     # create the cluster, build and load images, deploy world-server
just k8s-down         # delete the cluster
```

Local Postgres login is `fantasy` / `fantasy`, database `fantasy`. It is for local use only.

Compose runs Postgres 18. A volume made by the old Postgres 17 setup will not start on it. Reset it once with `docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml down -v`.

The `internal/db` tests use `TEST_DATABASE_URL` if set, else start `postgres:18` with testcontainers. Without Docker they skip, unless `CI` is set.

Other recipes: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.

## Godot client

The client is a 2D Godot 4.7 project in `client/godot`, written in GDScript. It uses the Compatibility renderer.

```sh
just client         # open the editor
just client-run     # run the game against a local server
just client-online  # run the game against the homelab server
just client-check   # import and run headless; prints "main scene loaded"
just client-test    # headless player tests: movement, walls, interact
just net-test       # start two worlds and three instances on a throwaway Postgres, then play the whole loop
```

Controls: WASD or arrow keys to move, Space or left click to attack in the direction the character faces, E to open the loot window on a chest or pile, then Take an item or Take all, I or Tab for the inventory, Escape to close an open window. The last mouse motion or move key sets the facing.

The server keeps your items by player name. Reconnect with the same name to get them back. Set one with `-- --name=ann`; without it the client picks a random name each launch.

To play against the server, start `just dev` and two `just instance` recipes, then run `just client-run`. The client joins the world server at `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/ws`. An instance server can run another cave with `CAVE=yard`, a small room with no enemies. The top-left label shows your player ID and the server tick. A white outline marks where the server thinks you are. Without a server the label says "offline", the game still runs, and the client retries every 2 seconds. Point at another server with `/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --path client/godot -- --server=ws://host:port/ws`.

The recipes use `/Applications/Godot.app`. For another install, pass the path: `just godot=/path/to/godot client`.

Commit the `*.uid` files Godot writes next to scripts. Godot uses them to keep references working when a file moves. `.godot/` is a cache and is ignored.

### Editing GDScript in Neovim

The Godot editor runs a GDScript language server on port 6005 while it is open.

1. Open the editor with `just client`.
2. Start Neovim with a server socket, so Godot can open files in it:

   ```sh
   nvim --listen /tmp/godot.pipe
   ```

3. In Godot, open Editor Settings > Text Editor > External. Turn on "Use External Editor". Set the path to `nvim` and the flags to `--server /tmp/godot.pipe --remote-send "<C-\><C-N>:e {file}<CR>:call cursor({line},{col})<CR>"`.
4. In Neovim, turn on the `gdscript` LSP config from nvim-lspco

Anxiety471/Adaptive-Hostiles.readme:
# Adaptive Hostiles

**Jev-assisted hostile raids and elite pawn tactics for RimWorld.**

> **Status: initial codebase / pre-alpha.** The TypeSafe API client, validated decision planners, deterministic fallbacks, unit-test harness, and RimWorld mod bootstrap are present. The game-independent core (roster generator, candidate enumeration, order revalidation, operative registry, async scheduler) is also implemented and tested. The RimWorld-facing hooks (raid interception, map sampling, job assignment, save/load) and in-game testing are **not yet implemented**. Hostile-raid composition hooks now exist in the Mod project but are **unverified in game** (no RimWorld references were available when written); map sampling and Operative job control are still missing.

## Design

Adaptive Hostiles is **not a storyteller**. Cassandra, Phoebe, Randy, and modded storytellers continue deciding *when* raid incidents occur. The planned integration replaces *how hostile humanlike raid forces are composed*, without relying on raid points, and occasionally adds a Jev-controlled elite **Operative**.

The Operative's movement decisions belong to Jev. RimWorld's native job and pathfinding systems only execute a **destination cell selected by Jev** from reachable cells supplied by the game. Jev also selects targets and a tactical stance; it does not emit arbitrary code or pathfinding instructions.

| System | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Vanilla/modded storyteller | Incident timing and scheduling, unchanged |
| Raid adapter *(planned)* | Intercept hostile raids and create a faction-compatible roster without raid-point budgets |
| Jev raid planner *(implemented)* | Choose raid scale and approach from structured colony state |
| Elite Operative adapter *(planned)* | Spawn, equip, and track an uncommon elite pawn |
| Jev tactical planner *(implemented)* | Choose an exact movement candidate, target, and stance from legal options |
| RimWorld jobs *(planned)* | Execute the chosen destination and actions, preserving native combat/pathfinding |

See [SPECS.md](SPECS.md) for behavior, interfaces, guardrails, and acceptance tests.

## Current repository structure

```text
About/About.xml                 RimWorld metadata and Harmony dependency
LoadFolders.xml                 RimWorld 1.7 assembly folder selection
Source/AdaptiveHostiles.Core/  API client, decision models, planners and fallbacks
Source/AdaptiveHostiles.Mod/   RimWorld 1.7 bootstrap (no gameplay hooks yet)
Tests/AdaptiveHostiles.Tests/  Dependency-free planner and client tests
1.7/Assemblies/                Build output (ignored by git)
```

## Build (RimWorld 1.7 unstable beta)

The 1.7 Waylith build uses **.NET 10**. You need the .NET 10 SDK and a local copy of RimWorld 1.7 plus the Harmony mod for 1.7. Proprietary game DLLs and Harmony DLLs are **not** checked into this repository.

```bash
# Run the game-independent tests first:
dotnet run --project Tests/AdaptiveHostiles.Tests/AdaptiveHostiles.Tests.csproj

# Build the RimWorld assembly. Paths must point to your own installs:
dotnet build Source/AdaptiveHostiles.Mod/AdaptiveHostiles.Mod.csproj -c Release \
  -p:RimWorldDir="/path/to/RimWorld" \
  -p:HarmonyDll="/path/to/Harmony/1.7/Assemblies/0Harmony.dll"
```

The mod project's build output is `1.7/Assemblies/`. Copy the **entire repository mod folder** (excluding Source, Tests, and .git if preferred) into RimWorld's local `Mods` directory and enable Harmony above Adaptive Hostiles. The mod replaces eligible hostile raid rosters (Harmony patches in `Source/AdaptiveHostiles.Mod/Raids`).

For development, set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in your environment. The core client sends requests to TypeSafe's official `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` endpoint with model `jev-latest`. Other decision models are selectable with `ADAPTIVE_HOSTILES_PROVIDER` (`jev`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `local`; default `auto` picks the first of `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`), with `ADAPTIVE_HOSTILES_MODEL` and `ADAPTIVE_HOSTILES_ENDPOINT` (any OpenAI-compatible server, e.g. a local Ollama) as overrides. **Never commit an API key.** The game-facing settings and background request scheduler have not yet been connected.

## Principles

1. **No storyteller replacement** and no change to raid scheduling.
2. **No raid points in our hostile raid composition algorithm**. Some other game systems still use vanilla points, and we will not corrupt those globally.
3. **Jev chooses the Operative's actual destinations** from valid, reachable candidates; it cannot teleport, navigate through walls, or fabricate a map coordinate.
4. **Nonblocking and recoverable.** Network calls must not run on the RimWorld main thread. A failed/missing/stale decision falls back to bounded local logic.
5. **Faction and mod compatibility first.** Elite equipment should be appropriate to its faction; no blanket changes to friendly raids, quests, traders, or unrelated incidents.

## Roadmap

- [x] Document technical scope and acceptance criteria
- [x] Set up .NET 10 projects, RimWorld mod manifest, and test harness
- [x] Implement Jev request/response validation and decisions from candidate lists
- [ ] Verify assembly references against an installed RimWorld 1.7 beta
- [ ] Add on-game-thread colony snapshot and background/cached Jev raid evaluation
- [x] Raid history: outcomes recorded per faction, saved with the game, fed into planning *(unverified in game)*
- [x] Replace **hostile raid composition** without consuming raid points *(hooks written, not yet verified in game)*
- [ ] Generate faction-appropriate rare Operatives and persist their identities
- [ ] Observe tactical map, enumerate reachable cells, and asynchronously ask Jev
- [ ] Convert Jev-selected cells/targets into RimWorld jobs with safe reevaluation
- [ ] Add settings, compatibility checks, dev-mode tools, performance and save/load tests

## References

- [TypeSafe System One API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one)

yaswanthkumarp21/shadow-rep.readme:
# Shadow Rep

**Your gym, your food, your progress — levelled up.**

Shadow Rep is a private, self-hosted training and nutrition tracker with a game-style "System" look: levels, XP, stats,
daily quests and record celebrations, all earned from your real workouts and meals. It runs in Docker on your own
computer and reaches your phone over a private HTTPS address — no accounts with anyone, no cloud, nothing to pay.

- **Train:** weekly plan, guided workouts, progression, body weight, stats, an optional AI Coach.
- **Eat:** food diary with calories and macros, foods, recipes, goals, water — in the same app, under the **Food** tab.
- **Level up:** a level, rank (E → S) and four stats (STR, END, AGI, VIT) computed from what you actually do; daily quests; a
  "NEW RECORD" moment when you set a personal best. Every number is tunable in one file.
- **Yours:** passkey sign-in (no passwords), data in plain folders on your PC, nightly backups, no analytics or trackers.

## Built on

Shadow Rep is **inspired by and built on two open-source projects**, combined into one app with its own name, artwork and features.
Thank you to their authors.

| Part | Foundation | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| Gym app (`apps/gym`) | **[OpenGym](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym)** by Duarte Santos, via the fork [alexpcosta/opengym](https://github.com/alexpcosta/opengym) | AGPL-3.0 |
| Food app (`apps/food`) | **[NutriTrace](https://github.com/TraceApps/nutritrace)** by TraceApps, run unmodified and re-skinned | AGPL-3.0 |

The full story of what was inherited and what was changed is in [`ORIGINS.md`](ORIGINS.md). The in-app credits are under
**Settings → Credits & licences**.

## Layout

```
shadow-rep/
  apps/gym/          the gym app (web + API). Shadow Rep additions: frontend/src/custom, api/custom
  apps/food/         the food app: compose file, the Shadow Rep skin + branding (theme/), Indian foods starter list
  proxy/             one address for both: /  -> gym app,  /food/ -> food app (through the skin proxy)
  scripts/           backup, restore, health check, start/stop helpers
  docker-compose.yml proxy + the skin proxy
  ORIGINS.md  NOTICE.md  LICENSE  BUILD_LOG.md  README_MY_SETUP.md
```

## Set it up (outline — details in `README_MY_SETUP.md` and `BUILD_LOG.md`)

1. Install Docker Desktop (WSL2) and Tailscale (free personal plan; enable HTTPS certificates). Choose your private hostname **once** —
   passkeys are tied to it (`RP_ID`).
2. `git clone <this repo>`, then in `apps/gym`: copy `.env.example` to `.env`, set `RP_ID`, `ORIGIN`, `RP_NAME`; in `apps/food`: copy
   `.env.example` to `.env` and set a long random `JWT_SECRET`.
3. Start everything: `scripts\start-all.bat`. Publish privately: `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:8090`
   (never use Funnel unless you want it public).
4. Create a read-only token in the food app (Settings → API Tokens, scope `mcp:read` only) and put it in `apps/gym/.env` as
   `NUTRITRACE_TOKEN` (see `.env.example`).
5. Check it: `scripts\smoke-test.bat` (19 checks). Schedule `scripts\backup.ps1` daily.

## Security

- No secrets are in this repository (checked across the full history). `.env` files, data, backups and tokens stay on your computer.
- Backup zips contain passkey data and the encrypted Coach token — keep them private.
- The AI Coach (optional) uses your own Claude account via a setup token, only after you consent; keep the app single-user.

## Licence

Shadow Rep contains OpenGym and NutriTrace (both **AGPL-3.0**), so the whole combined work is offered under the **GNU AGPL v3.0** — see
[`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Original notices are kept in [`NOTICE.md`](NOTICE.md) and `apps/gym/NOTICE.md`. If you let other people use your own
copy over a network, the AGPL requires you to offer them the source, including your changes.
Third-party material: exercise media (hasaneyldrm/exercises-dataset), Open Food Facts data (ODbL), MuscleMap (MIT), Orbitron and
Rajdhani fonts (OFL-1.1) — see the in-app credits. The logo, rank sigils and rune ring are original artwork made for this project.

AI Coach: Agent SDK + Codex provider
Remove retired Coach providers

AI Coach: swap Claude's CLI OAuth for the Agent SDK, add a real Codex provider

The old Claude path drove the raw CLI through a hand-rolled browser OAuth
copy-paste exchange pinned against a specific CLI version. It's replaced with
the official Claude Agent SDK plus a `claude setup-token` paste, which is the
supported way to authorize a headless Agent SDK job and drops an OAuth client
implementation this project shouldn't own.

Codex goes from an unauthenticated stub to a driveable provider: bundled CLI,
ChatGPT device-code sign-in that keeps the refresh token in Codex's own
isolated cache (never coach.json), a locked-down managed config.toml (no
shell, network, plugins, or root filesystem access), and a disabled-features
allowlist enforced on every invocation.

Dockerfile installs both runtimes and adds bubblewrap for Codex's sandboxed
exec; docker-compose mounts the Codex credential cache as its own volume,
separate from ./data. Docs, admin UI, and provider-setup guides updated to
match; api/test/config.test.js covers the new auth-state branches.

AI Coach: implementation report

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0135to9eqToex75k5THkAvGa

AI Coach: plan design and feedback-driven reviews from a local CLI agent

openGym could progress a plan but never write one, and never looked at the plan
itself — the engine adjusted weights inside whatever structure you built, and the
RIR/RPE ratings it collected were read by nothing. The Coach does both jobs the
engine deliberately doesn't: it designs plans, and it changes them when the
training says they should change.

Server (api/coach/):
- config store in data/coach.json, provider credential AES-256-GCM encrypted with
  a key derived from data/secret; COACH_DISABLED as the only env knob
- OAuth (PKCE) connect flow plus an API-key fallback, both driven from the admin
  dashboard — no .env editing, no restart
- job runner: per-profile single-flight, global cap of 2, 5-minute timeout, honest
  boot recovery, one repair round then a clean failure
- payload builder as a strict allowlist; identity, credentials, push subscriptions
  and other profiles cannot ride along
- validator gating every answer on a closed list of change types and real library
  ids — the actual security boundary of the feature
- adapters for Claude Code (bundled), Gemini, Codex, a custom-command contract and
  an in-repo fixture provider that drives the whole loop with no AI account
- cadence tick for scheduled reviews; proposals notify only when they carry changes

Client:
- lib/coach.js: plan fingerprint, per-change staleness, snapshots, atomic apply,
  revert, bounded log — pure functions, pinned against the server's own source
- Coach hub, six-screen intake, proposal review with per-change accept/reject and
  muscle-map preview, consent screen rendered from the payload allowlist
- admin card for provider, sign-in, caps and health; optional session rating on the
  finish summary; canned local provider so the demo build can show the loop

Packaging: the CLI is installed into the api image at a pinned version and verified
at build time; jobs run as an unprivileged user that cannot read /data.

Parity: an instance with no provider is the app it was before — no new UI, no new
requests, no change to synced state.

261 tests (54 api, 207 frontend), 171 new strings translated across all 11 locales.
