Dependabot: don't chase Node majors that were never LTS

The first run offered node:22-alpine → 25-alpine in both Dockerfiles. Odd
majors are Current, not LTS, and stop getting fixes about six months in — for
an image other people self-host that trades stability for nothing. Even majors
are still proposed, so 22 → 24 will show up as a PR, which is the move actually
worth reviewing.

Sessions you can actually end, and invite codes worth guessing at

SECURITY.md documented three weaknesses two hours ago. Documented is better than
hidden; fixed is better than documented.

Sessions were a signed cookie the server trusted for a year, and /api/logout
only cleared it in the browser you clicked it in — a copy left on a shared
machine stayed good until it expired, and the only way to end it was deleting
./data/secret and signing out the entire instance. The cookie payload now
carries the user's session version, and POST /api/logout/all bumps it, which
kills every cookie that account ever had. Settings grows a "Sign out
everywhere" row for it.

Cookies already in the wild have no version field. They read as version 0 and
match a user who has never bumped, so nobody is signed out by this deploy and
db.json needs no migration — sv appears lazily on the first bump. Verified
against a server running the new code with a db.json shaped like the live one.

Session default drops from 365 days to 90, overridable with SESSION_DAYS. The
expiry is baked into each cookie when issued, so lowering it never cuts an
existing session short.

Invite codes go from 32 to 64 bits. The app has no rate limiting by design and
/api/register/options answers whether a code is valid, so the code itself has to
be the part not worth guessing. Existing codes still work — validation is an
exact string compare. Unused old ones are worth revoking and reissuing.

What did not change: no rate limiting, still the reverse proxy's job, still the
first caveat in SECURITY.md. requireUserVerification stays false — raising it
could refuse passkeys that already exist, which is a lockout, not a fix.

Wake-lock test: stop assigning to a global Node now owns

The first CI run found this, which is the point of having one. Node 21+ defines
globalThis.navigator itself as a getter with no setter, so `globalThis.navigator
= {...}` throws under ESM strict mode. This box runs Node 20, where the global
does not exist and the assignment is fine — the test has never failed locally
and never would.

Only the first test failed: its afterEach deletes the built-in accessor, so
every later test assigned cleanly against the hole it left. defineProperty works
on both runtimes.

Production images are node:22-alpine (web/Dockerfile, api/Dockerfile), so the
version CI runs is the right one and the test was what needed fixing.

Demo: rate the sets, so the demo shows the effort stats

The live demo is the shop window, and it was the one place the new Effort card
could not appear — demoSeed fabricated twelve weeks of training with no ratings
at all, so every chart that reads effort rendered empty or absent.

The seed now rates about 82% of finished sets, deterministically as before:
effort tracks position in the session and the block's progression, one deload
week sits well away from failure, the first three weeks are written in RPE as if
imported from another app, and one exercise stays unrated throughout so the
partial-coverage case is visible rather than theoretical. Only reps-mode sets
are rated — a reps-in-reserve number on a cardio set would be nonsense.

A security policy, and dependency updates that stay quiet

openGym ships passkeys, a signed session cookie and an admin dashboard, and
people run it on the open internet. Until now someone finding a hole had no
option but a public issue.

SECURITY.md documents the model as it actually is, verified against server.js
rather than described from memory: what the session cookie is and how long it
lasts, that it cannot be revoked individually, that ./data is unencrypted and
its holder can mint a session for any account, that there is no rate limiting,
and what changing RP_ID costs. A self-hoster deciding whether to run this for
other people deserves that list up front.

Dependabot is monthly and grouped one PR per ecosystem — a default setup on a
solo project produces noise that stops being read, which is the opposite of the
point. Android/iOS are left out on purpose: Capacitor pins those to the npm
packages, so bumping them separately breaks the mobile build.

Also: api/ has had two dependencies since notifications landed. CONTRIBUTING
still claimed one.

CI: actually run the tests, and hold the locales to one key set

There are 159 unit tests and nothing ran them. Both existing workflows fire on
push to main only, so the two outside pull requests merged so far were reviewed
by eye alone. This runs the suite, the build and a locale check on every pull
request.

The locale check exists because of a bug that shipped last week: a feature added
17 strings to de.js only, and the other ten languages fell back to English
mid-sentence with nothing failing anywhere. The checker compares every locale
against the union of all keys, so a string added to one file flags the other ten
instead of passing unnoticed.

Changelog: the effort stats, under Unreleased

v1.2.3 is published, so this is the start of the next version rather than an
amendment to that one — it stays under Unreleased until there is a release to
fold it into.

Merge branch 'effort-stats': the effort ratings, read back as statistics

Sets have carried an RIR/RPE rating since v1.2.3, but nothing ever read it
back — the number lived in the set label and nowhere else. This is the other
half: a trend per week, the spread across the scale, the share of sets taken
near failure, a hard-sets mode on the muscle map, and the rating riding along
on each exercise's own curve.

Send questions to Discussions, and put a Sponsor button on the repo

Discussions has been enabled since the start and empty since the start, so
every question arrives as an issue — the tracker is carrying design debates and
"how do I" alongside actual bugs, and the answers end up buried in closed
issues where the next person searching won't find them.

The "New issue" screen now offers Q&A, Ideas and Show-and-tell before the
templates, which is where that traffic gets intercepted; README and CONTRIBUTING
say the same thing in a table.

FUNDING.yml does nothing until the account is enrolled in GitHub Sponsors —
GitHub simply doesn't render the button. Stated plainly next to it: openGym is
AGPL, there is no paid tier and nothing is held back for sponsors. A project
that starts selling access to its maintainer stops being the thing people
starred.

Effort stats: the other ten languages, and drop what nothing calls

The card shipped translated into German only, so every other UI language fell
back to the English source strings mid-sentence — the locale files have been
key-for-key identical until now, and they are again (607 each).

exerciseEffort() had no caller: Stats builds its per-exercise curve from the
points it already has, which are filtered by training mode, so the library
version would have drawn a different set of sessions. Removed with its tests
rather than left as a second answer to the same question.

Stats: read the effort back — trend, distribution, hard sets, per exercise

Rating a set only paid off inside the set label until now: Stats never looked at
rir/rpe at all. It reads them now, in four places.

lib/effort.js aggregates everything in RIR and converts back to whichever scale the
profile reads. A history that mixes the two — own logs in RIR, an imported file in
RPE — has to average as one series or every chart draws half the data, and RIR is the
internal unit because its zero is real where RPE's floor of 6 is a convention.

- an Effort card: average and share of sets taken near failure, the week-by-week curve
  with the week's volume in the tooltip, and where the sets land on the scale
- the muscle map gains a hard-sets mode: a muscle can lead on volume and still never
  be trained near failure
- Exercise progress carries effort on the top-set dots and as a curve of its own — the
  same weight with more left in the tank is progress a weight-only line draws flat
- LineChart learns an inverted axis (RIR counts down as it gets harder) and per-point marks

Every number carries how much of the training it speaks for: rating is optional and off
by default, so an unrated set is left out rather than read as failure, and an average
waits for five rated sets before it claims to be one.

Release v1.2.3: fold in the screen lock, the rest timer and the settings grouping

v1.2.3 was tagged but never published, so everything since v1.2.2 -- the last
published release -- belongs in this one version rather than a new number.

CHANGELOG gets the three new sections, README a feature bullet, SELF_HOSTING a note
that the Wake Lock API wants HTTPS (or localhost) like passkeys do and that iOS
refuses it in Low Power Mode. Website: the APK line said v1.2.2 while the download is
1.2.3, and the feature grid gained the screen-awake card.

Rest timer: take 15 seconds off, not only add them

addRest now accepts a negative step, and taking off more than is left finishes the
rest instead of counting into the negative -- which also kept a negative duration out
of the progress bar and out of the server-side push schedule.

Three controls and the clock do not fit one line on a phone: at 360px the bar was
left with about 30px and stopped saying anything. The rest variant stacks -- clock and
bar on top, controls beneath, -15 and +15 together in number-line order, Skip pushed
to the far edge so the button that ends the rest is not next to the one you tap to buy
more time. Scoped to #timer.rest, so the work timer keeps its single row. Back to one
line at >=1000px, and the card is nearly opaque now -- the set rows underneath were
reading through it.

Keep the screen awake while a workout is running

Locking and unlocking the phone between every set was the worst part of logging on
one. Settings -> During a workout -> Keep screen awake, on by default; the lock is
held only while S.active exists, so it follows the workout rather than the route and
lets go when you finish.

The browser drops the lock whenever the document stops being visible, which is what
happens the moment you glance at a message, so wakelock.js keeps its own 'wanted'
intent and re-acquires on every visibilitychange. It also releases a sentinel that
arrives after a release landed mid-request, and swallows the rejection iOS gives in
Low Power Mode. Where the API is missing the row shows disabled instead of offering
a switch that does nothing.

Settings is regrouped by what each thing affects while the row needed a home:
General (language, units), During a workout (rest timer, keep awake, sounds, effort),
Notifications, Appearance, Data. Nothing removed, no setting changed meaning.

Release v1.2.3: effort per set, and the RPE your old app already had

Everything published since v1.2.2 is one number: the RIR column from #21 and
the RIR/RPE scale choice built on top of it, plus the importer reading the
RPE that Hevy and Strong export.

Changelog, README, roadmap and the website all describe the feature as it
actually shipped — a rating that is optional, keeps its scale per set, and
is deliberately not an input to progression or the 1RM estimate.

Android versionCode 4: it has to increase strictly or the APK will not
install over the v1.2.2 build already out there.

Merge branch 'effort-metric': effort per set (RIR / RPE)

Adds an optional per-set effort rating on either of the two scales people
actually use, generalising the RIR column from #21 rather than bolting a
second one next to it, and teaches the importer to read the RPE that Hevy
and Strong already export.

Import: bring the RPE other apps already recorded

Hevy and Strong both write an RPE next to every set and the importer was
dropping the column, so a history imported from either arrived flatter than
the file it came from. It is read now, along with an RIR column if a file
happens to have one.

A blank cell stays unrated rather than becoming 0, and a written-out 0 is
only a rating on the RIR scale — RIR 0 is a set taken to failure, while RPE
runs 1-10, so an app writing 0 there means "nothing here" and reading it as
an effort would stamp one on every unrated set in the file. Ratings above
the scale are capped rather than thrown away, junk is ignored, and effort
only rides along on weighted rep sets — a treadmill row has nowhere to show
it. A file carrying both columns is read as RIR, the precedence setLabel
already reads them back with.

The import summary reports how many sets brought a rating, and says where
to switch the column on when the profile is not logging effort yet —
otherwise the ratings arrive invisibly and look like they were lost.

Export needed no change: the backup is the whole state serialised, so both
fields and the setting travel with it. There is a test pinning that now,
along with 11 for the import paths.

Effort stepper: count up from the bottom of the scale

The first + on an empty cell jumped straight to a "typical working set"
(RIR 2 / RPE 8), skipping 0 and 1 with no way to see why. A stepper that
lands somewhere other than where counting would take you is just puzzling,
so it now starts at the bottom of the scale and walks up in even steps like
every other stepper in the app: RIR from 0, RPE from 6 — the scale is only
meaningful for working sets and anything lighter is a warm-up nobody rates.

Stepping back off the floor clears the cell again, so a mistap is undoable
instead of sticking at 0 — which on the RIR scale claims the set went to
failure. − on a cell that was never filled in still leaves it empty.

The stepping moved out of the view into stepEffort/capEffort in history.js,
where it can be tested: 16 new cases covering the scale walk, the floor and
ceiling, the clear-on-undershoot, half-step rounding, junk settings values,
the showRir overlay every load path performs, and a session's worth of
logging end to end.

A typed value is still only capped, never floored — clamping up would turn
the "1" of "10" into the floor and fight the input.

The help sheet no longer claims the highlighted row is where + starts; it is
where working sets usually land. Reworded in all 11 language packs.

Effort help: show the two scales as one table, (i) before the control

The sheet explained RIR and RPE in three paragraphs, which is a bad way to
say "these are the same judgement counted from opposite ends" — you had to
hold both sentences in your head to see the correspondence. A conversion
table shows it in one look: RIR and RPE in fixed tabular columns you can
read straight down, the feel in words next to them, and the row a working
set usually lands on highlighted in the accent.

The table is built from the same parts as the app's grouped lists (surface
fill, inset hairlines) instead of a real <table>, so it inherits the card
look and wraps on a narrow phone.

The (i) moves ahead of the segmented control: you reach the explanation on
the way to the choice rather than past it.

The three paragraph strings are replaced by the table's strings in all 11
language packs.

Effort per set: RIR or RPE, whichever scale you think in

The RIR column becomes a three-way setting (Off / RIR / RPE). Both scales
measure the same judgement from opposite ends — RPE 8 is RIR 2 — so they
share one column and one stepper, but keep their own field on the set.

A set is never silently rewritten into the other scale: switching the
setting changes what new sets ask for, and old sets still read back with
the scale they were logged with.

Profiles carrying the old showRir boolean keep their column (effortOf
falls back to it until the new setting is chosen), so a backup or another
device that still has the flag does not lose the column.

The steppers now know the scale: the first + lands on a typical working
set (RIR 2 / RPE 8) instead of the end of the scale, and typed values are
capped at 10 — there is no RPE 12.

Merge PR #21: optional RIR column on reps-mode sets

octaviodimarco's RIR (reps in reserve) stepper for reps-mode sets, opt-in under
Settings → Units & timer, plus a fixup for the leftover RIR-0 stamp and the
header alignment.

RIR: an unlogged RIR stays unlogged, and the header lines up

A set that never had an RIR could still end up carrying one: NumberField mapped an
empty field to 0 and the − button clamped to 0, so one stray tap stamped '(RIR 0)' —
went to failure — on the set for good, in history and in backups, with no way back.
An optional field now clears to null (the key is dropped), and stepping down from
empty leaves it empty. A typed 0 still logs a real 0.

The row's three-stepper sizing also has to reach the header, or the labels sit up
to 5px off the columns they name.

i18n: add RIR strings to all 11 language packs

t('RIR') and the new Settings toggle label had no entries in
src/locales/ — RIR itself is kept as the acronym across languages
(same treatment as 1RM), only the surrounding label text is translated.

Remove RIR auto-check; gate the column behind a setting

Two blockers from review:

- NumberField.commit() fires onChange on every keystroke, so typing
  a decimal RIR (e.g. 1.5) committed the auto-check after the first
  character, before the value was finished — and the same auto-check
  turned a stray tap on an empty field's "−" (or clearing it) into a
  permanent "RIR 0", since 0 is indistinguishable from unset once the
  key exists on the set. Logging RIR is back to a plain field with no
  side effect; the checkbox is the only way to mark a set done, same
  as weight and reps.

- The RIR stepper narrowed every reps-mode row's +/- buttons for
  everyone, including the majority not running an RIR-based program.
  It's now behind a `showRir` setting (Settings → Units & timer,
  default off), so the existing row is untouched unless opted in.

Auto-check a set when its RIR is logged

Logging RIR is naturally the last thing you do for a set — by the
time you're rating how many reps you had left, you've already
finished it. Editing the RIR field (typing or the +/- stepper) now
checks the set off itself, same beep/vibrate/rest-timer as tapping
the checkbox by hand, so that's one less tap per set.

Weight and reps are unaffected — those are often set before the set
is performed (pre-filled targets), so editing them shouldn't imply
it's done. Guarded by !s.done so re-editing RIR on an already-done
set (e.g. a correction) doesn't re-fire the toggle side effects.

Add optional RIR (reps in reserve) to reps-mode sets

Adds a third stepper column, next to weight and reps, for logging RIR
on strength sets — not shown for cardio or timed holds, where it has
no meaning. RIR is purely a logging/display addition: it never
touches the progression engine (linear/Greyskull/double progression
only ever read weight/reps/seconds), and it round-trips through the
existing whole-object backup export/import with no code changes there.

The set object only gains an `rir` key once the user actually logs a
value (buildSets/addSet don't pre-seed it), matching how missing
fields already read as undefined elsewhere in the store — no schema
version or migration needed for existing logged workouts.

Fitting a third stepper next to weight+reps on narrow phones needed
the same treatment as the exercise-config sheet's three-steppers-in-a-row
(.cfgrow): narrower buttons and a smaller value font just for rows
that show RIR, verified by hand at 360-390px with edge-case values
(2-3 digit weight, double-digit reps, decimal RIR together).

"Last time" summaries now append "(RIR n)" when a set has one logged,
covered by new setLabel tests including the rir: 0 case (0 is a valid
RIR and must not be treated as absent).

Android: versionCode 3 for the v1.2.2 APK

Same versionName — v1.2.2 was never published, so this is still that release — but the code
has to increase strictly or Android refuses to install over the build already out there.

Release v1.2.2: docs, changelog and website for everything since v1.2.1

v1.2.2 was tagged but never published, so by the versioning rule everything since the last
published release — v1.2.1 — belongs in this one number: the mobile app, the importer, plan
sharing, the QA fix series, and now timed sets, progression rules and estimated 1RM.

The changelog was missing plan sharing and the fix series entirely; both are written up
here rather than left to the git log.

i18n: the new strings in all 11 language packs

49 keys per pack, 572 in total. The progression rules explain themselves in prose, so most
of these are full sentences rather than labels — a rule you cannot read is one you will
not trust, in any language.

The screens for timed sets, progression and estimated 1RM (#16 #17 #18)

Where the three features surface:

 · Routine editor — a progression rule for the whole routine, and per exercise a
   Reps/Time switch, an optional rule of its own and the step it moves in.
 · Workout — timed sets get a start button and the work-timer bar; every exercise says in
   one line why its target is what it is ("every rep last time — 2.5 kg more", "missed
   reps 3 sessions running — reset to 55 kg"). The weights are already right when the
   session opens rather than being suggested afterwards, which is what the old bump-hint
   button did.
 · Stats — the exercise curve switches between top set and estimated 1RM, and names the
   set the estimate came from. Timed exercises chart the longest hold.
 · Exercise detail — an estimated 1RM from your log plus a calculator for a set you have
   not done yet, so the number is reachable before there is any history.
 · Finish summary — a new best estimated 1RM is reported separately from a weight PR.
   Same weight for more reps is progress, but it is not a heavier lift.

Saving an exercise now replaces its config rather than merging into it, so switching back
from time to reps cannot leave a stale duration behind.

Automatic progression: named rules instead of one hard-coded hint (#17)

The old rule was a single line: all reps done, suggest 2.5 kg more. No rep ranges, no
AMRAP, no idea what to do after a bad session. This replaces it with a small set of
policies — linear, Greyskull LP, double progression, and adding time for timed work —
picked per routine and overridable per exercise.

Every function is pure and derives the next target from the log each time it is needed.
Nothing is written back into a finished workout and no counters are stored, so correcting
a mistyped set immediately produces the right next target.

Reading a session honestly is the whole point. Short reps count as a miss even when the
set was checked off; an unchecked set counts as a miss because it was not performed. A
session that fell apart can never advance the load as though it had succeeded.

Two cases the naive version gets badly wrong, both found against real data:

 · Workouts only started recording their prescription in this version. Judged against
   nothing, every past session scores as a miss — the demo history produced "missed reps
   11 sessions running, deload", and every existing user would have been greeted with the
   same on their first session after updating. Targetless history is judged against the
   exercise's current plan instead, which is what the old hint compared against.

 · Bodyweight work has no load to take off. "Reset your push-ups to 2.5 kg" is not advice,
   so with no external weight the rules progress in reps and leave the load alone.

An exercise can be logged by time instead of reps (#16)

Until now the logging model came from the body part alone: cardio meant duration, and
everything else meant weight × reps. A plank, a hang, a wall sit or a loaded carry could
only be timed by filing it under cardio, which then put it in the wrong charts.

A routine entry can now say so itself — reps, time or cardio. Entries without a mode keep
behaving exactly as before, so every existing plan, workout and shared plan file is read
unchanged and nothing needs migrating.

Timed sets get a work timer that counts the set itself, kept deliberately separate from
the rest timer: the two mean opposite things and must never run together. Finishing early
logs the time actually held, not the target, because crediting a full 45 seconds for a
38-second hold would quietly corrupt the log it exists to keep.

Finished workouts now also store what the session prescribed. Without it, history cannot
say whether a session hit its reps, and a timed session reads back as "0 reps".

Estimated 1RM: the calculation, and only from sets that can support it (#18)

Working out how strong a set was meant leaving the app. Epley by default, with Brzycki
and Lombardi available and documented.

Two things it deliberately refuses to do:
 · guess above 12 reps, where the formulas disagree by double digits and the answer says
   more about work capacity than about maximal strength;
 · read `topW`, the working weight you confirm after an exercise — it carries no rep
   count, so it cannot produce an estimate at all.

It also knows nothing about the exercise database. An estimate needs a weight AND reps,
and only reps-mode sets carry both, so cardio and timed sets drop out of every scan on
their own rather than through a type check that would need keeping in sync.

Tests: a runner for the pure helpers

The logic that decides what you lift next has no business being verified by hand in a
browser. Vitest is a dev dependency only — the app itself stays dependency-free.

i18n: the new strings in all 11 language packs

Twelve keys for the plan-import notice, the mixed-unit warning, the
singular counts, the weigh-in button and the error boundary, anchored
next to the strings they belong with. Drops 'Skip today' and
'{0} routines · {1} exercises', which the code no longer uses, and
retunes the German streak line ('13 Wochen in Folge').

All packs stay at the same key count.

UI fixes found while testing the workout flow

· The rest timer floats above the tab bar, so it covered the set rows
  underneath it — during a rest, the next set was behind the bar. The page
  now gets enough bottom padding while a rest runs to scroll clear of it.
· "Skip today", sitting right under "Save & start workout", reads like
  skipping the session rather than the weigh-in. It says "Start without
  weighing in".
· The calendar legend drew "Planned" in blue while planned days have
  always had a grey dot.
· Body weight showed "− 0" when it hadn't moved since the last weigh-in.
· In a superset both exercises are on screen at once, so their animations
  give way: 180px meant scrolling a full screen between two exercises you
  are meant to alternate.

Import from other apps: convert weights per row, not per file

The unit was decided once for the whole file: if any row said lb and none
said kg it converted, otherwise it did nothing. FitNotes writes the unit
next to every set, so a history recorded partly in pounds and partly in
kilos hit the 'otherwise' branch — the file was taken over unconverted
and "185 lb" was logged as 185 kg, while the summary claimed the file
does not say which unit it uses.

Each row now carries its own unit through to the conversion (falling back
to the file's, then to the profile's), and a mixed file says so in the
preview.

Also: the "exercises matched" tile counted matched rows, so three
exercises across five sets read as five. It counts distinct exercises
now, which is what the label says.

A shared plan file can no longer take the app down

Importing a plan whose exercise ids this build doesn't know — a
hand-edited file, an export from a build with a different dataset — put
those ids straight into a routine. The routine editor skipped them
silently (you could neither see nor delete them), and starting the
routine reached for ex.n on undefined: white screen, no tab bar, no way
back. The running workout is persisted, so it came back on every reload.

Three layers, so this class of bug can't reach the screen again:

  · parsePlan() drops ids that resolve to neither the library nor a
    custom exercise carried in the same file, and the import sheet says
    how many were left out.
  · exOr() renders an unresolvable id as a placeholder, so the routine
    editor shows it (and lets you remove it) instead of hiding it, and
    the workout view survives one.
  · an ErrorBoundary around the routes: it keeps the tab bar alive,
    offers a reload, and can discard a running workout that can't be
    drawn. It is keyed on the route, so switching tabs clears it.

Turning the schedule switch on now really replaces Mon–Sun, as the
switch has always claimed. It only wrote the days the shared plan filled,
so days it left empty kept your own routine and you silently ended up
training a mix of two plans.

Also here, because they sit in the same lines: the tags that carry a unit
or a whole sentence opt out of the capitalise rule ("Best: 85 Kg", "Last
Time You Hit All Reps"), and the workout header's "best" now includes the
working weight you confirmed, so it agrees with the sheet that asked for
it.

Numbers follow the UI language, volume stays in your own unit

fmtNum was pinned to en-CH, so every user in every one of the twelve
languages got Swiss apostrophes: "7'535 kg". It now uses the same locale
as the dates.

fmtVol turned anything over 10 000 into tonnes regardless of the profile's
unit — "18.8t" is meaningless for a pound profile, and inside one history
list "18.8t" next to "7'535 kg" is two numbers you can't compare. Volume
is now always shown in the unit you train in.

The weight slider's ceiling of 300 was a kg number applied to both units;
in pounds it cut off at 136 kg, below plenty of people's body weight and
well below an everyday squat. It now follows the unit.

Also: a shared exCount() so "1 exercises" reads "1 exercise", and
durPart() so imported workouts (which carry no clock) stop claiming
"0 min".

i18n: translate plan-sharing strings into all 11 languages

24 new plan-share/PDF strings added to every locale pack (513 keys each),
anchored on each pack's existing terms (routine/exercise/import/week).

Plan sharing: export/import a plan file + printable PDF

New "Share your plan" action in the Plan header (lib/plan-share.js):
- Export plan file: a small JSON with just your routines, the week schedule and any
  custom exercises they use — a friend imports it into their own openGym. Import
  merges (adds routines with fresh ids, dedupes customs by name+body part, optional
  "use this schedule"), so nothing they already have is overwritten.
- Print / Save as PDF: a clean, one-page-per-plan printout rendered in a hidden
  iframe; break-inside:avoid keeps every exercise (and each routine that fits) whole,
  so an exercise never splits across a page.

Icons: full-strength glyphs in the routine icon picker

The pickable routine icons were painted at --label-2 (60%), so the whole picker
looked faded when creating/editing a routine. Bring them to full --label; the
selected cell stays accent-on-accent.

Icons: render at full strength everywhere, drop the muted-grey chrome

Follow-up to the opacity removal: the remaining faded icons were muted by colour,
not opacity. Bring list chevrons (.chev) and row icons (.lrow-c) from --label-3 up
to full --label, and lift the empty-state icon to its caption strength (--label-2).
Semantic colours (accent/orange/yellow/green) are left untouched.

Icons: drop the opacity fade on tab-bar and tile icons

The .3/.32 opacity made those icons look washed-out/see-through. Remove it; the
active/inactive tab distinction still reads via colour (label vs accent) and the
heavier stroke on the active tab.

Icons: redraw abs and pullup so strokes stop crossing through each other

The hollow line icons showed overlapping strokes through their transparency:
- abs drew full-width crease lines through a full-height centre line (a see-through #);
  now a six-pack whose centre seam runs the gap between crease pairs, no crossings.
- pullup's head circle sat on the arm-V apex; lifted it clear so the body no longer
  reads as tangled lines behind a transparent head.

Website: milestones timeline builds itself from published GitHub releases

No more hand-maintained history on the about page — site.js renders one
timeline entry per published release (title, date, first paragraph of
the notes, link). Static entries remain only as an offline fallback.

Website: fix screenshot aspect ratio, embed the live demo, GitHub button in hero

The screenshot img tags carry width/height attributes; with only a CSS
width the height attribute won (240x2532 — stretched). height:auto fixes
it. New #demo section runs the GitHub-Pages demo in a phone frame right
on the page; nav gets a Demo link and the hero a GitHub star button.

Project website + one icon everywhere

website/ holds the source of opengym.duarte-santos.ch — landing with live
GitHub stats, docs and the story behind the app; no build step. The
native app icons are now generated (capacitor-assets) from the same
blocky dumbbell as the PWA icon, traced into resources/icon.svg, so the
APK, home-screen PWA, and website favicon all match.

ZioLadro/wf-vendor-overlay.readme:
# WF Vendor Overlay

🇬🇧 English · [🇮🇹 Italiano](README.it.md)

Shows next to the items of Warframe's vendors the **platinum price** (to the right of the name) and the
**24-hour trade volume** (below the name, centred; red = rarely traded, green = heavily traded), using
warframe.market data and reading the screen with OCR. It only uses screenshots: it never touches the
game's memory or files.

Price label: `12p` = platinum · `–` = nobody selling online · `n/a` = error / data unavailable.
For **mods and arcanes** the label shows two prices: `12p · max 45p` = rank 0 price (what you buy at the
vendor) and **max-rank** price. The volume is the total of the trades of all ranks.

## How it works
- **Starts active**: open a vendor and, when the screen settles, the overlay scans by itself.
- **Saved data** in `prices.json`: the last known values show up at once, then they are refreshed in the
  background. When a vendor opens, data older than 30 s is refreshed.
- **Every 180 seconds** prices and volumes of the vendors shown refresh by themselves.
- **Scrolling** with the mouse wheel: the labels vanish at once and come back ~0.5 s after scrolling stops.
  If the list changes in another way (dragged scrollbar, keyboard, vendor closed) the change is detected
  by comparing the pixels under the names.
- **Leaving the vendor**: the labels disappear as soon as you close the vendor or change page.
- **F7** opens/closes the **price list** · **F8** scan now (and resume if paused) · **F9** pause ·
  **F10** quit. The same actions are in the tray icon menu (click on the icon = price list).
- Warframe must run in **Borderless** windowed mode.

The OCR reads **only the Warframe window**, and only while it is the active window (Windows; setting *Read only the Warframe window*, turn it off if the game is not detected, e.g. cloud gaming). Labels are hidden when you switch to another window.

On the game screen, the **top 10 recommended items** (same ranking as the Recommendations tab, from the saved prices) get a small yellow *★ Recommended ★* tag above their name (settings *Stars on recommended items* / *Recommended items marked*).

Every tab shows a **player strip**: name (click to set it, the game files do not contain it), mastery rank, trades left, and a badge per syndicate with your rank and standing (hover for the daily standing left). Badges are drawn with the syndicate colours; to use the real logos put `<SyndicateTag>.png` files (e.g. `CetusSyndicate.png`) in the `icons` folder of the data folder. Nightwave series are not shown.

**Recognising the vendor screen.** After reading the names, the program checks which vendor's stock they belong to (from `vendors.json` and Baro's list). Labels appear only if at least 3 matched items (setting) and 60 % of everything matched belong to the **same vendor**; names that are not in that vendor's stock are dropped. This keeps labels off inventory, chat or codex pages that merely show some item names, and the overlay says which vendor it recognised. The program also **reads the vendor's name** on screen (only in the top 20 % of the game window, setting *Vendor name zone*; with several names the tallest text wins; a line equal to the vendor's name, e.g. *Cephalon Simaris*, *Red Veil*): when it is there and at least one item is that vendor's, labels are shown even with few items. *Require the vendor name* makes it mandatory (stricter, but vendors whose heading is not their name would never match). F8 writes everything it read to `last_scan.txt` in the data folder, to see why a vendor was or was not recognised. Turn it off with *Recognise the vendor screen*, or lower *Items needed* for vendors with very few tradable items.

## Price list window (F7)
The window **opens by itself when the program starts** (setting *Open the price list at start*). Six tabs. The overlay keeps working while the window is open: the window's own area is blanked before the OCR, so it never reads its own names.

### Price list
All the **tradable items that cost standing** (from `vendors.json`: vendors and syndicates), plus everything
sold by **Baro Ki'Teer**: they are all there from the start, even without data (price `–`, updated `never`).
Items that do not cost standing (and are not Baro's) are not listed. Columns: name, vendors that sell it, **standing cost**, type (Mod / Arcane / Other),
price, max-rank price (mods and arcanes), 24 h volume (coloured like the overlay), last update. Click the
headers to sort; search box and vendor/type filters.

- Standing cost comes from the game data. It is the base cost, without rank discounts. If an item costs
  standing at several vendors you see `min – max`; the tooltip shows vendor, cost and required rank.

SergShtelmakh/piano-tutor.readme:
# Piano Tutor

A gamified piano-learning web app: connect a MIDI keyboard (Web MIDI) and get real-time feedback on whether you play the right notes. Client-side only, no backend. See [specs/mission.md](specs/mission.md).

> Status: free play, a first lesson, and local progress (stars, XP, levels, daily streak) work and are deployed online (roadmap Phases 2–4): MIDI keyboard, computer keyboard, and on-screen piano all make sound, and a 13-lesson first-week curriculum trains note reading, melodies, intervals, and chords on a music staff. More content comes in later phases — see [specs/roadmap.md](specs/roadmap.md).

## Prerequisites

- [Bun](https://bun.sh) (npm also works)
- A Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge) for Web MIDI. Other browsers can still play with the on-screen piano and computer keyboard.

## Getting started

```bash
bun install
bun run dev      # http://localhost:3000
```

## How to play

- **MIDI keyboard:** click **Connect MIDI keyboard** and allow access. Every connected keyboard works, including the sustain pedal. Web MIDI needs Chrome or Edge and a secure page (HTTPS or `localhost`).
- **Computer keyboard:** `A S D F G H J K L ;` are the white keys (C D E F G A B C D E) and `W E T Y U O P` are the black keys. The left `Shift` key (`⇧`) plays the B just below the first C. `Z` / `X` shift the octave down / up. Keys are matched by physical position, so this works on QWERTZ and AZERTY layouts too.
- **On-screen piano:** click or touch the keys. The octave buttons change the shown range (B2–C5 by default: the B below the first C, two octaves, and the top C).
- **Home and lessons:** the app opens on **Home**, with 13 lessons in five units: right hand (treble clef), left hand (bass clef), both clefs, melodies (Mary Had a Little Lamb, Ode to Joy, Twinkle Twinkle), and intervals and chords. Press **Start** on a lesson card; the lesson marked **Next** is the first one you haven't finished, but nothing is locked. The staff shows a row of notes: the highlighted one is the one to play, played ones turn grey. For a chord, play all its notes in any order. A wrong key counts as a mistake and the target stays until you play it right. At the end you get your accuracy, 1–3 stars, and XP. Random lessons give a new order on every start.
- **Progress:** XP raises your level, and finishing at least one lesson per day builds a daily streak. Everything is saved on your device only; **Reset progress** on Home clears it.

## Scripts

| Script                 | What it does                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `bun run dev`          | Dev server on http://localhost:3000        |
| `bun run build`        | Type check + production build into `dist/` |
| `bun run preview`      | Serve the production build locally         |
| `bun run lint`         | TypeScript type check, then ESLint         |
| `bun run format`       | Format all files with Prettier             |
| `bun run format:check` | Fail if any file is not formatted          |
| `bun run test`         | Run unit tests once (Vitest)               |

CI (GitHub Actions) runs `lint`, `format:check`, `build`, and `test` on every pull request and every push to `main`.

## Deployment

The app is a static site, deployed to two hosts so they can be compared (see [specs/phase-03-deployment-device-testing/](specs/phase-03-deployment-device-testing/)). Web MIDI needs HTTPS, which both provide.

| Host                 | URL                                                                                                                                           | How it deploys                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GitHub Pages         | https://sergshtelmakh.github.io/piano-tutor/                                                                                                  | The `deploy-github-pages` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs after CI passes on `main`. No PR previews. |
| Cloudflare (Workers) | https://piano-tutor.sh-serg1993.workers.dev/ (branch preview: https://feature-deployment-device-testing-piano-tutor.sh-serg1993.workers.dev/) | Git integration: pushes to `main` update production; every other branch and PR gets a preview URL.          |

The footer of the app shows the commit and host of the running build.

**GitHub Pages setup (once):** repository Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**. The build uses `BASE_PATH=/piano-tutor/`.

**Cloudflare setup (once):** Workers & Pages → Create → Pages → Connect to Git → this repository, then:

- Production branch: `main`
- Build command: `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run build` (fallback if Bun fails: `npm install && npm run build`)
- Build output directory: `dist`
- Preview command (the branch Previews that Cloudflare creates for every non-production branch): `npx wrangler preview`. A Preview is its own resource, so `npx wrangler versions upload` fails there with "The name in your wrangler.jsonc file must match the name of your Worker". `wrangler preview` is an open beta command and once failed with API error 10013 on the asset upload; a retry fixed it. Check the command on the Preview page of each new branch if it was copied from somewhere else.
- `wrangler.jsonc` in the repo sets the Worker name (`piano-tutor`), the `dist` assets directory and the `previews` block that branch preview builds (`wrangler preview`) require.
- Environment variable `BUN_VERSION`: `1.4.4`
- Leave Web Analytics off (privacy by default).

Cloudflare sets `CF_PAGES*` (Pages) or `WORKERS_CI*` (Workers Builds, which is what the dashboard created: a `workers.dev` URL), which the build reads for the foot

# GemTD Solo

Fristående solospel inspirerat av Dota 2 GemTD. Bygg en labyrint, placera fem
slumpade gems och välj torn att behålla och kombinera. Godot 4.7.2, GDScript
och pixelgrafik; samma projekt för Windows och webb.

**Aktuell utvecklingsversion: 1.4.1-dev · innehållsversion 10.** Kampanjen är
spelbar och automatiskt verifierad. Mänskliga kampanjtester och slutbalansering
återstår; full likhet med Dotas motor är inte uppmätt.

## Dela webbversionen

Spela och dela: [GemTD Solo på GitHub Pages](https://adellestrand.github.io/GemTD/).
Publicering startas manuellt under **Actions → Publish web beta → Run workflow**.
Workflow kör tester och exporterar innan sidan ersätts. Den publika länken väljer
kampanjen direkt. `build.json` visar vilken commit och innehållsversion som körs.
Se [publiceringsflödet](docs/web-beta-and-leaderboard.md).

Gemensam topplista finns under **Run → Leaderboard**. Skicka en avslutad, ny
kampanjomgång med valfritt visningsnamn; ingen e-post behövs. Bästa resultat per
spelare sorteras på avklarade vågor och liv, separat för varje balansversion.
Resultat märks **unverified**. Se [leaderboard: användning och drift](docs/leaderboard.md).

## Innehåll

- 37×37 rutor, sju kontrollpunkter, 50 grundvågor och 50 prövningsvågor.
- Åtta gemtyper med sex kvaliteter, 43 kombinationstorn, 59 receptalternativ och
  24 stentavlor inklusive uppgraderingar.
- Källbaserade torn-/fiendevärden, adaptivt fiendeantal, alternativa fiender och
  bossar, verklig projektilflygtid, skadetyper, försvar, mark/luft och MVP.
- Gift, splash, multiskott, stun, förstening, auror och trapförmågor.
- Manuella gemchansköp med 150 sparad rabatt per besegrad grundboss.
- Fem tornflyttar **per hel omgång** under byggfasen, inklusive byte med sten.
- Receptbok med Locate/Track, vågöversikt, labyrintförslag, målprioritet, paus,
  2× hastighet, zoom, ljud, seeds och återspelbara testrapporter.
- Egna bilder för alla 43 kombinationstorn, animerade fiender och effekter som
  följer verkliga träffar, skadetick och tillstånd.
- Tornpanel med stödpåverkad skada/DPS, separata auravärden och listan
  **AFFECTING THIS TOWER** för MVP, stödkällor och tillfälliga effekter.
- MVP 10 med guldkrona, räckviddsring och markering av berörda torn.

## Starta från källkod

Kräver Windows x64, Python 3.10+ och PowerShell. Kör från repots rot:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/bootstrap.ps1
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/run.ps1 -Campaign
```

Bootstrap hämtar **Godot 4.7.2-stable** och exportmallar från den officiella
releasen med fasta SHA-256-kontroller. Verktygen placeras i `.tools/`.
`-SkipTemplates` hoppar över exportmallarna om du bara vill köra från källkod.
Öppna editorn med `python tools/godot.py --editor --path .`.

## Exportera och spela

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/export.ps1 -Release
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/run.ps1 -Web -Campaign
```

Öppna [kampanjen](http://127.0.0.1:8060/?profile=campaign). Webben använder WebGL 2
och en tråd utan krav på COOP/COEP-headers. Öppna genom webbservern, inte genom
att dubbelklicka på HTML-filen.

Exporterna skapas i `builds/windows/` och `builds/web/`. Behåll `GemTD.pck` bredvid
`GemTD.exe`. Välj kampanj via Run-menyn eller starta Windows-exporten med:

```powershell
builds/windows/GemTD.exe -- --campaign
```

`.tools/`, `builds/` och `output/` följer inte med i Git. En ny klon behöver
bootstrap/import och export enligt ovan. En GitHub-push publicerar inga spelbyggen.

## Spela

1. Under grundvågornas byggfas placerar du fem gems och avslöjar deras typer och
   kvaliteter. Placeringarna är bindande.
2. Behåll en ny gem, uppgradera lika gems, nedgradera en gem eller skapa en
   kombination. Tornvalet startar striden och gör övriga nya gems till sten.
   Traprecept med nya gems ger ett placeringssteg före **Start wave**.
3. Äldre material kan kombineras utan att förbruka rundans tornval. Äldre vanliga
   torn kan även kombineras under strid. Traprecept, trapflytt, tornflytt och
   rivning görs före strid.
4. Prövningarna 51–100 ger inga nya gems eller byggfaser. Nästa våg startar efter
   tre simulerade sekunder; paus fryser nedräkningen. Gemchansköp stängs efter 50.

Mest skadegörande berättigade torn får en MVP-nivå efter varje avklarad grundvåg:
+10% egen skada per nivå. MVP 10 ger dessutom +100% skada till andra torn inom
290/128 rutor. Samlad MVP-bonus har +500%-tak. Maxade torn undantas från nya

dorten9/boomyard.readme:
# BoomYard

A first-person demolition game for phones (iOS and Android, landscape). Each level is a street at sunset full of things to blow up: place a charge, light it, run, and destroy every target before the clock runs out. Unity 6 (URP), built entirely from code, like Overlane. The web build (WebGL) is for testing and demos.

Spec: the artifact **BoomYard Game Spec** (v2.0).

Everything is generated by code, with no external assets: meshes (`MeshKit`), PBR textures (`TextureLib`), materials, explosions, sound and music (`Sfx`). The only files are the two fonts (Rubik and Heebo, OFL).

## What is in it

- **Levels**: a map of 10 levels (`Core/Levels.cs`). Destroy all targets in time; stars by time left. Level 1 is an interactive tutorial.
- **Play**: place an item unlit, walk up and hold LIGHT to light it, then run; or light it in your hand and throw it. Wind, fuse timing, containment ×1.8, chains up to ×6, knockdowns, bonuses.
- **Feel**: layered explosions (flash, HDR fireball, sunlit smoke, dust ring, shockwave, embers, scorch marks, debris), hit-stop, slow motion on chains, camera kick, post-processing punch, vibration.
- **Look**: URP with ACES, bloom, SSAO, colour grading; golden-hour sun and sky, reflections; procedural PBR surfaces and bevelled models.
- **Sound**: synthesised and reverberated firecrackers, explosions (near and far), glass, metal, fire, lighter, fuse, evening ambience, menu music.
- **Menus**: home, level map, shop (explosives, lighters, upgrades), daily missions and a 7-day reward calendar, settings (audio, controls, graphics, accessibility, privacy and terms, reset, credits), pause, results.

## Open in Unity

1. Install **Unity 6000.6.6f1** (the same as Overlane) with Android, iOS and WebGL build support.
2. Clone the repo and **Add project from disk** in Unity Hub.
3. On first open, `Assets/BoomYard/Scenes/Main.unity` and `Assets/BoomYard/Generated` (the URP asset and template materials) are created. Rerun anytime with **BoomYard → Run Project Setup**.
4. Press **Play**. Keyboard and mouse: **WASD** move, **Shift** run, drag to look, **F** (hold) light, **Space** throw (hold for power), **E** place, **1–4** pick an item, **Esc** pause.

## Builds

| Target | How |
|---|---|
| Android | `BoomYard → Build Android`, or `.github/workflows/mobile.yml` (APK, or signed AAB with the upload key in secrets) |
| iOS | `BoomYard → Build iOS (Xcode project)`, then archive in Xcode on a Mac |
| Web | `BoomYard → Build WebGL`; every push to `main` builds and deploys to Vercel (https://boomyard.vercel.app) |

`claude/*` branches run `check.yml`: build, smoke test, and a screenshot timeline pushed to the `screenshots` branch.

Secrets: `UNITY_LICENSE`, `UNITY_EMAIL`, `UNITY_PASSWORD`, `VERCEL_TOKEN`. App id: `com.boomyard.game`.

## Layout

| Folder | What |
|---|---|
| `Scripts/Core` | Pure C# rules: catalog, levels, scoring, chains, fuses, wind, round, shop, missions, daily rewards |
| `Scripts/Game` | Game loop, player and hands, explosives, blasts and fire, destructibles, props and the street, rendering, effects, sound, save |
| `Scripts/UI` | HUD and menus (built from code), touch and keyboard controls |
| `Editor` | Project and pipeline setup, command-line builds |
| `Tools/SimTest` | `run.sh` core tests (Mono); `TexturePreview.cs` renders the procedural textures to PNG |
| `Tools/web` | Privacy policy, terms, Vercel headers |

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017QucE11CwajpMjAs2BD1h2

Re-synthesise the sound effects to sound like recordings

The owner found the car alarm and the other effects robotic. Everything is
still generated in code, but now from physical models: shock waves, noise
shaped by resonant filters, modal synthesis for metal, glass, mallets and
the spray can, randomised debris and drops, distance filtering, and an
outdoor reverb with randomised slapback off the houses.

- Car alarm: a six-tone siren cycling whoop, warble, hi-lo and chirp
  patterns. It is a band-limited pulse wave with pitch wander, run through
  horn speaker resonances and an overdriven amp, then heard from across the
  street. The 6 s loop runs its echoes round the loop, so there is no seam.
- Dog barks: Rosenberg glottal pulses with jitter, shimmer and a rough
  onset, plus breath noise, through moving formants; outdoor echoes; the
  three variants differ.
- Gas whistle: turbulent jet noise ringing a narrow, overdriven resonance
  that rises and wavers.
- Rain: 16k ticks, pats, metal taps and puddle plinks over a soft wash,
  filtered round the loop.
- Sfx: lighter, flame, fuse, firecrackers, explosions, glass, clang,
  debris, fire, tinnitus, thud, UI sounds and stings, spray and rattle.
  Loudness (A-weighted) is kept within about 2.5 dB of the old clips.
- SfxExport also renders spray and rattle and prints generation times.

dicefoxcreations/AnotherWorldbuilder.desc: Worldbuilding and campaign wiki for tabletop RPGs – local, private, shared with your group. In development.
dicefoxcreations/AnotherWorldbuilder.readme:
AnotherWorldbuilder

The wiki for your worlds and campaigns in tabletop role-playing games –
on your computer, with your data, together with your group.

Download · Example world · Run a server · Documentation · Build it yourself

> **In development.** Not meant for real use yet: formats may change, > and older worlds are not carried over when they do.

## What it does - **A wiki for the world:** articles with types and properties you define yourself – character, place, faction, creature, session. Links between them, an infobox, a side bar outline, search. Templates give you a start. - **Maps** to pan and zoom, with pins that lead to the article, regions, and layers that switch to the next map (the tower, its cellar). - **Calendar and timeline** in your world's own calendar – months, weekdays, eras and moons – plus family trees. - **Stat blocks and dice:** rolls you click in the text, a dice tray with log and favourites, 3D dice. Game rules are data of the world – no system is built in: the example world rolls 2d6 + ability, yours rolls what you write. - **Images** in a gallery of the world; metadata such as location and camera is removed. - **Who sees what:** sections for the GM only, for single players or for everyone, with read and write rights apart. Characters can be assigned to players. - **Versions:** everything is saved automatically; earlier versions can be viewed. - **Writing together**, with visible cursors – see below for the ways to meet. | | | | --- | --- | | | | | A character: links, a section only the GM sees, the family tree | A stat block: the rolls in the text go to the dice log | | | | | The timeline, in the world's own calendar and moons | Your worlds, and where each one lives | ## Where your worlds live A world lives where you make it – and only there, until you move it. | Where | What it means | What you need | | --- | --- | --- | | **This device** | A folder on your computer. Works offline, alone or as the host for your group. | Nothing. | | **Another folder** | An external drive, a network drive or a folder your cloud app keeps in step – it counts as local. A shared cloud folder is also how a group can meet without any server: everyone works on the same world folder. | A folder; for a group, a sync app you already use. | | **A server** | Always on, so players can work while the GM's computer is off. It holds no keys and is not the GM. | `aw-server` in Docker – on a NAS, a home server or a rented one. [How to run it](source/docs/server-setup.md) | **Move or copy** is one button at the world (*Options → World → Where it lives*), for the GM only: to another folder, onto a server, back off it – or as a copy, a new world of its own. Bringing a world onto a server shows how far it is and goes on after a restart. **Players** never hold the world itself. They reach it through the GM's device, the shared folder or the server, and keep a local copy only if the GM allows it – of an encrypted world, where each copy opens only that player's part. **Ways to meet**, all without an account: - **At home:** with *Local network* switched on, the app finds the GM's worlds in the same network by itself. - **Over the internet, directly:** the GM's device gets a host code; players enter it. A forwarded port or IPv6 makes it reliable; often it works without. - **Through a shared cloud folder:** devices of a world in such a folder meet there and then connect directly. - **Through a server** of your own, as above.
## Your data - Everything lies in folders on your computer; you choose which ones on first start. - No account and no server of the maker. The group connects directly or through what it runs itself. - Encryption can be chosen per world and costs nothing extra. Unencrypted, a world's folder also holds a readable copy: a text file per article, images as files. ## Try the example world *The Gullwind Coast* is a small, made-up world – a map with places, a family with secrets, a creature with a stat block, events on a timeline and two sessions. Download `Example-world.zip` from the [release](../../releases/latest), unzip it, create a new world in the app and choose *Options → Transfer → Import* → the folder `Example world.awpack`. Change it, take it apart, delete it. ## Download The current version is under **[Releases](../../releases/latest)**: | File | For | | --- | --- | | `AnotherWorldbuilder__amd64.AppImage` | Linux, no installation | | `AnotherWorldbuilder__amd64.deb` | Linux (Debian, Ubuntu), installed | | `AnotherWorldbuilder.exe` | Windows, no installation (needs WebView2) | | `Example-world.zip` | The example world above | | `DnD-5e-template.zip` | Template for D&D 5e: types and outline only, no content | | `aw-server`, `aw-server--docker.tar` | The server for a group | The server is also on Docker Hub: [`dicefoxcreations/anotherworldbuilder-server`](https://hub.docker.com/r/di

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tables in the visual editor; a section's preview finds its part

A table is drawn in the visual editor as it is read — a click in a cell
writes in it, the side bar adds, takes and aligns rows and columns —
instead of standing there as bars and dashes. A row's mark written after
its last bar counts, in its last cell; the parser dropped it as a cell
beyond the head's. A link's preview looks for its part with nothing
folded. An embedded document ends the section of a folded heading above
it, so folding a heading no longer takes the embeds after it along.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A reader who misses a part between two keeps both; players make what their types allow

A part a player cannot open, between two they can, made the two read
back as one — and the parts after it took the keys of those before, so
any change of theirs there was refused as removing a part. Parts of the
same access one after the other stand apart now, and a block's parts

el-ente/daiji.readme:
# Daiji

A fast, games-first home screen for Android TV and Google TV. It shows your
retro games and your TV apps in one place, and launches games in RetroArch or
standalone emulators.

Native Kotlin with Compose for TV. No analytics, so it starts fast and stays
light on 2 GB devices like the Chromecast with Google TV. The network is used
only when you ask for it: **Settings → Set up RetroArch** downloads RetroArch,
its cores, box art and game info from libretro.

## Install

1. Open the latest run under **Actions → Build APK** and download the
   `daiji-apk` artifact. Unzip it to get the APK.
2. Install it over ADB:

   ```sh
   adb connect <tv-ip>
   adb install -r app-release.apk
   ```

3. Give Daiji access to your ROMs. On Google TV the settings screen for this
   is often missing, so use ADB:

   ```sh
   adb shell appops set --uid io.github.elente.daiji MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE allow
   ```

4. Make it the home screen by disabling the Google TV launcher:

   ```sh
   adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
   adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
   ```

   To undo, run the same commands with `pm enable` instead of
   `pm disable-user --user 0`. System updates sometimes re-enable the stock
   launcher, so you may need to repeat this step.

## ROMs

Put each system in its own folder inside a `ROMs` folder:

```
/storage/emulated/0/ROMs/
  snes/Chrono Trigger (USA).sfc
  psx/Crash Bandicoot (USA).chd
  gba/...
```

Daiji finds a `ROMs`, `Roms` or `Games` folder on internal storage, SD cards
and USB drives by itself. You can also browse to any folder with the remote
in Settings → ROMs folder.
Region and dump tags like `(USA)` or `[!]` are hidden from titles. Discs
listed in an `.m3u` playlist are hidden behind the playlist.

Folder names follow the ES-DE and RetroArch conventions: `nes`, `snes`, `n64`,
`gb`, `gbc`, `gba`, `nds`, `gc`, `wii`, `mastersystem`, `genesis` or
`megadrive`, `segacd`, `sega32x`, `gamegear`, `saturn`, `dreamcast`, `psx`,
`ps2`, `psp`, `pcengine`, `atari2600`, `ngp`, `wonderswan`, `neogeo`,
`arcade` and `mame`.

### Artwork

Daiji does not download artwork. It shows covers and screenshots you already
have, matched by file name:

- `ROMs/<system>/media/covers/<game>.png` and `media/screenshots/<game>.png`
- ES-DE's `ES-DE/downloaded_media/<system>/covers` and `screenshots`
- RetroArch's `RetroArch/thumbnails/<Platform>/Named_Boxarts` (covers),
  `Named_Titles` and `Named_Snaps` (screenshots), as downloaded by its
  Playlist Thumbnails Updater. Thumbnails are matched through the game's label
  in the RetroArch playlist, so your ROM files can be named anything. Needs the
  retroarch.com build, whose folder is `/storage/emulated/0/RetroArch`.

Games without artwork get a colored tile with their title.

## Home

Home is the first screen, and Back always returns to it, to the element you left.

- **Header:** greeting, clock and date, and pills for the network (opens Wi-Fi settings) and Daiji's settings.
  The Wi-Fi name needs location access, which a TV never asks for:
  `adb shell pm grant io.github.elente.daiji android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`. Without it the pill says Wi-Fi.
- **Dock:** up to 6 pinned apps; the focused app's name shows above it, over a glow in its banner's colour.
  Until you pin one, the first four TV apps show; the rest are in the Apps rows below.
- **Games:** a row in the dock's style: up to three games played last (▶), your favourites (★) and a random
  pick (🎲), then All games. The line above names the focused game, its system and when it was last played.
  Holding OK on the random pick picks another; on the others it adds or removes the favourite.
- **All games:** every game in a grid. The pills on top (All, ★ Favourites, one per system with more than one
  game) switch on OK. Holding OK on a game adds or removes it from favourites.
- **Apps:** every app not pinned to the dock, smaller, below the games. Other home screens (a previous launcher, the
  Settings app's fallback home) are left out. Holding OK on any app pins it to the dock, unpins
  it, or opens its info page.

Remotes with a Menu key can use it wherever holding OK works.

## Remote buttons

Settings › Remote buttons maps any remote button to an app, a TV input (HDMI, AV) or an action: close all apps
(goes Home, then stops every app in the background), Home, Back, recent apps, mute, sleep or Android settings. A
button can do something else when held. Add one by pressing it; the arrows, OK, Back, Home and volume can't be mapped.

The buttons work from any app through an accessibility service, which Android makes you turn on once:

```sh
adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services io.github.elente.daiji/.remote.RemoteKeyService
adb shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1
```

That replaces the whole list; add other services separated by `:`. Android switches the service off when Daiji is
updated. To let Daiji switch it back on by itself, grant it once:

```sh
adb shell pm grant io.github.elente.daiji android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
```

## Emulators

| Emulator | Systems |
| --- | --- |
| RetroArch | Everything with a libretro core |
| PPSSPP | PSP (default when installed) |
| Dolphin | GameCube, Wii |
| DuckStation | PlayStation |
| NetherSX2 | PlayStation 2 |
| Ask Android | Any system, using Android's app picker |

For each system Daiji uses the first installed emulator, preferring the
standalone one where it is listed as the default. Change it per system in
Settings, or with the button next to **Play**.

RetroArch needs the matching core downloaded in RetroArch's own core
downloader, for example `snes9x` for SNES. The core per system is in
`app/src/main/java/io/github/elente/daiji/data/Systems.kt`.

## Building

CI builds a signed release APK on every push. To build locally you need the
Android SDK and JDK 17:

```sh
./gradlew assembleRelease
```

Release builds are mi

derang-app/derang.readme:
# درنگ

اپ شخصی و آفلاین برای مدیریت کتاب‌ها و بردگیم‌ها؛ وب‌اپ نصب‌شدنی (PWA) با رابط فارسی و راست‌به‌چپ.

## نصب روی گوشی

آدرس اپ: **https://derang-app.github.io/derang/**

1. آدرس اپ را در Chrome اندروید باز کن.
2. از منوی ⋮ گزینهٔ «نصب برنامه» یا «افزودن به صفحهٔ اصلی» را بزن.
3. از این به بعد درنگ مثل یک اپ با آیکن خودش باز می‌شود و بدون اینترنت کار می‌کند.

به‌روزرسانی‌ها خودکارند: هر بار که اپ را باز می‌کنی یا به آن برمی‌گردی (حداکثر یک بار در دقیقه)، نسخهٔ جدید بررسی و در پس‌زمینه دریافت می‌شود و اپ خودش به نسخهٔ تازه بارگذاری می‌شود؛ اگر در حال تایپ باشی، صبر می‌کند تا از کادر بیرون بیایی.

## داده‌ها کجا هستند؟

همهٔ کتاب‌ها، بازی‌ها، یادداشت‌ها و عکس‌ها فقط روی همین گوشی، در حافظهٔ مرورگر، ذخیره می‌شوند. هیچ سرور و حساب کاربری‌ای در کار نیست.
اگر «پاک کردن داده‌های سایت» در Chrome را بزنی یا Chrome را حذف کنی، داده‌ها پاک می‌شوند؛ برای همین **مرتب پشتیبان بگیر**.

## پشتیبان‌گیری و بازیابی

- تنظیمات ← پشتیبان‌گیری و بازیابی ← «ساخت و ذخیرهٔ فایل پشتیبان». یک فایل `.drng` ساخته می‌شود که می‌توانی در Drive، تلگرام یا هر جای دیگر نگه داری.
- فایل شامل همهٔ اطلاعات و عکس‌هاست، اما کلید سرویس هوش مصنوعی و آدرس واسط را ندارد.
- برای بازیابی همان صفحه را باز کن و فایل را انتخاب کن. اول محتوای فایل بررسی و نمایش داده می‌شود و تا خودت تأیید نکنی چیزی جایگزین نمی‌شود. به‌طور پیش‌فرض قبل از بازیابی از داده‌های فعلی هم پشتیبان گرفته می‌شود.

## تنظیم هوش مصنوعی (اختیاری)

1. در [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com) یک کلید API بساز و برایش سقف هزینهٔ ماهانه بگذار.
2. در اپ: تنظیمات ← تنظیم کلید سرویس AI ← کلید را وارد کن و ذخیره بزن.
3. مدل پیش‌فرض `claude-opus-5-5` است و از همان صفحه قابل تغییر است.

کلید رمزنگاری‌شده فقط روی گوشی می‌ماند. عکس‌ها و اطلاعات فقط وقتی فرستاده می‌شوند که خودت شناسایی یا یکی از قابلیت‌های همراه را شروع کنی. ارسال یادداشت‌ها و برداشت‌ها را می‌توانی در تنظیمات خاموش کنی.

قابلیت‌های هوش مصنوعی:
- شناسایی کتاب از عکس جلد یا شناسنامه، و شناسایی بازی اصلی از عکس جعبه؛ پیشنهادها قبل از اعمال فیلد به فیلد قابل بررسی‌اند.
- همراه مطالعه: سؤال برای ثبت برداشت، ایدهٔ خلاقانه، و ارتباط با کتاب‌های دیگر.
- توضیح انتخاب بازی برای جمع، برداشت از آمار، و پیشنهاد برای فهرست علاقه‌مندی.

پاسخ‌های قبلی ذخیره می‌شوند و آفلاین هم قابل مشاهده‌اند.

## اتصال BoardGameGeek (اختیاری)

BGG از سال ۲۰۲۵ برای استفاده از API خود ثبت برنامه و توکن شخصی می‌خواهد:

1. در [boardgamegeek.com/applications](https://boardgamegeek.com/applications) با حساب خودت یک برنامهٔ غیرتجاری (non-commercial) بساز.
2. تأیید BGG ممکن است تا یک هفته طول بکشد. بعد از تأیید، در بخش Tokens یک توکن بساز.
3. در اپ: تنظیمات ← اتصال BoardGameGeek ← توکن را وارد کن و «آزمایش اتصال» را بزن.

بعد از آن، در صفحهٔ بازی (منو یا «مشخصات فنی») گزینهٔ «پیدا کردن این بازی در BGG» را بزن. بازی اصلی را انتخاب کن و تعداد بازیکن مجاز، زمان، پیچیدگی (وزن BGG)، تعداد پیشنهادی جامعه و سبک را فیلد به فیلد تأیید کن. مقدارهایی که خودت دستی وارد کرده‌ای به‌طور پیش‌فرض دست نمی‌خورند. عکس نسخهٔ خودت فقط وقتی عوض می‌شود که گزینهٔ «تصویر باکیفیت جعبه از BGG» را تیک بزنی. توکن مثل کلید هوش مصنوعی رمزنگاری‌شده فقط روی گوشی می‌ماند و درخواست‌ها مستقیم از گوشی به BGG می‌روند.

## جلد باکیفیت

روی جلد کتاب یا بازی بزن (یا از منو «جلد باکیفیت» را انتخاب کن). سه راه هست:

- **اسکن با دوربین:** از جلد نسخهٔ خودت عکس بگیر. هوشواره (اگر تنظیم شده) چهار گوشهٔ جلد را پیدا می‌کند و تو می‌توانی جابه‌جایشان کنی؛ بعد کجی صاف می‌شود و نور و رنگ اصلاح می‌شود. صاف کردن و اصلاح روی خود گوشی انجام می‌شود؛ برای پیدا کردن گوشه‌ها فقط یک نسخهٔ کوچک‌شده از عکس فرستاده می‌شود. بدون هوشواره هم گوشه‌ها را دستی می‌گذاری.
- **لینک طاقچه (کتاب):** برای کتاب‌های دیجیتال، لینک کتاب را از اپ یا سایت طاقچه کپی کن و در همین صفحه بچسبان؛ جلد اصلی ناشر (حدود ۸۰۰×۱۱۷۰ پیکسل) دریافت می‌شود. این تصویر هم مثل تصویر BGG از طریق wsrv.nl دریافت می‌شود.
- **تصویر جعبه از BGG (فقط بازی):** تصویر اصلی جعبهٔ بازی‌ای که به BGG وصل است. تصویر از طریق wsrv.nl (یک سرویس عمومی کش تصویر) دریافت می‌شود، چون BGG اجازهٔ خواندن مستقیم تصویر را به وب‌اپ نمی‌دهد؛ فقط آدرس تصویر به آن فرستاده می‌شود.
- **ChatGPT:** متن درخواست آماده (مشخصات کتاب یا بازی و استاندارد تصویر اپ) کپی و ChatGPT باز می‌شود. تصویر ساخته‌شده را ذخیره کن و از همان صفحه انتخابش کن.

جلد تازه اولین عکس می‌شود و عکس‌های قبلی پاک نمی‌شوند.

## چرا آدرس جداگانه؟

درنگ روی آدرس مخصوص خودش (`derang-app.github.io`) است. اگر دو اپ نصب‌شدنی روی یک آدرس github.io باشند، Chrome اندروید هنگام باز کردن اپ دوم خطای «Could not open app» می‌دهد.

## توسعه

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # سرور توسعه
npm test         # تست‌ها
npm run build    # خروجی نهایی در dist/
```

ساختار: `src/db` (مدل داده و Dexie)، `src/lib` (منطق انتخاب بازی، پشتیبان، تاریخ شمسی، جست‌وجوی فارسی)، `src/ai` (لایهٔ قابل‌تعویض هوش مصنوعی)، `src/screens` و `src/ui` (رابط).
مرجع طراحی: بستهٔ UX Pilot، نسخه‌های انتهایی هر صفحه.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let go of the database while the app is in the background

Android freezes a copy of the app soon after it leaves the screen. A copy
frozen in the middle of a database read keeps its lock, so saves in the
visible copy wait forever and every page that reads books waits behind
them; only Settings (a separate table) still opened. Dexie re-reads in
every copy whenever any copy saves, so a background copy (a share from
Taaghche, the app also open in a Chrome tab) is reading exactly when the
visible one writes. Reproduced with two copies, one frozen mid-read.

A hidden copy now closes its connection (via Dexie's own back/forward
cache path, with auto-open off so nothing reopens it) and reconnects and
re-reads everything when it is back on screen; nothing remounts, so a
half-filled form survives. Shares and launches also reuse the open window
(launch_handler navigate-existing) instead of starting a second copy.

Accept shared images so Derang shows up when sharing from Taaghche

Taaghche shares its share image together with the link text, and Android
only offers targets that accept every shared type, so the GET text-only
target never appeared. The share target is now a multipart POST that also
takes images: the service worker keeps the image and opens the add screen.

Repair page: check each database table for a stuck lock

Reads every IndexedDB table in its own read-only transaction with a
timeout, plus storage usage and a tiny settings write, so a phone where
only Settings opens can show which tables no longer answer. Never creates
the database if it is missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Recover from a dead database connection instead of hanging

On Android the IndexedDB connection can die while the app is in the
background; saves then never finish and pages wait on their data forever.
Saves now time out with a clear message and reconnect, the AI results
buttons get a busy state and visible errors, a loading screen that stays
stuck checks the connection and reloads into a fresh one, and a page that
throws shows a recovery card instead of a blank screen.

Keep the web manifest out of the offline cache

Chrome reads the manifest through the service worker when installing and
updating the installed app. A precached old copy hid the new share

rmstdope/audio-studio.desc: Audio tool for narratives and music used in games
rmstdope/audio-studio.readme:
# audio-studio

Audio tool for narratives and music used in games. Run it from inside a game repository: it reads
the repository's `audio-studio.json`, and writes voice files and their metadata in place. Committing
them is up to you.

See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the design.

## Status

Steps 1 to 5 of the delivery plan (`docs/architecture.md` §12): the studio validates the project,
shows each part's characters and the state of every line's clip, adopts clips recorded before it,
and casts voices by audition: it searches Fish Audio's library by keywords, records each candidate
saying the audition phrase in the character's style, and runs keep/drop rounds until one voice is
left, which it writes to the cast. It records narration: line by line, or a whole part (or one
character) as a job with a plan, progress and Cancel, removing orphaned clips when asked (step 4).
Each take is checked with Whisper, and recorded again (up to three times) until enough of its
words are heard; the manifest gets real word timings. A line never heard well enough shows as
weak: retake it from its row, or from Generate when asked. Clips recorded before the studio (or
unchecked) can be measured with Whisper without new audio. A character's style is edited on its
audition page, a line's own cue by clicking it in the lines table, and the pronunciation table on
All characters (steps 6.1 and 6.2). **Changes** lists what git sees of the studio's files, so
you know what to commit (step 6.3); the studio itself never commits. **Refresh dialog** runs the
project's `refreshDialog` command for a part and shows what changed; cues left without a line are
listed on the part's overview, to give to the reworded line or remove (step 6.4).

Recording needs [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) to encode clips (`brew install ffmpeg`; with
`"output": { "lufs": -16 }` each clip is also levelled to that loudness, as RetroQuest's `level.py`
does), and checking
takes needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) on Apple silicon (mlx-whisper; the first take loads
the model). Without them, set `"quality": { "transcriber": "none" }` in the project file.

Audition takes and sessions are kept in `.audio-studio/` in the game repository; add it to that
repository's `.gitignore`.

## Install

Needs [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4 or later.

```sh
bun install
bun link          # puts `audio-studio` in ~/.bun/bin
```

`~/.bun/bin` must be on your `PATH`. Bun's own installer adds it; a Homebrew-installed Bun does
not, so add it to `~/.zshrc` yourself:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
```

There is no need to run `bun link audio-studio` in the game repository: the studio is not a
dependency of the game.

## Use

```sh
cd ~/repos/retroquest   # any repository with an audio-studio.json
audio-studio            # opens the studio in your browser
```

Options: `--project <file>` to use a specific project file, `--port <n>`, `--no-open`, `--help`.

## Develop

`audio-studio --dev` reloads on every change to the studio's own code: server changes are picked
up in place (same port, no restart) and UI changes are pushed to the open page. Use it in a game
repository while working on the studio.

```sh
bun run dev          # the studio on test/fixtures/sample, with reloading
bun test
bun run typecheck
bun run format       # prettier
bun run check        # format:check, typecheck and tests, as CI runs them
```
