WolfLikesKKS/KKS-Studio-Chara-Filter.readme:
# Studio Chara Filter

by **WolfLikesKKS**

| Game | Repository | Download |
|---|---|---|
| Koikatsu Sunshine | [KKS-Studio-Chara-Filter](https://github.com/WolfLikesKKS/KKS-Studio-Chara-Filter) | [Releases](https://github.com/WolfLikesKKS/KKS-Studio-Chara-Filter/releases) |
| Koikatsu / Koikatsu Party | [KK-Studio-Chara-Filter](https://github.com/WolfLikesKKS/KK-Studio-Chara-Filter) | [Releases](https://github.com/WolfLikesKKS/KK-Studio-Chara-Filter/releases) |

Both are built from the same source code; install the one that matches your game.

I've been using CharaStudio for a few years now and somehow it never occurred to me that a character filtering mod might be useful.

Studio Chara Filter turns CharaStudio's character list from a long list of names into something you can actually search.
Filter thousands of cards by body sliders, outfits (towel, swimwear, nothing on…), zipmod content and missing mods,
author, folder and name. It works from a background index, so no cards need to be loaded. It also makes CharaStudio
itself faster: a 933-card folder that took 3.8 seconds to open now opens in 13 ms, and hovering over names no longer
stutters. For collections with missing mods, it lists exactly which zipmods are missing, how many cards need each one,
and where to get them.

I hope this is useful to the community - it's my thanks for all the character cards and scenes over the years.

## What it's like to use

1. **Install** (see [Installation](#installation)) and open CharaStudio, then **Add > Female** (or Male).
   The filter window opens next to the character list.
2. **The first time**, the plugin reads your card folders in the background and shows its progress in the window.
   You can keep working meanwhile. A large collection takes a few minutes once; after that, the index is loaded from
   cache in under a second and only new or changed cards are read.
3. **Pick where to look** at the top: the folder the list is showing, a few folders you tick, or all folders.
4. **Open the sections you need and narrow down.** Every filter you set applies together with the others, and the
   result count updates right away. The character list shows only the matching cards; click one to add it as usual.
5. **Clear** resets everything; each section also has its own Clear.

Some things people use it for:

- *"Tall characters with a bath towel outfit"*: Body > Height range, Clothing > Bath towel: has one.
- *"Which of my cards will load with missing hair?"*: Content mods > Hair: Missing.
- *"What do I need to download?"*: Missing mods report - every missing zipmod, how many cards need it, and links.
- *"Cards by one author"* or *"cards I added this week"*: Card authors, Card file > Added.
- *"Find my duplicate saves"*: Card file > Find duplicates.

Tips:

- **Ranges**: type several in one box, e.g. `1-10, 35-40, 90`, to match any of them.
- The little **graph above each slider** shows where your cards are - handy for finding outliers.
- Filters are additive, so a result of 0 usually means one section is too strict; the counts per section help find it.
- **Arrange** lets you reorder the sections; F1 decides which body/face sliders appear (with three saveable presets).
- Nothing on your cards is changed. Card removal is off unless you enable it, and even then cards are moved, not deleted.

There are two builds from the same source: `KKS_StudioCharaFilter.dll` for Koikatsu Sunshine and
`KK_StudioCharaFilter.dll` for Koikatsu / Koikatsu Party.

## Features

### Where to look
- **Current folder**: filters whatever the list is showing (works with Browser Folders).
- **Choose folders**: tick one or more folders in a folder tree (with card counts, optional subfolders, search).
- **All folders**: every card in your collection, regardless of folder.
- **Name search**: character name or file name; several words must all match. Works in every scope.
- Large results are split into pages, with a **Show all** option.
- Counts and distribution graphs in the window follow the current scope (the missing mods report always covers all folders).

### Random filters

- **Random filters** (next to *Reset all*) clears the filters and sets a random few: ranges on 2-5 random sliders and
  sometimes a hair or eye color, picked from your own cards. Press again for another mix.
- **Random** on a slider gives it a random range; **+ random range** adds another one that doesn't overlap the ranges it
  already has (it's picked in a gap between them, so it always adds cards that weren't shown before).

Ranges always come from the cards (a random card's value, widened to hold a good share of what still matches), so a random
filter never lands on an empty stretch. How narrow it gets follows the size of the collection: about 3 x the square root of
the cards in scope remain (100 cards -> ~30, 1,000 -> ~95, 5,000 -> ~210, at most 300).

### Random characters (Studio)

A **Random** row under the match count picks characters at random from the cards that match your filter in the current
scope (all pages, for the open female or male list):

- **Add** - adds that many random characters to the scene.
- **Replace selected** - replaces the characters selected in the Workspace with random ones.
- **Replace all** - replaces every character of that sex in the scene (click twice).
- **No repeats** - each card is used once until all matching cards have been used.

Replacing uses Studio's own "Change character", so each character keeps its place, pose and animation. Example: select five
copies of a default character, filter (or pick a folder) down to your own 26 cards, press *Replace selected*. Turn the row
off in F1 > Display > Show random character buttons.

**Undo, one character at a time:** every replacement made in the session - by these buttons or by Studio's own *Change
character* - is listed under the row (*Replaced characters*), newest first, each with an **Undo** button that changes that

# KlarKunde Akquise

Baue ein "Cold Call Tool" (Lead-Management & Kaltakquise) komplett neu, auf Deutsch, mit modernem, klarem Design (hell/dunkel), mobil nutzbar. Login per E-Mail/Passwort (Supabase Auth), mehrere Caller-Accounts mit Rollen (Admin/Caller).

Funktionen (gleicher Umfang wie die bisherige App, aber sauberer):
1. Leads: CSV/Excel-Upload mit Spaltenzuordnung und Import-Bestätigung ("Lead Batches"), Liste offener Leads, Suche/Filter, Lead-Detailansicht mit Notizen, Lead löschen/verschieben/wieder öffnen, "Alle offenen Leads löschen".
2. Anruf-Ablauf: nächster offener Lead, Gesprächsleitfaden/Script mit Platzhaltern, Ergebnis-Buttons: Nicht erreicht, Kein Interesse, Callback (Datum/Uhrzeit), Termin buchen, Deal in Produktion. Statuswechsel werden protokolliert (StatusChange-Historie).
3. Callbacks: Liste fälliger Rückrufe, "heute fällig" hervorgehoben.
4. Termine: Termin buchen, eigenen Termin eintragen, Filter "Nur meine Termine", Kalender-/Listenansicht.
5. Meine Kunden und Erledigte Leads (Completed).
6. Angebote: Kunden, Produktkatalog (Produkte anlegen/bearbeiten), Angebot erstellen (Angebotsnummer, Positionen, Hinweis im Angebot), Angebotsliste, Angebotsdetail, Einstellungen/Vorlagen.
7. Statistiken: Tagesstatistik, Meine Statistiken, Auswertung (Leads pro Wochentag, Anrufe, Termine, Quoten) mit Charts.
8. Pipedrive-Sync: Leads/Deals bei Termin bzw. Produktion nach Pipedrive übertragen (API-Token in den Einstellungen), Fehler "Pipedrive Sync fehlgeschlagen" sichtbar mit Retry.
9. Einstellungen und Account-Verwaltung für Admins.

Neu: Bei jedem Lead und jeder Aufgabe zeigt die App einen kurzen, hilfreichen Vorschlag für den nächsten Schritt (z.B. "3x nicht erreicht: andere Uhrzeit probieren", "Callback überfällig") sowie einen Fortschrittsbalken pro Lead-Batch. Beginne mit Auth, Datenbank-Schema, Lead-Import und dem Anruf-Ablauf; die übrigen Bereiche danach Schritt für Schritt.

This project was built with [Lovable](https://lovable.dev).

## Development

Prefer working locally? You need Node.js and npm — [install with nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm#installing-and-updating).

```sh
git clone <this-repository-url>
cd <repository-name>

```

## Lovable-Cloud-Backend

Die vollständige Backend-Bereitstellung und Verbindung ist in
[LOVABLE-BACKEND-SETUP.md](docs/LOVABLE-BACKEND-SETUP.md) beschrieben.
Die vorhandene Lovable Cloud bleibt zuständig; kein zusätzliches Projekt anlegen.
Die neue Anbindung ist bis zur Bereitstellung über `VITE_ATOMIC_BACKEND_ENABLED`
ausgeschaltet. Die RPC-Verträge stehen in
[person-a-backend-handoff.md](docs/person-a-backend-handoff.md).

```sh
npm test

npm run types:backend:check

`npm run test:backend` führt PostgreSQL-WASM-Tests ohne Cloudzugang aus.

`BACKEND_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/postgres npm run test:backend:concurrency`
ausführen. Der Test lehnt nicht lokale Hosts und vorhandene Geschäftstabellen ab.

hoanglt1223/anygba.readme:
# AnyGBA

AnyGBA is a static recompiler that turns a Game Boy Advance ROM into a native Windows, Linux, or macOS
executable. The ROM's ARM/Thumb code is translated to C ahead of time and linked against `libanygba`, a
high-level runtime that provides the BIOS, video, audio, and I/O. There is no emulator loop; an
interpreter exists only as a fallback for code the recompiler missed.

## Why this exists

I grew up with the Game Boy Advance. In primary school, the games I couldn't afford I played on a family
PC through VisualBoyAdvance: Pokémon, a cheat code scribbled in a notebook, a save state before every hard
fight. Those evenings are a big part of why I write software today.

AnyGBA is my way of giving something back to that childhood. I want to bring those games back to life,
make them run better than they ever did on that old PC (native code, sharp at 4K, instant saves), make up
for what that kid couldn't have, and carry the feeling forward for the next person who opens their old
cartridges. VBA kept these games alive for a generation; this project hopes to carry them a little further.

> *Mình làm AnyGBA vì tuổi thơ, vì tình yêu với GBA và VBA từ những ngày tiểu học: để hồi sinh, cải thiện,
> bù đắp và tiếp nối tuổi thơ ấy.*

Status: every plan phase is implemented and tested on Windows, including one commercial title from the
user's own cartridge dump (Pokemon Emerald reaches gameplay and saves); Linux/macOS CI is still to come.
Compatibility: [compat/](compat/) (page: `python tools/compat-site/generate.py`).

What works:

- Decoder, function discovery, C code generator, and runtime core (bus, scheduler, interrupts, DMA,
  timers, fallback interpreter). jsmolka's arm, thumb, memory and bios tests pass as recompiled native code.
- HLE BIOS: every GBA SWI from 0x00 to 0x2A. Math, memory copy, decompression and affine functions are
  native; Div, Sqrt and ArcTan/ArcTan2 match mGBA's HLE BIOS bit for bit on 640 inputs, and the
  decompressors reproduce data packed by grit. Unknown SWI numbers stop the game with an error.
- PPU: scanline renderer for all six video modes, 128 regular and affine sprites, windows (including
  the OBJ window), alpha blending, brightness, mosaic, and green swap. 48 test pictures from the tonc
  demos, jsmolka's PPU tests and Varooom 3D match mGBA pixel for pixel, including an HBlank DMA raster
  effect; the only accepted differences are documented rounding differences in the reference itself.
- APU: the four PSG channels (sweep, envelopes, length, wave banks, 7/15-bit noise) and both
  DirectSound FIFOs fed by DMA, mixed per GBATEK at 32768 Hz. Self-authored test tones correlate with
  mGBA's output above 0.99 (noise 0.98, a panned mix 0.988); tonc's snd1_demo and a Varooom 3D sound
  effect match as well. Generated games print a count of DirectSound FIFO underruns on exit.
- Saves: SRAM, Flash 64/128 KB and EEPROM 512 B/8 KB, detected from the ROM or set per game, written to
  the per-user data folder with a backup of the previous file. jsmolka's save tests pass and keep their
  save across restarts.
- 41 open-source titles (34 tonc demos, Varooom 3D, ARMWrestler, jsmolka's PPU/NES/unsafe tests) run
  60 s as recompiled code without errors, well above full speed, with the same final picture as the
  interpreter (except tonc `txt_se2`, which prints its own timing measurements); their frame hashes
  are CI checkpoints.
- `anygba build game.gba`: one command from ROM to a program with the ROM embedded
  ([docs/user/USAGE.md](docs/user/USAGE.md)). Controls come from `anygba-input.ini`
  ([docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md](docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md)).
- VisualBoyAdvance-style player features in every generated game:
  - Save states in nine slots (Shift+F1-F9 save, F1-F9 load). A state saved and loaded later, in the
    same run or a new one, continues with the same frames, even though the game is native code
    ([docs/dev/SAVE-STATES.md](docs/dev/SAVE-STATES.md)).
  - Speed 100/200/300/400% with the sound resampled instead of broken up, plus a hold-to-fast-forward key.
  - Cheats: GameShark v1/v2, Action Replay v3 (GameShark SP), CodeBreaker and raw codes, encrypted
    forms included, with conditions, button codes and ROM patches. They come from an in-game menu with
    categories and value pickers, typed codes, a per-game cheat file, or the command line
    ([docs/user/CHEATS.md](docs/user/CHEATS.md)). A curated Pokemon Emerald database ships with AnyGBA;
    `tools/cheats/import-libretro.py` converts the libretro community lists for about 490 more games.
  - An in-game menu (Escape or Back+Start) for states, speed, cheats and rebinding keys and gamepad
    buttons; on-screen messages; gamepad hot-plug with SDL's controller database and the left stick.
- AI agents can play and debug a running game through `anygba-mcp`, an MCP server shipped in the package
  ([docs/user/AI-CONTROL.md](docs/user/AI-CONTROL.md)): screenshots, frame-accurate input, pause and step,
  save states, cheats, memory, named game variables (a Pokemon Emerald symbols file ships), breakpoints at
  function entries and memory watches. A play journal records every agent command, your own actions,
  snapshots and thumbnails so later sessions can learn from earlier ones. Both are off by default, can be
  switched on and off while playing (menu Settings, F10, F11), listen on 127.0.0.1 with a per-user token,
  and give way as soon as you press a button.

What does not work yet:

- Audio and windows: never run on a real sound device or window on the development PC (headless
  only), so windowed playback, real keyboard/gamepad input, audio-led pacing at every speed and the
  drawn menu are untested; the same code paths run headless with scripted input in the tests.
- The real-time clock some cartridges have (Pokemon Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald) is not emulated: those
  games report a dry battery and skip time-based events.
- EEPROM is checked by unit tests only; no open-source test ROM in the corpus uses it.

feat(difftest): shapes plant random bytes at fixed addresses

Functions that branch on globals (a glyph's width and height in the
font buffer) only saw the base state's values, so random states left
most of their blocks uncovered. A shape's memory list plants random
bytes at fixed writable addresses for each state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(recomp): resolve agbcc's switch with the table behind a bls

agbcc compiles a switch as `cmp rI, #n ; bls table ; b default`, with
the table load at the branch target. Each path started from an empty
state, so the case bound was lost and the jump went through the
dispatcher. Taken unsigned lower-or-same/lower branches now carry the
case bounds. Emerald's frames, EWRAM and VRAM over a 9,000-frame run are
unchanged; its text printer state machine becomes one function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(build): no C++ module scanning for games with C++ overrides

CMake 3.28 scans C++20 sources for modules, which needs clang-scan-deps;
Linux clang packages often lack it, so games with C++ override modules
failed to build. Generated games use no modules.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(difftest): report game errors as errors, not as a failed difftest

The game exits with 1 both for a failed difftest and for errors such as
a wrong ROM or an unknown function. The anygba difftest front end now
always has the game write its JSON report and accepts a verdict only
when the report's status matches the exit code; anything else is exit 2.
The decomp loop checks the status the same way.

did not decode) was generated with no body and returned without moving
the PC, so the game called it forever. Such discovered entries now stay
with the interpreter; entry points named by the config inside a skip
range are a config error.

feat(video): HD PPU path with internal scale, replacement art packs and dumps

The HD renderer redraws each captured frame at N x N sub-pixels: layers at 1x
exactly as the scanline PPU, replacement art sampled per sub-pixel, affine
layers and sprites at sub-pixel precision, then windows and colour effects per
sub-pixel. Sub-pixel (0, 0) reproduces the 1x PPU. VRAM is copied per line only
when the game wrote it, so mid-frame changes are kept.

Packs are folders of PNGs named by content key (tile, palette-independent tile,
whole sprite, bitmap frame) at 1x-16x, loaded lazily, resampled to the internal
scale and hot-reloaded. Dump mode writes each new piece of art with a JSON index.

feat(cheats): pointer and key-XOR raw codes, a Pokemon Emerald database and a libretro importer

Raw codes may write through a pointer ([03005D8C]+0490:VALUE) and XOR the value with memory (VALUE^[03005D90]+00AC), which games that move and encrypt their save data need. cheats/BPEE.toml lists Emerald money, coins, Poke Balls, items, PC items and level items with pickers, each checked on the ROM by reading memory. anygba build copies the databases for the ROM next to the game; games load <code>.toml, <crc32>.toml and numbered variants from cheats/ folders, skipping entries that do not decode. tools/cheats/import-libretro.py converts libretro-database cheat lists (CC BY-SA 4.0, fetched, not shipped). --dump frame:FILE writes the last picture.

fix(recomp): remove function shards left from an earlier run with more of them

The generated CMakeLists globs *.c, so a stale funcs_NNN.c was compiled into the game and duplicated its functions.

fix(recomp): leave through r[15] when a branch target was never decoded

A label for code the walk could not read (RAM code outside the known region) produced a goto to a label that was never emitted, and the generated C did not compile. Seen with Pokemon Emerald after a feedback pass.

feat(player): save state slots, speed control, cheat menu and on-screen display

Generated games get VisualBoyAdvance-style controls: nine state slots next to the save file, 100-400% speed with resampled sound plus an unthrottled hold, cheats from cheat databases, a per-game cheat file and the command line, and an in-game menu with a cheat tree, value pickers, typed codes and a Controls page. Headless runs take scripted input (--script, --keys), print the menu and messages, and can dump memory, which the new player tests use.

feat(input): player hotkeys, gamepad chords and in-place rebinding

anygba-input.ini gains SaveState1-9, LoadState1-9, SpeedUp, SpeedDown, Menu, FastForward and CheatButton for both keyboard (with Ctrl/Alt/Shift chords) and gamepad (button chords such as Back+Start), a [player] section (Speed, StickDeadzone), and rebind() with conflict swapping. The left stick drives the d-pad. The platform input reports key presses and gamepad arrivals by name and can load gamecontrollerdb.txt mappings.

feat(runtime): cheat code engine for GameShark, Action Replay, CodeBreaker and raw codes

Codes are decrypted (GameShark v1/v2 and Action Replay v3 TEA, CodeBreaker's bit shuffle, as GBATEK describes them) and decoded into one instruction list run once per frame: writes, fills, slides, pointers, arithmetic, conditions and button codes. ROM patches go into the ROM image; the recompiler now records each function's ROM footprint and emits an AG_ENTER check, so functions whose code a patch covers run in the interpreter.

feat(runtime): save states taken at resumable safe points

A snapshot is taken at the end of a scheduler tick outside interrupt handlers, or inside a BIOS halt (resumed by running the SWI again). Saving and loading both restart dispatch at r[15], so the run that saved and the run that loaded follow the same path. Files carry a format version, the ROM's SHA-256 and a CRC-32; a failed load leaves the machine unchanged.

fix(runtime): set instruction fetch costs at reset

Until a game wrote WAITCNT, every fetch cost zero cycles, so games that never write it ran their code for free. Three tonc checkpoints change; prio_demo and swi_vsync still match the interpreter.

hoanglt1223/anyswf.desc: Compile Flash (AS1/AS2) games ahead of time into native PSP homebrew and PC/Android apps.
hoanglt1223/anyswf.readme:
# AnySWF

Ahead-of-time compiler that turns Flash (AS1/AS2) SWF movies into native PSP
homebrew (`EBOOT.PBP`), and into native Windows, Linux, macOS and Android games.
ActionScript bytecode is compiled to C and vector art is tessellated at build time,
so the PSP only runs native code and draws triangles.

```sh
anyswf build game.swf --target psp|linux|windows|macos|android -o out/game
```

See [docs/user/EXPORT.md](docs/user/EXPORT.md) for building and
[docs/user/USAGE.md](docs/user/USAGE.md) for controls, per-game settings, saves and the
supported ActionScript. Compatibility: `compat/*.toml`, rendered
by `tools/compat-site/generate.py`; how to test a game and report it:
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Status: early. The platform layer, the asset pipeline (`swf2c assets`), the renderer
(display list, timeline, colour transforms, masks, add/multiply/screen blend modes),
the AVM1 compiler (`swf2c compile`) and the runtime built-ins games use (MovieClip
methods and events, the drawing API, buttons, Key, Mouse, Sound, SharedObject,
TextField, Date, timers) work on PC and under PPSSPP; nothing has been checked on PSP
hardware yet. No game content ships with this project: bring your own files. The only
SWFs in the repository are Ruffle's MIT/Apache test movies in `tests/ruffle/`,
`tests/ruffle-avm1/` and `tests/ruffle-avm1-builtins/`.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `swf2c/` | Rust workspace for the SWF-to-C compiler and asset converter (`swf2c`) and the `anyswf build` front end (`src/anyswf/`) |
| `runtime/` | C11 runtime (libswfrt): assets.bin loader, display list, timeline, renderer, AVM1 VM, built-ins, sound mixer, profiler |
| `apps/player/` | `anyswf-player`: plays an assets.bin; headless PNG screenshots for tests |
| `docs/dev/assets-bin-format.md` | The assets.bin file format |
| `docs/user/USAGE.md` | Controls, `anyswf.toml`, saves, sound, supported ActionScript, profiler |
| `platform/platform.h` | Small platform API: frame pacing, input, audio, files, clock |
| `platform/psp/`, `platform/sdl/` | PSP (pspsdk/GU) and PC (SDL3/OpenGL 2.1, OpenGL ES 1.1 on Android) backends |
| `platform/android/` | APK template (manifest, `GameActivity`, resources) for `anyswf build --target android` |
| `compat/`, `tools/compat-site/` | Compatibility records and the page generator |
| `apps/hello/` | Hello triangle + tone, the smoke test for both backends |
| `tests/platform/` | Platform unit tests (PC) |
| `tests/swf-src/` | Self-authored AS2 tests (`*.as`) with expected trace output and optional `*.toml` (frames, scripted input, runs); `make-base-swfs.py` writes the self-made movies some compile into |
| `tests/runtime/` | Runtime unit tests (loader validation, timeline, config, mixer, drawing tessellation, texture cache) |
| `tests/render/` | Render tests: cases, Ruffle reference PNGs, comparison scripts |
| `tests/ruffle/` | Render test SWFs copied from Ruffle (MIT/Apache-2.0) |
| `tests/ruffle-avm1/` | AVM1 test SWFs and Flash Player traces copied from Ruffle (MIT/Apache-2.0) |
| `tests/ruffle-avm1-builtins/` | Ruffle AVM1 tests of the built-ins, run as a separate suite with its own floor |
| `tests/avm1/` | AVM1 conformance runner (compile, build, run headless, diff traces) |
| `tests/psp/` | The AS2 corpus as EBOOTs under PPSSPPHeadless (trace diff) |
| `cmake/psp.cmake` | PSP toolchain file (wraps pspdev's) |
| `docker/psp-build.Dockerfile` | Pinned `pspdev/pspdev` build image |

The platform layer is application-neutral and is shared with the other PSP
ports in this workspace; keep Flash-specific code out of `platform/`.

## Build

PC (SDL3 3.4.18 is downloaded and built by CMake, pinned by hash):

```sh
cmake -S . -B out/msvc -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64      # Windows
cmake --build out/msvc --config Release
ctest --test-dir out/msvc -C Release --output-on-failure
out/msvc/apps/hello/Release/hello.exe --smoke                  # hidden window, silent audio, self-checking

cmake -S . -B out/linux -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release     # Linux
cmake --build out/linux && out/linux/apps/hello/hello
```

`hello` flags: `--frames N` exits after N frames, `--headless` hides the window
and uses SDL's dummy audio driver, `--smoke` is headless and checks pixels,
audio progress and the save-file round trip (exit code 1 on failure).

PSP (needs Docker; works from Windows through Git Bash):

```sh
scripts/psp-build.sh                                  # -> out/psp/apps/{hello,player}/EBOOT.PBP
PSP_CMAKE_ARGS=-DBUILD_PRX=ON scripts/psp-build.sh    # PRX for psplink
```

Copy `EBOOT.PBP` to `ms0:/PSP/GAME/ANYSWFHELLO/`. Saves go to
`ms0:/PSP/SAVEDATA/<APP_ID>/`.

Compiler and asset converter:

```sh
cd swf2c && cargo build --release && cargo test
swf2c inspect game.swf                      # header and character table
swf2c assets game.swf -o assets.bin         # meshes, textures, sounds, timelines
             [--target psp|pc|android]      # screen and detail settings (default psp)
anyswf-player assets.bin                    # PC playback (windowed)
anyswf-player assets.bin --screenshot f.png # headless, frame 1 as PNG
```

Player options for tests (`anyswf-player` and exported games): `--headless` runs
deterministically (one SWF frame per display frame, frame-based clock, sound mixed on
the game thread), `--input F:BUTTONS[@X/Y],...` scripts buttons and the cursor,
`--save-dir DIR` keeps saves out of the user folder, `--wav out.wav` writes the mixed
sound, `--config anyswf.toml` overrides the settings file, `--profile` logs the profiler
once per second.

Render tests (generated SWFs, Ruffle test movies and scripted AS2 movies from
`tests/render/as`, compared with references rendered by Ruffle; see
`tests/render/make-render-refs.py` for how they are made; needs MTASC):

```sh
tests/render/run.sh out/msvc/apps/player/Release/anyswf-player.exe
```

Test corpus (MTASC 1.14, fetched with a pinned checksum into `tools/`):

```sh
tests/fetch-mtasc.sh
tests/build-corpus.sh            # -> o

hoanglt1223/rpy2psp.desc: Convert Ren'Py visual novels into native PSP homebrew.
hoanglt1223/rpy2psp.readme:
# rpy2psp

Convert Ren'Py visual novels into native PSP homebrew. Scripts are compiled on PC into a compact bytecode, images become GPU-ready textures, and a small native engine plays them on a PSP with custom firmware. No Python runs on the PSP.

## Status

The script compiler, the asset pipeline, and the engine (vnpsp) work. The three target games play start to finish in the PC engine, headless, with saves, rollback and Japanese text. The PSP build runs in PPSSPP with screenshots matching the PC engine, saves in `ms0:/PSP/SAVEDATA/`, and gapless music. `rpy2psp build` makes a folder ready to copy to the PSP. Testing on a real PSP-3000 is still to come. Per-game results: [compat/](compat/).

- Scope: dialogue-driven visual novels (labels, menus, jumps, images, transitions, music, simple variables). Games that rely on custom Python code or Python-driven screens are reported as unsupported, with file and line. Details: [docs/dev/census.md](docs/dev/census.md).
- Coverage: the three target games (The Question, Zero Echoes, Arcance) compile fully. Overall, 5 of the 15 games in the census corpus compile.
- Formats: [docs/dev/bytecode.md](docs/dev/bytecode.md) (script) and [docs/dev/pack-format.md](docs/dev/pack-format.md) (DXT textures, glyph atlases, MP3, PCM and ADPCM). Prior art: [docs/dev/prior-art.md](docs/dev/prior-art.md).
- Engine: [docs/dev/engine.md](docs/dev/engine.md) (building, controls, saves, rendering, what is verified).

Roadmap: [anyport plans](https://github.com/hoanglt1223/anyport/tree/main/plans/261023-1558-renpy-to-psp).

## Usage

User guide: [docs/user/USAGE.md](docs/user/USAGE.md). Supported Ren'Py features: [docs/user/SUPPORTED-FEATURES.md](docs/user/SUPPORTED-FEATURES.md).

Python 3.11 or later.

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m rpy2psp build path/to/game -o out/MyNovel --font-dir <Ren'Py SDK>/renpy/common   # EBOOT.PBP + script.vnb + data.pak for ms0:/PSP/GAME/
python -m rpy2psp compile path/to/game -o out/            # script.vnb + manifest.json, or errors with file:line
python -m rpy2psp compile path/to/game -o out/ --language japanese
python -m rpy2psp pack path/to/game -o out/ --font-dir <Ren'Py SDK>/renpy/common   # data.pak
python -m rpy2psp verify path/to/game -o out/ --font-dir <Ren'Py SDK>/renpy/common # decode back and compare
python -m rpy2psp disasm out/script.vnb
python -m rpy2psp coverage --manifest tools/census/games.json --games-dir <corpus>
```

Windows and Linux builds are attached to GitHub releases (no Python needed; they include the PSP engine). Ren'Py's default font (DejaVuSans) and the CJK font (SourceHanSansLite) come with the Ren'Py SDK, not with games, so pass `--font-dir` when a game relies on them. Movie conversion needs ffmpeg on PATH.

The game folder is the one that contains `game/`, or `game/` itself. The compiler reads `.rpy` sources. When only compiled scripts are available, it reads `.rpyc` files and `.rpa` archives. A restricted decoder handles them, and game code is never executed.

### Engine

The engine is C11 with CMake. On Windows (MSVC):

```sh
cmake -S . -B out/msvc -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 && cmake --build out/msvc --config Release
out/msvc/vnpsp/Release/vnpsp.exe out/                      # play a converted game in a window
sh scripts/psp-build.sh                                    # PSP EBOOT.PBP via the pspdev Docker image
```

On Linux, configure with `-G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang` into `out/linux`. `rpy2psp build` wraps the PSP engine with a game; tagged releases also attach the engine alone (`vnpsp-<tag>-psp.zip`). Controls and details: [docs/dev/engine.md](docs/dev/engine.md).

## Tests

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
ctest --test-dir out/msvc -C Release --output-on-failure   # engine unit tests, the test game, a platform smoke run
```

PSP checks in PPSSPPHeadless (Docker image `ppsspp-headless:local`): `tests/psp/ppsspp_run.py` plays a button timeline and compares its screenshots with the PC engine, and `tests/psp/music_loop_check.py` checks gapless music; see [docs/dev/engine.md](docs/dev/engine.md#testing-in-ppsspp).

The engine tests in `tests/engine/` build a self-written test game, play it headless through the engine, and compare every event with the reference interpreter. They are skipped until the engine is built (or `VNPSP_EXE` names it).

The tests use small self-written scripts. `tests/compiler/test_target_games.py` and `tests/engine/test_target_games.py` also check the three target games when they are present in `%TEMP%/rpy2psp-census/full`, or in the folder named by `RPY2PSP_TARGETS`. They are skipped otherwise. Fetch them with `python -I tools/census/fetch_games.py --full <dir> the_question arcance zero_echoes` (a full checkout at the pinned commits, outside the repo).

## Legal

Tool and engine only. No game scripts or assets are included. Convert only games you have the right to use.

## License

MIT. Third-party code: [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md).

hoanglt1223/anypsp.desc: Game-agnostic PSP static recompiler to native PC, macOS, Linux and Android.
hoanglt1223/anypsp.readme:
# AnyPSP

Game-agnostic static recompilation of PSP games to native Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android executables. No emulation loop: Allegrex/VFPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and linked against HLE reimplementations of the PSP system modules, in the spirit of [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5).

## Status

Early. Phases 01 (base) and 02 (loader and analysis) are done; 03 (code generation) and 04 (HLE) are in progress.

- **CPU.** A reference Allegrex interpreter adapted from PPSSPP (`runtime/cpu/`) covers every integer, FPU and VFPU instruction, VFPU prefixes and PPSSPP's bit-exact special functions. Generated code translates the common integer, memory and FPU instructions inline and calls the interpreter for everything else; a random-state differential test checks the inline translations against it. With the interpreter, 37 of 55 pspautotests CPU tests match their expected output, the same set PPSSPP passes apart from three.
- **First games.** A user's own unencrypted Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Heroes executable runs headless from boot through the menus into a battle, both in the interpreter-only runner and as a translated `psp_recomp` runner (all 32,681 discovered functions translated, no missing code in 1,500 frames, about 1.4x faster than the interpreter on the same 8,000-frame input). Ultimate Ninja Heroes 2 reaches its story mode in both runners (translated: 10,000 frames in 80 s, 1.3x the interpreter). Every import of both games has an HLE implementation. Game files never enter this repository.
- **HLE.** Runners list the imports that have no implementation at start, per library. Calling one stops the run and names it, unless a per-game `--hle-stubs` file lists it. Network modules behave as an offline PSP (WLAN switch off, no ad hoc peers). The kernel has variable and fixed pools, thread suspension and the Refer*Status calls; `anypsp_hle_tests` covers HLE functions directly. pspautotests kernel programs (`threads/`, `io/`, `sysmem/`, `rtc/`) pass 14 of 186 so far (2,011 of 8,611 expected lines).

- **Base.** The [PSPRecomp](https://github.com/jessicanataliagta/PSPRecomp) framework at `f6e7d41` is under `recomp/`, with [psp-web-recomp](https://github.com/snuri00/psp-web-recomp)'s ten framework patches applied. psp-web-recomp's generic HLE host is under `runtime/`. Provenance is in [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md); the decision is in [docs/dev/decision-base.md](docs/dev/decision-base.md).
- **Loader and analysis** ([docs/dev/loader-and-analysis.md](docs/dev/loader-and-analysis.md)):
  - EBOOT/PRX loading with all three PSP relocation formats;
  - several modules at a fixed layout, with imports linked between them;
  - a 3,953-entry NID database;
  - iterative function discovery: exports, thread entries and other code-pointer APIs, jump tables, tail calls, unreferenced code;
  - delay-slot aware CFGs;
  - trace feedback from the runtime.

  On the pspautotests demos that keep a symbol table, every function symbol is found statically.
- **Headless host.** It builds with MSVC: the HLE kernel and the software GE, with no window and no audio. A runner per translated program runs homebrew and writes feedback. Many pspautotests programs still stop at Allegrex instructions the code generator does not lower yet (phase 03).
- **Desktop play.** `anypsp-play <game.iso|disc folder>` opens a window with sound, keyboard and gamepad input, and keeps saves in the per-user data folder; translated runners take `--window`. See [docs/user/desktop.md](docs/user/desktop.md).
- **GE.** OpenGL 3.3 and Vulkan backends share one surface manager (`runtime/host/ge_surfaces.cpp`) and the same shaders; Vulkan runs headless with optional MSAA and an on-disk pipeline cache (`--renderer vulkan`). 18 of the 28 pspautotests GE screenshot tests match PPSSPP's reference pictures exactly on both.
- **`anypsp build`.** One command from a game (ISO, disc folder, EBOOT or module) to a packaged native program: analysis, translation, a CMake build against the runtime, and a folder with the program and the game files (`.app` on macOS). Verified end to end on Linux x64 with UNH 1; Windows builds the same way with MSVC. `--target android` writes an APK (Vulkan renderer with an OpenGL ES 3 fallback, touch, gamepad and keyboard controls, the disc picked through the storage access framework). Linux arm64 cross-compiles with `cmake/toolchains/aarch64-linux-gnu.cmake`. See [docs/user/build.md](docs/user/build.md) and [docs/user/android.md](docs/user/android.md).
- **Compatibility and coverage.** `compat/*.toml` per title and `tools/compat-site/generate.py` render the progress page and badges for HLE functions by NID, VFPU instructions translated natively and GE commands (`anypsp-coverage`); see [compat/schema.md](compat/schema.md) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). CI (Linux, Windows, Linux arm64 cross build, Android APK) and tagged releases are in `.github/workflows/`.
- **Not yet:**
  - a Vulkan window or swapchain on the desktop (the Android app presents Vulkan through its own swapchain);
  - tests on a real ARM handheld and an Android phone (phase 06);
  - message pipes, thread-local pools, virtual timers and callback notification (phase 04);
  - a check of the web/EGL build after the renderer seam.
- Prior art and evaluation: [docs/dev/prior-art.md](docs/dev/prior-art.md).

Build and test:

```
cmake -S . -B out/msvc -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64      # Linux: -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build out/msvc --config Release
python tests/fetch-corpus.py      # pinned pspautotests binaries into tests/corpus/ (git-ignored)

out/msvc/Release/anypsp.exe build Game.iso -o games            # the whole pipeline to a packaged program
cmake --install out/msvc --config Release --prefix <dir>       # the release package layout (cm

anypsp-input.ini) and Settings (English or Vietnamese, dark or light theme, menu size,
reduce motion, a frame-rate badge). Keyboard, gamepad, mouse and touch drive it. The
drawing toolkit and Noto Sans subset come from AnyGBA (MIT, OFL).

feat(desktop): per-game memory patch files

--patches auto applies patches/<disc ID>.ini and --patches FILE a named
file: value writes once after loading or after every vblank, directly or
through a pointer, optionally only while the old value matches. Documents
why UNH 1's frame interval cannot be patched to 60 fps at correct speed.

feat(desktop): monitor refresh, frame pacing, VRR, sync to monitor and fps caps

The window shows each PSP vblank on evenly spread monitor vblanks with
vsync, the refresh detected per monitor or set by hand, while the game keeps
59.94 vblanks per second. VRR presents each vblank when ready, sync to
monitor runs vblanks at the monitor rate within 1% with resampled sound, and
a pause key, pause fps and an fps cap save power. Hotkeys F4-F9 switch them
while playing and the title shows monitor Hz, game fps and shown fps.

fix(gpu): round texture buffer width to 16-byte rows

The GE ignores the low bits of the texture buffer width, and a width under
16 bytes means 16 bytes. UNH 1 draws its 16x32 CLUT4 glyphs with bufw 16,
so every other text row was sampled from stale bytes.

feat(desktop): optional smoothing for games drawing at 30 fps

With smoothing on, the vblank where a new game frame appears shows a 50/50
blend with the frame before when that one was up for exactly two vblanks;
60 fps frames, uneven frame times and scene cuts are shown as they are.
Off by default; F9, --smoothing and the new anypsp-display.ini.

fix(desktop): pace windowed vblanks by timer only, show game frame rate

With vsync on, the frame pacer's 59.94 Hz wait and the swap's wait for the
monitor added up, and windowed play ran about 32 vblanks per second. Swap
without vsync and let the pacer alone set the rate. The window title now
shows vblanks per second and the frames the game finished, for example
"60 Hz / game 30 fps"; headless runs print the game frame count.

feat(gpu): lazy VRAM coherence by default, deterministic timing

The GL renderer wrote every GPU surface back to guest VRAM after each
display list (--coherent 1), which held UNH 1 at about 20 fps. Without
it (--coherent 0) games that read their framebuffers break: UNH 1 draws
its fighters as dark streaks.

GuestMemory now tracks VRAM in 4 KiB pages. The GL renderer marks pages
it draws as GPU-dirty and every surface page as watched. A CPU or HLE
access (memcpy, memset, DMA, file reads) to a GPU-dirty page first
downloads the surfaces there; a write to a watched page queues those
rows for reload into the surface before the next list or present.
Lazy is the new default; --coherent 1 keeps the per-list readback for
debugging.

--deterministic drives guest time and time slices from executed code
and fixes the calendar date, so scripted runs repeat frame for frame.
tests/ge-screenshots.py takes --coherent.

Merge branch 'feat/desktop-host'

# Conflicts:
#	README.md
feat: opt-in interpreter fallback profile and headless run timing
docs: translated runner status for both games
test: build translated conformance runners in parallel
fix(codegen): link branches test rs before writing ra

feat(desktop): playable window host with audio, input mapping, saves and ISO launcher

anypsp-play boots an ISO image or extracted disc folder (unencrypted
BOOT.BIN/EBOOT.BIN only) in a resizable vsynced window paced at 59.94 Hz,
with SDL3 audio from the HLE mixer (backlog capped at 100 ms), keyboard
and gamepad input from an ini remap file, F11 fullscreen, and saves in the
per-user memory stick folder. The interpreter and per-game GPU runners take
--window and stay headless by default; --wav records audio headless.

feat(hle): variable pools, thread suspension, refer status for kernel objects, io remove and rmdir

Adds the pspautotests threads, io, sysmem and rtc programs to the pinned corpus manifest.
test(hle): unit tests for rtc, utility, thread, network, sas noise and rename HLE
fix: GE projected q at or below zero samples the last texel
fix: GE sprites with projected texture coordinates interpolate q per pixel
fix: GE 8-bit texture coordinates in through mode scale by 1/128
docs: record PPSSPP-derived GE curve and immediate-mode code
feat: GE Bezier and spline patches; 32-bit vertex indices
feat(hle): offline network modules, noise voices, rename, resume thread and remaining UNH imports

feat: GE primitive continuation (prim type 7)
feat(hle): list imports without an HLE implementation at runner start
feat: GE projective texture q per pixel, lines and 1/16-pixel vertex snapping
feat: --hle-stubs, --input and NID names in the GPU runner
docs: README status for the interpreter, codegen fallback and first game

fix: generated units include the interpreter header; runners can share one build

psp_recomp output now includes cpu/interp.h for its interpreter calls.
ANYPSP_RUNNERS builds several runners in one tree (shared host build),
generated units compile in parallel (ANYPSP_RUNNER_JOBS), and
tests/translated-conformance.py translates pspautotests programs and
checks their output with the resulting runners.

fix: GE culling, through-mode 8-bit positions and short display surfaces

Culling now applies in through mode and never to clears, in both the GL and
the software paths (pspautotests gpu/commands/cull). 8-bit positions decode
as zero in through mode. Presenting a framebuffer taller than its GPU surface
shows the remaining rows from VRAM instead of stretching the surface edge.
The GE screenshot check ignores the scheduler's [r]/[x] line marker.

feat(hle): strict unimplemented imports, per-game stub list, lightweight mutexes

Calling an imported function with no HLE implementation now stops the
guest naming the library, function and NID (AnyPS5 strictness), unless
the runner's --hle-stubs file lists it with a return value. Runners load
data/nids.toml for those names. Adds sceKernel*LwMutex with the lock
state in the guest workarea (after PPSSPP), the kernel-side sceIoDevctl
and the instruction cache calls.

feat(hle): sceDmacMemcpy, sceDmacTryMemcpy, sceDisplayGetAccumulatedHcount, sceUmdReplace*

The first HLE gaps Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Heroes calls; sceDmacMemcpy
used to return 0 without copying.
docs: record the PPSSPP-derived interpreter in THIRD_PARTY.md

feat: scripted controller input and frame dumps for headless runs; feedback driver takes a disc

anypsp-run-*/anypsp-interp accept --input frame:buttons,... and
--dump-at frame,...; tests/feedback-pass.py passes --disc and
--guest-path through for game executables.

feat: desktop OpenGL 3.3 GE backend with an offscreen frame runner

The GE's GL renderer, written for OpenGL ES 3, now also builds against desktop
OpenGL 3.3 core: functions are loaded at run time and the GLSL ES shaders get
a 3.30 version line. A hidden SDL3 window carries the context, so runs open no
visible window and play no audio.

anypsp-interp-gpu (and anypsp-run-<name>-gpu for translated games) renders with
GL or the software rasterizer and writes PNG frames, per-frame hashes and the
picture at a test's screenshot request. Coherent mode keeps guest VRAM current
around every display list for programs that read or write framebuffers with
the CPU. tests/ge-screenshots.py compares the pspautotests GE tests with their
reference screenshots the way PPSSPP's headless does; the corpus manifest now
pins those tests.

test: random-state differential test of generated code against the interpreter

anypsp-difftest-gen emits the lowered C++ psp_recomp produces for a
seeded sample of encodings of every inline-translated kind;
anypsp_cpu_difftest runs each from identical random register and memory
states through that code and through anypsp::cpu::execute. Fixes what it
found: srl/srlv decoded rotr/rotrv only for rs/sa == 1 (Allegrex reads
the low bit), divu by zero, sqrt.s of negatives, round.w.s ties, the
div.s divide-by-zero cause bit, and NaN operands chosen by host operand
order.

feat: screenshot hook for the emulator device's devctl 0x20

pspautotests GE tests request a screenshot through the emulator: device.
The kernel now forwards that request to an optional sink; nothing changes
when no sink is set.

feat: generated code calls the reference interpreter for untranslated instructions

Instruction emission moves to recomp/codegen/emit_cpp. Instructions are
translated inline only when their kind is on the checked list and the
reference tables decode the word the same way; everything else, all VFPU
arithmetic included, calls anypsp::cpu::execute. Control flow the
generator does not model (eret, branches in delay slots, encodings the
two decoders read differently) continues in the interpreter instead of
halting. add/sub follow the reference and do not trap.

feat: reference Allegrex/FPU/VFPU interpreter adapted from PPSSPP

Replaces the fallback interpreter with PPSSPP's interpreter semantics
(integer, FPU, VFPU with prefixes and bit-exact special functions), adds
the interpreter-only runner anypsp-interp, the emulator: test output
device, PPSSPP's initial thread register state, and tests/conformance.py
to compare pspautotests output with the .expected files. The corpus
manifest gains the pspautotests cpu tests.
chore: ignore Python bytecode

docs: loader and analysis pipeline, formats and current status

docs/dev/loader-and-analysis.md describes loading, layout, import
resolution, function discovery, the CFG, the analyzer outputs, trace
feedback and the headless host. tests/feedback-pass.py --base-first
starts from the framework's own seeds to exercise the feedback loop.

fix: untranslated entries into a unit run interpreted and become feedback

A dispatch to a PC inside a translated unit's span that the unit never
translated stopped the guest as an invalid internal entry. It now goes
through Runtime::run_missing_code, which records the address as analysis
feedback and runs the interpreter fallback.

fix: jal to an import stub in the same unit reaches the HLE wrapper

In small modules the import stubs share a unit with their callers, and a
fixed same-unit jal became a local goto into the stub's jr ra, so system
calls silently did nothing.

test: corpus check for loading, import resolution and symbol coverage

ctest runs anypsp-analyze over the fetched pspautotests binaries (skipped
when they are not fetched): no invalid relocation, every import resolved
or listed as unknown, every function symbol found. Gap seeding now builds
the CFG of each seeded function so runs of unreferenced functions are
found in one pass, and .gitattributes keeps sources LF.

feat: renderer-free Windows host build for runs and feedback

The GE front end now talks to its GPU backend through GeRenderer, so
the host builds without GL: anypsp_host holds the HLE kernel and the
software GE, and -DANYPSP_RUNNER_NAME/-DANYPSP_RUNNER_GENERATED builds a
headless runner for one translated game (no window, no audio) that loads
through the AnyPSP loader and writes runtime feedback. savedata and the
ATRAC shim build with MSVC. tests/feedback-pass.py drives analysis,
translation, a run and re-analysis with the feedback.

fix: sparse-dispatch units compile and are entered by PC

Units whose entries span more than the dense table switched on ctx.pc
but shared the plain-JR code that writes local_pc and entry_id, so they
did not compile; and callers chained into them with dense entry ids they
ignore. Sparse units now declare those locals and get no entry ids, so
fixed cross-unit calls into them go through the exact per-PC path.

feat: record code the runtime reaches without translation as feedback

Dispatch misses and interpreted jumps to untranslated addresses are
appended once each to the file named by PSPRECOMP_FEEDBACK_FILE (or set
with set_runtime_feedback_file), which anypsp-analyze --feedback reads
as function seeds for the next pass.

danielriosgarza/system1_doom.readme:
# system1-doom

A ViZDoom agent whose every decision is made by Liquid AI's d1-ultra.
Five senses (survival, combat, navigation, resource, goal) are each one
d1-ultra call that sees only its own slice of the evidence and decides
whether to send a message: an action, a reason, a strength. A central
d1-ultra call hears the messages, with each sense's track record, and
chooses the action; the motor presses that action's fixed keys, aiming
only at targets d1-ultra chose (the combat sense picks which visible enemy
to aim at, the resource sense which remembered pickup to walk to). The code
renders evidence, keeps the bounds and presses the keys; it never ranks,
scores or picks an action itself, and a missed answer is recorded as a
miss rather than filled in by a rule. An asynchronous slow path can
propose new macro-actions, which enter the menu only on an admit
instance's yes.

The design is in
[`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-d1-decision-maker-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-d1-decision-maker-design.md);
System 1 (the senses and the central), System 2 (a slow loop that
changes what each instance sees) and the web app that shows both are
built.

## System 2

System 2 changes what the agent's instances see while it plays, one
change at a time, and every one of its decisions is a d1-ultra instance
too. On its own thread, every 20 decisions or at the end of an episode,
nine reflectors read System 1's history: one for each sense, one for
the central, one each for the menu, the strategy and the exploration
level. Each may propose one change from a finite menu the bounds allow:
widen or narrow a scope by one channel, ask the slow path for a macro or
retire one, switch the strategy, change the level. System 2's central
chooses one change or none. A scope change must first pass a history
test (the instance re-run under the new scope on 24 of the agent's own
stored ticks); then the change takes effect at a tick boundary, is
observed for 60 decisions, and a trial judge keeps or reverts it. Every
cycle is logged to `reflections.jsonl`. The configuration reached is
saved to `runs/<scenario>/configuration.json`, and the next run in that
folder starts from it (`--fresh-configuration` starts from the design's
version 1; each run says which on stderr). `--no-system2` switches System 2 off in
`cli`, `train`, `export` and `serve`. A cycle without a history test is
at most 10 calls, about $0.0003; a history test adds 28 calls, about
$0.001.

## Play

Every decision is a d1-ultra call, so playing needs `LIQUID_API_KEY`, in
the environment or in `.env`:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m system1_doom.cli --scenario basic.cfg --disable-slow-llm      # 15 decisions, JSON summary
python -m system1_doom.cli --scenario deadly_corridor.cfg --episodes 1 --visible
```

A tick takes about 0.8 s (five sense calls in parallel, then the
central) and costs about $0.0002 at the measured usage. `cli`, `train`,
`export` and `serve` all exit with a message when the key is missing;
`--call-budget`, `--explore`/`--exploit`, `--seed`, `--configuration`,
`--fresh-configuration` and `--no-system2` work on each.
`--codex` lets the slow path ask the Codex CLI for proposals instead of
its templates.

The same hierarchy runs on TypeSafe's Jev, a System One decision model
that answers the same `noul`, `choice` and `score` questions, with
`--decider jev` on `cli`, `train`, `export` and `serve`. Every
instance's call then goes to `api.typesafe.ai` (it needs
`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`), the screen goes as an image asset scaled up to
Jev's minimum side, and the cost is counted at Jev's published $0.042
per million input tokens, since its usage block names none. Nothing
else changes: the same evidence, questions, bounds and misses, and a
bundle or a summary says which decider played (`decider`) and which
model version answered (`models`).

## Web explainer

**<https://danielriosgarza.github.io/system1_doom/>** opens on the agent
playing the corridor at its own pace, and beside the game what each of
the six d1-ultra instances answered at that decision: which senses spoke
or stayed silent, with what action, reason and strength, and what the
central picked. Every decision can be checked: a click on a row opens
that instance with the evidence it was sent, verbatim, the channels in
its scope and those it was not shown (the survival sense never sees the
pickups unless System 2 widens its scope), and its answers as bars. The
slow system's screen shows every configuration version with the change,
the reflector that proposed it and System 2's central's choice, the
history test's whole table, the trial and the judge, and the relevance
ledger; Learning, Growing the menu and Reference (the one rule, a drawing
of the two systems, the glossary) follow.

It ships five recordings of `deadly_corridor.cfg` with the best
networks as evidence. Three were played by d1-ultra: seeds 9 and 11 from
the design's version 1 (both clear the corridor, in 59 and 179
decisions) and seed 9 again from version 2, the strategy System 2 chose
and kept on the same run folder (it tries another strategy, the judge
reverts it, and the episode dies after 233 decisions). Two were played
by Jev with `--decider jev`, seeds 9 and 11 from version 1 (seed 9
cleared in 42 decisions; on seed 11 System 2 tried exploring, reverted
it, and the episode died after 211), so each decider can be watched on
the same seed; every card and the top bar say which model played. The
app reads trace schema 2 and is described in
[`web/README.md`](web/README.md); the bundles, the screens and how they
are made are in
[`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` §8.15](docs/DOCUMENTATION.md#815-episode-bundles--the-web-explainer--exportpy-servepy-web),
and the recordings' numbers in §15.

To watch it decide live, `python -m system1_doom.serve` plays on your
machine and the same app follows each decision as it is made, and each of
System 2's records as it is written:

```bash
(cd web && npm install && npm run build)
py

ilyalissoboi/goosestation.desc: GooseStation: a GPLv3 PlayStation emulator, forked from the last GPL-licensed DuckStation (a5bf1ba5, 2024-09-01), with save sync through emusync
ilyalissoboi/goosestation.readme: # GooseStation - PlayStation 1, aka. PSX Emulator [Features](#features) | [Downloading and running](#downloading-and-running) | [Building](#building) | [Licence and credits](#licence-and-credits) GooseStation is a simulator/emulator of the Sony PlayStation(TM) console, focusing on playability, speed, and long-term maintainability. The goal is to be as accurate as possible while maintaining performance suitable for low-end devices. "Hack" options are discouraged, the default configuration should support all playable games with only some of the enhancements having compatibility issues. GooseStation is a fork of [DuckStation](https://codeberg.org/vimuser/duckstation), taken from its last commit published under the GPLv3 (`a5bf1ba5cee7`, 2024-09-01). It adds **memory card sync**: memory cards are synchronised save by save between your devices through S3-compatible storage, using [emusync](https://github.com/ilyalissoboi/emusync). GooseStation is not affiliated with DuckStation or its developers; please do not report GooseStation issues to them. A PS1 or PS2 "BIOS" ROM image is required to to start the emulator and to play games. You can use an image from any hardware version or region, although mismatching game regions and BIOS regions may have compatibility issues. A ROM image is not provided with the emulator for legal reasons, you should dump this from your own console using Caetla or other means. ## Features GooseStation has a full desktop frontend built with Qt, and a fullscreen/TV UI ("Big Picture") based on Dear ImGui. - Memory card sync between devices with emusync (Settings -> Memory Cards). - CPU Recompiler/JIT (x86-64, armv7/AArch32, AArch64, RISC-V/RV64). - Hardware (D3D11, D3D12, OpenGL, Vulkan, Metal) and software rendering. - Upscaling, texture filtering, and true colour (24-bit) in hardware renderers. - Accurate blending via Rasterizer Order Views/Fragment Shader Interlock. - PGXP for geometry precision, texture correction, and depth buffer emulation. - Motion adaptive deinterlacing. - Adaptive downsampling filter. - Screen rotation for vertical or "TATE" shmup games. - Post processing shader chains (GLSL and Reshade FX). - "Fast boot" for skipping BIOS splash/intro. - Save state support, with runahead and rewind. - Windows, Linux, macOS support. - Supports reading directly from CD, bin/cue images, raw bin/img files, MAME CHD, single-track ECM, MDS/MDF, and unencrypted PBP formats. - Preloading of disc images to RAM to avoid disk sleeping hitches. - Automatic loading/applying of PPF patches. - Direct booting of homebrew executables. - Direct loading of Portable Sound Format (psf) files. - Time stretched audio when running outside of 100% speed, and surround sound expansion. - Digital and analog controllers for input (rumble is forwarded to host). - GunCon and Justifier lightgun support (simulated with mouse). - NeGcon support. - Automatic content scanning - game titles/hashes are provided by redump.org. - Optional automatic switching of memory cards for each game. - Supports loading cheats from existing lists. - Memory card editor and save importer. - Emulated CPU overclocking. - Integrated and remote debugging. - Multitap controllers (up to 8 devices). - RetroAchievements. - Video capture with Media Foundation (Windows) and [FFmpeg](https://www.ffmpeg.org/) (All Platforms) backends. ## System Requirements - Windows 10 (1809) or later, macOS 14.4 or later, or a Linux distribution as recent as Ubuntu 22.04 (the oldest each supports with Qt 6.12). - A CPU faster than a potato. But it needs to be x86_64 (SSE4.1), AArch32/armv7, AArch64/ARMv8, or RISC-V/RV64. - For the hardware renderers, a GPU capable of OpenGL 3.1/OpenGL ES 3.1/Direct3D 11 Feature Level 10.0 (or Vulkan 1.0) and above. So, basically anything made in the last 10 years or so. - SDL, XInput or DInput compatible game controller (e.g. XB360/XBOne/XBSeries). DualShock 3 users on Windows will need to install the official DualShock 3 drivers included as part of PlayStation Now. ## Downloading and running GooseStation is in early development. Its builds are published as the [preview release](https://github.com/ilyalissoboi/goosestation/releases/tag/preview), which is replaced by hand with newer builds from time to time; its title gives the version, such as `0.1-49`. Or [build it yourself](#building). | Platform | Download | |---|---| | Windows x64 | `goosestation-windows-x64-release.zip`: extract it to a folder and run `goosestation-qt-x64-ReleaseLTCG.exe`. | | Windows ARM64 | `goosestation-windows-arm64-release.zip`, the same way. | | Linux x86_64 | `GooseStation-x64.AppImage`: make it executable (`chmod +x`) and run it. `goosestation-x64.flatpak` installs with `flatpak install --user goosestation-x64.flatpak`. | | macOS (Universal) | `goosestation-mac-release.zip`: extract it and move `GooseStation.app` to Applications. The app is not notarized yet, so the first time, right-click it and choose Open. | The Windows, macOS and AppImage builds can update themselves from the preview release (Help > Check for Updates). GooseStation keeps its own settings, memory cards and save states, separate from DuckStation's (see [User directories](#user-directories)). ### LibCrypt protection and SBI files A number of PAL region games use LibCrypt protection, requiring additional CD subchannel information to run properly. libcrypt not functioning usually manifests as hanging or crashing, but can sometimes affect gameplay too, depending on how the game implemented it. For these games, make sure that the CD image and its corresponding SBI (.sbi) file have the same name and are placed in the same directory. GooseStation will automatically load the SBI file when it is found next to the CD image. For example, if your disc image wa

Deps: keep mtimes when merging macOS universal binaries

Deps: keep mtimes when merging macOS universal binaries

merge_binaries rewrote each x86 binary with lipo, giving it a new mtime.
make 3.81 compares whole seconds, so when a library was merged in a later
second than one that links it, make install relinked the latter for x86_64
only and installed it over the universal binary. In CI this hit libwebp
(merged before libsharpyuv), and Qt's arm64 WebP plugin failed to link.

lipo now writes to a temporary file that takes the x86 binary's mtime
before replacing it, so make sees the build tree as just built.

frontend's QPlatformNativeInterface (for the X11 and Wayland display in
qtutils.cpp) now finds GuiPrivate and links Qt6::GuiPrivate on Linux,
instead of relying on Qt6Gui_PRIVATE_INCLUDE_DIRS. displaywidget.cpp
included the same private header without using it; removed. Its guard
tested APPLE, which C++ doesn't define, rather than __APPLE__; fixed in
qtutils.cpp. The minimum Qt is now 6.11, the oldest any build uses (the
Flatpak's runtime).

The Linux dependency script's patch to keep qttools from looking for
libclang no longer applies to 6.12's configure.cmake; CMake's
CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_WrapLibClang does the same without editing
Qt.

for every module, as the dependency scripts already do.

Build with clang 21 and Qt 6.12 without deprecation warnings

fmt 10.1.1's compile-time format string checks don't build with clang 21
and later, which VS 2026 (clang-cl 22), the Linux build (clang 21) and
the Flatpak (LLVM 21) now use: FMT_STRING calls in format-inl.h and
os.cc are "not a constant expression" (fmtlib/fmt#4740, unfixed in
fmt's releases). Those compilers now check format strings at run time;
others keep the compile-time checks.

Qt 6.10 deprecated QSortFilterProxyModel::invalidateRowsFilter() (now
beginFilterChange() and endFilterChange(Direction::Rows)) and
QDateTime::fromSecsSinceEpoch() with a Qt::TimeSpec (now QTimeZone::UTC).

Recursive CreateDirectory() tried to create every path prefix, starting

Memory card sync: cards already open wait until they are reopened

Start() followed cards that were already open with a 1 ms session.
es_session_begin applies what already waits for a card before it
returns, whatever the timeout, so a change from an earlier run could be
written to a card the emulator had already read, and the next save would
write the old copy back over it. Registering such a card without a
session is no better: every background sync writes to it.

Start() now leaves open cards alone (not registered) until they are next
opened, and says so once ("Memory cards in use sync from the next time
they are opened"). A card still in OnCardOpening() when Start() runs is
not counted as open: it is followed there after the start, with the
normal 3 s wait, instead of getting the 1 ms session (which also made its
own FollowCard return early).

rstropek/ai-scratch.readme:
# Digiferien KI-Scratch

The official Scratch 3 editor with a German AI helper ("KI-Helfer") beside it. Kids describe what they want,
and the helper asks questions, builds small parts of their game, points at things in the editor, adds sprites
and backdrops from the Scratch library, and draws new sprites.

It was built for **Digiferien**, a one-day AI workshop: about 200 kids aged 10–16 at 10 Austrian schools,
coding beginners who know a little Scratch. Each kid works through a video tutorial at their own pace, with
adults in the room.

## How it works

```
Browser                                         Server (Hono, Azure)            AI services
┌──────────────────┬───────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────┐
│ Chat (React)     │ Scratch 3 editor      │───▶│ access code, limits │───────▶│ Claude Haiku 5.5  │
│ runs the AI's    │ (unmodified, iframe)  │◀───│ builds the AI input │        │ (Anthropic)       │
│ tools ──────────▶│ live project          │    │ logs every AI call  │───────▶│ Jev (TypeSafe):   │
└──────────────────┴───────────────────────┘    └─────────────────────┘        │ kids protection   │
                                                                               └───────────────────┘
```

- **The AI works on the live project in the browser.** Its tools (read and add scripts, point at a block,
  add a sprite …) run right in the editor, so the kid watches the changes happen.
- **The kid is the game designer.** The helper leads with questions and builds only small, clearly defined
  parts, usually one script at a time. Answers are short.
- **Scripts in a format models get right.** The AI reads and writes a compact JSON form of real Scratch
  blocks, which the app compiles into blocks: 96% correct in our tests, against 80% for raw Scratch project
  data.
- **Every AI call is logged** with its token use, for research on how kids work with AI.
- **Saving:** Scratch's *Datei* menu saves the project as an .sb3 file, or in the kid's **CoderDojo Locker**
  ("Im Locker speichern" / "Aus dem Locker laden" / "Locker in neuem Tab öffnen", with the code on their
  Locker sticker;
  [docs/locker.md](docs/locker.md)). Nothing else is stored for the kid, and
  the chat ends when the tab closes.

## What kids see

- **Left: the chat.** Its purple top bar continues Scratch's menu bar and holds the font size buttons, a
  toggle for the AI's tool calls (off by default; kids see "baut an deinem Projekt…") and a fold button. The
  chat width and input height can be dragged; the browser remembers these settings.
- **KI-Energie** under the top bar: **3 hearts** (one per message, one refills every 20 s) and the
  **Gedächtnis** gauge, which fills as the conversation grows. When it is full, the kid clicks
  "Zusammenfassen" or "Neu anfangen". Both teach that AI isn't free or unlimited.
- **"Rückgängig"** under every AI answer that changed the project puts the project back to how it was before
  that answer (Scratch's own undo can't undo AI changes).
- **Right: the Scratch 3 editor**, unmodified, plus one block category of ours: **KI** with
  `frage KI [ ]`, so kids can build their own chatbot (first one question at a time, then one that remembers
  by joining the conversation into a variable). Each question costs a heart, like a chat message, and is
  screened like one. Projects with this block open only in this app, not on scratch.mit.edu.
  Details: [docs/ki-block.md](docs/ki-block.md).
- Until the school's **access code** is entered (or comes with the link as `?code=`), only the chat is locked;
  Scratch works.

## The slide deck

The slides Rainer records into the video tutorial live in [slides/](slides/README.md): a standalone
[Slidev](https://sli.dev) app in a sticker-album look, with its own packages, sharing only the Scratch
colours with the app. The app serves the built deck at **`/slides/`** without an access code
(https://ai-scratch.azurewebsites.net/slides/, presenter view at `/slides/presenter/`).

## Keeping kids safe and costs bounded

- **Adults supervise** every session; the technical layers are deliberately lean.
- **Kids protection:** every kid message (and every text of the "frage KI" block) is screened by TypeSafe's Jev before it reaches Claude. Flagged
  messages get a fixed German answer, for example a kid in distress is sent to an adult. What was tested:
  [docs/kids-protection.md](docs/kids-protection.md).
- **Limits:** hearts per kid, the Gedächtnis limit, a cap on answer length and on AI steps per message.
- **Access codes**, one per school. **Budget:** 200 €/month.

## Sample prompts

Handy for trying the assistant by hand; each one exercises a different tool family.

| Prompt | Exercises |
|---|---|
| Wo finde ich den Block "wiederhole fortlaufend"? Ich will ihn selbst einbauen! | pointing at the palette (ui tools) |
| Bau: 3 mal 50 Schritte gehen und 1 Sekunde warten. Zeig mir dann, wo im Skript gewartet wird. | building scripts, then pointing at a block |
| Füge eine Fledermaus hinzu, die mit den Flügeln schlägt. | library sprite + animation script |
| Ich mache ein Weltraumspiel. Gib mir einen passenden Hintergrund. | library backdrop |
| Zeichne mir einen grünen Drachen als neue Figur. | drawing an SVG sprite |
| Wo kann ich mein Projekt speichern? | explaining the editor (file menu) |

## Run it locally

Requires Node.js 24 or later.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env   # then fill in the Anthropic and TypeSafe keys and the access codes
npm run dev            # http://localhost:5173/?code=<one of your access codes>
```

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key (server only) |
| `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` | sent as `anthropic-workspace-id`; needed for identity-linked keys |
| `ACCESS_CODES` | comma-separated, one per school; not case-sensitive; codes starting with `admin_` have no heart limit (testing) |
| `JEV_API_KEY` | TypeSafe key for the kids-protection guard (server only) |

# ROADVANTA — Drive Your World.

A 3D open-world driving game that runs entirely in the browser. React + TypeScript + Three.js (React Three Fiber) + Vite.
No accounts, no backend, no API keys: progress is saved locally in the browser.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173 (also exposed on your LAN)
npm run build      # type-check + production build into dist/
npm run preview    # serve the production build
npm test           # unit tests (save validation, physics, navigation, config)
```

**Test on a phone:** run `npm run dev`, then open `http://<your-computer-LAN-IP>:5173` on a phone on the same Wi‑Fi. Use landscape and the **Low** graphics preset first (Settings).

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accelerate / brake & reverse | W / S or ↑ / ↓ | GAS / BRAKE |
| Steer | A / D or ← / → | ◀ ▶ |
| Handbrake | Space | HB |
| Camera (chase / far / cockpit) | C | CAM |
| Reset car onto the road | R | RST |
| Horn | H | – |
| Pause | Esc | II |

Gamepad (left stick, triggers, A) is also read when connected. The game auto-pauses when the tab loses focus.

## What is implemented

- **City:** 7×7 block procedural city (~0.7 km²): arterial roads and streets, intersections with working traffic signals, sidewalks, crosswalks, lane/stop markings, apartments/towers/shops/houses, parks, parking, trees, lamps, bus stops, benches, hydrants, fences. Day/night cycle with window glow and lit streets.
- **Vehicles:** 6 drivable vehicles (hatch, sedan, SUV, sports coupe, supercar, motorcycle) with distinct procedural models and physics. AI traffic also has vans, buses, bicycles and police cruisers. Colours, paint, and engine/tyre/brake upgrades change the real physics values.
- **Physics:** custom arcade-sim vehicle model (grip-limited lateral dynamics, handbrake slides, suspension pitch/roll) with OBB collisions against buildings, props and other vehicles. *Rapier is not used* — a purpose-built 2D model was far more stable and cheaper on phones.
- **Traffic & pedestrians:** AI cars follow lanes along the road network, obey signals, yield to vehicles/pedestrians, turn at junctions and recover when stuck. Pedestrians use sidewalk graphs, wait for crossings, and react when hit.
- **Modes:** Free Drive (wanted level from speeding, red lights, crashes, hitting pedestrians), Career (destination, timed, delivery, distance, speed and drift challenges), Street Racing (countdown, checkpoints, AI rivals with rubber‑banding, placement payouts), Police Chase (escape or reach the safe house). 16 missions with level gates.
- **Progression:** XP, levels (30), coins, par‑time bonuses, replay reward reduction (25 %), level milestones, garage (buy / select / paint / upgrade), local save with versioning, validation and reset confirmation.
- **UI/UX:** main menu, modes, mission list, garage with live 3D preview, settings (graphics preset, camera distance, speed unit, 4 volume controls, mute), HUD with speed/gear/rpm/objective/timer/position/wanted, rotating minimap, pause menu with confirmations, results screen, first‑run controls guide, error boundary, loading screen, touch controls and a rotate‑device hint.
- **Audio:** fully procedural WebAudio (engine, tyre squeal, wind, city ambience, collisions, horn, sirens, UI sounds, ambient music). It is not positional 3D audio.
- **Performance:** merged static geometry, instanced props and pedestrians, pooled vehicle rigs, fixed sub‑stepped physics, no React renders per frame, and Low/Medium/High presets (resolution, shadows, fog, traffic and pedestrian counts).

## Architecture

```
src/
  config/     vehicles, missions, game tuning (all numbers in one place)
  core/       store (zustand UI state), save (versioned + validated), runtime (mutable game state), input, audio, math
  vehicles/   physics, collisions, procedural models
  world/      city layout, textures, buildings, roads, props, sky/lighting
  sim/        navigation graph, traffic, pedestrians, police, race AI
  game/       session (modes/missions/rewards), GameScene (loop, camera, markers)
  ui/         menus, garage, settings, HUD, overlays, touch controls
tests/        vitest unit tests
```

## Honest limitations

- No multiplayer, no accounts, no cloud save (by design).
- Buildings are procedural low-poly with generated textures, not photoreal assets; interiors do not exist.
- Only the Ronin 650 motorcycle is drivable among two-wheelers; bicycles and extra motorbikes appear in traffic only.
- Collision damage is cosmetic‑free (impacts cause shake, sound and heat, not deformation).
- Audio and graphics were validated in headless Chromium (software rendering); real‑device frame rates were not measured, so start on Low on older phones.
- Dev builds expose `window.__rv` for debugging; it is stripped in production.

- 📜 Kinh thánh game (cốt truyện, nhân vật, 5 vùng đất, lời thoại, lộ trình): `bible/index.html`
- 🕹️ Bản 5 lượt cũ (Bíp Bụp gốc): `legacy/bip-bup-5-luot.html`, đang chạy ở https://bip-bup.vercel.app

## Cấu trúc
| Đường dẫn | Nội dung |
|---|---|
| `src/sprites.js` | 12 nhân vật pixel art vẽ bằng text, không cần file ảnh |
| `src/world.js` | cốt truyện, 5 vùng, kẻ địch, cấu hình 16 cửa, lời thoại, vẽ nền |
| `src/audio.js` | mixer 3 bus, hiệu ứng tổng hợp, giọng blip theo dấu tiếng Việt, nhạc nền theo vùng |
| `src/game.html` | giao diện, HUD, trận đấu trên canvas, sao, chia sẻ, link thách cửa |
| `build.js` | gộp `src/` thành thư mục tĩnh `public/` (Vercel phục vụ thư mục này) |

```bash
node build.js https://ba-khi.vercel.app   # sinh public/index.html, sprites.js, world.js, game.js
```

Không có bước cài đặt. Mở `public/index.html` là chơi được. Toàn bộ âm thanh, nhạc và tiếng nói nhân vật được tổng hợp bằng WebAudio, không có file âm thanh.

## Luật
- Màn chờ: aura dâng. Màn xanh + Gà Bíp gáy = BỤP. Sát thương theo mili giây phản xạ (dưới 180ms là CHÍ MẠNG).
- 3 tim. Bụp sớm, mắc bẫy Vịt Giả Gà (màn đỏ, tiếng CẠC), thả sớm khi tích khí, bụp trượt điểm sáng hoặc ngủ quá 1 giây là mất 1 tim.
- Nhịp đôi: bụp cái thứ hai trong 0,45 giây được +25% đòn. Tích khí: giữ trên 0,6 giây rồi thả đúng lúc được +60%. Điểm sáng nhỏ: +30%.
- Sao: ★ thắng · ★★ không mất tim · ★★★ phản xạ trung bình dưới 250ms.
- Cấp bá khí theo 60 cú bụp gần nhất: Tân Thủ Cỏ → Võ Giả Tre → Cao Thủ Sắt → Vương Giả Vàng → Đế Vương Bụp.
- Link thách cửa: `https://ba-khi.vercel.app#c12-231` (cửa 12, 231ms).

## Lộ trình
1. **Đợt 1 (xong):** vùng Làng Tre + Chợ Đêm, 16 cửa, trùm Lý Trưởng Ngáp và Anh Hai Hàng Hiệu, thẻ chia sẻ, link thách cửa, lưu tiến trình.
2. **Đợt 2 (xong):** Sông Băng (nhịp đôi: BÍP BÍP bụp hai cái; tích khí: giữ rồi thả), Núi Lửa (khói che màn, bụp đúng điểm sáng đang nhỏ dần), Thiên Đình (trộn mọi mánh, Gà Bíp hô trước), trùm cuối Lão Rùa Thiên Tuế 3 hiệp, chế độ luyện tập trùm (5 tim, không tính sao). Nhân vật: Hỏa Yến (mở sau cửa 16, đòn +30%, cửa sổ hẹp hơn), Băng Nhi (sau cửa 24, tha 1 lần bụp sớm), Thạch Lão (sau cửa 32, 5 tim, cửa sổ rộng, đòn yếu).
3. **Đợt 3:** Cửa Hằng Ngày, bảng xếp hạng (Supabase), nhạc nền theo vùng.

Mọi tên, hình ảnh, thuật ngữ trong game là sáng tác mới.


## Lõi 2 (10/2025)

Trong lúc chờ gà gáy, đối thủ ra đòn có mũi tên báo trước: vuốt theo mũi tên để đỡ (chuỗi đỡ nhân sát thương cú bụp), mũi tên hồng run rẩy là đòn giả. Giữ ngón tay là cược x2.2, thả dưới 160ms thì thắng. Chế độ Chạy 60 giây: đối thủ ngẫu nhiên, tính điểm, kỷ lục. Chi tiết ở `docs/upgrade-plan.md`.

## Ngôn ngữ / Languages

Ba ngôn ngữ: tiếng Việt (BÁ KHÍ: Battle Aura), tiếng Anh (**Don't Trust the Duck**), tiếng Trung giản thể (**别信鸭子**). Lần đầu vào có hộp chọn ngôn ngữ, sau đó đổi bằng thanh 🇻🇳 🇬🇧 🇨🇳 trên trang chính hoặc `?lang=vi|en|zh`. Mỗi bản là viết lại hài (transcreation), không dịch: `src/lang/<mã>-world.js` và `src/lang/<mã>-story.js`; chuỗi giao diện ở `src/i18n.js`.

Build bản quốc tế (meta và mặc định theo ngôn ngữ): `node build.js https://donttrusttheduck.com en` hoặc `... zh`.
