henryclub/3D-Driving.readme:
# UAE Driving

A 3D open-world driving and action game that runs in the browser and on Android. Your home sits in the middle of an endless city. Step outside, take the Fortuner or the Koenigsegg Jesko from your driveway, call any car or bike with your phone, run missions for cash, or cause trouble and outrun the police.

Built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/). The game is a single `index.html` plus a local copy of `three.min.js`, so it also works offline.

## Download the game
Every push to `main` builds fresh downloads automatically. Open the repo's **Releases** page and take the newest release:
- **Android:** `UAE-Driving.apk`. Open it on your phone to install. Android will ask you to allow installing from this source the first time.
- **Windows PC:** `UAE-Driving.exe`. Double-click it and the game opens in its own window, no install needed. Press `F11` for fullscreen. Because the file is not code-signed, Windows may show "Windows protected your PC": click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

## Features
- **Main menu and pause menu.** The game opens on a main menu with a Play button. In game, the ☰ button (or `Esc`) pauses with Resume, Restart and Leave to main menu. Full instructions are in the phone's **Help** tab.
- **Dubai.** The endless city is dressed as Dubai, and the district name shows at the top left:
  - **Sheikh Zayed Road** (the road just south of your home) runs east to west under the elevated **Dubai Metro**, with palm-lined medians, green overhead signs and stations every 160 m where silver trains stop and pull out.
  - **Downtown Dubai** has the **Burj Khalifa** (a spiralling tiered tower with a spire), The Dubai Mall and the Dubai Fountain lake with dancing jets. **Emirates Towers**, the **Dubai Frame**, the **Museum of the Future** and the twisting **Cayan Tower** are around the city.
  - **Jumeirah Beach** has the Arabian Gulf, beach umbrellas, lifeguard huts and resorts. A causeway leads out to the **Burj Al Arab** on its own island; at night its sail glows in changing colours. **Palm Jumeirah** and **Atlantis** are further along the coast (drive up the road at the east end of the beach).
  - Jumeirah villas with walled gardens and pools, mosques with minarets, old Dubai with wind towers and dhows on **Dubai Creek**, Dubai Marina towers, and the desert with dunes, camels and tents beyond the city. Cash is in AED.
- **Life in Dubai.**
  - **Clock and prayers.** A day lasts 16 minutes, with dawn, day, dusk and night. You get a message at Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. Walk into a **masjid**, do **wudu** (the ablution is shown step by step), then pray with the jamaat. The prayer is acted out with the real rak'ahs for each time.
  - **Food bar.** The FOOD bar under your health drops slowly. Eat at **restaurants** or the **Dubai Mall food court**: sit at a table, order from the menu, the waiter brings it, you eat, then pay at the counter. Leave without paying and the **guards** catch you, take you to the counter and charge you with a fine.
  - **Hotels.** Every hotel (and the **Burj Al Arab**) has a lobby with reception and lifts. Book a room, choose the floor and how long you stay, ride the lift up, sleep, order room service and look at the view.
  - **Dubai Mall inside.** A huge hall with an aquarium wall, shops on two levels, a food court and **Fashion Avenue**. Clothes you buy appear in **Phone > Settings > Outfit**. The phone **Store** sells real phones.
  - **Burj Khalifa.** Walk in to a huge lobby with a central statue ringed by small fountains, a big restaurant, and a reception where you book a room on any of 160 floors. Ride the lift up, or buy an **At the Top** ticket (from AED 10,000) for the open rooftop deck above the clouds, with the city lights far below at night.
  - **Burj Al Arab.** Drive over the causeway and under the gate right up to the porch, then go inside to the gold atrium, reception, royal suites and restaurants.
  - **Dubai Mall, five floors.** Lifts connect five levels of shops that all sell real items: Fashion Avenue (every outfit), the Gold Souk with a live gold price per gram, tech, sports, books, cinema and more. Your purchases go in the **Bag** tab. Sit at the food court, order, the waiter brings the food and then the bill. Leave without paying and the guards take you to the counter.
  - **Airport and flights.** **Dubai International Airport** sits on its own island with a causeway, a runway, a tower and real planes that land and take off to a timetable. Phone > **Travel**: search a city, pick a flight, class and seat, then pay. You get reminders before boarding. At the airport, check in, go to your gate, take the airport bus to the plane, find your **green** seat and press E to sit. The crew close the door, the plane takes off, you can speed up the flight, and on landing you walk out through arrivals into the new city.
  - **The world.** Book flights to countries: India, Pakistan, United Kingdom, United States, France, Japan, Egypt, Turkey, Singapore, Australia, China and Saudi Arabia. Each has its own look, street names, landmarks (Eiffel Tower, Big Ben, Statue of Liberty and more), local clothes, restaurants and an airport to fly home.
  - **India by train.** India has Delhi, Mumbai, Agra (Taj Mahal), Jaipur (Hawa Mahal) and Kolkata (Victoria Memorial). Each has a Railway Station: buy a ticket, board at the platform and ride to another city.
  - **Burj Al Arab market.** Two lifts face each other in the lobby: ROOM LIFTS and a MARKET LIFT (no room needed). Eight floors: shirts, denim jeans, phones, shoes, traditional wear, watches, bags and sunglasses, oud and perfume.
  - **Phones.** 40 phones from Apple, Samsung, Google, OnePlus, Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi, Realme, Nothing, Huawei, Motorola, Honor and Vertu. The phone at the bottom of the screen looks like the one you bought, and foldables open with an arrow on their side.
  - **Airport road.** A real road crosses the sea to Dubai International Airport.
  - **Maps.** Tap the minim

PongsakornNaklang/portfolio-cafe.readme:
# NAKANG

A portfolio built as a tiny 3D Bangkok shop. You scroll to walk across the street up to the window, and you click things in the shop to learn about the work.

**Live:** https://pongsakorn-naklang.vercel.app

![The storefront by day, a tuk-tuk passing](docs/storefront-day.jpg)

## What you can do on the page

| Object | What it does |
|---|---|
| Things in the PROJECTS case | Each opens its project (the list comes from the database) |
| Bankza behind the counter | Says hi and tells you about himself; order a drink and he walks to the machine and makes it while you watch, then you pick a seat; "💬 Ask me anything" to chat with him (AI, answers from what's on the site); opens the portfolio book; dances while the music's on |
| Menu stand | Skills, listed like a coffee menu |
| A-frame sign | A short hello |
| Door | Opens and closes; when it's open you can scroll on into the shop |
| Seats | Sit down with your drink: tap it to sip, drag to look around |
| Record player | Music on/off; the tone arm drops onto the record and it spins |
| Vinyl shelf | The records come off it into a row to flip through; pick one to play, or request a song |
| Yellow book on the table | The portfolio book: about me, my work (a page for each thing I built), skills, every project, page by page; tap or drag a page to turn it |
| Blue board | Draw a note on the shared guestbook |
| Box on the bookshelf | UYES, a card game against Bankza |
| Sleeping cat | Pet it |
| Tip jar | Tip a coffee by PromptPay, TrueMoney or Ko-fi |
| Wall clock | Shows the visitor's real time |
| Lamps | Switch each light on/off |
| Red mailbox | Contact links |
| 7-Eleven across the road | The door chime |
| Passing taxi or tuk-tuk | A beep; double-tap it and it stops, the driver asking if you want a ride: hop in and ride in the back while they chat (tap the driver: faster, slower, or a wheelie in the tuk-tuk), then "Get out" drops you at the shop |
| Mynas on the wire | Shoo them off |

Some things are left for you to find: pouring your own latte art, a game of checkers (หมากฮอส) at the centre table, and two secret records.

The time of day follows the visitor's clock (add `?time=day`, `sunset` or `night` to the URL to force it). A tour of everything you can tap runs on the first visit; the **?** button opens it again.

## How it's built

```
blender/build_storefront.py   builds the whole scene in Blender from code (headless)
blender/export_web.py         exports web/storefront.glb (Draco) + web/rig.json
blender/export_mixamo.py      exports the character in an A-pose for Mixamo
blender/prep_meshy.py         shrinks the raw Meshy street models into meshy/street/*.glb
mixamo/                       the Mixamo-rigged character with Waving and Breathing Idle clips
web/                          the static three.js page (no build step)
web/api/                      small Vercel Functions: the display case's projects, the shared guestbook board, the visitor counter, shared tallies, Bankza's chat
db/                           the database tables (Neon Postgres, connected through Vercel)
```

**Rebuild the model and the web files** (Blender 4.2 or newer):

```bash
/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b -P blender/build_storefront.py -- --time day --out out/storefront_day.blend --render out/day.png
```

```bash
/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b out/storefront_day.blend -P blender/export_web.py -- web
```

**Run the page locally** (with the API, so it reads the database; the first run links the Vercel project and pulls its settings into `web/.env.local`):

```bash
cd web && npm install && vercel dev --listen 5173
```

**Edit the text on the cards** in [web/content.js](web/content.js), including `work` (my jobs, for the book's Work chapter and Bankza's chat).

**Edit what's in the display case** in the Neon console (Vercel → Storage → nakang-db → Open in Neon → Tables → `projects`): one row per project, in `position` order across the top shelf then the bottom (8 spots). `model` picks the 3D model: a Blender one such as `ipod_classic`, or a shape, `sphere`, `cube` or `pyramid`; left empty it's a sphere. `image` lists its pictures, comma-separated (paths in `web/projects/` or URLs; the first is the cover, more make a gallery), `tagline` a short line under the title, `tags` its highlights as chips (comma-separated) and `repo` adds a "Source on GitHub" button. The site shows changes within a minute. The tables are described in [db/](db/).

**Bankza's chat** (`web/api/chat.js`) runs on Claude Haiku 5.5 and needs an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var in Vercel. He answers only from `web/content.js` (including the CV in `cv`, which only he uses) and the `projects` table, so edit those to change what he knows. Each visitor gets 20 messages a day and the whole site 1000, counted in the `chat_uses` table.

**The guestbook board** is shared: every save adds a row to the `guestbook` table and the site shows the newest. The last 50 are kept, so to undo a spoiled board, delete the rows newer than the good one. More detail on the Blender side is in [blender/README.md](blender/README.md).

## Versioning and releases

Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org), read for a website:

- **Major**: the scene or the way you move through it changes in a big way.
- **Minor**: a new object, interaction or page feature.
- **Patch**: fixes, text and small visual tweaks.

Every release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). To cut one:

1. Move the **Unreleased** notes in `CHANGELOG.md` under a new version heading with today's date.
2. Commit, then tag it: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z"` and `git push --follow-tags`.
3. Deploy: `vercel deploy --prod` from `web/`.
4. Publish the GitHub release from the changelog notes: `gh release create vX.Y.Z --notes-file <notes>`.

## Credits

- Sign font: Archivo by Omnibus-Type, SIL Open Font License (`blender/fonts/OFL-Archivo.txt`).
- Character, tuk-tuk, taxi and myna models: generated w

Kepin17/olyzano-notch.readme:
# Olyzano Notch **A temporary file shelf that lives at the top edge of your screen.** Move the mouse (or a dragged file) to the top-centre and it slides out. Drop files on it, take them back out whenever you need them, send them to a phone with a QR code. Files are **copied** into Olyzano Notch's own storage and cleaned up automatically after a few days; your originals are never touched. Runs on **Linux (KDE Plasma, Wayland or X11)** and **Windows 10 / 11**. - [Install](#install): Linux · Windows · [optional components](#optional-components) - [Features](#features) - [Using Olyzano Notch](#using-olyzano-notch) · [the dock](#the-app-dock) · [live activities](#live-activities-and-the-idle-clock) · [timer & Pomodoro](#timer-and-pomodoro) · [stretch reminder](#stretch-reminder) - [Share via QR](#share-via-qr) - [Settings and storage](#settings-and-storage) - [Build from source](#build-from-source) - [Project layout](#project-layout) --- ## Install The easiest way is the **[install page](https://kepin17.github.io/olyzano-notch/)**, which links the newest download for your system. ### Linux **Needs** a 64-bit distribution with **Qt 6.5 or newer**: Debian 13, Ubuntu / Kubuntu 25.04 or newer, KDE neon. Made for **KDE Plasma** (Wayland or X11); other desktops work with fewer extras (see [what works where](#what-works-where)). Tested on Kubuntu 26.04 (Qt 6.10, KDE Plasma on Wayland). **1. Download** `notch__amd64.deb` from the **[install page](https://kepin17.github.io/olyzano-notch/)** or the **[latest release](https://github.com/Kepin17/olyzano-notch/releases/latest)**, or from a terminal: ```bash wget https://github.com/Kepin17/olyzano-notch/releases/download/v0.11.0/notch_0.11.0_amd64.deb ``` **2. Install** it. `apt` pulls in everything it needs (Qt 6 runtime, `layer-shell-qt`, Poppler, Ghostscript, `gocryptfs`, `fuse3`, `pulseaudio-utils`, …): ```bash sudo apt install ./notch_0.11.0_amd64.deb ``` **3. Start** **Olyzano Notch** from the application menu, or turn on **Settings → General → Start at login**. For OCR, KDE Connect and the rest, see [optional components](#optional-components). **Update:** install the newer `.deb` the same way, then restart Olyzano Notch (`pkill notch; notch &`). Your shelf and settings stay. **Remove:** `sudo apt remove notch`. Your shelf is kept; delete it yourself with `rm -r ~/.local/share/notch ~/.config/notch`. > On Wayland the shelf is pinned to the real top edge through `layer-shell-qt`. Without it the app still > runs but cannot sit over the panel. Details in [docs/wayland-limitations.md](docs/wayland-limitations.md). ### Windows 1. Download **`Notch--windows-x64-setup.exe`** (installer) or **`Notch--windows-x64-portable.zip`** from the repository's **Releases** page (a `v*` tag builds one), or from the latest **Windows** run under *Actions → Artifacts*. 2. Run the installer. It installs for your user (no administrator prompt), adds a Start-menu entry and can start Olyzano Notch when you sign in. The portable zip needs no install: extract it anywhere and run `notch.exe`. 3. The build is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen says *"Windows protected your PC"*: click **More info → Run anyway**. **Good to know** - Sharing over WiFi: Windows asks once to let Olyzano Notch through its firewall. Allow it on **private** networks. - PDF and OCR tools need Poppler, Ghostscript and Tesseract on your `PATH`: download links and steps are in [optional components](#optional-components). The image tools need nothing. - Settings and files live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\notch`. **Remove:** *Settings → Apps → Olyzano Notch → Uninstall* (installer), or delete the folder (portable). Delete `%LOCALAPPDATA%\notch` too if you want your shelf gone. ### Optional components Olyzano Notch runs without these; each one switches on a feature. Olyzano Notch finds them by itself once they are installed (restart Olyzano Notch after installing). | Component | What it adds | Linux | Windows | |---|---|---|---| | **Tesseract OCR** + a language | *OCR* in the Tools menu (text from images and scanned PDFs) | `sudo apt install tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng`
(more languages: `tesseract-ocr-ind`, `tesseract-ocr-deu`, …) | [UB Mannheim installer](https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/tesseract/wiki): tick the languages you need, then add `C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR` to `PATH` | | **Poppler** | PDF page count, split, extract, PDF → image, OCR of PDFs | included in the `.deb` (`poppler-utils`) | [poppler-windows releases](https://github.com/oschwartz10612/poppler-windows/releases/latest): unzip, add its `Library\bin` folder to `PATH` | | **Ghostscript** | *Compress PDF* | included in the `.deb` (`ghostscript`) | [Ghostscript downloads](https://ghostscript.com/releases/gsdnld.html) (64-bit AGPL release); its installer adds it to `PATH` | | **KDE Connect** (computer + phone) | *Send to device*, files from your phone, incoming calls, phone notifications and a low phone battery in the notch | `sudo apt install kdeconnect` and on the phone [KDE Connect for Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.kde.kdeconnect_tp) ([F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/org.kde.kdeconnect_tp/)) or [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/app/kde-connect/id1580245991); pair them once | [KDE Connect for Windows](https://kdeconnect.kde.org/download.html) (the installer; Olyzano Notch looks for it in its install folder, so the Microsoft Store version is not found) and the same phone app; pair them once | | **KDE Plasma's KWin** | Dock: real running apps, a click raises or minimizes the app's window, the window list | part of Plasma | built in (Windows windows) | | **Plasma blur effect** | Frosted-glass blur behind the dock | *System Settings → Window Management → Desktop Effects → Blur* | – | | **Spectacle** auto-save | *Add new screenshots* | in Spectacle: *Configure → Save → save automatically* (Olyzano Notch has a button for it) | built in (Win + PrtSc)

Locked categories on Windows: a file-based vault engine

gocryptfs and FUSE don't exist there, so Vault gains a second engine with
the same API: each file is its own AES-256-GCM container (ShareCrypto's
format, the name inside, the file named by a keyed hash) under a random
key wrapped by the password. Unlocking decrypts into a Temp folder kept
out of the search index; locking encrypts what changed, drops what was
removed and deletes the plain copies. After a crash the plain files are
taken as the latest state on the next unlock. Linux keeps gocryptfs; the

M0nsT3rG/ProjectMordor.readme:
# Project Mordor

A research project into whether two legitimate owners of *Middle-earth: Shadow of War* (Steam, Windows x64) could one day play the campaign together in co-op.

**Status: Phase 1 (research and feasibility) is complete.** The result is a conditional NO-GO for game integration and a GO for lawful groundwork. Read [docs/phase1-report.md](docs/phase1-report.md).

> This repository contains **no game code, no game assets and no game integration**. The networking prototype is standalone and has never been connected to the game. Nothing here claims co-op in Shadow of War works.

## Progress

*Last updated 2026-10-25.*

**Overall: about 16% (a rough estimate).**

```
[███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░]  ~16%
```

- **This is not a forecast that co-op will work.** The [feasibility matrix](docs/feasibility-matrix.md) deliberately gives no odds of success. Every game-side milestone is unverified, and none may start before gate G0.
- **Everything done so far is groundwork that does not touch the game.** In-game co-op is at 0%.

| Area | Weight | Done | What it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1: research and feasibility | 5% | **100%** | Complete: inventory, prior art, evidence system, risks, report ([phase1-report.md](docs/phase1-report.md)) |
| Networking groundwork (standalone, no game) | 15% | **~60%** | Done: host and client; two transports (raw UDP and Valve GameNetworkingSockets); encrypted and authenticated sessions (DTLS); reconnect; reliable game events; real-time soak tests with fixed pass/fail gates; immutable test evidence. Still open: tests over a real LAN and the internet, the slow-recovery tail on GNS under heavy loss (KI-35), an independent security review, NAT traversal, delta snapshots and desync digests. |
| Gate G0: legal position (D-007) and target platform (D-008) | 5% | **50%** | **D-007 decided** (2026-10-25): the owner proceeds with interoperability work and accepts the legal risk; no protection is ever bypassed. **D-008 pending:** the Steam build is protected, so it cannot be the target; GOG lists the game as DRM-free (a store claim, to be verified on a purchased copy). G0 stays closed until D-008 is decided. |
| In-game milestones M1–M10 (observe the game, sync the player, puppet character, movement, combat, AI, Nemesis, missions, saves, full campaign) | 75% | **0%** | Blocked by G0. See the [matrix](docs/feasibility-matrix.md). |

**How the number is computed:**

- 5% × 100% + 15% × 60% + 5% × 50% + 75% × 0% = 16.5%. The "60%" for the networking work is itself a judgement, so read this as "between 12% and 18%".
- The weights say where most of the unknown work lies: inside the game. They are an estimate, not a measurement.

**Where the newer work is:**

- Everything after Phase 1 is in open pull requests, stacked one on another (#1 → #22), each reviewed. **None is merged into `main` yet**, so `main` still shows the Phase 1 code. The [pull requests](../../pulls) and their review comments have the details.
- The live status and test results are on the newest branch, in `.ai-collaboration/PROJECT_STATUS.md` and `TEST_RESULTS.md`.

## Contents

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `docs/` | Report, architecture notes, feasibility matrix, risk register, decisions, protocol |
| `evidence/` | Findings (`F-*`) and experiments (`EXP-*`) as JSON, validated by `tools/evidence/evidence.py` |
| `tools/environment/` | Read-only game discovery and PE inventory (Python stdlib only) |
| `src/` | C++20 networking prototype: `common`, `network`, `simulation`, `host`, `client` |
| `tests/` | Unit, integration (loopback UDP) and network-impairment test suites |
| `scripts/` | `build.ps1`, `test.ps1`, `inventory.ps1` |

## Quick start

Requirements: Windows 10/11, Visual Studio with the MSVC C++ toolset, CMake 3.25 or later, Python 3.10 or later.

```powershell
./scripts/build.ps1
./scripts/test.ps1 -E2E
./scripts/inventory.ps1   # optional: needs the game installed via Steam; strictly read-only
```

## Rules

The project's non-negotiable rules are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). The most important ones:

- never modify the game or saves;
- never bypass DRM, anti-tamper or licensing;
- never touch official online services;
- never redistribute game files;
- never invent evidence.

giampierofiorelli/Fandome.readme:
# ✦ Fandome

**The social network for music fans.** Your fan story is your profile, concerts are where you meet.

> Prototype. Independent fan platform — not affiliated with, authorised or sponsored by any artist.
> All data is demo data stored in your browser. Future concert dates are fictional.

## What's inside (and where each idea comes from)

| Feature | Inspired by |
|---|---|
| Fast posts, threads, quote posts, hashtags, **Trending in <fandom>** | Twitter/X ("stan Twitter") |
| **Fan Passport**: fan since, Top 4 albums, star ratings, short reviews, diary of shows | Letterboxd |
| **Repost with tags** (tags as commentary) | Tumblr |
| One **room per artist**, topic feeds, **auto-translate** posts | Weverse |
| **Starter packs** at sign-up (shareable link), custom topic feeds, **detach your post from a quote** | Bluesky |
| **Listening party**: everyone hears the same track at the same time (music stays on Spotify/Apple Music) | Stationhead |
| **Concert pages**: "I'm going" / "I was there", live chat, setlist, memories | — |
| **Share cards** (PNG for Instagram/TikTok stories) — the growth loop | Spotify Wrapped |
| **Finite feed**: "You're all caught up" | Instagram |
| **Export my data** | lesson from Amino's shutdown |

## Listening parties with Spotify

Like Stationhead, Fandome never streams audio: it remote-controls **your own Spotify app**
(Spotify Connect) so everyone hears the same song at the same second.

1. Create a free app at https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard (tick **Web API**).
2. Add the Redirect URI shown in **Settings → Spotify** (e.g. `https://<user>.github.io/Fandome/`).
3. Paste the Client ID in Settings, tap **Connect Spotify**, then **Sync my Spotify** in a party.

Notes: playback control requires Spotify **Premium** and an open Spotify app on any device.
New Spotify apps start in development mode (only allow-listed users, max 25).
Login uses OAuth PKCE, so no server or secret is needed. Apple Music needs a paid
Apple Developer account (MusicKit), so it currently opens Apple Music instead.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev       # http://localhost:5173/Fandome/
npm test          # reducer + helpers tests
npm run build     # production build in dist/
```

## Deploy (GitHub Pages, free)

Every push to `main` builds and deploys via `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.
One-time setup: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**.
Free GitHub Pages requires the repository to be **public**.

Site URL: `https://<user>.github.io/Fandome/`

## Stack

React 18 + TypeScript + Vite, `HashRouter` (Pages has no server routing), state in a reducer persisted to `localStorage`.

## Next

- Supabase (free plan) for real accounts, posts, realtime chat and storage — still hosted on GitHub Pages.
- Moderation tools: report → case → decision → appeal → audit log.
- Concert data source (setlist.fm API is free for non-commercial use only).

## Roadmap

Features decided for later and what is waiting on the owner: see [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

- `update/normal/subsdk9` : 通常版 (268 以前の版が取る場所)

eugenia9797/Acne_game.readme:
# 擠痘木頭人

一二三木頭人玩法的擠痘痘網頁小遊戲。你是滿臉痘痘的病人，趁皮膚科醫師背對你打病歷時偷偷擠痘痘。醫師跟著音樂唸「被我抓到你在擠痘痘你就完蛋了」，音樂一唱完她就回頭，手還在臉上就出局。

## 玩法

- 按住痘痘不放就是在擠，放開會保留進度。
- 每輪開頭的兩聲「嗒、嗒」代表這輪的速度（1 倍到 3 倍），整體速度會越來越快。
- 醫師轉一半是假動作，音樂沒停就不用放手。
- 同一次醫師背對期間連續擠破痘痘會累積 COMBO，分數倍率從 ×1.5、×2 一路加到最高 ×5，醫師一回頭就重新計算。
- 護理師路過前會先有腳步聲，她走進畫面後不能擠，後面可能一次來兩個。
- 偶爾會冒出「超大膿痘」，周圍有倒數圈。在倒數結束前擠掉可得 80 分（可疊 COMBO），但膿會噴滿整個螢幕約 10 秒、擋住視線；放著不管會爆炸扣 50 分並留下痘疤。
- 醫師每唱完一輪會冒出 1～2 顆新痘痘，左邊的「不開心」量表爆表（20 顆）就輸。
- 每 100 分升一級，共 30 種痘疤稱號。分數畫面的臉就是被抓到那一刻的樣子：臉上剩下的痘痘、這局留下的痘疤都會保留。
- 分數畫面的「分享」會直接打開手機的分享選單，帶著一張分享圖（痘疤臉、分數、稱號）和一段文字加網址，玩家自己選要傳到哪裡。不支援的瀏覽器會改成顯示圖片（可長按儲存）和複製文字的按鈕。`og.png` 是貼網址時的預覽圖。
- 支援中文、English、日本語、한국어，開始畫面可切換，會自動依手機語言預選。
- 右上角可開關音效、切換語言、結束遊戲；每局結束後回到開始畫面。

## 技術

單一 `index.html`，不需要建置步驟。已裝 Google Analytics（GA4，評估 ID `G-FTBL57HWEV`），除了瀏覽量還會送出遊戲事件：`game_start`、`game_over`、`game_quit`、`share`、`share_action`、`language_change`、`derm_link_click`。分數畫面連到青春痘衛教頁的網址帶有 `?from=acne-game`，在衛教頁那邊也能算出從遊戲過來的人數。畫面用 Canvas 繪製，音樂和音效用 Web Audio API 即時合成，字型來自 Google Fonts（Huninn、Kosugi Maru、Jua、Lilita One）。

## 網址與部署

正式網址是 **https://esheen.skin/acne-game/**。

- 這個 repo 就是正式版：推到 `main` 後，Cloudflare Pages 會部署到 acne-game.pages.dev，大約一分鐘內 esheen.skin/acne-game/ 就會是新版，不需要動網站 repo。
- esheen.skin 那邊（[eugenia9797/follicle-school](https://github.com/eugenia9797/follicle-school)）用 `functions/acne-game/[[path]].js` 把 `/acne-game/` 的請求轉接到 acne-game.pages.dev，並在 Cloudflare 邊緣快取 60 秒。
- 直接打開 acne-game.pages.dev 的玩家，會被頁面開頭的一小段程式導到 esheen.skin/acne-game/。轉接時不受影響，因為那段程式只在瀏覽器裡、網址是 acne-game.pages.dev 時才會執行。

AJBats/daytona-cce95.readme:
# daytona-cce95

Daytona USA Circuit Edition, with the feel of the original Saturn Daytona USA.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cd164af-e87e-4776-865a-485d1c2815b0

No game data is included: you need your own copies of both discs.

## Building

Requires Python 3 and `make`.

1. Put the disc images in `external_resources/`:
   - `Daytona USA (USA)/Daytona USA (USA) (Track 01).bin`
   - `Daytona USA - Circuit Edition (Japan)/Daytona USA - Circuit Edition (Japan).cue`
     and its `(Track 01).bin`
2. `python3 -m venv .venv`
3. `make disc`

Output: `build/disc/cce.cue`.

## Contents

- `patches/`: one byte patch per change, each with a header explaining it
- `tools/`: patching, disc building and analysis tools
- `docs/`: how both games' driving code works, and how each patch was tested

commits.msg:
Attract scene 1 on DUSA's cars: its demo recorded, played back by the wall clock

DUSA drives its demo cars as drones, bumping in turn 1 and switching to a
cheaper mode off camera, so the scene is recorded from DUSA running in the
debugger (tools/attract_record.py, cached in build/attract) rather than
modelled. tools/build_attract.py packs each car's track (13.5 KB) into
DEMOTTL.BIN for VDP2 VRAM; src/attract.c plays them back, every 30 Hz frame
placing each car where DUSA's would be at that moment, hiding it where DUSA
doesn't draw it, and taking CCE's extra AI cars off its list.

Per tick from a fresh boot: cars within 0.0001 units of DUSA's, the camera
within 0.014 units.

CCE turns its tunnel echo on when a front corner reads road type 2 (17
after the corner contact's table). DUSA's ground had no type 2, so no
course echoed since the ground transplant. Polygons at least half under
CCE's type-2 ones, at the same height, now carry it: Three Seven's cover,
the tunnels of Dinosaur Canyon and Seaside. The generated ground no
longer writes type -1 for cells of mixed types (19 polygons on National
Park and Desert City read 128 KB past the type table).

purrcateth/purrcat-reel.readme:
# Purrcat Reel

The portfolio site of Lara (Purrcat), a creative technologist in Istanbul. It covers shorts, shows, podcasts, the Lovebombing community and the Lovebombing app.

Live at https://agentic-scenester.vercel.app (Vercel), with a copy at https://purrcateth.github.io/purrcat-reel/ (GitHub Pages).

## How to change text or links

1. Open `index.html` on GitHub and click the pencil icon to edit.
2. Find the sentence or link you want to change (Cmd+F helps) and edit it.
3. Click "Commit changes". Vercel and GitHub Pages both republish the site in about a minute.

## What is where

- `index.html`: the whole page, with the text, links and styles
- `fonts/`: TAY Bang, TAY Sundae, ChiKareGo2 and Apple Garamond Light, from the Lovebombing design system
- `assets/`: the cloud sky, the flower sticker, the "Take me there" button, the glove cursor, icons and the link preview image (`og.jpg`)

The design comes from the Lovebombing app (https://lovebombing.vercel.app): classic Mac windows, pinstriped title bars and Aqua buttons on a cloud sky.

Tanay3484/slow-start.desc: Slow Start: TCP-style goals for lazy people, with a pixel-art giant to look after (DEV Hacktoberfest 2026 Week 3)
Tanay3484/slow-start.readme:
# Slow Start

A fitness game for lazy people. Your daily step goal and your next workout are set the way TCP sets how
fast a connection may send: **start small, double after each success, grow slowly once you're near your
level, and halve after a miss, never to zero.** A second limit, TabPFN's prediction of what you'll
probably manage tomorrow, stops it asking for too much on a day the history says will be a low one.

You look after **Slumbrock**, a pixel-art stone giant that wakes up as you keep going. The idea comes from
a monster whose ability, also called Slow Start, halves its stats for its first five turns. The creature,
art and names here are original; nothing is taken from Pokémon or Nintendo.

Built for the DEV Hacktoberfest 2026 Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 3: *Slow and Steady*.

**Live:** <https://slowstart.onrender.com> (the game is at `/play`, the field guide at `/guide`).

## Who wrote what

The project was built with an AI coding agent (Claude) under a spec-first workflow
([`specs/`](specs/)). Four core functions were set aside to be written by hand:

| Level | Function | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | The step controller (`backend/slowstart/controllers/steps.py`) | Tanay, from a skeleton |
| H3 | The evaluation statistics (`backend/slowstart/evaluation/stats.py`) | Tanay, from a skeleton |
| H2 | The exercise controller (`backend/slowstart/controllers/exercise.py`) | Claude, handed over by Tanay to make the deadline |
| H4 | The XP and stage rule (`app/src/game/xp.ts`) | Claude, handed over by Tanay to make the deadline |

Everything else (the app, the art, the engine, the backend, the evaluation harness) was written by Claude
and reviewed by Tanay through pull requests.

## What the first evaluation found

On the public Fitbit data (33 people, two months, 2016), on held-out days:

- A fixed 10,000 steps is met on **34.6%** of days.
- The first controller (a 250-step climb after each win) met **86.6%**, but only by asking for **half** of
  what people usually walk. The goal-level guardrail caught it.
- With the climb chosen on a validation window by a rule fixed in advance (1,500 steps), Slow Start meets
  **71.1%** of days while asking for **74%** of a usual day. A plain "your own 30th percentile" meets
  **69.7%** at **79%**. The difference is +1.4 points (95% interval −4.8 to +7.4): **a tie**.
- TabPFN's cap on its own ties the plain percentile too (−3.1 points, −9.1 to +2.2).

So Slow Start is as good as the best simple rule here, not better. What the simple rule cannot do is start
on day one; it needs four weeks of history. The protocol and every table are in
[`results/steps.summary.md`](results/steps.summary.md) and [`results/steps.sweep.md`](results/steps.sweep.md).

## How it works

| TCP | Slow Start |
|---|---|
| Congestion window, grown by the sender | **Window:** the step controller's goal |
| Receiver window, advertised by the receiver | **Cap:** TabPFN's 30th percentile of tomorrow's steps |
| Effective window = min(cwnd, rwnd) | **Goal** = min(window, cap) |
| Slow start: double per success | Double the goal after a met day |
| Loss: halve, set the threshold | Missed day: halve the window, set the threshold |

Code decides every number. TabPFN v2 (open weights, CPU) predicts. Gemma reads a one-line check-in and
speaks as the giant; it never sets a number.

## Layout

```
backend/     Python 3.11, FastAPI: controllers, TabPFN cap, importers, check-in, API
app/         TypeScript + Vite pixel-art game; the same build is wrapped as an Android APK (Capacitor)
scripts/     evaluation and data scripts; every number in the post comes from here
results/     what the scripts wrote
specs/       the brief, requirements, design and tasks (AI-PDLC)
```

## Run it

```bash
python -m venv backend/.venv
backend/.venv/Scripts/pip install -e "backend[dev,model]"   # model = CPU torch + TabPFN
backend/.venv/Scripts/pytest backend
backend/.venv/Scripts/uvicorn --factory slowstart.api:app_factory --reload
```

```bash
cd app && npm install && npm run dev                # the game, with /api proxied to :8000
python scripts/levels.py                            # progress on the four hand-written levels
python -I scripts/evaluate_steps.py --features v1   # the steps evaluation (cached after the first run)
docker build -t slowstart . && docker run -p 8000:8000 slowstart   # one image: app + API + TabPFN
```

The Android app is the same build wrapped with Capacitor: `cd app && npm run build && npx cap sync android`,
then build `app/android` with Android Studio or `gradlew assembleDebug` (set `VITE_API_BASE` to the server's
address first, or the app runs offline-only).

Tests use a fake predictor and need no model, network or GPU. The real predictor downloads TabPFN v2
weights from Hugging Face on first use.

## Known limits

- The public step data is short and old; a backtest cannot show whether a goal changes behaviour.
- The place search uses OpenStreetMap's public Overpass servers. They were not reachable from the
  development machine (the main server answered 406 to every request), so the live query is covered by
  tests and a mocked end-to-end run, not by a live one. The app degrades to "no suggestions".
- The Android build is a debug-signed APK, installed by hand.

## Credits

- **Golden Hour** (same author, Week 1, MIT): the Ollama client pattern and the OpenStreetMap place
  queries are adapted from it.
- **Fitbit Fitness Tracker Data** (Mobius, Kaggle, CC0): the public step history behind the evaluation
  and the bundled cold-start prior.
- **TabPFN v2** (Prior Labs, Apache 2.0 with attribution): the predictor.
- **Gemma** (Google) through Ollama: check-in reader and the giant's voice.

## Licence

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Draxer21/FactoriaCraft.readme:
# FactoryCraft

Mod de NeoForge para Minecraft 26.2, enfocado en herramientas y maquinaria industrial.

## Herramientas disponibles

- **Martillos:** rompen un área de 3×3; cada bloque adicional consume durabilidad.
- **Taladros:** funcionan como picos con minería rápida.
- **Motosierras:** funcionan como hachas para madera.
- Cada herramienta tiene tiers de piedra, hierro, diamante y netherita.
- Incluye texturas pixel art de 64×64 con sombreado, modelos cúbicos 3D, cadena animada en las motosierras, pestaña creativa y nombres en español e inglés.
- **Excavadora industrial:** se coloca y monta con clic derecho; se conduce como un bote y al avanzar excava un frente de 3×3. No rompe contenedores, fluidos ni bloques irrompibles.

## Requisitos

- Java 25
- NeoForge 26.2

Abre el proyecto como Gradle en IntelliJ IDEA o Eclipse. La configuración sigue el [MDK oficial NeoForge 26.2](https://github.com/NeoForgeMDKs/MDK-26.2-NeoGradle).

GiuseppeValguarnera/Duat.readme:
# Duat

Roguelike action nell'oltretomba egizio, fatto con Godot 4.7.

**Stato:** fase 2. C'è la Sala del Giudizio (base tra una discesa e l'altra, con Anubi e il Libro dei Morti) e la Prima Ora completa: 10 stanze, un guardiano a metà, il Traghettatore, Am-heh alla fine, con nemici diversi, ricompense, doni degli dèi, patti di Set e Forma Divina. La grafica è provvisoria (forme semplici) di proposito: prima si rende divertente il gioco, poi arrivano gli sprite.

## La storia

Il protagonista crede di essere lo scriba del faraone Akhet, il cui nome è stato cancellato da ogni pietra d'Egitto, e scende nel Duat per ricomporlo. Nella Sala del Giudizio, sopra il cancello, il cartiglio di Akhet riprende un segno a ogni vittoria. Ogni vittoria sul boss della Prima Ora fa riaffiorare un **Ricordo dello scriba** (nei Papiri di Thoth, in cima; il leggio brilla d'oro finché non lo leggi), e il Traghettatore cambia voce e prezzi man mano che la storia avanza. La trama completa, i colpi di scena e le regole per scrivere le battute sono in [`docs/storia.md`](docs/storia.md): contiene spoiler.

## Come provarlo

1. Apri Godot 4.7, clicca **Import** e scegli il file `project.godot` di questa cartella.
2. Premi **F5** per avviare.

## Giocare dal telefono

La versione web è su **https://giuseppevalguarnera.github.io/Duat/**. Su iPhone: aprila con Safari, poi *Condividi → Aggiungi alla schermata Home* e aprila dall'icona: così va a schermo intero, senza barre del browser (dentro Safari iOS non permette lo schermo intero; se apri il gioco da Safari una schermata lo spiega). Gioca in orizzontale.

Sul telefono il gioco si avvicina un po' e testi, carte e menu sono più grandi (`Fx.ui` in `scripts/fx.gd`); il formato si allarga per riempire anche gli schermi più lunghi del 16:9. Per vedere la versione telefono sul computer: avvia Godot con `-- --mobile`.

**Salvataggio a metà discesa:** all'inizio di ogni stanza la discesa viene salvata. Se chiudi il gioco (o il telefono chiude la pagina), al prossimo avvio riparti dall'inizio di quella stanza. Morte, vittoria e abbandono cancellano il salvataggio.

Sul telefono: levetta virtuale a sinistra (appare dove appoggi il pollice), a destra l'arma (tieni premuto), scatto, Occhio di Horus e Forma Divina, in alto pausa e doni. Mentre ti muovi colpisci nella direzione in cui vai, con un aiuto alla mira se c'è un nemico più o meno davanti; da fermo la mira va da sola sul nemico più vicino (si può spegnere: Opzioni, *Mira automatica*). Nella Sala il pulsante grande diventa *Azione*; nei menu si tocca direttamente.

Per aggiornare la versione web dopo una modifica: `tools/deploy_web.sh /percorso/di/Godot` (serve il modello di esportazione *Web* di Godot 4.7.2).


**Aggiornamenti senza reinstallare:** quando esce una versione nuova, nella Sala, in basso a destra (sul telefono sopra il pulsante *Azione*), lampeggia piano la scritta *Nuova versione, aggiorna!*: toccarla apre le Opzioni sulla voce giusta. Solo nella Sala, non durante la discesa, perché aggiornare la farebbe perdere. *Aggiorna il gioco* scarica la versione nuova e riapre il gioco: i progressi restano, perché l'app non viene cancellata. (Su iPhone, cancellare l'app dalla schermata Home cancella anche il salvataggio.) Funziona così: `tools/deploy_web.sh` scrive un numero di versione nella pagina e in `version.txt`; la pagina (`web/shell.html`) li confronta all'avvio e ogni 5 minuti; `scripts/updater.gd` lo mostra nel gioco.
## Comandi

| Azione | Tastiera e mouse | Controller |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Muoverti | WASD o frecce | Levetta sinistra |
| Mirare | Mouse | Levetta destra |
| Khopesh (tieni premuto per la combo) | Clic sinistro o J | RB (o X) |
| Scatto (invulnerabile) | Spazio, Shift o K | LB o A |
| Occhio di Horus | Clic destro o L | RT (o Y) |
| Forma Divina (quando il Sekhem è pieno) | Q | LT |
| Vedi i tuoi doni (mette in pausa) | Tab | Select |
| Mostra/nascondi hitbox | F1 | |
| Parla / apri il Libro (nella Sala) | E | Y |
| Pausa (nella Sala: opzioni) | Esc o P | Start |
| Torna alla Sala (dopo morte o vittoria) | R | Start |

**Lo scatto ha due cariche:** due scatti di fila, poi una pausa di 1,2 secondi dall'ultimo prima che tornino tutte e due (i doni e il capitolo 56 accorciano la pausa, mai sotto 0,6 secondi). Le cariche sono i due puntini sotto i piedi del personaggio: pieni = pronte, si riempiono man mano durante la pausa, e un piccolo lampo avvisa quando tornano. Prima si poteva scattare ogni mezzo secondo: nessun attacco faceva paura.

## Aspetto: il protagonista, la luce, i colori

**Il protagonista** crede di essere uno scriba: porta alla cintura la tavolozza con i due pozzetti d'inchiostro (nero e rosso), ha gli occhi con il kohl e il gonnellino di lino con la cintura d'oro. Ma in testa ha il *khat* a righe blu e oro, il copricapo della gente comune che ricorda il nemes dei faraoni, e un mantello scuro e logoro; il collare blu e oro lo fa risaltare nella penombra. Cammina davvero (gambe e braccia che si alternano, di profilo quando va di lato), durante lo scatto lascia due scie, e nella **Forma Divina** il khat diventa per un attimo il nemes dorato con l'ureo sulla fronte: un indizio per chi conosce l'Egitto (`_draw_hero` in `scripts/player.gd`).

**La luce** è vera (le luci 2D di Godot, `scripts/atmos.gd`): una penombra leggera di fondo, calda nelle stanze e blu notte nella Sala; torce e bracieri fanno pozze di luce che tremolano; le colonne fanno ombra (solo per i bracieri e le lampade della Sala, perché ogni luce con ombra costa e il telefono deve reggere); le porte brillano del colore della loro ricompensa; attorno al personaggio c'è una luce debole che lo tiene sempre visibile; i bordi dello schermo sfumano nel buio e nell'aria c'è polvere sospesa. Nella Sala si illumina ciò che conta: la luna dal cancello sulla bilancia, lampade calde su Anubi, sul Libro e sui Papiri. Il buio è atmosfera, non un ostacolo: le chiazze chiare sul pavimento (la sabbia) ora sono scure, perché sembravan

ntwyman/32blit-chuckie-egg.readme:
# Chuckie Egg for 32blit

![Build](https://github.com/ntwyman/32blit-chuckie-egg/workflows/Build/badge.svg)

A work-in-progress port of the classic Chuckie Egg, originally developed in
[ntwyman/32blit-beta](https://github.com/ntwyman/32blit-beta/tree/a6f2bce8b749c0004990718a892a6ca9fcd325d4/examples/chuckie-egg)
and moved here (built on the
[32blit boilerplate](https://github.com/32blit/32blit-boilerplate)) to build
against the current [32Blit SDK](https://github.com/32blit/32blit-sdk).

## Credits

Chuckie Egg is the original game by A & F Software. This port is based on Paul
Brook's C source, [Chuckie Egg](https://github.com/pbrook/Chuckie-Egg),
released under the GNU GPL v3. A read-only copy of that source, pinned to one
commit, is in [`third_party/pbrook-chuckie-egg/`](https://github.com/ntwyman/32blit-chuckie-egg/tree/main/third_party/pbrook-chuckie-egg).
The level and sprite data in `levels.cpp` and `sprites.cpp` come from Paul
Brook's `leveldata.c` and `spritedata.c`.

## License

This port is released under the GNU GPL v3, the same license as the C source it
is based on. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Each source file carries an SPDX header
that credits Paul Brook and this port.

The port changes the original as follows.

* It is C++ on the 32Blit SDK. The original's SDL, OpenGL, and ncurses front
  ends are not used.
* It draws the game from a 32Blit sprite sheet, not from the original's
  renderers and 3D models.
* It does not play the original's sound yet.

## Building

For local builds this is:
```
mkdir build
cd build
cmake -D32BLIT_DIR=/path/to/32blit-sdk/ ..
```

### VS Code Dev Container

The `.devcontainer` folder defines a Linux (Ubuntu 24.04) development
container with the 32blit SDK (`/opt/32blit-sdk`), the Pico SDK
(`/opt/pico-sdk`), the PicoVision libraries (`/opt/picovision`), the 32blit
tools (built from source), SDL2, `gcc-arm-none-eabi`, Emscripten, the GitHub
CLI (`gh`) and the [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) CLI
preinstalled. Claude Code's and `gh`'s logins and settings are kept in Docker
volumes, so they survive rebuilds.

With Docker and the VS Code [Dev Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers)
extension installed, run "Dev Containers: Reopen in Container". CMake Tools
is preconfigured; pick a kit to choose the target:

* the detected GCC kit for local (SDL) builds
* "32Blit" for device builds
* "PicoSystem" for PicoSystem builds (produces a `.uf2`; to flash, hold X
  while powering on and copy it to the `RPI-RP2` drive)
* "Emscripten" for web builds (serve the build directory with
  `python3 -m http.server 8000`; the port is forwarded)

From the terminal, `cmake ..` finds the SDK automatically for local and
device builds. For PicoSystem, pass the toolchain:

```
cmake .. -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=/opt/32blit-sdk/pico.toolchain
```

Other RP2040 boards can be selected with `-DPICO_BOARD=` (e.g.
`pimoroni_picovision`, which uses the preinstalled PicoVision libraries), and
RP2350 boards with `pico2.toolchain`.

Web builds need the SDK passed explicitly, as the Emscripten toolchain only
searches its own sysroot for packages:

```
emcmake cmake .. -D32BLIT_DIR=/opt/32blit-sdk
```

The SDK/tools/Pico SDK/PicoVision revisions and Emscripten install can be
changed via the build `args` in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`.

Note that Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows can't pass USB devices through, so
`32blit flash` only works from the container on a Linux host (see the
`runArgs` comment in `devcontainer.json`). Elsewhere, copy the `.blit` file to
the device or flash it from the host.

Platform/Editor specific insctuctions [can be found in the main 32blit repo](https://github.com/32blit/32blit-sdk#you-will-need)
(For Visual Studio, you should follow the "Option 2" instructions, as the boilerplate does not contain a solution file)

fix(live): release held keys when drive.sh keys is interrupted

cmd_keys sent keydown, slept, then sent keyup with no cleanup. A
standalone `drive.sh keys` that received INT or TERM mid-hold left the

and golden still run their cleanup. On a signal the handler restores

status as before.

bkhiron-dot/Hironic-games.readme:
# Hardline MTB

A downhill mountain bike game for the browser, built with Three.js.

## Play locally

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the address Vite prints: the home page is the game, and `/v1.html` is the original version.

## Run the tests

```
npm test
```

The tests check every jump still lands smoothly at the speeds we tuned it for, that the trail keeps v1's shape, that the ground has no cliffs, and that a scripted rider can drop in at the trailhead and ride to the finish.

## Make your own trail

Trails are plain data in `src/trails/`. Copy `flow-monster.js`, change the numbers (wiggle, width, slope, jumps, splits, difficulty) and add it to `src/trails/index.js`; `npm test` checks it and says what to fix if something doesn't fit together. For now the game rides one trail at a time (Flow Monster), picked in `src/main.js`.

## Working on it with Claude Code

Open a terminal in this folder and run `claude`. Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` for the project background, tuned numbers and the roadmap. `KICKOFF.md` has the first message to send.

## Play online (GitHub Pages)

Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`: it runs the tests, builds with Vite and publishes `dist/` to
https://bkhiron-dot.github.io/Hironic-games/ (the game; v1 at `/Hironic-games/v1.html`).

**Branches**: `main` is the live game. New work is merged into `next` first. To try it out, open a pull request from `next` into `main` with the `preview` label and play the preview link. Merging that pull request releases it to the live game.

**Previews**: add the label `preview` to a pull request and the workflow also publishes that pull request at `https://bkhiron-dot.github.io/Hironic-games/preview/pr-<number>/` (it comments the link on the pull request). It's rebuilt on every push while the label is on; remove the label or close the pull request and it's taken down. Use it for bigger or riskier changes you want to play on a phone before merging. (Previews only work once this workflow is on main, and only for pull requests from this repository.)

One-off setup in GitHub: **Settings -> Pages -> Build and deployment -> Source: GitHub Actions**. Pages on a private repo needs a paid GitHub plan; the published site is public either way.

Deploy: don't let a merged release PR cancel the publish of main

Merging release PRs #14 and #22 (labelled preview) started two runs in
the same second: the push to main and the PR "closed" run. Both build
the whole site in one concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, so the
closed run cancelled main's publish. It happened to build main itself,
so the live game updated, but only by luck of timing.

A pull request merged into main now skips the build: the push to main
rebuilds everything, and closed previews drop out because only open
labelled PRs are built. Takes effect once this reaches main.

Fix black dirt and trunks on phones: keep painted textures as pixels

Ben's phone (Android Chrome, live game): the dirt, gum trunks and fence
tape drew black. Those are exactly the textures painted on a canvas.
Likely cause: a phone drops the page's WebGL context when you switch
tabs or apps and can wipe hidden canvases to save memory; on restore
Three.js re-uploads each texture from its canvas, and a wiped one is
black.

Painted textures are now copied into memory once (a DataTexture, rows
flipped, smooth and mipmapped like before), so a restore always has the
real pixels. Desktop render is pixel-identical; after a forced context
loss and restore it still draws correctly.

Jakusukaj/Whistle-game.readme:
# Whistle

A living-room party game. Everyone uses their own phone. Take turns whistling a classic song shown only on your phone; the others guess out loud or by typing. Your time is your score, lowest total wins.

## Run it on your computer (optional)
    npm install
    npm start
Open http://localhost:3000. The microphone only works on https (or localhost), so for phones use the hosted version below.

## Put it online (Render, free)
1. Create a free GitHub account and a new empty repository.
2. Upload every file in this folder to it (not node_modules): Add file > Upload files.
3. Create a free Render account, choose New > Web Service, and connect that repository.
4. Settings: Runtime Node, Build Command `npm install`, Start Command `npm start`, Instance type Free.
5. When it deploys, Render gives you an https address. Open it on every phone.

The free tier sleeps when idle, so the first visit after a quiet spell takes about 30 seconds to wake. Open it a minute before game night.

## Playing
One person taps Host a game and shares the 4 letter code. Everyone else taps Join room. Allow the microphone when asked; typing always works as a backup.

## Changing things
Songs: edit songs.js (title, artist, difficulty). Defaults (rounds, 60s cap, shuffle penalty, multipliers): top of game.js.

## Tests
`npm test` runs the matcher and game rule tests.

Whysodeep1994/strawhat-simulator.readme:
# Strawhat Simulator

An unofficial, open-source simulator for the One Piece Card Game.

> **Not affiliated with Bandai.** This is a free, non-commercial fan project. "ONE PIECE" and the
> One Piece Card Game are trademarks of their owners. Card data lives in a separate repository;
> see [docs/CARD_ASSETS.md](docs/CARD_ASSETS.md).

## Goals

1. **Rules accuracy:** match the official Comprehensive Rules, proven by automated tests.
2. **Online multiplayer:** a server runs the game, so hidden cards stay hidden.
3. **Easy updates:** new sets, errata, and banlists are data, not new code.
4. **Friendly and modern:** clean UI, deck builder, tutorial.
5. **Fast:** quick to load, light on resources.

## Status

The rules engine works, and a playable game runs in the browser: you against a simple computer
opponent, with the official cards and art from
[strawhat-card-data](https://github.com/Whysodeep1994/strawhat-card-data), on a table laid out
like the official playmat. Each player can upload a picture to use as their playmat. See [PROJECT_LOG.md](PROJECT_LOG.md) for what's done and what's next,
and [docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md](docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md) for which rules are tested.

## Project layout

| Folder            | What it holds                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/engine` | The rules engine: pure game logic, no graphics.  |
| `packages/web`    | The browser app: game board and computer player. |
| `docs`            | Contributor docs, asset policy, rules questions. |
| `.github`         | Automatic checks (CI) and issue/PR templates.    |

## Developing

You need [Node.js 22](https://nodejs.org/) and [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation).

```sh
pnpm install   # download the tools
pnpm check     # format check, lint, typecheck, and tests
pnpm test      # tests only
pnpm coverage:rules  # rebuild docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md
pnpm --filter @strawhat/web dev  # play in your browser at the address it prints
pnpm build     # build everything; the game becomes packages/web/dist/strawhat-simulator.html
```

The app needs the card data next to it. Clone
[strawhat-card-data](https://github.com/Whysodeep1994/strawhat-card-data) and copy its cards,
decks and images into the app (they are not stored in this repo):

```sh
node packages/web/scripts/card-data.mjs ../strawhat-card-data
```

The single-file build loads them from a `card-data` folder beside it, so serve both from the
same place.

`pnpm check` also runs automatically before every commit.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## License

[GNU AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE). Anyone may use, change, and share this code. If you run a
modified version as an online service, you must share your changes under the same license.

kdrgny-dev/kervan.readme:
# Kervan

Nimble Quest tarzı snake + otomatik savaş roguelite. Kahraman kafileni ızgarada yönet, kahramanlar kendiliğinden saldırsın, dalgalara dayan, kazandığın altınla kafileni güçlendir.

Web (tarayıcı) ve masaüstü (macOS, Windows, Linux) aynı koddan çıkar. Tasarım dokümanı: [docs/GDD.md](docs/GDD.md).

## Kontroller

| | Klavye | Gamepad | Dokunmatik |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yön | Ok tuşları / WASD | D-pad / sol çubuk | Kaydır |
| Onay, tekrar | Boşluk / Enter / R | A | Butonlar |
| Duraklat | Esc / P | Start / B | Sağ üstteki II |
| Tam ekran | F11 | — | Ayarlar |

## Geliştirme

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5190
npm test             # birim testleri + denge bekçisi
npm run balance      # bot ile senaryo başına 40 tur, denge tablosu
npm run build        # dist/ içine web sürümü
```

## Masaüstü (Tauri 2)

Yerelde derlemek için [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) gerekir (macOS'ta Xcode Command Line Tools da).

```bash
npm run desktop:dev     # pencerede geliştirme
npm run desktop:build   # src-tauri/target/release/bundle/ altına kurulum dosyaları
```

İkon kaynağı `src-tauri/app-icon.svg`; değiştirirsen `npx tauri icon src-tauri/app-icon.svg` ile yeniden üret.

## Sürüm çıkarma

1. `package.json` ve `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` içindeki `version` alanını artır.
2. Etiket at ve gönder: `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`
3. **Release** iş akışı macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel), Windows ve Linux kurulum dosyalarını ve itch.io için web zip'ini derleyip **taslak** bir GitHub Release'e koyar. Kontrol edip yayınla.

macOS ve Windows sürümleri şimdilik imzasız: kullanıcı ilk açılışta güvenlik uyarısını onaylamalı. İmzalama için Apple Developer hesabı ve Windows kod imzalama sertifikası gerekir.

## Web yayını

**Web** iş akışı `main`'e her push'ta testleri çalıştırıp siteyi GitHub Pages'e yükler. Bir kez repo ayarlarından **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions** seçilmeli. (Private repolarda Pages ücretli plan ister.)

itch.io için: sürümdeki `kervan-web-vX.Y.Z.zip` dosyasını HTML5 oyun olarak yükle; dosya yolları göreli olduğu için alt dizinde de çalışır.

## Yapı

```
src/sim/      Saf oyun mantığı (Phaser'dan bağımsız, test edilir)
src/data/     Denge tabloları
src/meta/     Kayıt, dükkan, ekonomi
src/scenes/   Phaser sahneleri
src/render/   Sprite'lar, efektler
src/audio/    WebAudio ses efektleri ve müzik (dosyasız)
tools/        Denge botu ve simülatörü
src-tauri/    Masaüstü paketleme
```

# Lock Desk

A fantasy basketball assistant for the Sleeper league **we back (TBK)**, built around Sleeper's Lock-In mode.

Live site: https://rwalwan.github.io/fantasybasketball/

## What it does

- **Locks:** when to lock or wait in each slot. Uses optimal stopping and a joint slot assignment, and checks each call against your win chance in the matchup.
- **Week:** today's lineup vs. the plan, same-day relief swaps, and the full game grid.
- **Moves / Waivers / Trades:** adds with the best drop and trade ideas, valued by each player's remaining schedule in Lock-In.
- **Research / Insights:** every player's games this week, matchup context, role trends, and why games went the way they did.
- **News / Experts:** a polite crawler that respects robots.txt and reads public expert sources. Each expert's calls are graded against what actually happened.

## How it runs

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `app/` (Python) | Data, memory store, context model, news, and expert grading |
| `site/` | Static app that recomputes in the browser every minute |
| `tools/` | Moves, the AI model eval, and the site health check |
| `worker/` | Cloudflare Worker: lineup snapshots and the 15-minute job trigger |
| `.github/workflows/` | Update job every 15 minutes, worker deploy, and the AI model eval |

Saved state lives on the `state` branch.

## Credits

Built by Ryan Alwan ([@rwalwan](https://github.com/rwalwan)) with Claude (Anthropic).

Professor-Jeff/tictactoe-nn.readme:
# Tic-Tac-Toe — Three Ways to Build a Player

**Live (play in the browser):** https://professor-jeff.github.io/tictactoe-nn/

Companion to [pick-activity](https://github.com/Professor-Jeff/pick-activity) for COMP 138.
The same tiny neural network, written from scratch in NumPy, learns tic-tac-toe
two different ways — and a classic search algorithm plays it a third way.

1. **Minimax** — the deterministic program. Looks ahead and plays perfectly.
2. **Supervised network** — trained on positions that minimax labels. Never sees minimax.
3. **Reinforcement network** — the *same* network, trained only from wins and losses. No labels at all.

## In the browser

Open the live link. Press **Train** under *Supervised* (about 10 seconds) and under
*Reinforce* (about a minute), watch the learning curves, press **Evaluate all players**,
then pick an opponent and play. `index.html` is a single self-contained file; edit it
and push to `main` and GitHub Pages redeploys within about a minute.

## Run the Python version

```bash
pip install numpy
python3 tictactoe_nn.py
```

That trains both networks (about 3 minutes), prints how each does against a
random player and against minimax, then lets you play the reinforcement network.

Options:

```bash
python3 tictactoe_nn.py --mode supervised     # just the supervised network (~35 s)
python3 tictactoe_nn.py --mode reinforce      # just the reinforcement network
python3 tictactoe_nn.py --rounds 3000         # quicker, weaker reinforcement training
python3 tictactoe_nn.py --no-play             # skip the interactive game
```

## The one line that changes

Supervised training pushes the output toward the correct answer:

```python
dz2 = probs - Y                      # predicted minus CORRECT
```

Reinforcement training pushes it toward whatever the network actually did,
scaled by how the game ended (+1 win, -1 loss, 0 draw):

```python
dz2 = G * (probs - chosen)           # predicted minus WHAT I DID, scaled
```

Everything below that line — backpropagation and the weight update — is identical.

# BioglowRX Sciences Learning — website (Phase 1)

A plain static website: no login, no database, no build step. Upload the whole folder as it is.

## What's inside

```
index.html                    Hub home page (5 subjects, featured game, "continue where you left off")
subjects/<subject>/index.html Chemistry, Anatomy & Physiology, Pharmacology, Nutrition, Health & Wellness
games/element-rush/           Element Rush (runs on the shared engine)
engine/                       Shared code: game formats, rewards, sounds, illustrations, hub pages
data/catalog.js               Subjects, chapters, games and their status (Live / Up next / Soon)
data/element-rush.js          All Element Rush content (118 elements)
data/README.md                How to write a new game
assets/                       Design tokens, component styles, favicon
```

## Putting it online

1. Upload everything in this folder to your host, keeping the folder structure.
   It works at the root of a domain (bioglowrx.com) or in a sub-folder (gafferiq.com/learn): all links are relative.
2. Open the address of `index.html` in a browser. That's the hub.
3. No server settings are needed. HTTPS is recommended (most hosts do this automatically).

You can also preview it before uploading: double-click `index.html` on your computer.
Note: "continue where you left off" and best scores are saved per browser and per device.

## Updating the live site

Before every push run `python3 tools-bump-version.py`: it stamps the script and style links with a version so browsers load the new files at once (GitHub Pages otherwise lets them keep old copies for up to 10 minutes).

## Changing content

- **Fix a fact or an everyday example:** edit the text in `data/element-rush.js`.
- **Change a chapter's status or title:** edit `data/catalog.js`.
- **Change the home-page carousel:** edit `featuredList` at the top of `data/catalog.js` (one entry per slide; it switches every 6 seconds and pauses on hover, focus or the pause button).
- **Add a game:** follow `data/README.md`. You need one data file, one copied page and one line in the catalog.

## Not in Phase 1 (by plan)

- Ads, consent banner and privacy page: Phase 3.
- New game content (Bone Rush, Drug Class Sort, Nutrient Rush, pH Patrol): Phase 2.
- All game formats are now built: Study notes, Card Explorer, Quick Quiz, Find It, Sort It, Match Pairs, Sequence, True or Myth, Build It, Case Files and Calculator Challenge (see `data/README.md`).

## XP and levels

Every game and lab shares one XP total (saved per browser, `bgx_xp`). 20 levels from Lab Trainee to Doctor Researcher;
the table, XP rules and level-up pop-up live in `engine/core.js` (`BGX.LEVELS`, `BGX.xp`). Change a level's name,
line or XP threshold there. The header chip and the hub card open the full list of levels.

# Alpha Scout · Lock-In

**Live app:** https://nattieon.github.io/alpha-scout-app/

Lock-or-pass calls for Sleeper **Lock-In** fantasy basketball. Type your Sleeper
username, pick your league, and the page pulls everything from Sleeper:

- your matchup, your lineup, and your opponent's lineup
- your league's own scoring (bonuses included)
- every player's games this week, with per-game projections (Rotowire via Sleeper)
- injury tags and back-to-backs

From that it shows four things:

- **Win probability** for the week.
- **Decide now:** your players whose game just ended and who still have games left.
  Each gets **LOCK** or **PASS**, the score he needs (the bar), and your win odds
  either way.
- **Tonight:** the score to lock at for each player who plays today. There's also a
  "what if he finishes with…" box for live games.
- **Lineups:** both teams' slots, marked locked / your call / open / final, with each
  slot's projected value.

Nothing to install, no accounts, no server. Everything runs in your browser
against Sleeper's public read-only API. Settings and your lock marks stay in your
browser only.

## How the call is made
The bar is an optimal-stopping value. It's the expected final score of the slot if
you pass, playing the rest of the week optimally:

```
V_last = (1 - p_last) · μ_last                        # an open slot takes his last game, even a DNP
V_i    = p_i · max(0, V_{i+1}) + (1 - p_i) · E[max(X_i, V_{i+1})],   X_i ~ N(μ_i, σ_i)
```

- **μᵢ** is that game's projection, scaled by how he has actually played against his
  projections (shrunk, capped at ±25%).
- **His score shape** comes from his own game log: last season plus this one, scored with
  your league's rules, as ratios to his average. It's blended with 8 prior games so a
  short log can't go wild, which gives boom-or-bust players higher bars than steady ones.
  Every score is also shown as a **percentile of his recent games**.
- **pᵢ** is the chance he sits, built per player from his own log (`js/availability.js`).
  The reasons combine as `1 − Π(1 − hᵢ)`:
  - **Ordinary-game rate:** `(sat + 20 × 4%) / (games + 20)`. Injury stretches (5+ straight
    missed games) and the 15 games after them are left out. This season counts double.
  - **Back-to-back pairs:** `q = (rested one night + 8 × 19%) / (pairs + 8)`, and which night
    `s = (night-2 rests + 6 × 73%) / (rests + 6)`. Night 1 gets `q·(1−s)`. Night 2 is linked
    to night 1: `q·s / (1 − q·(1−s))` once he has played night 1, and ~0 extra if he sat it.
    The league figures (19% / 73%) come from last season.
  - **Durability:** `0.04 × share of his team's games missed in the last 82`.
  - **Return ramp:** after a 10+ game absence (one that ran into the offseason only counts if it was 40+ games), `+60% × (1 − games back / 15)` on back-to-back
    rest (25 games after a 40+ game absence). Each back-to-back he plays both nights of
    halves what's left. Also `+3% × ramp` on other games.
  - **Sleeper injury tag** (Questionable 45%, Out 97%…) fading 30% per game, and 85% if the
    projection has him sitting.
  - **"Sits B2Bs?" checkbox:** sets his back-to-back rest chance to 95% until you uncheck it.
  The lock recursion branches on night 1 (played vs sat), so the bar for night 1 uses the
  raised night-2 risk.

**Bench swaps** (`js/swaps.js`). Any open slot can go to a bench player, or another open
starter, before his next game. Following Sleeper's rules, only starters' games count, and
an open slot takes the final game of whoever is in it at week's end. The app picks the
best player for each open slot for the rest of the week: positions respected (G = PG/SG,
F = SF/PF, UTIL = anyone), each player used once, solved exactly with the Hungarian
algorithm. A slot's lock bar is therefore what keeping it open is worth with your whole
bench available. **Swaps before tip-off** lists the moves the calls assume you'll make.
Your opponent's swaps are a setting (**Opponent's bench swaps**), off by default. When it's
on, his open slots get the same treatment, which lowers your win probability against a
deep bench.

**Win-probability mode** (the default) also uses your opponent's slots. Locked
scores count exactly; the rest are modeled the same way. The call picks whichever
of LOCK and PASS gives the higher chance to win the week, so with a safe lead it
locks a bit early, and when behind it chases upside. The rule was picked by a Monte
Carlo bake-off of seven strategies; details are in the Alpha Scout repo.

## What Sleeper doesn't tell us
Sleeper reports each slot's current score, not whether it's locked:

- If a slot shows an **earlier** game's score, it's locked. The app detects that.
- If it shows his **latest** game, it's ambiguous until his next game starts.
- Every slot on both lineups has a picker. By the rules, only a player's **latest** game can
  still be locked. An earlier game counts only if you locked it before his next game, so the
  picker has two jobs:
  - **Locked:** record a lock made at the time. Any completed game can be picked, which
    lets you catch up after the fact, or copy your opponent's lock icons from Sleeper.
  - **Not locked:** about his latest game. Either *he started, still lockable* (the app makes
    the call), or *on my bench, can't lock*. Sleeper doesn't keep past lineups, so a game
    played from your bench looks lockable until you say so. The "He wasn't in my starting
    lineup" box on his card does the same.
  - **Auto** uses what Sleeper's numbers imply. An opponent's score above his bar is
    assumed locked.
- **Banked** counts only certain locks and the ones you entered.
- **Proj** (top) counts locked slots at their score. Every other slot counts
  Sleeper's projection for his next game, in your scoring. Settings can switch this
  to the expected final, which includes future locks and sit risk. The win
  probability always uses the full model.
- **Bench** players are listed under each lineup with their games and next-ga

# Aksa si Pemadam Cilik 🚒

Game petualangan pixel art untuk belajar berhitung (usia ±6 tahun).
Aksa, pemadam kebakaran cilik, dan Ara, mobil pemadam kebakaran mini sahabatnya, menolong warga Desa Ceria dari ulah Api Jahil dengan menjawab soal berhitung.

## Isi Wilayah 1: Desa Ceria

Dunia top-down ala Pokemon. Ketuk tanah untuk berjalan, Ara mengikuti di belakang. Warga yang butuh bantuan ditandai ❗; ketuk warganya (atau tombol **A**) untuk bicara. Semua soal dikerjakan dalam **battle**.

Enam masalah muncul bersamaan dan boleh diselesaikan dengan urutan bebas:

| Masalah | Warga | Materi |
|---|---|---|
| Kucing di Pohon | Bu Ani | Penjumlahan ≤ 10 (menyambung tangga) |
| Api di Tumpukan Daun | Api Jahil | Penjumlahan ≤ 20 |
| Toko Roti Terbakar | Pak Budi | Pengurangan ≤ 20 |
| Tangki Truk Kosong | Pak Joko | Tambah/kurang + **1 soal perkalian** (hasil ≤ 15) |
| Anak Ayam Lepas | Bu Siti | 1 soal penjumlahan ≤ 10 |
| Hidran Bocor | Kakek Udin | 1 soal pengurangan ≤ 20 |

Setelah keenamnya selesai, **Raja Api Jahil** muncul di depan Balai Desa sebagai boss terakhir (campuran tambah & kurang).

- Tidak ada "kalah". Battle berisi 3 pilihan jawaban. Kalau salah, soal langsung diganti soal baru supaya anak benar-benar menghitung, bukan menebak.
- Ara (mobil pemadam mini) jadi asisten: setiap kali satu masalah selesai, saat game dibuka, atau saat Ara diketuk, Ara mengingatkan tinggal berapa warga lagi dan siapa saja.
- Masalah yang sudah selesai bisa dimainkan lagi lewat **Latihan lagi** untuk mengejar 3 bintang.
- Hadiah: lencana + aksesori Ara (sirene ganda, stiker bintang, kacamata keren, velg emas, bendera pahlawan) yang bisa dipakai/dilepas di **Koleksi**.
- Musik latar chiptune (lagu desa & lagu battle) dan efek suara, bisa dimatikan dari tombol 🎵 atau ⚙️ Pengaturan. Tidak ada narasi suara.
- Progres dan posisi Aksa tersimpan otomatis di perangkat.

## Wilayah 2: Kampung Hijau — "Perjalanan Menuju Porseni" (Juz Amma)

Dipilih dari layar judul kapan saja. Aksa dan Ara menjemput teman-teman TPA yang kesulitan, murajaah bersama, lalu semuanya tampil di panggung Porseni.

| Teman | Masalah | Surat untuk murajaah |
|---|---|---|
| Dika | Ban sepeda kempes di sawah | An-Nas, Al-Falaq, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Lahab, An-Nashr |
| Salma | Kehujanan, payung rusak di pasar | Al-Kafirun, Al-Kautsar, Al-Ma'un, Quraisy, Al-Fil |
| Umar | Takut menyeberang jembatan | Al-Humazah, Al-'Ashr, At-Takatsur, Al-Qari'ah, Al-'Adiyat |
| Aisyah | Membantu Nenek menjemur padi | Az-Zalzalah, Al-Bayyinah, Al-Qadr, At-Tin, Al-Insyirah |

- Bersama teman: **Sambung Ayat** (dengar ayat, pilih ayat berikutnya) dan **Tebak Surat** (dengar awal surat, pilih namanya). Setiap pilihan bisa didengar dengan tombol 🔊.
- Di panggung Porseni (Ustadz Hasan, setelah keempat teman ikut): **Susun Ayat** (Al-Fatihah & satu surat pendek) dan **Kata yang Hilang**.
- Teman yang sudah dijemput ikut berjalan di belakang rombongan.
- Teks Latin dari **equran.id (Kemenag RI)**, ditampilkan sebagai bacaan waqaf (tanpa akhiran dalam kurung). Audio: **Syaikh Mahmud Khalil Al-Husary (Mu'allim)** dari everyayah.com, disimpan di `audio/husary-muallim/`.
- Data dibuat dengan `node tools/ambil-juzamma.mjs` (di lingkungan dengan proxy: `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node tools/ambil-juzamma.mjs`). Mohon teks dicek ulang oleh orang tua/guru.

## Game kedua: Penjaga Rimba 🦉🐻

Folder `penyelamat/` → `https://radmahardika.github.io/Game-Aca/penyelamat/`

Game penyelamatan first person 3D pixel di hutan malam untuk **anak + orang tua di dua iPad**. **Tutu**, Burung Hantu yang suka membantu, bisa melihat dalam gelap dan menandai hewan dengan ⭐. **Benhat**, Si Beruang Hebat, hampir tidak bisa melihat. Ia membawa alat dari **Pohon Sarang** (tas hanya muat 3 kotak) dan menolong hewan yang posisinya diacak setiap main. Keduanya harus saling bicara.

- **3 level:** Level 1 *Malam Bulan Purnama* (5 hewan, cukup satu alat, tanpa menyeberang sungai), Level 2 *Malam Bulan Separuh* (10 hewan, ada yang butuh 2 alat), Level 3 *Malam Gerimis Berkabut* (15 hewan: kabut, jembatan putus yang harus diperbaiki dengan papan, alat baru gunting tumpul & keranjang, anak ayam yang berlari). Level berikutnya terbuka setelah level sebelumnya selesai.
- **Main berdua:** iPad pertama memilih *Buat ruangan* dan perannya, lalu muncul kode 4 gambar. iPad kedua memilih *Gabung ruangan* dan mengetuk gambar yang sama. Keduanya perlu internet.
- **Main di satu iPad:** gantian peran dengan tombol ⇄.
- Progres tersimpan di iPad pembuat ruangan.

## Main di iPad

1. Buka link GitHub Pages: `https://radmahardika.github.io/Game-Aca/` di **Safari**.
2. Ketuk tombol **Bagikan** (kotak dengan panah ke atas), lalu pilih **Tambahkan ke Layar Utama**.
3. Buka dari ikon "Aksa" di layar utama. Game tampil layar penuh seperti aplikasi.
4. Pegang iPad dalam posisi **mendatar (landscape)**.

Kalau musik tidak terdengar: pastikan mode senyap iPad mati dan volume menyala.

## Mengaktifkan GitHub Pages (sekali saja)

Di halaman repo GitHub: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: Deploy from a branch → Branch: `main` / `(root)` → Save**. Tunggu ±1 menit sampai link aktif.

## Menjalankan di komputer

Tidak perlu build. Jalankan server statis apa saja dari folder ini, misalnya:

```
npx http-server .
```

## Struktur

- `index.html`, `css/style.css`: halaman dan tampilan UI
- `js/sprites.js`: pixel art (Aksa, Ara, warga, Api Jahil, ikon)
- `js/world.js`: partikel, gambar bangunan tampak samping, layar judul
- `js/overworld.js`: peta Desa Ceria top-down, gerak 4 arah, Ara mengikuti, ketuk untuk berjalan
- `js/battle.js`: layar battle ala Pokemon dan bantuan hitung
- `js/missions.js`: cerita, dialog, dan daftar soal tiap masalah
- `js/questions.js`: pembuat soal acak
- `js/audio.js`: efek suara dan musik latar chiptune
- `js/game.js`: alur game (judul, dunia, dialog, hadiah, koleksi, pengaturan)
- `js/kampung.js`: peta & cerita Kampung Hijau
- `js/murajaah.js`: layar murajaah dan panggung Porseni

dickie947/isle-of-ru.readme:
# Isle of Ru

A calm maths adventure for children. Single page, no server, no accounts. Progress is saved in the browser on each device.

## Put it online with GitHub Pages
1. On github.com create a new repository (for example `isle-of-ru`). Public is simplest; Pages on private repos needs a paid plan.
2. Click "Add file" then "Upload files" and drag in everything in this folder: `index.html`, `manifest.webmanifest`, the three `.png` icons, `.nojekyll`, and this `README.md`.
3. Commit the upload.
4. Go to Settings, then Pages. Under "Build and deployment" choose "Deploy from a branch", branch `main`, folder `/ (root)`. Save.
5. After a minute the game is at `https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/isle-of-ru/`.

## On the iPad
Open the link in Safari, tap Share, then "Add to Home Screen". This matters: Safari can delete a website's saved progress after about a week of not using it, but a Home Screen app is not treated that way.

## Moving progress between devices
Progress is not shared automatically. Open the lock button (grown-ups), choose the Settings tab, and tap "Copy save code". On the other device open grown-ups, Settings, paste into "Restore from code" and tap the button. Do this every few weeks as a backup too.

## Updating the game
Replace `index.html` in the repository with the new version. Saves are versioned and are upgraded automatically, so progress is kept, as long as the address stays the same. A new address means a fresh start, because saves live under the address.
