Keep the legs striding when attacking or casting on the move (#186) (#202)

Attacks and casts on the move played on the whole body, so the legs froze in
the swing's stance while the unit kept its speed and slid along the ground.

While a humanoid in Attack or Cast moves faster than 0.3 m/s, the action's
clip now drives `spine_01` and up while the walk, jog or sprint clip for its
speed drives the hips and legs. The upper body then turns about the vertical
toward where the clip's own hips faced it, capped at 60 degrees of chest-to-hip
twist (or the clip's own twist, if more), so side-on stances still aim forward
and whole-body pivots keep a believable spine.

Walk, jog and sprint now share one stride phase that runs on through actions
and speed changes, so the feet never restart mid-step. Kneeling, the downed,
getting up and beasts stay whole-body.

sorin-c/Harbinger-Recomp.readme:
# Harbinger-Recomp

A clean-room, portable reimplementation of **Harbinger** (Silverback
Entertainment, 2003), in the spirit of DevilutionX: modern Windows and Linux
first, other platforms later, with full controller support.

This repository contains **no game data**. You need your own copy of the game;
the engine reads the original `res0.sqh` / `res1.sqh` archives.

## Status

- Step 1, mapping the game: first pass done. See [docs/findings.md](docs/findings.md).
- Step 2, rebuilding the engine: under way. See [docs/engine.md](docs/engine.md).
- What is left, in order: [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md).

What exists so far:

- `.sqh` archive reader and `sqhtool` (list / extract)
- `.gim` image decoder and `gim2tga`
- `Vfs` (archive mounting and the game's path rules)
- Parsers for interface layouts (`.itf`), fonts (`.fnt`), resource indexes
  (`.mgr`), cursors (`.acr`) and the animated button items (`.itm`)
- Audio: `.wav` and `.mp3` decoding, `Harbinger.ini`, `config.cfg`
- `harbinger`, the game: the front end (main menu, character screen,
  Options, Load Game), drawn from the original files, with the menu music and
  sounds, and mouse, keyboard and gamepad input. Play opens the first level
  (floor, walls, objects, characters and music so far) to look around in,
  with the HUD and the inventory screen (CHAR, I or the pad's View button;
  D-pad / stick, A, X and B drive it on a controller, see `docs/inventory.md`)
- Level (`.chk`), brush (`.brs`), gizmo (`.giz`), agent (`.agt`), animation
  (`.anm`) and cutscene script (`.gsc`) parsers, and `levelshot`, which renders a whole level with its
  objects and characters to an image
- `harbinger-viewer`, an SDL3 sprite browser (keyboard or gamepad)
- Gameplay in main so far: walking (mouse, keyboard or gamepad), gear and
  melee and ranged combat, player health and death, enemy AI with melee and
  ranged attacks, spawners, portals and umbilicals between levels (with
  umbilical codes and the Level Selection screen), scripted cutscenes and
  enemy moves, gizmo use (doors, consoles), chest loot, experience and levels
  with the stats panel, the HUD and inventory screen with full controller
  navigation, and NPCs, dialogue and the quest state behind them (`.dlg`,
  `.qst`; the conversation screen with mouse, keys or pad, see
  `docs/dialogue.md`)

```
harbinger --data "C:/Games/Harbinger"
```

Without `--data`, `harbinger` looks for `Harbinger.ini` next to itself and
then in the current folder, so on Windows you can copy `harbinger.exe` and
`SDL3.dll` into your Harbinger folder and double-click it. A ready-built
Windows zip (`harbinger-windows`) is attached to every CI run under the
repository's Actions tab. Your settings are kept in
`%APPDATA%\harbinger-recomp\harbinger\` (`config.cfg`, and `display.ini` for the
window size or fullscreen and the 4:3 or 16:9 widescreen view, set in Options or with Alt+Enter); the game folder is only read.

## Build

```
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja      # fetches SDL3 if it isn't installed
cmake --build build
HARBINGER_DATA="/path/to/Harbinger" ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

Tests that need the original files are skipped when `HARBINGER_DATA` is unset.

## Approach

Every format and behaviour is documented with its evidence and labelled
proven, likely or guessed (see `docs/`). Decompiler output is used only as a
reference and never copied into the source tree.

frederico-kluser/cyberpunk-2077-mods.readme:
# Cyberpunk 2077 Mods

Open-source mods for **Cyberpunk 2077** on PC. Every mod lives in its own folder under [`mods/`](mods/), is written in Redscript, ships as a plain zip that you extract into the game folder, and is covered by the same build, validation and release pipeline. [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) ## Mods | Mod | Version | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | [**Desert Eagle**](mods/DesertEagle) | 0.1.0 | Desert Eagle .50 AE on the Tsunami Nue skeleton and animations: CS:GO timings, maximum Handling, zero spread in any state (it goes where you aim, even running), no attachments. **QUE OTA** (formerly Lethal Headshots): every headshot fired with it kills, with a red label above the crosshair over a killable head. The CS2 model and the CS gunshot (Valve's, non-commercial fan use) ship only in the release zips; the gunshot needs the free REDmod DLC. | | [**Force Push**](mods/ForcePush) | 0.2.0 | V extends the right palm (own first-person animation for both V bodies) and a force wave sweeps 20 m ahead: NPCs ragdoll and fly, vehicles are thrown, loose props jump. Mouse 4 by default (CET → Bindings); a weapon in hand is holstered for the gesture and drawn again. | | [**Grapple Hook**](mods/GrappleHook) | 0.3.0 | Batman-style grappling hook fired from V's left-arm Projectile Launch System: the first click arms the game's own launcher with its aim animation, zoom and crosshair (the arm follows the camera, only the arms show) plus a range label; the second fires a hook up to 100 m that pulls V in up to 4 s along a rope from the launcher. V then clings to the wall with free look until the next hook, a wall leap, a drop or a slow rope descent; a controlled descent avoids fall damage. Mouse 5 aims and fires, Mouse 4 descends (CET → Bindings). Needs TweakXL for the launcher. Tested in game by the owner (0.2: arm, rope, pull, perch, leap, rope descent). | | [**Neurodança**](mods/NeuroDance) | 0.1.0 | Mind hack by braindance: V sits and puts on the BD wreath (the vanilla first-person clip), looks at a person and clicks to see and control that NPC in first person; hops from body to body (L opens the jump crosshair), right-click or look at V to go back. The body has the NPC's health and its armor as a shield, V's money goes with you (vendors work), dying returns you to V, jumping into an enemy starts no fight and every character keeps its own wanted level. L by default (CET → Bindings). Built and verified offline; not yet tested in game. | | [**Log Sentry**](mods/LogSentry) | 0.3.0 | Logging, metrics and the development bridge every mod uses: a logging API for redscript and CET mods (live events, errors as `Erro: … — Solução: …`), game and mod metrics every 5 s, and the MCP server `logsentry` (`.mcp.json`) or `tools/cetbridge.py` to read it all live and run Lua inside the game. Required whenever a mod is built or edited. | ## Requirements - Cyberpunk 2077 for PC, **patch 2.5** (game version `3.0.88.x`). - [redscript](https://github.com/jac3km4/redscript/releases) **0.5.32 or newer** (0.5.32 is the first release that supports the 2.5 script bundle). - Desert Eagle: RED4ext **1.31.0+**, ArchiveXL **1.28.0+** (or 1.28.0-rc.1), TweakXL **1.12.0+** (or 1.12.0-rc.1), Cyber Engine Tweaks **1.38.0+** to give yourself the weapon, the free REDmod DLC for the gunshot. Any RED4ext plugin built before 2.5 closes the game at startup. - Grapple Hook: RED4ext **1.31.0+**, Cyber Engine Tweaks **1.38.0+**, TweakXL **1.12.0+** (the arm launcher), the Phantom Liberty expansion (the rope). - Force Push: RED4ext **1.31.0+**, Cyber Engine Tweaks **1.38.0+**, game launched with `-modded`. - Log Sentry: Cyber Engine Tweaks **1.38.0+**, game launched with `-modded` (below). ## Install a mod The [releases page](https://github.com/frederico-kluser/cyberpunk-2077-mods/releases) has one zip per released mod (`GrappleHook-.zip`, `DesertEagle-.zip`, `LogSentry-.zip`), a pack with all of them (`Cyberpunk2077-Mods-.zip`) and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Each zip mirrors the game folder (no wrapper folder) and carries a bilingual manual (Portuguese and English) — also in [`docs/manual/`](docs/manual/README.md): requirements with links, manual / Vortex / Mod Organizer 2 install, keys, checks, uninstall and troubleshooting. 1. Install the mod's requirements into the Cyberpunk 2077 folder. 2. Extract the zip into the Cyberpunk 2077 folder, merging folders — or install it with Vortex or Mod Organizer 2. 3. Start the game. The Desert Eagle gunshot also needs the free REDmod DLC and a REDmod deploy (see its manual). To uninstall, delete the files the mod's manual lists. From a clone, developers install with `pwsh -File tools/deploy.ps1 -ModId ` plus each mod's own deploy script. ## The CET gate (special launch command) Cyber Engine Tweaks — required by the **LogSentry** diagnostic mod — must load **only** when you deliberately ask for it. A gate wrapper decides before the game starts. Add this to **Steam → Cyberpunk 2077 → Properties → General → Launch options**: ``` "C:\Users\kluse\Tools\cet-gate.bat" %command% -modded ``` > **This is a Steam field value, not a terminal command.** `%command%` is a > placeholder tha

feat(logsentry): add MCP server and logging API for all mods (#112)

The owner asked for LogSentry to be an MCP server for live logs, errors
and metrics, and for every mod to log what it changes through it.

LogSentry 0.3.0:
- Redscript API in its own module, LogSentry.Api (Sentry.Log, Debug,
  Info, Warn, Error, Metric). Mods use it as a soft dependency through
  @if(ModuleExists("LogSentry.Api")); an old 0.2 install or none still
  compiles. Each line goes to FTLog and to a 512-line ring that the CET
  side drains every frame into events.jsonl. The ring lives in a
  ScriptableService, because GetGameInstance() is empty in UI and
  player-state-machine callbacks; a ScriptableSystem ring is the
  fallback.
- CET API: GetMod("LogSentry") returns mod(name) loggers (info, warn,
  error, metric), guard() for callbacks and metric(). The LS global and
  every LS.* helper are kept.
- Every event has lvl, mod and a per-session seq. Errors carry
  "Erro: ... — Solução: ...".
- metrics.jsonl every 5 s: fps, p95 frame time, hitches, events and
  errors per mod, bridge command time, Lua memory and the mods' own
  metrics.

Agent side:
- tools/logsentry_mcp.py: stdlib-only MCP server over stdio, as two
  .mcp.json entries.
  - logsentry (read-only): status, events, wait_event (long-poll),
    logs, errors (every source, grouped), metrics, session_report,
    crash.
  - logsentry-control: run_lua (owner confirms each call), run_test,
    watch, unwatch, watches, tweak, screenshot.
- tools/logsentry_core.py is shared with tools/cetbridge.py. The CLI
  keeps its commands and adds errors, metrics, report and event
  filters.

Mods:
- DesertEagle, ForcePush and GrappleHook get a Log.reds adapter and a
  lazy Lua logger. They log state changes, spawns, items given,
  key actions and errors, plus metrics.
- NeuroDance gets only the agreed adapter edits.
- validate.ps1 now requires the adapters, GetMod("LogSentry") on CET
  sides, and LogSentry in every deploy script.
- The DesertEagle deploy now installs LogSentry.
- The directive is in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md; the details are in
  mods/LogSentry/README.md.

Verified offline:
- redscript lint of all mods together and each alone, and each adapter
  with LogSentry 0.3, 0.2 and none (18/18).
- test_bridge.py: the real init.lua under LuaJIT.
- test_mcp.py: both servers over stdio against a fake game folder, with
  the real init.lua as the game.
- validate.ps1 -Static: 93 checks.
- build.ps1 packages the new files.
Not yet run in

Fixes from an independent review of the merged mod (nothing tested in
the game yet):

- Wanted records: a body left during the 4 s quarantine saved 0 stars
  (the pending stage is used now); the heat limits are read once per
  braindance and restored only at its end, and the restore runs after
  the phase step with Safe always queued, so a switch in the same tick
  can no longer freeze the limits at 0 or leak stars to the new body.
- Quest restrictions: every new body runs the game's replacer
  restrictions on attach, which strip BlockFastTravel/BlockAllHubMenu
  from V; the quest ones are snapshot before the first jump and put
  back, and the mod's own block uses its own instigator.
- A released body is despawned 0.5 s later and only once the player no
  longer controls it; a failed control switch now returns to V with a
  clear message, and the return retries the switch.
- The CET side runs on V's main object, so a vanished body still
  returns to V; pending despawns are dropped on a new game session.
- Health/shield and the death listener wait for the body's stat pools;
  a body that dies during the next jump releases its NPC dead; one
  threshold for listener and poll.
- The clock is the game's sim time (stops in menus and pause).
- Vendors are refused; NPCs in a workspot leave it and the vessel
  retries; a failed copy order no longer corrupts the next copy;
  MoveMoney reports only money that moved.
- Tests: 08 switches inside the quarantine and reports whether police
  exist there; 04/05 spawned NPCs are removed by 09.

fix(grapplehook): aim with the arm launcher, rope points at the hook (#109)

The owner's video of #107 (16:08) showed three problems:

- V's body still showed and did not follow the camera.
- The arm stayed behind when looking around and left the screen.
- The rope stood vertical until V reached the target.

The arm was a gesture in a workspot, and a workspot camera does not
follow the body. The rope and hook entities had no root component, so
the first mesh became the root and the game ignored its rotation.

Changes:
- No workspot. The first click puts a Projectile Launch System in V's
  left hand through the game's own equip request, and the vanilla
  LeftHandCyberware machine plays its equip, aim, zoom and crosshair.
  V's installed PLS is used if there is one; otherwise a TweakXL copy
  (Items.GrappleHookLauncher) enters the inventory and leaves it when
  the arm lowers.
- While the mod owns the launcher, wrapped decisions keep it aiming,
  never fire a PLS round and put it away at the end. GetActiveCyberware
  returns it so the vanilla unequip only empties the left hand.
- A pending equip is cancelled when the arm lowers, and the mod only
  lets go once the launcher is out of the hand and the slot.
- Rope and hook entities get a root and a pivot (slot components);
  meshes bind to the pivot, which is aimed with SetLocalOrientation.
  The log measures the real rope axis (ev=rope_axis).
- The rope starts at the launcher, offset by V's step this frame.
- Legs lock with NoMovement and NoJump from the pull on; the camera is
  the normal one. A walk-only scene zone releases V with the
  controlled descent.
- Build packs the entities straight with WolvenKit; the 42 gestures,
  the workspot and the camera set are gone.

tests (27), an independent review. Not yet seen in game.

JakeA-UKSBS/Shardbreaker.readme:
# Shardbreaker (roguelike)

A run-based tactics roguelike in the style of GBA Fire Emblem. Built for PC first (map left, command panel right), and still playable on phones. Forked from Nightbound's engine.

See [docs/VISUALS.md](docs/VISUALS.md) for pictures of every region, boss, monster, class, weapon, tile and scene, and [docs/INFO.md](docs/INFO.md) for the numbers: recruit odds, base stats and growths, weapons, effectiveness, skills, relics and regions.

## Run it
Open `index.html` in a browser (or serve the folder, e.g. VS Code's Live Server). `index.html` is just the page shell; the styles are in `css/style.css` and the game is split into numbered files in `js/`, loaded in order (plain scripts sharing one global scope, no build step). On PC: Esc or right-click backs out of a move or menu, E ends the turn, the mouse wheel zooms.

## Music
Drop mp3 files into a `music/` folder next to `index.html`: `title.mp3`, `tavern.mp3`, `mushroom.mp3`, `shadow.mp3`, `swamp.mp3`, `forest.mp3`, `mountain.mp3`, `ship.mp3`, `labyrinth.mp3`, `desert.mp3`, `snow.mp3`, `cavern.mp3`. Each loops while you're in that region (map and battles). Missing files are skipped. "Sound and music" in Options turns it off.

## Regions
Each run picks 2 of these 10 as its acts (`BIOMES`, `ACTS`). Each has 2-3 battle maps, a boss map, a monster pool and a rule.
| Region | Monsters | Rule | Boss |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mycelia | Sporelings, Mindsnails | Spores poison on a hit (3 HP a turn for 3 turns; a Salve cures it) | King Morel the Blighted |
| Sunless Isle | Skeletons, Skeleton Archers, Ghosts | Ghosts pass through walls; dark magic drains | The Bone Wyrm (raises skeletons every other turn) |
| Bog of Eternal Stench | Bog Lurkers, Lamias, Mud Monsters | Starting a turn in ankle-deep water or mangrove roots costs 1 Move; sand is solid | Krondis the alligator |
| Cursed Woodland | Wolves, Cursed Stags, Blighted Treants | Cursed thickets: +25 Avoid, 2 Move to enter | The Hollow Bear |
| Volcanic Isle | Boulder Golems, Fire Sprites, Harpies | Magma blocks foot units; fliers and fire creatures cross it | Pyraxis, the Magma Dragon |
| The Flying Ship | Harpies, Wyverns | Defend the deck for 5-6 turns; fliers arrive every turn | The Great Roc |
| The Labyrinth | Gremlins, Beholders (stone gaze) | Maze corridors | A Minotaur lord |
| Sandstone Desert | Jackals, Sand Worms, Sandstone Golems | Quicksand costs 1 Move next turn; sandstone outcrops (cream feldspar with smoky quartz) give cover | The Pyrite Colossus |
| Agate Peaks | Frost Wolves, Frost Sprites, Agate Golems | Deep snow costs 1 Move next turn (snow creatures ignore it); frozen lakes −10 Avoid; blue agate gives cover | Glacius, the Agate Wyrm |
| Gemstone Caverns | Gremlins, Gemsnails, Gem Golems | Chests everywhere: gold, or worthless pyrite; emerald, ruby and sapphire clusters give cover; walls are iridescent rock | Amethyra, the Amethyst Turtle |

Only creatures are enemies; there are no human foes.

Defend fights: from floor 2, a quarter of normal battles (outside the Flying Ship and the Labyrinth) are a settlement to hold for 5-7 turns, with monsters arriving from the top of the map each turn (`TOWN`, `town_<region>` maps, each region's `town` ground and cover). Chests (`C`) on any map hold 15-30 gold, or pyrite (30%).


## A run
- Title subtitle: "Break the blight". Battle titles are just the place name ("Oasis", "Old Mineshaft (Elite)").
- Every opening draft includes at least one Mender (healer).
- Early ease: in Act 1, enemies deal 3 less damage on floors 1-3, 2 less on 4-6 and 1 less on 7-9; the first two floors have 2 enemies.
- A run opens in Ithren the Sage's tent (`sageScene()`): he talks over his crystal ball (4 lines, naming the run's two regions), then asks how deep into the blight to go once Ascension is unlocked. Then the Crossroads (`musterScene()`): Your candidates stand around a campfire, with the run's two regions on the signpost. Travellers start at Lv 2. Tap travellers to see their card and choose 3, then Set out. Each act's map starts from a flag node at the bottom. Fallen units are gone for the rest of the run; you only lose when the whole squad falls.
- Each act is a branching node map (`genMap()`): 10 floors of 3 lanes, then a shared campfire (rest) on floor 11 and the boss on floor 12.
- Every path holds exactly `MIX`: 3 battles, 1 elite (never before floor 4; shown as a red horned skull on the map), 1 recruit, 1 tavern, 1 rest, 2 events, 1 treasure. One lane swaps a battle for a second elite (`MIX_HARD`), so the riskier route is there if you want it. Lanes are shuffles of the same mix, and a crossing between lanes is only kept if every path through the map still matches, so no route skips the treasure room. Change `MIX` to change the length and mix.
- Nodes: Battle; Elite (Elder leader, always drops a relic (1 of 2) and a jade weapon for a unit you choose); Recruit (pick 1 of 3; team caps at 6, `TEAM_CAP`); Rest (train one unit +1 level); Treasure (pick 1 of 3 items); Event (`EVENTS`); Tavern; Boss.
- Gold: 30 to start, then 25 per battle, 45 per elite, 80 per boss (`GOLDWIN`). Spent at taverns.
- Tavern (`tavernNode()`): talk to Marla the innkeeper and pick as many options as you can afford before leaving. Drinks (`DRINKS`): a round of ale (+30 EXP for everyone) or a spirit for one unit (+1 to a stat for good). Food (`MEALS`): squad-wide buffs for 2-3 fights (+2 damage, +15 Hit, +2 Def/Res, +1 Move, poison immunity), counted down after each won fight and shown on the map. Sellswords: 3 units for hire at 40 + 15 per level. Rumours: a hint about the region's boss and rule. Music slot: `music/tavern.mp3`.
- Events (`EVENTS`) don't repeat within a run while fresh ones are left. They open a full-screen scene drawn for that event (`eventScene()`, tinted to the region), with choices underneath and the outcome shown in the same box: Wandering Smith, Abandoned Armoury, Shrine of Trial, Training Ground, Travelling Merchant (3 items for

vince202/PROJECT-BUTTERFLY.readme:
🇫🇷 Français · [🇬🇧 English](README.en.md)

# BUTTERFLY

**Vingt habitants, une journée qui se répète. Suivez l'un d'eux, et dépensez quelques gestes pour que sa journée enfin réussisse.**

BUTTERFLY est une simulation déterministe d'une petite ville française : vingt habitants, de 06:00 à minuit, minute par minute, où chaque événement a des causes enregistrées. On peut créer une seconde réalité, la réalité B, en y modifiant un détail (« Et si le bus avait trois minutes de retard ? ») et voir précisément ce qui change. Ce moteur est devenu un **jeu de boucle temporelle** : la journée se répète, personne n'atteint son but par la faute de coups du sort, et vous avez quelques gestes pour y remédier. Prototype expérimental.

| ![Écran « Choisir qui suivre » : vingt quêtes classées par difficulté](docs/screenshots/start.jpg) | ![La ville à 09:46 : bulles d'alerte, fil dramatique, objectif de Léa](docs/screenshots/bubbles.jpg) | ![La terrasse du Café Le Papillon à 07:40](docs/screenshots/cafe.jpg) |
|---|---|---|
| Choisir qui suivre : vingt quêtes, de 1 à 5 | La boucle en cours : bulles, fil dramatique, objectif | Le café le matin (ville 3D, modèles CC0) |

---

## Le jeu en deux minutes

**La boucle.** La réalité A est la journée telle qu'elle se répète : une chorégraphie où, par construction, aucun des vingt habitants n'atteint son objectif. Chaque histoire du jour porte ses **coups du sort** : Léa ne retrouve pas son sac et rate le bus, une urgence retient Nadia au cabinet, Élodie oublie son portefeuille au comptoir. Ce sont des événements visibles (« Coup du sort : … »), produits par les mêmes mécaniques que vos interventions, mais sans observateur. Certains ne frappent que si l'habitant est au bon endroit : on peut donc les esquiver.

**La partie.**

1. On choisit un habitant sur l'écran « Choisir qui suivre ». Les quêtes sont classées de 1 (tutoriel) à 5 (très difficile) ; Léa, « À l'heure au lycée », sert d'entraînement.
2. On regarde la journée se dérouler **vers l'avant seulement**, dans une réalité B, avec un petit budget de **gestes** par boucle (deux à quatre selon la difficulté). On ne peut pas revenir en arrière dans la boucle.
3. À minuit, la boucle se ferme. Le bilan donne l'issue de l'objectif (réussi, échoué, coup de théâtre ou inachevé), les destins modifiés chez les autres habitants et les gestes utilisés. On peut rejouer la journée ou changer de personnage.
4. Le **carnet** garde tous les gestes déjà essayés avec ce personnage, avec leurs issues, et les rejoue en un clic (« Réutiliser ») dans la boucle suivante.

**Ce que le joueur voit.**

- Des **bulles** au-dessus des personnages et un **fil dramatique** (en bas à gauche) qui ne montrent que ce qui compte : événements notables ou graves, marqués « lié à votre quête » quand ils touchent votre personnage, la personne visée, le lieu de l'objectif ou votre histoire.
- La carte d'**objectif** : titre de la quête, échéance, jauge de gestes restants, bouton « Faire un geste », carnet.
- La **planification A/B** : l'interrupteur « Voir la journée telle qu'elle se répète » bascule sur la réalité A, toujours consultable, pour repérer l'endroit où l'histoire déraille, puis revient à votre boucle.
- Un **geste** se formule en texte libre en français ou en gestes rapides (retarder un bus, retenir chez soi, faire se croiser, imposer une décision, fermer un lieu plus tôt, changer la météo). Il porte toujours sur le futur.

**Clavier.**

| Touche | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Espace</kbd> | lecture / pause |
| <kbd>G</kbd> | faire un geste |
| <kbd>N</kbd> | ouvrir le carnet |
| <kbd>Échap</kbd> | fermer la fenêtre ouverte |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | basculer entre le jeu (mode spectateur) et le laboratoire |
| <kbd>+</kbd> / <kbd>−</kbd> | changer de vitesse (×1, ×5, ×20, ×60) |

**Le tutoriel.** Léa arrive en retard au lycée dans la réalité A. Un seul geste suffit : tapez **« Et si Léa partait au lycée à 7 h 30 ? »** (touche <kbd>G</kbd>). Le test `tests/drama.test.ts` vérifie qu'aucun arc n'est accompli en A et que ce geste fait réussir Léa.

### Le laboratoire

Le mode **laboratoire** (<kbd>Tab</kbd>) garde toute l'analyse : liste des habitants, inspecteur (« Pourquoi fait-il cela ? »), chronologie 06:00–24:00 avec marqueurs d'événements et de divergence, panneaux « Et si… », Causalité, Comparer, Rapport. La barre du haut regroupe l'horloge, la météo, la lecture (▶, ×1 ×5 ×20 ×60, « Journée complète », aller à une heure), la bascule Réalité A / Réalité B et un menu « ⋯ Plus » (graine, jour suivant, politique de décision, état de l'IA).

La journée entière est calculée en quelques centaines de millisecondes à l'ouverture ; la lecture est une relecture, on peut donc sauter à n'importe quelle heure et retrouver des positions, activités et relations réellement simulées. La vitesse ×1 est le temps réel (une minute simulée dure 60 secondes) ; à ×60, la journée dure 18 minutes.

| Inspecteur | Comparaison des réalités | Explorateur causal |
|---|---|---|
| ![Inspecteur](docs/screenshots/inspecteur.jpg) | ![Comparaison](docs/screenshots/comparaison.jpg) | ![Causalité](docs/screenshots/causalite.jpg) |

---

## Lancer

Prérequis : **Node.js 20 ou plus**.

```bash
npm install --legacy-peer-deps
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:5173
```

Aucune clé n'est nécessaire. Tout le cœur de l'application (simulation, gestes, comparaison, rapports, jeu) fonctionne **hors ligne**, avec des replis déterministes. L'IA est un supplément optionnel : les clés restent sur votre machine (lues par `server/index.ts` depuis `.env`) et ne sont envoyées qu'au fournisseur que vous avez choisi. Le LLM ne modifie jamais l'état simulé : il produit une intervention structurée que le moteur valide, ou il reformule des faits enregistrés.

### Adaptateurs IA (optionnels)

```bash
cp .env.example .env         # puis renseignez ce que vous voulez utiliser
npm run server               # port 8787, proxifié par Vite sous /api
```

druidsmickey/falcon.readme:
# ITB

Bet-taking and settlement tool for horse racing. Staff enter bets against a meeting's races, the app keeps a live book (books, profit and loss, average) per horse, and works out each client's profit or loss at the end, including special withdrawals, Rule 4 deductions and dead heats. Reports can be printed. Bets sent by clients in WhatsApp are read into an inbox for approval.

The same code is deployed as two separate apps, **Phantom** and **Detori**, each with its own database and users.

- **Frontend:** Angular 21 (standalone components, Angular Material), installable as a PWA with an offline queue (IndexedDB via Dexie).
- **Backend:** Node.js, Express 5, MongoDB (Mongoose), JWT login, `whatsapp-web.js` for WhatsApp.

## The tabs

| Tab | What it is for |
|---|---|
| Entry | Fast bet entry: pick race, horse, client, books/odds, tax |
| Single | One race at a time: live books, P&L and average per horse, tap a horse to bet |
| Chart | All races side by side with the same figures |
| Inbox | Bets read from WhatsApp messages, to check and save |
| WhatsApp | Connect WhatsApp, copy the phone's contacts, give each a nickname and choose whom to listen to |
| List | Every bet of the meeting, search, cancel/uncancel, print |
| Winners | Tick the winner of each race (several for a dead heat) |
| Reports | Client reports: detail and summary (Collect / Pay), add-ons, print |
| Merge | Combine up to 4 meetings into one client report |
| Params | Horse names, Special and Rule 4 withdrawals with times and deduction % |
| Init | Create a meeting, its races and number of horses; choose the selected meeting; delete a meeting |
| Password | Change your password |
| Pinball | A pinball game with four tables, missions, stars, levels and a daily streak. It is the tab that opens after logging in |
| Online / Sync | Connection status and the offline queue |

Only one meeting is *selected* at a time. All tabs work on the selected meeting, except Merge.

## Settlement rules

These are applied in Reports, Merge, Chart, Single and List.

- **Special withdrawal:** if a horse is withdrawn "special", every bet in that race placed *before* the withdrawal time is void.
- **Rule 4 horse:** every bet on the withdrawn Rule 4 horse is ignored, whenever it was placed.
- **Rule 4 deduction on the other horses:** a bet placed *before* a Rule 4 time has its payout reduced by that deduction. With several withdrawals the reductions multiply: a 10,000 payout with a 10% then a 20% withdrawal after the bet becomes 10,000 × 0.9 × 0.8 = 7,200.
- **Dead heat:** payout is divided by the number of winners.
- **Profit/loss per client** = (stake + tax) minus payout. Purchases (negative stake) reduce the total.

Bet amounts: with **F500**, stake = F500 × books and payout = books × 500. With **Odds**, books = stake × odds / 50000 and payout = odds × stake / 100.

## Running it on your computer

You need Node.js 22 and a MongoDB database (a free Atlas cluster is fine).

1. **Backend**
   ```bash
   cd backend
   npm install
   ```
   Create `backend/.env` (it is git-ignored):
   ```
   PORT=3000
   MONGODB_URI=mongodb+srv://USER:PASSWORD@CLUSTER.mongodb.net/itb_dev?retryWrites=true&w=majority
   JWT_SECRET=a-long-random-string
   ```
   Put a database name (here `itb_dev`) in the connection string. Without one MongoDB uses `test`. Use a database of your own so that testing never touches real data.

   Create the first user, then start the server:
   ```bash
   APP_SCOPE=phantom npm run create-user   # see AUTHENTICATION.md
   npm start
   ```
2. **Frontend** (project root)
   ```bash
   npm install
   npm start
   ```
   Open http://localhost:4200. In development the app talks to `http://localhost:3000` (see `src/environments/environment.ts`).

## Tests and builds

```bash
npm run build            # production build of the frontend
npm test -- --watch=false   # frontend tests (Vitest)
cd backend && npm test      # backend tests (Node's built-in test runner)
```

- **Frontend tests** cover the Rule 4 calculation (`src/app/services/settlement.spec.ts`) and the login session rules, including the 4-minute and 1-hour limits (`auth.service.spec.ts`).
- **Backend tests** (`backend/test/`) cover the check of incoming bets, the fields of a single-horse update, how rows are saved, and the login rate limit. `integration.test.js` starts the real server against a throwaway MongoDB (the first run downloads a small test database program) and checks the data protections: simultaneous saves leave no duplicate rows, winners survive saves, leftover duplicates are removed at start-up, meetings older than 6 days are deleted, the server listens only on `127.0.0.1`, and it refuses to start without a JWT secret.
- The deploy workflow runs both before it builds anything; a failing test stops the deploy.
- The screens themselves (components) have no automated tests. After changing a calculation, compare Reports, Merge, Chart and Single on real data before deploying.

## Deployment

Pushing to `main` of this repository runs `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which builds the frontend twice (once per app) and deploys both to the droplet over SSH.

| | Phantom | Detori |
|---|---|---|
| Web address | `/Phantom/2027/` | `/Detori/2027/` |
| API address | `/api-phantom-2027/` | `/api-detori-2027/` |
| Folder on the server | `/root/Phantom/itb/2027` | `/root/Detori/itb/2027` |
| Backend port | 3010 | 3011 |
| PM2 process | `phantom-backend-2027` | `detori-backend-2027` |

- nginx (`/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/apps`) serves `dist/itb/browser/` of each folder and forwards the API paths to the ports above. Use the address **with the trailing slash**; without it nginx answers 404.
- Each app's backend reads `backend/.env` **on the server**. The workflow does not write it and does not overwrite it. To change a database or secret, edit that file and run `pm2 restart <process>`. The file needs `PORT`, `MONGODB_URI` and `JWT_SECRET`; the server **refuses to start without `JWT_SECR

# DOM VIRUS · coded.design

## Play and develop the Astro site

Product page: https://coded-dot-design.github.io/dom-virus/ (available after Pages is enabled and the deployment succeeds). Created by **Chris Cooley / coded.design**.

Use Node **24** (`nvm use`), then run from this repository, where `package.json` lives:

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open the exact local URL Astro prints, including the `/dom-virus/` base path. `npm ci` uses the committed lockfile. `npm run dev:playground` keeps the original Vite regression playground available. The product site loads built game distributions; after editing game source, run `npm run build` and restart `npm run dev`.

```sh
npm run check
npm run site:build
npm run site:preview
```

`site:build` writes static output to `artifacts/site` and checks the launch script, styles and Pages asset paths. Pages builds run on every push to `main`; PR checks also build the product site. One-time setup: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**. No custom domain or paid hosting is required for this public repository. If the deploy job ran before enabling Pages, rerun that failed job afterward.

The page defaults to your system color scheme, with persistent light/dark overrides. Game launches are explicit and lazy-loaded. Recall destroys the active controller and restores eligible game-owned edits. Menu controls, code examples and the launcher are excluded from game targets.



**The page is the game board.** A local arcade playground and small shared runtime for four independently usable MIT-licensed games.

| Game | Play |
| --- | --- |
| [Swarm Protocol](https://github.com/coded-dot-design/swarm-protocol) | Defend letters and buttons from an evolving bug swarm. |
| [Null Invaders](https://github.com/coded-dot-design/null-invaders) | Fly through a webpage, corrupt letters into binary, and destroy alien factories. |
| [Byte Runner](https://github.com/coded-dot-design/byte-runner) | Eat letters, collect power orbs, and turn the tables on button-spawned ghosts. |

This first cut is a development playground. The public launcher and Chrome extension are future work. Swarm remains its existing v1.1.0 implementation and API.

## Run all four games

Use Node **22.12+** or Node 24, npm, and Git:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/coded-dot-design/dom-virus.git
cd dom-virus
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open the URL Vite prints, normally **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. Choose a cartridge and select **Launch game**. The default fictional page needs no target attributes: headings, paragraphs, list text, buttons, and button-style links are automatically selected within its board.

On the first run, the setup script clones the game versions in `games.json` into `.games/`. It does not install their development dependencies or execute their install scripts. GitHub is accessed during setup; the running playground uses local files only.

If sibling checkouts named `null-invaders`, `byte-runner`, or `swarm-protocol` are present, the playground uses those sources instead. This lets you iterate across separate repositories with Vite reloads. Managed copies use `.games/<game>/<version>/`, so changing a pin fetches a fresh version without touching old copies. Sibling checkouts take priority; pull all sibling repos together. An older sibling source layout reports the exact pull command instead of failing later in Vite.

## Controls and scenarios

- Null Invaders: mouse movement or arrows/WASD; hold click or Space to fire. Combat XP upgrades the gun from one to four shots within a wave; the run has four waves.
- Byte Runner: arrows/WASD. Every six fresh letters spawns an orb nearby. Collect it to stop spawning and eat ghosts for six seconds; stacked power is capped at nine seconds. Glitch fruit appears periodically.
- Swarm Protocol: click/tap bugs to defend the page. Its original behavior and controls remain intact.
- New games: **P** pauses/resumes, **G** jumps to the next offscreen gate, **Escape** recalls the page. Coarse-pointer devices receive on-screen directional controls and an auto-fire toggle for the shooter.
- Recall removes the game and restores its owned effects. Switching cartridges does the same before loading the next game.

The scenario picker supports generic page detection, explicitly marked targets, letters only, and a nested scrolling room. The form is intentionally protected. The page and game HUD follow system light/dark preferences. Reduced-motion preference suppresses decorative particles and idle pulses without disabling essential gameplay movement.

For local inspection, `window.playground.getSnapshot()` returns the current game's snapshot. This global exists only in the development playground; game packages add no globals.

## Update existing local checkouts

From the folder containing all four repositories, pull each game and the playground, then install from the committed lockfile:

```sh
git -C null-invaders pull --ff-only origin main &&
git -C byte-runner pull --ff-only origin main &&
git -C swarm-protocol pull --ff-only origin main &&
git -C dom-virus pull --ff-only origin main &&
cd dom-virus && npm ci && npm run dev
```

If an initially empty clone has an untracked `package-lock.json`, move that file outside the clone before pulling. Do not replace the repository's committed lockfile with it. `npm ci` requires the committed `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.

## Independent packages

Each new game repository provides a separate npm-compatible package, a self-contained `dist/index.js`, an optional `/react` adapter, its own Vite page, MIT license, tests, and size check. The shared runtime is bundled into each built game, so a consumer needs only the selected game. No runtime download from this repository is required.

The runtime source is maintained once in this repository. Games pin a generated runtime snapshot with a source fingerprint and bundle it during a release. Runtime changes do not silently change already release

aaskjer/aaskjer.github.io.readme:
# aaskjer.github.io

Source of [aaskjer.github.io](https://aaskjer.github.io), the overview page for my Streamer.bot extensions.

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, published by GitHub Pages straight from the `main` branch. There is no build step.

- `assets/js/projects.js` lists the projects; the start page and the project pages are built from it.
- Each project has its own page in a folder named after it (`blackjack-game/index.html` and so on). The page shows the project's README, setup guide, manual and FAQ, loaded live from its repository, and a changelog (its `CHANGELOG.md`, or else its release notes or commit history), so it never needs updating when the documents change. For a new project, copy one of the folders, change the title, descriptions, picture and `data-repo`, and add `page` to its entry in `projects.js`.
- Each project page also carries the project's name, tagline and features as plain text for search engines, and `sitemap.xml` lists every page. Both come from `projects.js`: after adding a project or changing those fields, run `node _tools/update-pages.js`.
- `_scenes/` holds the sources of the example scenes on the project cards (see `_scenes/render.ps1`).

## Credits

Headings are set in [Sora](https://github.com/sora-xor/sora-font), licensed under the SIL Open Font License (see [`assets/fonts/OFL.txt`](assets/fonts/OFL.txt)).

The project pages turn Markdown into HTML with [marked](https://github.com/markedjs/marked) (MIT License) and clean it with [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify) (Apache License 2.0 or Mozilla Public License 2.0), both in [`assets/js/vendor/`](assets/js/vendor) with their license notices.

# Devil x Slime Wiki

The wiki for **Devil x Slime**, the High School DxD addon for Tensura: Reincarnated.

Read it at **https://malwikpl.github.io/devil-x-slime-wiki/**.

## Editing

Every page is a Markdown file in `docs/`. Edit one on GitHub (the pencil on any wiki page links here), commit to `main`,
and the site rebuilds itself in about a minute.

- Page order and titles: `nav` in `mkdocs.yml`.
- Pictures: `docs/assets/images/`.
- Colours: `docs/assets/stylesheets/extra.css`.

To preview locally:

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve
```

then open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

The mod's source is not in this repository.

# Storm Shelter (GeauxHack 2026, "Life in Space")

*A style survival round game on the Moon and Mars: every map is built from the live NOAA space-weather reading, a pre-recorded ElevenLabs mission-control voice warns you, and you must reach the right radiation shelter in time.*

## Team
- Jaydon
- Zach
- Johnae

(Garri was on the team at the start and left during the event; his dust-storm and demo-script tasks were retired.)

**Live demo:** https://zacharynguyen001.github.io/Hackathon-Fall-2026/

## About
Built with: TypeScript, React, Vite, HTML Canvas 2D (no game framework), Vitest.

A browser 2D platformer in the style of "Natural Disaster Survival", set on the Moon and Mars.
Every round you get 20 seconds to explore, a voiced warning plays, then a radiation storm hits. Reach the
right shelter before your dose hits the limit. Doses and facts are real or clearly labeled as game values.

Run it: `npm install` then `npm run dev` (open the printed address). Tests and typecheck: `npm run validate`.

### External tools and APIs
Exactly two: **NOAA SWPC** (space-weather data, fetched from the browser) and **ElevenLabs** (voice and sound effects, baked ahead of time). GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages are CI/hosting for the static site, not APIs the game calls. `src/rules.test.ts` fails if any other web address appears in our code.

### ElevenLabs (API 2)
- **What we generated:** 20 voice lines (mission-control warnings S1-S5 for drill and live, EVAC, all-clear, a drill notice, and the 7 fact cards read on the results screen) and 5 sound effects (Geiger click, klaxon, coin, jump, Moon suit hum). The Mars wind loop is a NASA recording, not AI-generated.
- **Why it is baked ahead of time:** the site is static (no backend), so baking keeps the API key out of the browser, adds no delay at the moment of the warning, and works offline. Fallback if a clip is missing or slow: the browser's built-in voice, and the caption is always shown.
- **Voice:** "Jaydon (Me)", a voice cloned by Jaydon from his own voice (not a library voice, and not anyone else's). [Jaydon: confirm this wording.]
- **How to re-bake:** put `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` and `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` in a git-ignored `.env.bake.local`, then run
  `node --env-file=.env.bake.local --experimental-strip-types scripts/bake-audio.ts` (voice, into `public/audio/voice/`) and
  `node --env-file=.env.bake.local --experimental-strip-types scripts/bake-sfx.ts` (effects, into `public/audio/sfx/`).
  Both scripts skip files that already exist (delete an mp3 to regenerate it), then commit the mp3 files.

### Credits and boilerplate
- **Voice and sound effects:** generated with ElevenLabs (premade library voice, no cloning), baked ahead of time by the scripts in `scripts/`. Logged in `docs/AI_USAGE.md`.
- **`mars-wind-loop.mp3`:** Mars ambience, a NASA recording (not AI-generated). Source page and usage terms: https://science.nasa.gov/resource/perseverance-rovers-supercam-records-wind-on-mars https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/
- **Art (sprites and palettes):** Johnae Avery, drawn by hand.
- **Font:** Bitcount (OFL-1.1) via `@fontsource-variable/bitcount`.
- **Space-weather data:** NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC).
- **Boilerplate:** we started from the `create-deepspace` scaffold (commit 9f04037) and removed it in 3ab1517; the final project uses no backend. The GitHub Pages workflow in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` is CI config.

### AI generated / assisted code
Claude Code helped write much of the code and docs. Every AI-assisted file and change is listed, with the real commit time and a reviewer column, in [`docs/AI_USAGE.md`](docs/AI_USAGE.md), along with every ElevenLabs-generated audio file. No images or video were AI-generated; all art is hand-drawn by Johnae Avery.

**Rules we follow**

- **External APIs (max 2):** NOAA SWPC (space-weather data) and ElevenLabs (voice). Nothing else, and no backend.
  The project started on a hosted backend platform, but the organizers counted it as an API, so it was removed.
- **AI-assisted code:** every file Claude wrote or changed is logged in `docs/AI_USAGE.md`.
- **No AI-generated images or video.** All art is hand-made by a human (Johnae Avery, see `docs/ART_GUIDE.md`). Where a picture is missing the game falls back to a flat placeholder shape.
- **Font:** Bitcount (OFL-1.1), bundled via the npm package `@fontsource-variable/bitcount`.
- **Real vs tuned values:** `docs/DATA_SOURCES.md` lists the real facts; `src/game/tunables.ts` tags every number as GAME VALUE or REAL.

## Prerequisites
- Node.js 22.15 or newer (with npm)
- A modern desktop browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge)
- Only if you want to re-make the audio: an ElevenLabs API key (not needed to play or build)

## Build from source
```bash
git clone https://github.com/ZacharyNguyen001/Hackathon-Fall-2026.git
cd Hackathon-Fall-2026
npm install
npm run dev        # play locally at the address it prints
npm run validate   # typecheck + tests
npm run build      # static site in dist/
```
Pushing to `main` publishes the site to GitHub Pages through `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (repo owner: Settings -> Pages -> Source = **GitHub Actions**, once). The hosted copy is always built from the committed code; for submission, make sure the last push to `main` is the commit tagged `submission`.

`npm install`, then `npm run build` makes the static site in `dist/` (paths are relative, so it works from any folder). The live demo must be built from the tagged commit (`submission`).

chudxster/RetroBall.readme:
# RetroBall

A Retro Bowl-style 2.5D pixel-art basketball game. Plain HTML5 canvas and JavaScript: no build step, no dependencies.

## Play

Open `index.html` in a browser (double-clicking works), or serve the folder from any static host.

The game opens on the **main menu**, with the computer playing a game against itself behind it. A dock on the left
holds the modes: **Career**, **Locker room**, **Casual** and **2 Player** (each slides a drawer out beside the dock:
Casual has a 3v3 game with its options under it, the daily game and the practice drills; 2 Player has Local and
Online tabs), **Customize** (your team's look
and names) and **Settings** (controls and display), plus a Fullscreen button. Along the bottom runs your career
season as a road, a stop for every game: played weeks show their score (green for a win, red for a loss), this
week's stop is yellow, and the semifinal and final come last. Above this week's stop are its matchup and three
challenges: pick one to tip off straight from the menu (Upgrades opens the Career screen).
Click, or use the arrow keys / WASD and Enter or Space; Esc goes back. In a game, Esc (or P) opens the pause menu, whose **Main menu** button leaves the game (in a career game it asks first: a game
left early is a forfeit loss, also if the page is closed mid-game) and **Restart** starts it over (not in career).

**Career** is a season in an 8-team league: every team plays every other once, then the top 4 play semifinals and a
final, and the next season starts with tougher opponents. Each AI team has its own colors and strength; their other
games are simulated for the standings. The Career screen shows the season, the next opponent and the standings.
Before each game pick one of three challenges from different tiers, in random order (Easy x1.1, Medium x1.25, Hard
x1.5, Pro x2), shown top left during the game. Meet a
stat challenge (threes, steals, dunks, blocks, points) and a little jingle plays as its box flashes and floats away; a
win, win-by or hold-them goal can still slip until the buzzer, so its jingle plays then. A game pays a token per point your team scores, x1.25 for a win or
x0.75 for a loss, times the challenge's multiplier if you completed it, rounded up. Spend tokens on the Career screen
(a level costs 10 x its number); the career team has its own names and levels, separate from the free testing
upgrades. After a career game, shoot takes you back to the Career screen for the next one. Career progress saves
automatically in the browser after every game and upgrade (the Career screen warns if the browser can't save, as in
some private windows).

The **Locker room** (main menu) is a room you walk around in as your player: the coach at the whiteboard, your two
teammates at their lockers and a reporter by the TV camera each hand out quests (walk up and press your dunk key,
Enter or Space to talk). A quest is a goal for your games, in one game or added up over several (Quick game, career,
the daily game and 2 Player co-op count); a yellow ! means a quest to pick up, a bouncing green one tokens to claim.
Claiming pays career tokens and counts toward the Locker Room trophy. The trophy case on the right wall holds
every trophy you've earned: pick which ones (up to 13) stand on the scoreboard's shelf in games. You come in through
the black door under the EXIT sign on the left wall; walk back out through it (or press Esc) to leave. The doorway
under the TO COURT sign on the right wall is the tunnel to the court, a lit hallway: walk on through it to be asked
"Ready for the next game?" and pick a challenge to tip off your next career game.
Talking shows the speaker's portrait, their line and a quest card (goal, progress, reward) while the room dims;
markers show a speech bubble for a new quest, the progress for one under way and a spinning gold token for tokens
to claim. The room remembers your last game, once: streamers, confetti and the score on the whiteboard after a win,
towels over heads and a blue half-light after a loss. Once your first career season is finished it becomes the
**Dynasty Room**: a banner for every title, open wood stalls with your jerseys, a trophy wall with the Finals cup
and a DYNASTY rug (with `?dev=1`, the UI tab can switch it on to test).

**Casual** (a drawer beside the dock) starts a **3v3 game** (full court, AI teammates and opponents, half-court
defense). Its options sit right under it: the court, a difficulty (Rookie, Pro or All-Star: how good the AI opponents
are; 2 Player co-op uses it too), the half length, the shot clock and free throws (Career and 2 Player games use those
rules too).

The **Daily game** (in the Casual drawer) is one short game a day, the same for everyone: today's date picks
the opponent (a league team in its colors), how good they are, their upgrades and a goal, and seeds every random
roll after tip-off. It always plays two 1.5-minute halves with no upgrades on your side. Your first game each day
counts: meet the goal on consecutive days to build a streak. Replays are fine but don't change the day's result, and
leaving a daily game early counts as a miss.

**2 Player** (a drawer beside the dock, Local tab) is two people on one keyboard: **Versus 3v3** (each runs a team with two AI teammates), **Versus 1v1**,
or **Co-op** (together, plus an AI teammate, against three AI players). Player 1 plays with WASD, R (shoot), E
(dunk/steal) and Q (pass/switch); player 2 with IJKL, P, O and U; both sets can be changed in Settings (the Controls
tab), and only Esc pauses. Before tip-off both players get the same random number of upgrade points and spend them
on a split screen at the same time (up/down to pick, right to add, left to take back, shoot when ready), with both
players' keys drawn on a shared keyboard below (each player's in their color, lighting up while held): in versus
they upgrade their whole team, in co-op their own player. At halftime they get more. After the final buzzer player

Vedat-Ozkan/cadence-finder.readme:
# Cadence Finder

Search for chord progressions and cadences in three annotated corpora by Beethoven and Mozart (DCML, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; see [NOTICE](NOTICE)).
- Structured queries like `Ger ... @PAC` ("a German sixth leading, within four chords, to a perfect authentic cadence").
- Similar-passage search over embeddings.
- Plain-English questions, turned into validated structured queries by Claude.

**Live demo:** the wake link (`terraform output wake_url` in the `live` workspace) starts the server on demand. Allow about 85 s for a cold start; after that the app is at https://cadence-finder.duckdns.org.

## How it works

- **Upload:** a TSV goes to S3.
- **SQS:** the S3 event lands on SQS, with a dead-letter queue after 3 receives.
- **`ingest-worker` (Spring Boot):**
  - parses the file into chord tokens;
  - sends 8-chord passages to the `embedder` (FastAPI, Voyage, pgvector);
  - writes the movement plus an n-gram index to DynamoDB.
- **`search-api` (Spring Boot):**
  - answers `/search` from the DynamoDB index plus a matcher;
  - answers `/passages/{id}/similar` from pgvector, with optional rerank;
  - answers `/nl-search` by having Claude write the structured query, which goes through the same validator;
  - answers `/ask` from up to 8 retrieved passages, with citations checked against them.
- **Hosting:** everything runs on one k3s node on EC2, built with Terraform, with Traefik and Let's Encrypt.
- **Tracing:** an ADOT collector sends traces to X-Ray, metrics as EMF, and logs to CloudWatch.
- **Scale to zero:** the node stops itself after 30 idle minutes, and a Lambda function URL wakes it.

## Measured (details in [docs/results.md](docs/results.md))

| | |
|---|---|
| `/search` at 80 RPS on 2 vCPUs | p50 34 ms, p95 57 ms, p99 216 ms, 0 errors |
| Max rate with p99 < 200 ms | ~80 RPS |
| `/nl-search` (Claude) | p50 1.6 s, p99 3.6 s |
| Ingestion | 14,788 passages in 164 s (~90/s) |
| Cold start from stopped | ~85 s to first result |
| Retrieval, self-labelled hit rate@5 | `/nl-search` 1.00; text search 0.62–0.69, rerank 0.69–1.00 |
| One trace across the API, SQS, worker and embedder | yes, a single X-Ray trace |
| `/ask` (RAG with validated citations) | 8/8 grounded; 8/8 prompt-injection cases pass; p50 9 s |
| In-cluster `/search`, after warm-up | one k3s node: 320 RPS at p99 152 ms; EKS with 2 nodes: 240 RPS at p99 19 ms |
| Game day | stalled worker detected in 6.5 min, bad file in 9 min, Postgres kill self-healed with no failed requests |

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `corpus-core/` | TSV parser, tokenizer, query grammar, matcher, passage text |
| `cadence-store/` | DynamoDB table access |
| `ingest-worker/`, `search-api/` | Spring Boot 4.1 on Java 25 |
| `embedder/` | FastAPI on Python 3.14, pgvector |
| `wake/` | Lambda that wakes the node |
| `deploy/k8s/` | Kustomize base plus `kind`, `k3s` and `eks` overlays |
| `infra/terraform/` | Workspaces `dev` and `live` |
| `e2e/` | docker compose with LocalStack; golden, NL, DLQ, reindex and recall tests |
| `loadtest/` | k6 smoke test (in CI) and ramp |
| `docs/` | [build plan](docs/build-plan.md), [runbook](docs/runbook.md), [results](docs/results.md) |

## Running the tests locally

```
scripts/fetch-corpus.sh
./gradlew build :ingest-worker:bootJar :search-api:bootJar
set -a; . ./.env; set +a
docker compose -f e2e/compose.yaml up -d --build --wait
uv run --project e2e pytest e2e -q
```

`.env` needs `LOCALSTACK_AUTH_TOKEN` and `VOYAGE_API_KEY`. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is only needed with `RUN_NL=1`.

siyanshvir/TruckHomeEatsBot.readme:
# Truck Home Eats — Night Shift bot

Python 3.8+, standard library only. Learns customer demand and competitor habits,
then optimizes quality, price, and inventory within your location and pricing rules.

Configure `NIGHTSHIFT_KEY` in your existing `.env` or environment. Keep it private.

```sh
python3 bot.py                                         # live game and final
python3 bot.py --practice --seed check-a --rivals 5      # private practice
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Start only one live process for your truck. A GitHub push does not restart an
already-running bot. This rebuild removes the old starter/contrarian/learning
entry points; use `bot.py`.

## Current location and pricing rules

Production orders are restricted to the **three smallest customer forecasts**.
The two smallest receive preference. The third can win only when its predicted
profit exceeds the best of the bottom two by at least $15 or 15%, whichever is
larger, and its risk-adjusted score is also better. The three busier spots are
excluded regardless of their predicted profit. Event/weather effects are already
included in the supplied forecast counts used for this ranking.

Price ceilings are **$5.50 cheap, $7 standard, $8.50 premium**. Thompson's ceilings are 39% higher ($7.64, $9.73, $11.81) via `spot_price_lift`.
The optimizer can
charge less when supported by its sales forecast, with a $7.25 premium floor.
Production uses an additional downside-loss weight of 0.08 (previously 0.15);
all inventory still pays full ingredient costs, including unsold meals, and
quantities are optimized against forecast demand rather than automatically increased.
The fallback also uses the
bottom two and caps standard at $7. These are deliberate user constraints and
can reduce achievable profit compared with unrestricted optimization.

## Decisions

The bot reads `state.features` every update. With `fair_choice`, eligible trucks
split customer flow by `exp(value / 1.5)`, redistributing when stock runs out.
With `walk_over`, all local queues run first, then hungry customers may walk to
the nearest acceptable stocked location with probability `0.7 * exp(-metres/400)`
using the published campus distances. Original price limits and minimum quality
are retained. These are expected fluid flows, not the server's individual draws.
Inventory optimization caps projected uncapped demand; it approximates how our
own stock changes other trucks' leftovers.

With `salvage`, profit and downside include a refund of 25% of the ingredient
cost of unsold meals. Full cooking cost still counts against the $500 budget.
Flags enter rule fingerprints and separate customer-learning banks. Old
checkpoints retain their legacy posterior; a new combination starts broad.
While walking is enabled, crowd and rival learning continue, but local preference
fitting is withheld to avoid fitting transferred buyers as locals. Captured order
flags label realized results even if tomorrow's flags have already changed.

With walking enabled, candidate searches cover all qualities at the three
eligible locations; all six campus spots still contribute crowds and walking
flows. Under legacy rules, all six locations are searched before refinement.
Each searched spot receives equal effort. Active-night feature toggles trigger
a replan; unchanged accepted orders are not resubmitted. Missing flags use legacy
rules. Your location constraints and low price bounds are unchanged.

The model learns a distribution over customer budget and minimum-quality
preferences from observed sales across the market. Sequential customer-choice
modeling includes reputation, affordability, stockouts, and overflow. A sellout
is a lower bound on demand, not evidence that demand stops at the sold count.
Rival scenarios use a learned mixture of location models: uniform uncertainty,
multi-day habits, repeat behavior, crowd chasing, context matching, and opportunity
seeking. Historical neighbors match tomorrow's announced events, weather odds,
and crowd shares. Pricing combines contextual historical prices with repeat,
undercut, and price-cycle hypotheses. Quality and stock use multiple historical
observations. Attendance is learned from both orders and absences. Only
registered rivals are modeled; no invented extra competitors are added.

For each location/quality/price, every feasible integer inventory, including
zero, competes on expected revenue minus food costs and a downside-loss penalty.
Published API crowds are used directly: they are not reduced a second time for
inactive trucks. Participation scaling at three production levels is reserved
for synthesized full-roster forecasts (explicitly marked by the offline simulator).
A bounded reputation benefit declines toward the end of a market;
a small information bonus encourages early exploration. Prices obey the low ceilings above, the game's limits, and the maximum
nonnegative customer value for that quality and reputation. Within those limits,
they do not have to undercut every rival: overflow and reputation can still matter.

`forecast.expected_customers` is the starting point. It already incorporates
weather/events. Weather scenarios are normalized around those counts, and online
calibration learns remaining forecast errors. Explicit zero forecasts stay zero.

Crowd variability is learned separately for each location and actual weather,
with sparse data shrunk toward the original +/-15% noise prior. Old checkpoints
load without retraining or discarding existing history; the new variance
statistics accumulate from newly observed forecast/result pairs. Production
evaluates 32 joint scenarios by default. Cached customer preference calculations
reuse work across crowd levels while retaining finite stock and overflow rules.
Quantity is still optimized, with no automatic stock increase after a sellout.
Production can then add a forecast-supported inventory cushion of up to 8%

When more than three items are matched, keep the three most likely card names: on the
cards around the re-roll line, then in the biggest text, then the closest reads. On the
reported 4-item iPhone scan (tooltip text read as Weapon Shielding) this keeps Rapid

Tuned on batch 3 (26 Mina photos), where the flagged Superior Cooldown was read but not
marked Enhanced:
- If the greyscale read of the strip under a name misses "ENHANCED", read it again from a
  cyan-only image (blue well above red, letters split from glow with Otsu's threshold). The
  greyscale label blended into green/orange card rings and overexposed glows.
- An Enhanced label only marks the name directly above it, not the nearest card when that
  card's own name wasn't read (Knockdown was marked instead of Superior Cooldown).
- Hovering a card shows a tooltip whose text was read as items: drop matches in much
  smaller text than two other names, require near-exact matches inside long lines, and
  don't let one word of a sentence ("...or weapon") name an item.
- A name slot that reads nothing is retried with the crop moved down/up (angled photos).

Benchmark on all saved photos: 201/204 items, 0 wrong, all 10 Enhanced labels.

Watch the shared screen and read drafts automatically, plus an always-on-top pop-out

Deadlock keeps the mouse until Esc (which dims the screen) and Alt-Tab minimises it, so a
Scan click can't happen during a draft. Sharing the screen now starts a watch: about once a
second a small crop where "Re-Roll Remaining" sits is read (a whole-screen search finds it the

On desktop browsers the Scan button becomes "Scan screen": the first
click asks which screen to share (the game monitor), then each click

Scan: infer layout from found names, read Enhanced labels under names

From batch 2 of real captures:
- When "Re-Roll Remaining" isn't read, two names already found pin down
  the layout, so the missing third name's position can still be read
  (recovers e.g. Divine Barrier on an iPhone capture).
- The small "ENHANCED" label under a name is read directly instead of
  relying on whole-photo OCR noticing it; catches labels that were
  previously missed (Swift Striker, Indomitable) with no false flags.
- Scan log shows these label reads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix sideways iPhone captures and read names by anchored crops

Tuned on 39 real phone captures (Android + iPhone):
- Camera photos are turned to match the preview's orientation (iPhone
  returned them sideways, so nearly nothing was read); photo files that
  read nothing upright are retried turned either way.
- When the whole-photo read misses names, each name position is cropped
  relative to the "Re-Roll Remaining" line under the re-roll button and
  read as a single line, which handles the glowing cards far better.
- Matching prefers the name covering more of the text (no "Leech" inside

  a closer match for fragments joined together.
- Greyscale uses Rec. 709 weights so purple/orange glows go dark.
- Scan log keeps the per-name-area reads.

0 wrong (was ~40/105 before the orientation fix).

Each scan is saved on the device (IndexedDB, newest 50): the capture as

highlights, per-image download, delete, an on/off switch, and Export all

- Request 4K camera video and use a still photo (ImageCapture) when the

mlgzipo-sketch/fo4vr-npc-touch.readme:
# NpcTouch for Fallout 4 VR

Physical interaction with NPCs in Fallout 4 VR, inspired by PLANCK for Skyrim VR. Built on top of ROCK (hand physics) and FRIK (full body).

## Features

- **Hands collide with NPCs.** Invisible capsules follow each nearby NPC's torso, head, arms and legs, so your physical hands stop against bodies instead of passing through.
- **Bodies react to touch.** A push turns the touched body, head or arm with your hand, then it springs back.
- **NPCs react with their own voices.** Regular NPCs say "Huh?" or "Hey...", then warn you if you keep touching them, especially on the chest or pelvis. Companions react according to their affinity and romance. Lines come from the game's own dialogue, so there is no extra .esp.
- **Shoves.** A fast hand makes NPCs stagger in the direction of the push.
- **Grabs.** Hold grip on an arm, shoulder, head, chest, hips or legs. Arms and heads follow your hand, the elbow bends, and shoulder or chest grabs sway the upper body. Your fingers wrap the part you hold and your palm stays on it. Clothes and hats move with the body instead of stretching.
- **NPCs react to being held.** They look at you, complain, and pull free once they are annoyed enough. Companions don't mind.
- Every feature can be tuned or turned off in `NpcTouch.ini`.

## Requirements

- Fallout 4 VR 1.2.72
- [F4SE VR](https://f4se.silverlock.org/)
- VR Address Library for F4SEVR
- [FRIK](https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/mods/53464) 0.79.1 or newer (needs FRIK API v2.3+)
- [ROCK](https://github.com/brunocatani/ROCK) 0.9 or newer, with `npcDynamicCollisions = true` in `ROCK.ini` (the default)

## Installation

Install the archive with Vortex or Mod Organizer 2, or unpack it into the game's `Data` folder. You should end up with:

```
Data\F4SE\Plugins\NpcTouch.dll
Data\F4SE\Plugins\NpcTouch.ini
```

The latest build of every commit is under **Actions** (download the NpcTouch archive at the bottom of a green run).

## Settings

All settings are in `Data\F4SE\Plugins\NpcTouch.ini`, and each one has a comment. The main switches are:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bEnableReactions` | NPCs talk and look at you when touched |
| `bAllowCombat` | An NPC who is touched too much starts a fight (off by default) |
| `bEnableShoves` | Fast hands make NPCs stagger |
| `bHandsCollideWithNPCs` | Hands stop against NPC bodies |
| `bFlinch` | Bodies give way to a push and spring back |
| `bShapeFingers`, `bPinHand` | Fingers wrap what you hold, and the palm sticks to it |
| `bShoulderMovesBody` | Shoulder and chest grabs sway the upper body |
| `bDebugLog` | Detailed log for bug reports |

## Reporting bugs

Set `bDebugLog=1`, reproduce the problem, and attach `Documents\My Games\Fallout4VR\F4SE\NpcTouch.log`. The first lines show the build number.

## Known limitations

- There is no ragdoll yet. NPCs can't be lifted or thrown, only moved and posed. Full active ragdoll is planned once ROCK's companion project SCISSORS is out.
- Sitting and dead NPCs can be touched, but not grabbed.
- Only the 4 nearest NPCs (configurable) get collision bodies.

## Building

You need Visual Studio 2022, CMake and vcpkg (`VCPKG_ROOT`).

```powershell
git clone --recursive https://github.com/mlgzipo-sketch/fo4vr-npc-touch
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release
```

## Credits

- **FlyingParticle (adamhynek)**: the idea. [PLANCK](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/66025) for Skyrim VR showed how physical NPC interaction in VR should feel. This mod is my attempt at bringing that to Fallout 4 VR.
- **brunocatani**: [ROCK](https://github.com/brunocatani/ROCK) and the [RPS SDK](https://github.com/brunocatani/RPS_SDK). ROCK provides the physical hands. The NPC collision bodies are adapted from ROCK's physics body code, and the plugin runtime is based on the RPS SDK examples.
- **FRIK authors**: [FRIK](https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/mods/53464) and its API for finger poses and hand placement.
- **CommonLibF4 / CommonLibF4VR contributors** and the **F4SE team**.

## License

GPL-3.0, the same as ROCK, whose code it adapts. The full source is in this repository.

plissken2013es/e1809-digital.desc: versión digital del juego de mesa Elviña 1809
plissken2013es/e1809-digital.readme:
# Elviña 1809 — prototipo digital

Versión web de **Elviña 1809**, wargame de motor de cartas para dos jugadores sobre la batalla de Elviña (A Coruña, 16 de enero de 1809): Moore defiende el embarque británico frente a Soult. Es un prototipo para **depurar y equilibrar las reglas** (reglamento v1.6c).

**Jugar:** https://plissken2013es.github.io/e1809-digital/ · **Reglamento:** https://plissken2013es.github.io/e1809-digital/rules.html

- Dos jugadores en la misma pantalla, o contra un bot (cada bando puede ser humano o bot).
- Mapa ilustrado con las fichas, tarjetas de unidad, mano, Mercado de Táctica, dados 3D y registro.
- Cada decisión queda grabada: deshacer, guardar, compartir una partida como código (`E18.…`) y repetirla.

## En local

Sin dependencias ni compilación (JavaScript con módulos ES). Hace falta un servidor (los módulos no cargan desde `file://`):

```
python tools/serve.py 8012
```

y abrir http://localhost:8012. Tests: `npm test` (Node 22).

## Documentos

- [`docs/01-reglas-y-mecanicas.md`](docs/01-reglas-y-mecanicas.md): las reglas formalizadas y las decisiones `[D-n]` tomadas para la versión digital.
- [`docs/02-plan-tecnico.md`](docs/02-plan-tecnico.md): arquitectura, herramientas y hoja de ruta.

El arte, las cartas y el reglamento son del material del diseñador del juego; las escenas de combate usan pixel-art y sonidos propios del autor del prototipo (de su versión digital de W1815); el código usa three.js y cannon-es (MIT, en `vendor/`) para los dados 3D.

GiladGlo/StarSwarm.readme:
# Star Swarm
*Ten sectors. Ten capital ships. One pilot.*

![Star Swarm in action](Code/monsters-ingame.gif)

Star Swarm is a fast arcade shooter inspired by the classic formation shooters of the '80s. Every ship, monster, asteroid and explosion is generated by the game itself at startup, with no art files. Lighting, shadows and glow effects give each one a detailed, 3D-like look.

Fly through 60 stages across 10 sectors. Each sector brings four alien waves, a dense meteor field, and a boss battle against a towering capital ship. After each boss, tear open a hyperspace window and dive through to the next sector.

## Features

- **A living space bestiary:** Nova Urchins, Void Mantas, Nebula Jellies, Comet Imps, Asteroid Brutes and Cosmic Leviathans. Each one is fully animated, swoops in along its own flight path and dives at you.
- **Ten capital-ship bosses:** each is armoured, covered in detail and has a beating reactor core. Every boss is tougher than the last, with signature weapons such as spiral barrages, homing missiles, sweeping lasers and meteor storms.
- **Meteor fields:** tumbling asteroids split apart as you shoot them, and volatile rocks set off chain reactions. Mining outposts drift through, carrying supplies for anyone who blasts them free.
- **Five weapon classes:** Photon Torpedo, Spread Cannon, Pulse Laser, Homing Swarm and Ion Burst. Armoured Courier ships carry new weapons and upgrades, each weapon goes up to Lv3, and a max-level upgrade calls in a wingman drone that dodges fire at your side.
- **A ship that feels alive:** your fighter banks into turns, fires its side thrusters and warps in on every respawn. It's protected by a one-hit force field that recharges over time.
- **Arcade at heart:** high scores, extra lives, a campaign progress bar, and one goal: destroy all ten capital ships and save the galaxy.

![The ten capital ships](Code/bosses-preview.png)

![Hyperspace jump after a boss](Code/hyperspace-ingame.gif)

## Play

Run **StarSwarm.exe** (Windows, nothing to install).

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrows / WASD | Move |
| Space | Fire (hold) |
| P / Esc | Pause (Esc opens the menu) |
| F11 / Alt+Enter | Fullscreen |

Full gameplay details, scoring and build instructions: [Code/README.md](Code/README.md).

*Written in C++ with raylib. Runs as a single Windows executable with nothing else to install.*

Developed by Gilad Globen. Dedicated to Daniel Globen.

amaeteventurestudios/agent-grand-prix-.readme:
# Agent Grand Prix

A free browser racing game. Your two AI drivers race; you are the team principal and make the calls:
tyres, pit stops, battery, attack or defend, and the rain call. Static site, Three.js r160 vendored, no build step.

- **Daily Grand Prix**: one race a day, same circuit, grid and weather for everyone (seeded by date; #1 = 23 Oct 2026, Abuja). Share card.
- **Season**: 25 rounds, Abuja to Abu Dhabi, saved in the browser.
- **Quick race**: any venue, Short, Medium or Long (`LENGTHS` in `js/game.js`); Sakhir and Singapore are the featured picks, and Race again repeats the last one.

**Racing Academy** (`js/academy.js`, wired up in `js/main.js`): five short lessons on a real race. Each step is taught by the
engineer (voiced in every engineer voice: `assets/voice/<voice>-academy.js`, made with `LINES=academy art/voice/gen.py`), points at
the control and moves on when you do it, through the same `cmd()` path as buttons and the team radio. No AI model: same actions, same
lesson. Lessons run on a staged race (`stage` in `setupRace`: start positions, weather, no failures, a safety car on cue). Progress is
saved as `S.academy`; all five give the Academy graduate trophy. The lessons: Meet your team, Command your drivers (attack, defend,
team orders), Master the circuit (Driver DNA, lent for the lesson), Strategy (tyre rule, a safety car on cue, rain) and Your first
Grand Prix (a full race with the coach on, starting on the engineer's plan). A race that ends mid-lesson offers a rerun. The Race guide
(ten ways to win) lives in the Academy. Free practice (`freePractice()`) is a medium race at Sakhir that counts for nothing.

**Phone race control** (upright phones and tablets, `PHONE_UP` in `js/main.js`): the race fills the screen with your two cars as
cards on top (tap to give a car calls, tap again for its Strategy panel), BOOST, RADIO and BOX in one row, and Strategy, Timing and Radio
in a panel that swipes up from the tab bar (`app.dataset.sheet`: peek, half, full). A lesson opens the panel when it points at a control
in it and closes it again after. The engineer's suggestions show as a card with the call on a button, and every call gets a short
"copied" chip.

**Race coach and beginner assist**: the coach card folds into a small pill (`S.settings.coachMin`). *Engineer calls the stops* on the
pit wall (`S.settings.assist`, the `assist` command in `js/sim.js`) lets the engineer box both cars while you keep pace, battery and battles.

**First visit** (`onboard()` in `js/main.js`): a welcome card offers three ways in: *Racing Academy*, *Jump into a race* (a short guided race at Sakhir with the
default team) and *Free practice*, plus *Build my team first*. Anyone who has raced or done a lesson skips it. Building a team is six screens, one decision each: team name and code, car, colours (the showroom in its `wizard` mode),

short first race at Sakhir with the coach on. A half-built team is kept as `S.team.draft` and races as the default team until finished.
**Race setup** (`pre(o, step)`) is four screens: circuit (Quick race only), car, tyres (length, starting tyres, engineer's plan, tyre
guide) and race settings (calls, coach, radio voice, Driver DNA, Go to the grid).

**Race calls**: the floating BOX button (and *BOX, BOX* in the pit-wall panel) boxes the car you're running this lap; the engineer says
"Box, box" and the driver answers in his own voice (switch replies off in Radio voices). The radio voice can be changed mid-race from
the Team radio tab or the pause menu. Pit stops show jacks, wheel guns with hoses to the gantry, tyres and the lollipop, and the garage
has two screens: live timing and the race as the TV shows it.

**Refresh**: the engine is deterministic, so the page keeps the race setup and every call you made (`agp.live.v1` in localStorage) and a
refresh rebuilds the race to the same moment. This works on one device; carrying a race across devices needs the game server.

Files: `js/data.js` (calendar, teams), `js/track.js` (original circuit generator), `js/sim.js` (deterministic 20 Hz race engine, Node-testable),
`js/game.js` (race setup), `js/world.js` (3D world), `js/cams.js` (cameras), `js/main.js` (UI). `artifact.html` is `index.html` without the document wrapper, for the hosted preview.

On track both of your cars carry a ring (the one you follow is brightest). The race engineer talks to
your drivers all race (`js/main.js`, `engineer()`): every lap each car hears its position, the gap
ahead and behind and whether it's closing, plus tyres, battery, pace or laps to go; a car in a fight
hears the gap again mid-lap; every button you press is confirmed by voice. These updates only play
when the radio is quiet, so real calls always come first. Radio lines are in `art/voice/lines.json`,
recorded for all 13 voices by `art/voice/gen.py`. Your crew watches a live timing screen at the front
of your garage (`js/paddock.js`) and celebrates places gained (with a quick cut to them in Live and TV
view) or holds their helmets when one is lost; poses come from `art/people/people.py`.

**Voice team radio** (`js/teamradio.js`, the radio block in `js/main.js`): hold the mic button (or T) and talk. `parseCall()` matches
what the browser's speech recognition heard to the same calls the buttons make, in JavaScript, with no server or AI call (well under
