samerrahman/CalHacks-13.0.readme:
# HUSH

**A first-person horror game you play with your face.** You are sealed in a research shelter while something blind hunts outside it by sound. Your webcam reads your pulse, breathing and fear, and the thing outside can hear all of it.

Built at CalHacks 13.0 with React, Three.js, Electron, Gemini, ElevenLabs, Presage and SpacetimeDB.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![The opening film: CONTAINMENT BREACH](docs/screenshots/opening.jpg) | ![The sealed shelter, with the recorded briefing on the radio](docs/screenshots/shelter.jpg) |
| ![Co-op: the player hears the fault, the friend's manual says which machine](docs/screenshots/coop.jpg) | ![The spectator page: one live FEAR reading and the readings behind it](docs/screenshots/spectator.jpg) |

## The game

The containment tube fails, you run for the emergency shelter, and the door seals behind you. A recorded message from the station director explains the rules: the specimen is nearly blind but hears everything. The only way out is the basement, whose door has four locks. Each research protocol on the terminal releases one. You have **five minutes** before the sedative wears off.

- **Everything you do makes noise.** Running machines, wrong answers and the door motor all raise your exposure. There is no alarm and no countdown: you hear its footsteps get louder and quicker, from the direction it is in, and it pounds on the wall when it is there.
- **Go quiet in time.** Pull the lever (Q) to silence the machines and let it lose interest, then bring the power back (hold F) once the steps fade. You have three isolation cells, and get one back per completed stage. Once it commits at the wall, it is too late.
- **Your body is an input.** With the camera on, Presage estimates your pulse, breathing and facial fear. A racing heart makes the heartbeat mask and the calm hold harder, and calming down makes it lose your trail. These are camera estimates for a game, never medical readings, and the game plays fine without a camera.

| Stage | Puzzles (order shuffled per run) | Releases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Find 6 faults by ear (the rack key plays each machine's sound once) · patch 6 cables · rotate the conduit | Lock 1 |
| 2 | Repeat a growing signal sequence (3 → 5) · tap along to mask your heartbeat · transmit the lure to emitter A | Lock 2 |
| 3 | 8 faults by ear, two at a time, with a new sound key · 12 cables · mark it on the sonar three times | Lock 3 |
| 4 | A longer sequence (4 → 6) · breathe with the calm pacer until it loses your trail · emitter B | Lock 4 |
| Final | Send the last decoy and start the (loud) basement door motor | The ending |

## Ways to play

- **Begin with tutorial:** seven guided practice cards, read aloud by the radio, with the threat paused. The real run follows.
- **Skip tutorial & start:** straight into a run. A session's first run opens with Dr. Hale's recorded briefing.
- **Play with a friend:** send a link and your friend becomes your lifeline. Co-op is asymmetric: they hold an eight-page field manual you cannot see (fault sounds, cable codes, conduit boards, signal symbols, radar keys, the breathing pacer, the heartbeat mask, the door key), so you describe what you hear and they tell you what to press. Neither of you can finish alone. They can also flash a warning lamp in your shelter, fire decoys far out in the trees, and talk to you over optional voice chat.
- **Spectate:** anyone with the link watches live, read only: a shelter camera rebuilt from the game (your researcher at their station), the creature's distance, a map with physics props, key moments, predictions, your optional webcam and, only if you allow it, one live **FEAR** reading with your heart rate, breathing, expression, blink rate and heart-rate variability under it.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Click equipment / **E** | Use the terminal, the sonar monitor or the lever |
| **Space** | Step back from the equipment |
| **1–4** | Answer the current task (faults, conduit, heartbeat taps, memory, sonar marks) |
| **T** | Transmit a lure, engage the conduit, or start the door motor |
| **R** | Replay the signal sequence (free, but it costs time) |
| Drag a cable, or select cable then socket | Patch the relay |
| **Q** | Isolate the equipment (one cell) |
| Hold **F** | Restore power (from 4 s into an isolation; it restores itself at 25 s) |
| Hold **B** | Breathe in with the calm pacer; release to breathe out |
| Station buttons / drag | Face the terminal, the sonar or the lever; look around |
| **Esc** | Pause. **Settings** there turns on captions (off by default), reduced motion and softer scares; fixed memory tempo is under Operator settings on the start screen |

## Run it

```sh
git clone https://github.com/samerrahman/CalHacks-13.0.git
cd CalHacks-13.0
npm ci
cp .env.example .env.local   # optional provider keys; never commit
npm run dev                  # http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

The dev server reads `.env` / `.env.local` only at startup, so restart `npm run dev` after changing keys. Without keys the game still runs: the director falls back to its seeded rules and spoken lines fall back to captions.

```sh
npm run desktop       # build and launch the Electron app (native Presage camera, providers)
npm run check         # typecheck, all tests, web and Electron builds
npm run spacetime:generate   # regenerate client bindings after a module schema change
npm run cutscene -- render   # re-render the opening film (see cutscene/README.md)
```

Verified on macOS (Apple Silicon), Node 22 and Electron 45. WebGL and Web Audio are required. The desktop app uses Presage's native SDK; the browser build estimates pulse from the camera itself.

## How it is built

| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `src/game/` | The deterministic game: a fixed-step reducer owns time, the creature, puzzles, danger and the deadline. Nothing waits on the network, and every AI proposal is revalidated here. |
| `src/render/`, `src/ui/` | Three.js renders the

# Blackthornes Farmer

A WoW: Forever addon that answers one question: **where do I farm this?**

Type a material and it gives you back every source it knows about — the mob or
the node, the zone, and the level range you will be fighting in — sorted lowest
level first.

```
/farm wool cloth

- Wool Cloth (Cloth, 20 spots)
  MOB   SOURCE                  WHERE                                  LEVEL   DROP
  MOB   Shadowfang Moonwalker   Silverpine Forest / Shadowfang Keep    22-23   ####------  45%
  MOB   Shadowfang Darksoul     Silverpine Forest / Shadowfang Keep    23-24   ####------  42%
  MOB   Syndicate Rogue         Hillsbrad Foothills / Durnholde Keep   25-26   ###-------  32%
  MOB   Blackrock Champion      Redridge Mountains / Stonewatch Keep   24-26   ###-------  30%
```

Levels are coloured the way the game colours a target, so you can see at a
glance what you can actually kill. Click any row to print it to chat with its
coordinates, which is how you paste a spot to someone.

The same box takes a zone or a mob name too, so it also answers "what is worth
farming here?":

```
/farm defias      ->  Linen Cloth, off Defias Trappers and Smugglers in Westfall, 12-18
/farm un'goro     ->  everything the database has in Un'Goro, by level
```

Built for the WoW: Forever beta client (`## Interface: 16001`), without Ace3 or
LibStub, matching [Blackthornes Tradeskills](https://github.com/Blackthornes/Blackthornes_Tradeskills).
The two share a palette on purpose — they are worn together.

## Install

### Linked to your working copy (recommended while developing)

Run this once, and from then on testing a branch is pulling it and typing
`/reload`:

```powershell
.\tools\link.ps1
```

It junctions `Interface\AddOns\Blackthornes_Farmer` to this folder, so the
client reads your checkout directly. Nothing is copied, so there is no deploy
step to forget.

Two things `/reload` will **not** pick up, because the client only reads them at
startup:

- a file that was **added, removed or renamed**
- any change to **`Blackthornes_Farmer.toc`**

After pulling a branch that did either, restart the client once. Everything
else — a changed Lua file, new data, a UI tweak — is live on `/reload`.

### Copied into the client

If you would rather keep the client's copy separate from the repo:

```powershell
.\deploy.ps1              # syntax check, lint, then mirror into Interface\AddOns
.\deploy.ps1 -SkipCheck   # skip the checks (not recommended)
```

Both scripts default to `D:\Blizzard\World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_`. Pass
`-GamePath` if the client lives somewhere else.

The addon folder name has to stay `Blackthornes_Farmer`, matching the `.toc`
inside it. If they differ, the client ignores the folder and says nothing.

## Use

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/farm <text>` | search, and show the results in the window |
| `/farm` | open or close the window |
| `/farm settings` | open the settings window (`options` and `config` work too) |
| `/farm tracker [on\|off]` | show or hide the kills and loot panel (`reset confirm` clears the tallies) |
| `/farm tracker clear` | empty what the kills and loot panel shows and start a new run (the tallies are kept) |
| `/farm tracker group [on\|off]` | move the panel aside from the party and raid frames when grouped (on by default) |
| `/farm tracker size [small\|normal\|large\|50-150%]` | how big the kills and loot panel is drawn |
| `/farm kills [mob]` | a mob's kill tally and drop rates in chat |
| `/farm fishing [all]` | what you have caught in this zone, or everywhere (`reset confirm` clears it) |
| `/farm gathering [all\|check]` | herbs and ore you have gathered in this zone, or everywhere; `check` lists herbs or ore credited to a mob (`reset confirm` clears it) |
| `/farm markers [on\|off]` | markers where you gathered herbs and ore, on the world map and minimap (on by default; `map on\|off` or `minimap on\|off` for one, `clear confirm` removes them) |
| `/farm celebrate [on\|off]` | the fanfare when a mob reaches 20 kills, a fishing spot 20 casts or a node 20 gathers, and its rates unlock (on by default) |
| `/farm effects [full\|subtle\|off]` | how much the addon moves: in the kill panel, glows, the value counting up and loot floating off the panel; in the windows, fading up as they open, results coming in row by row and bars growing (full by default; subtle drops the floats and the row-by-row; off stops it all) |
| `/farm raresound [on\|off]` | a chime when something green or better drops (on by default) |
| `/farm rankup [on\|off\|sound on\|sound off\|show]` | a pop-up when a kill moves a mob up your top 15 by worth per kill, or onto it, with a short chime (both on by default); `show` holds up the top 15 as it stands |
| `/farm goal <item> <amount>` | set a gathering goal, e.g. `/farm goal Copper Ore 40`; on its own, lists your goals (`remove <item>`, `clear` for finished ones, `bank on\|off` to count your bank) |
| `/farm where <item>` | the best places near you to farm it, nearest first |
| `/farm arrow [on\|off]` | an arrow on screen that points to the nearest place to gather a goal (on with your first new goal, unless you have turned it off; `next` for the next place, `<goal>` to follow that goal, `check` for what the game lets it read, `tomtom` to use TomTom's arrow or not, `reset` puts it back) |
| `/farm tooltip` | turn the "Farm:" line on material tooltips on or off (on by default) |
| `/farm killcount` | turn the kill count on mob tooltips on or off (on by default) |
| `/farm skinning [on\|off]` | show skinning, or leave it out and show only drops: no skinning spots, leather or hides in search, Rankings, Grind, a mob's drops or its worth (left out by default; nothing recorded is lost) |
| `/farm hide <name>` | hide a mob, node or item from the search, Rankings, Grind and the kills panel (or right-click it there); `/farm unhide <name>` shows it again, `/farm hidden` lists what you hid |
| `/farm goals [dock]` | show or hide the goals pan

# Blackthornes Butler

A WoW: Forever addon that tells you what to do with every item in your bags:
keep it, sell it, post it on the auction house, disenchant it, or mail it to
the alt who needs it.

Built for the WoW: Forever client (`## Interface: 16001`), without Ace3 or
LibStub, matching
[Blackthornes Farmer](https://github.com/Blackthornes/Blackthornes_Farmer),
[Blackthornes Tradeskills](https://github.com/Blackthornes/Blackthornes_Tradeskills),
[Blackthornes Equipment](https://github.com/Blackthornes/Blackthornes_Equipment)
and [Blackthornes Pets](https://github.com/Blackthornes/Blackthornes_Pets).
They share a palette and a framework on purpose, and Butler asks each of
them about your items when they are installed. Without them it still works,
from vendor prices and the game's own quest marks.

- **The Butler window** lists every item in your bags in groups, each
  with its count and what it is worth:
  - **Sell**: grey items, your Always sell list, items a vendor pays
    more for than the auction house, and, if you set an amount, anything
    worth less than it.
  - **Auction**: items worth more on the auction house, after the cut
    (marked down when they sell slowly).
  - **Disenchant**: items worth more as enchanting materials, when you can
    disenchant them.
  - **Mail**: items an alt needs for their crafts (only what your own
    crafts can spare), gear that's an upgrade for another of your
    characters, or that your enchanter alt should disenchant. Right-click
    an upgrade to stop mailing that item, or any upgrade, to that character.
  - **Look at it**: everything Butler can't judge yet, with what a vendor
    pays. Soulbound green or better gear never goes under Sell.
  - **Keep**: quest items, upgrades and tools, what your Farmer goals and
    craft queue need, your pet's food, anything a vendor won't buy, and your
    Always keep list.

  Click a group's heading to fold it; Keep starts folded. Without the other
  addons, Butler sorts by vendor price and the game's quest marks alone.
- **Right-click** an item to always keep it, always sell it, always bank it,
  always mail it to one of your characters, or let Butler decide again. The
  lists are account wide.
- **It learns from you.** Buy back something Butler sold and it keeps it
  from then on. Sell an item yourself at a vendor on two visits and it goes
  under Sell. Mail an item to the same one of your characters twice and it
  goes under Mail to them. Your own right-click choices always win, and
  right-click can forget what it learned. "Learn from what you do" in
  Settings turns it off.
- **Sell below** (Settings, or `/bbutler sellbelow 50s`): set an amount
  and anything worth less than it, at the most it could fetch from a
  vendor, the auction house or a disenchant, goes under Sell. Quest items,
  upgrades, goal and craft materials, pet food, soulbound green or better
  gear and your Always keep, bank and mail items are never included, and
  nothing sells until you click Sell. It needs Blackthornes Tradeskills for
  auction prices; off until you set it.
- **Gold fund** (Settings, Gold, or `/bbutler goldmin 50g`): set how much
  gold every character keeps, and a different amount for any one of them
  if you like. At a mailbox, a character with more is offered a gold mail
  to each of your characters below theirs (the Gold rows), never going
  below its own amount; Fill mail puts the gold in and you press Send.
  Balances are as last seen when each character played, and the row says
  how old. `/bbutler gold` lists everyone's. Needs Blackthornes
  Tradeskills; off until you set it.
- **Ammo** (hunters): at a vendor that sells ammo for your bow, crossbow
  or gun, Butler offers to fill your quiver or ammo pouch with the best
  ammo there you can use, as many as fit, and the Fill button buys it. It
  says so when your bag doesn't match your weapon. Your own ammo is never put under Sell.
- **At a mailbox,** the window comes up in place of Tradeskills' mail panel
  (close it to get that back), with a **Fill mail** button when something
  is under Mail. Each click fills the game's Send Mail page for one
  character; you check it and press Send. Once that mail goes, Butler fills
  the next one straight away, so a run of mail is one Send a character
  ("Fill the next mail" in Settings, or `/bbutler fillnext`). Needs
  Blackthornes Tradeskills.
- **At the bank,** **Move to bank** puts away everything on your Always bank
  list, and **Take from bank** brings out what your craft queue needs (with
  Tradeskills). Both move whole stacks.
- **All characters** lists every item on all your characters in one place,
  with a search box. Each line says who has it and how many in all; click
  it to see each character's bags, bank and mail, and how long ago that was
  seen. Your other characters come from Blackthornes Tradeskills, which
  remembers them as you play each one; without it you see your own bags.
- **Butler's voice:** open the window and Karazhan's butler says "You
  rang?"; close it and he picks up where he was. Never over a vendor or
  other NPC, at most once every few minutes, and off with a tick box in
  Settings.
- **Sell at a vendor.** The window comes up by itself at every vendor, with
  a Sell button at its foot when there is something to sell. Nothing sells until
  you click it, and it only ever sells what is under Sell. Each click sells
  one stack; if `/bbutler selltest` finds the game lets Butler sell from its
  own code, each click sells up to 12, which is what the vendor's Buyback
  tab holds, so every sale can be bought back.

## Install

### Linked to your working copy (recommended while developing)

Run this once, and from then on testing a branch is pulling it and typing
`/reload`:

```powershell
.\tools\link.ps1
```

It junctions `Interface\AddOns\Blackthornes_Butler` to this folder, so the
client reads your checkout directly. Nothing is copied, so there is no deploy
step to forget.

Blackthornes/Blackthornes_Tradeskills_Cl.readme:
# Blackthornes_Tradeskills

Tradeskill addon for WoW: Forever. It works out which crafts are worth making,
scans the auction house for the prices that answer depends on, and manages a
craft queue, a shopping list and a posting list around it.

Built without Ace3 or LibStub, because neither is known to work on Forever yet.
The small framework in `Core/` is written for this addon instead, so it does not
have to wait for anyone else to update theirs.

## Layout

| Folder | What is in it |
|---|---|
| `Core/` | Slash commands, settings, checking what the game supports, saving your data between sessions, and spacing out requests to the auction house |
| `Data/` | Everything read from the game: prices, auction scans, recipes, bags and bank, your own listings, vendor prices |
| `Logic/` | Craft cost, profit, the queue, starting crafts, posting, and export/import |
| `UI/` | Theme, reusable widgets, the main window, the auction house side panel, and the seven tabs |
| `Probe/` | `/bts probe`, which checks what the running game actually supports instead of guessing |

`Blackthornes_TS.toc` lists every Lua file in load order. A file that is not in
it does not load, and WoW says nothing about it.

## Development

Not shipped to the client: `tools/`, `docs/`, `deploy.ps1`. `deploy.ps1`
excludes them.

```powershell
.\deploy.ps1              # syntax check, lint, then mirror into Interface\AddOns
.\deploy.ps1 -SkipCheck   # skip the checks (not recommended)
```

```bash
python tools/syntaxcheck.py   # parse every Lua file with a real 5.1 parser
python tools/lintcalls.py     # find calls to methods, and constants, never defined
python tools/runtests.py      # run the pure-logic tests outside WoW
```

These checks matter because WoW quietly turns off an addon when one of its
files has a typo in it, and a call to a function that no longer exists only
fails when that line of code runs.

`tools/` requires `lupa` (`python -m pip install --user lupa`).

## A note on saved data

Since WoW: Forever build 1.60.1.70009 (2026-09-24) the game keeps the addon's
saved data (`BlackthornesTSDB` and `BlackthornesTSCharDB`) across a restart,
so nothing else is needed. The old workarounds, a generated data addon and
storage in macros, were removed; `Core/OldMacros.lua` deletes the leftover
`BTSd` macros on a login where the saved data loaded. The CVar store in
`Core/Persist.lua` stays as a fallback and stands down whenever the saved data
loads. `/bts db` and `/bts persist` show what loaded.

## API findings

`docs/FOREVER_API_FINDINGS.md` records what the game actually does, as found
with `/bts probe` rather than taken from documentation. Read it before changing
anything to do with the auction house or professions.

## Releasing

Releases are cut by pushing a tag like `v0.2.0`.
`.github/workflows/release.yml` then:

1. refuses the tag unless `CHANGELOG.md` opens with a `## 0.2.0` section
   (`tools/check_release.py`);
2. runs the tests;
3. builds the player-facing zip with the
   [BigWigs packager](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager), uploading
   nothing;
4. checks that zip is clear to post (`tools/check_package.py`): only the
   addon's own files, and nothing that looks private, such as a Windows path,
   an email address, a saved-variables dump or a token;
5. only then uploads that same zip to CurseForge (project 1763353, Tradeskills Classic) and
   attaches it to a GitHub release.

To release from GitHub Desktop: add the new version's section to the top of
`CHANGELOG.md` and merge it to `main`, pull `main`, then **History**, right-click
the newest commit, **Create Tag...**, name it `v0.2.0`, and **Push origin**.

The version is never typed by hand. The TOC says
`## Version: @project-version@` and the packager fills in the tag. Running
straight from a clone there is no packager, so the addon shows
`ns.RELEASED_VERSION` from `Core/Init.lua`, the newest version in
CHANGELOG.md: the release PR changes both, and `tools/check_release.py`
refuses a tag they disagree with. The middle number moves for new
behaviour, the last for fixes alone; a tag like `v0.3.0-beta1` is uploaded as a beta.

`.pkgmeta` leaves `tools/`, `docs/`, `deploy.ps1` and this README out of the
zip. The upload needs the `CF_API_KEY` repository secret; without it the
workflow still builds and checks the zip but uploads nothing to CurseForge.

## For addon authors

Other addons can read Tradeskills' auction prices through one global. Check
that it exists, since Tradeskills may not be installed:

```lua
local api = BlackthornesTS_API
if api then
    local copper = api.GetPrice(2589)          -- item ID or item link; copper for one, or nil
    local age = api.GetPriceAge(2589)          -- seconds since this account's own scan saw it, or nil
end
```

- `GetPrice` is the market value Tradeskills itself uses: the player's own
  scans first, then guild prices and other price sources for items not
  scanned. It is per realm and faction.
- `GetPriceAge` is nil when the price did not come from this account's own
  scans.
- Neither call raises an error; anything it can't answer is nil.
- `BlackthornesTS_API.version` is 1. These calls will not be renamed or
  changed; new ones raise the version.

malinkin-s/naruto-rise-of-a-ninja-nx.desc: Nintendo Switch homebrew port of Naruto: Rise of a Ninja (Xbox 360): static recompilation with ReXGlue, Renut renderer on deko3d. Work in progress, bring your own game.
malinkin-s/naruto-rise-of-a-ninja-nx.readme:
English · Русский

A Nintendo Switch (homebrew NRO) port of **Naruto: Rise of a Ninja** (Ubisoft Montreal, 2007, Xbox 360 exclusive). The game's PowerPC code is statically recompiled with [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk); the Xbox 360 GPU is not emulated: Direct3D calls are drawn by Renut, a Direct3D-level renderer, on deko3d, the Switch's native graphics API. > [!IMPORTANT] > **[Version 0.1.1](https://github.com/malinkin-s/naruto-rise-of-a-ninja-nx/releases/tag/v0.1.1) is the first test > build.** The story mode and fights play on a real console, but expect bugs and crashes. The game's files are not > included: you need your own copy of the game (installation: [the release page](https://github.com/malinkin-s/naruto-rise-of-a-ninja-nx/releases/tag/v0.1.1)). ## Status **Version 0.1.0, 2026-10-25.** Measured on a Nintendo Switch at stock clocks (handheld, CPU 1020 MHz, GPU 460 MHz). | Area | Switch | Notes | |---|---|---| | Boot, logos, menus | **Works** | 24–29 FPS in menus | | Story mode (Konoha, the open world) | **Works** | about 20 FPS (the game's logic runs at 30); ground shadows fixed | | Fights | **Works** | 32–47 FPS at 1280×720, 46–58 FPS at 854×480 (fights run at 60) | | Saves on the SD card | **Works** | Created, listed and loaded | | Bink video (cutscenes) | **Works** | The intro and the first story scenes; not checked through the whole game | | Controller | **Works** | Played by hand in the story mode | | Settings (`naruto.toml`) | **Works** | Render resolution handheld / docked, the game's anti-aliasing | | Audio | Plays | Not checked in depth | | Character DLC (3 extra engines) | Not yet | | | Known issues | | Possible crashes when quitting; the "Saved Game Warning" scroll border differs from the Xbox 360 | Performance so far: sa2-nx's enhancements, an optimised code generator (registers as locals, direct calls, guest memory without volatile, float-mode switches skipped), store cards for Renut's caches. Next: the GPU (fights are GPU-bound at 720p) and the CPU work of the open world. ### What was solved to get here - **Older Direct3D than any earlier Renut port** (XDK 2.0.6274, LTCG): the private device layout, functions and offsets were mapped using the PC recompilation's renderer as a reference ([docs/d3d-census.md](docs/d3d-census.md), [docs/renut-retarget.md](docs/renut-retarget.md)). - **3,322 game shaders** from `xeshader.sdb` translated (XenosRecomp → DXC → SPIRV-Cross → uam for deko3d). - **Tiled rendering**: the game draws its 3D scene in three 1280×256 tiles with 4× MSAA (the Xbox 360's EDRAM); Renut's targets now cover all tiles. - **The game engine `ai2c.dll`** is linked into the NRO as a static module. - **Automated console tests over nxlink** (`tools/switch/nxtest.sh`): the game runs for a set time, sends its log, renderer frames, its profile and crash reports to the PC, and exits by itself. - **Ground shadows**: the game's polygon offset (depth bias) was ignored by Renut, which cut decal shadows into wedges. The full story, with evidence for every step, is in [docs/port-journal.md](docs/port-journal.md). ## Screenshots Taken from the renderer on a Nintendo Switch (half size, 640×360), version 0.1.0 at stock clocks.
Story mode: Konoha The village plaza

## How it is built | Part | From | |---|---| | Recompiled code | ReXGlue SDK, the [sa2-nx](https://github.com/ChanseyIsTheBest/sa2-nx) fork (Horizon layer, static guest modules) | | PC base and reference | [jorjbarbosa/naruto-rise-recomp](https://github.com/jorjbarbosa/naruto-rise-recomp): seeds, hooks, the Direct3D map | | Renderer | Renut (masterspike52) on plume's deko3d back end, from sa2-nx, retargeted to Naruto's Direct3D | | Toolchain | devkitA64 (GCC 16.1) in Docker, libnx, deko3d | ### Installing Through the installer page, which makes the game's shaders from your own disc: **https://malinkin-s.github.io/naruto-nx-installer/**. reseed-ops/bubbles-even-g2.readme:
# Bubbles – a sideways bubble shooter for Even G2

A minimal Frozen Bubble / Puzzle Bobble style game for Even Realities G2
glasses. No characters, no art: an aim line, bubbles stacked against the right
edge, and the touchpad.

- **Swipe up or down** to aim, also while a shot is still flying. Each swipe moves the aim to the next cell the bubble could land in, turning by at most 8°, so no reachable spot is skipped. The line shows where the bubble will go, bounces included.
- **Tap** the touchpad or R1 ring to shoot. Three or more of a kind pop; anything left hanging falls. A tap while a shot is still flying queues the next one, fired the moment this one lands; clearing the level cancels it.
- **Hold** the touchpad to swap the loaded bubble with the next one. (Centering the aim moved to the menu; every new game starts centered.)
- **Tap, then hold** to open the G2 contextual menu, where you can restart or center the aim.
- **Double tap** to open the G2 system exit confirmation from any screen.
- **Tap, then hold** also switches mode (classic, pulley, endless, puzzle) and
  cycles the difficulty.
- **Swipe on the title or game-over screen** to pick the level to start on, up to
  the highest level you have reached. A returning player starts where they got
  to; after a game over, "play again" continues on the same level. Starting
  higher always starts at score 0.

The aim guide ends in a landing marker and stays up while a shot is in
flight, so you can line up the next one straight away: the moment a bubble
leaves, the queued bubble moves into the launcher and the line is its line.
During the flight the prediction is against the board as it stands; it
corrects itself when the shot lands. Clearing a board gets a short level card
before the next layout appears,
and the game-over screen says when you have set a new best.

During play, a dotted line marks the loss zone, the launcher tilts with the
selected angle, and the queued bubble is labeled at bottom left. A tick (┫) moves
down the wall once per shot to show when its eight-shot advance is approaching.
Flying bubbles leave a two-cell trail. Matches animate through sparkle, burst
and ring glyphs, while detached bubbles visibly fall for the same three frames.
The level number stands in fullwidth digits down the top-left corner, in the
column no bubble can ever occupy; score and best live on the phone page and
the end screens.

Scoring: 10 points per bubble popped, and bubbles that fall because a match
detached them pay exponentially, 20 for one, 60 for two, 140 for three and so
on (20 × (2ⁿ − 1), capped at eight), so the shot that cuts a cluster loose is
worth more than the easy match. Clearing a level is 100. The best score only
competes among games started at level 1; a game started higher shows its score
but cannot set a best. A clear of five or more bubbles blasts: an extra effect
frame and a ring of empty cells ripples outward; ten or more gets two rings.

### Special bubbles

From level 3 the layouts carry a few specials, drawn with glyphs the firmware
font has. A star ☆: a shot that lands next to it clears every bubble of the
shot's colour. A rainbow ※ joins any colour, so it bridges matches; the odd
shot is a rainbow too, and it takes whichever neighbouring colour pops most.
A bomb ♨ (from level 4): a shot landing beside it blows away everything
around it, and any bomb caught in the blast goes off too. Ice ▦ (from level
5): a pop beside it cracks it to ▤, a second pop frees it. A stone ▩ (from
level 6) never pops and only falls when nothing holds it. Mystery bubbles ？
are ordinary colours hidden until a shot lands or a pop happens beside them.

### Pickups and the second chance

From level 2 a ＋ sometimes appears in the open part of the field. A shot that
flies through it loads a special as the next bubble: a rainbow, a bomb that
goes off where it lands, or a star that clears the colour it lands against.
Aim for the pickup on the way to the target. One pickup is out at a time.

Once per game, a game over offers a continue: tap, and the three columns
nearest the shooter are cleared (puzzle mode also gets five shots back) and
play goes on. The run no longer counts for the best score; the best was
recorded at the moment you first went down.

### Scoring extras

Consecutive shots that remove something build a combo: the second pays
double, the third triple, up to five times, shown as Ｘ２ … Ｘ５ under the
launcher. A shot that removes nothing resets it. The bubble after next is
shown above the next one. Each mode keeps its own best score.

### Pulley mode

The Bust-A-Move 4 idea: two groups hang from one axle (╋ on the shooter row),
the rows above it and the rows below, each on its own wall. The group with
more bubbles hangs closer to you, one column per four bubbles of difference,
up to four. Pop on one side and the other side swings in; anything a shift
tears loose falls. Levels are the same 100 layouts with the axle row left
clear. Pulley is the default; switch to classic from the G2 menu, the phone
page, or `?mode=classic`. The choice is remembered.

### Endless and puzzle modes

Endless: a random board five columns deep, and every six shots a fresh column
pushes in from the wall (with the odd gap and, from wave 2, specials). The
wall never moves; the pushes are the pressure, and the hurry-up pushes a
column instead of moving the wall. Waves count up in the HUD; the palette
widens every three waves. Clearing the board pays the level bonus and deals a
new one.

Puzzle: the same 100 layouts with a shot limit, half the level's bubbles plus
five, counted down under the launcher. No wall advance and no hurry-up: run
out of shots with bubbles left and the game is over.

### Difficulty, levels beyond 100, and stats

Difficulty (phone page or the G2 menu): easy moves the wall every 10 shots
and never hurries you; normal every 8 with the hurry-up; hard every 6 with a
faster hurry-up. Puzzle mode gets 8, 5 or 3 spare shots. In endless, waves
start

Pressing Measure push cost while a frame was in flight made every probe
push drop instantly, so the run finished in a millisecond with NaN
results. Each probe now waits for the slot first. The blast ring no
longer marks cells beyond the wall, which replaced the wall glyphs with

Shots stop only on head-on or side contact

# Phredd's Card Table, Puzzle Table, Mahjong, Word Search and Marble Challenge

Relaxing game apps for Android phones and Amazon Fire tablets, designed for comfortable play: big, clear pieces, large buttons, unlimited undo, and no ads, accounts or timers unless you want them.

- **Phredd's Card Table** (`app/`): Klondike, Spider and FreeCell Solitaire.
- **Phredd's Puzzle Table** (`puzzle-app/`): Sudoku in 4 × 4, 6 × 6 and 9 × 9, four difficulties, and a daily puzzle (made on the device, each with exactly one answer); and Towers of Hanoi with 3 to 8 discs.
- **Phredd's Mahjong** (`mahjong-app/`): Mahjong Solitaire with six boards from 24 to 144 tiles and three original tile styles (Flower Garden, Bright Shapes, Classic). Every deal can be cleared.
- **Phredd's Word Search** (`wordsearch-app/`): 19 themes, three sizes, three difficulties and a daily puzzle.
- **Phredd's Marble Challenge** (`marbles-app/`): six games, each with four levels up to Expert. Marble Sort (Classic, Hidden Marbles and Tall Tubes), Peg Solitaire (ten boards, including the Fireplace, Arrow and Diamond), Code Breaker (Phredd makes the code, or play together and let a friend make it), Memory Match (Everyday Pictures, Farm Animals or Garden), Marble Lines, and Marble Sudoku (Sudoku with nine colors of marble instead of numbers). Every Marble Sort deal is checked to be solvable, and hints in Sort and Peg Solitaire come from a solver.
- **Shared parts** (`core-ui/`): the theme, large buttons, dialogs, settings rows and help pages used by all five apps, the Sudoku puzzle maker shared by the Puzzle Table and Marble Sudoku, the sound effects, and the opening picture of Phredd, a chestnut and white Appaloosa, in his barnyard (drawn in code in `core-ui/src/main/java/com/avistable/core/ui/PhreddSplash.kt`).

## Installing a test build

Every change pushed to `main` is built automatically by GitHub.

1. On your phone or Fire tablet, open this repository's **Releases** page and choose **Latest test build**.
2. Tap `PhreddCardTable-….apk`, `PhreddPuzzleTable-….apk`, `PhreddMahjong-….apk`, `PhreddWordSearch-….apk` or `PhreddMarbleChallenge-….apk` to download it, then open it. These need Android 9 / Fire OS 7 or newer. For older tablets (Fire OS 5 or 6), run the build from the Actions page with "Also build the Classic apps" ticked, and choose the `…-Classic-….apk` files.
3. If asked, allow installing apps from this source:
   - **Android phone:** Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Special app access ▸ Install unknown apps ▸ your browser ▸ Allow.
   - **Fire tablet:** Settings ▸ Security & Privacy ▸ Apps from Unknown Sources ▸ your browser (Silk) ▸ On.
4. Each new build installs over the previous one, and your saved game and settings are kept.

## For developers

- Kotlin and Jetpack Compose; needs no Google Play services. Every app has two builds: **Modern** (Android 9 / Fire OS 7 and newer) and **Classic** (Android 5.1 / Fire OS 5 and newer), which leaves out screen fades, confetti and card animations so older tablets keep up.
- `./gradlew :app:testModernDebugUnitTest --tests '*KlondikeTest' --tests '*SpiderFreeCellTest' :puzzle-app:testModernDebugUnitTest --tests '*SudokuTest' --tests '*HanoiTest' :mahjong-app:testModernDebugUnitTest --tests '*MahjongTest' :wordsearch-app:testModernDebugUnitTest --tests '*WordSearchTest' :marbles-app:testModernDebugUnitTest --tests '*MarblesTest'` checks the game and puzzle rules.
- `./gradlew recordPaparazziModernDebug` renders the art and screens to each app's `src/test/snapshots/images/` for review without a device.
- The Large Print and Classic faces and the first seven backs are original artwork, drawn in code (`app/src/main/java/com/aviscardtable/ui/cards/`). The vintage styles are described below.
- `python3 tools/make_sounds.py` remakes the sound effects in `core-ui/src/main/res/raw/`. Every sound is synthesized from scratch, so they are all our own.
- `app/test-signing.jks` is a shared key for test builds only. Store releases will use a separate key that is never committed.

## Vintage card art

The **Victorian** and **Early American** card styles, and their matching backs, use scans of two public-domain 19th-century decks from the Bibliothèque nationale de France (source: gallica.bnf.fr / BnF), obtained through Wikimedia Commons:

- B.P. Grimaud, Paris: American-style deck (court cards, engraved Ace of Spades, blue back)
- Thomas Crehore, Boston: full-length court cards and a starred back

`tools/prepare_vintage_art.py` crops each figure to its printed frame, removes library stamps and evens the paper colour, writing the results to `app/src/main/res/drawable-nodpi/`. Gallica allows free non-commercial reuse with this credit; check its terms again before any paid release.

cgolivaresv/carioca-app.readme:
# Carioca

Juego de carioca para 1 jugador contra 1 a 4 bots (mesas de 2 a 5 jugadores), con 10 avatares para elegir. Sin build ni dependencias: son archivos estáticos que funcionan como PWA (instalable y sin internet).

## Estructura
- `index.html`, `style.css`: página y estilos.
- `src/engine.js`: reglas de las combinaciones (trío, escala, contratos, solucionador). Sin interfaz.
- `src/game.js`: reglas de la partida para 2 a 5 asientos (repartir, robar, bajarse, pegar, descartar, cerrar la ronda, puntaje y `viewFor`, que entrega a cada jugador solo lo que puede ver). Sin pantalla ni almacenamiento: la app y, más adelante, el servidor multijugador usan el mismo módulo.
- `src/bots.js`: jugadores virtuales (solo usan información pública; el reparto y los desempates son aleatorios).
- `src/app.js`: estado de la partida, turnos, pantalla, guardado y estadísticas (localStorage).
- `src/safe.js`: escapado de nombres para HTML y validación de la partida guardada.
- `src/online.js`, `src/net.js`, `src/config.js`: cliente del multijugador (traduce el estado del servidor a tu vista, WebSocket con reconexión y la dirección del servidor).
- `worker/`: servidor de Cloudflare (`core.js` = lógica de la sala, `index.js` = Worker y Durable Object). Config en `wrangler.toml`.
- `src/roster.js`, `src/avatars.js`, `src/lines.js`: jugadores, avatares (con respaldo SVG) y frases de los bots.
- `src/audio.js`, `src/joker.js`: sonidos y dibujo del comodín.
- `tools/sim.js`: simulación de partidas para medir el balance de los bots.
- `sw.js`, `manifest.webmanifest`, `icons/`, `avatars/`: PWA e imágenes.
- `tests/`: pruebas automáticas (`engine`, `bots`, `safe`, `mesa`, `game`).

## Reglas
- 10 rondas con contratos: 2 tríos · trío + escala de 4 · 2 escalas de 4 · 3 tríos · 2 tríos + escala · 2 escalas + trío · 3 escalas · 4 tríos · escala sucia · escala real.
- Trío: 3 o más cartas del mismo número. Escala: 4 o más del mismo palo y consecutivas. Los comodines deben ser menos que las cartas naturales de la combinación.
- Las escalas son circulares: `K-A-2-3` es válida. La escala de 13 cartas va de `A` a `K`; es sucia si mezcla palos o lleva comodines y real si es de un solo palo y sin comodines.
- Al bajarse no se pega en ese mismo turno. Puntos en mano: comodín 25, A 15, 10–K 10, 2–9 5.
- Si el mazo se agota dos veces, la ronda termina sin ganador y se cuentan las cartas en mano.

## Probar en tu computador
```
npm test            # pruebas automáticas
npm run sim         # simulación de bots (opcional: node tools/sim.js 300)
npm start           # servidor local en http://localhost:8080 (requiere Node.js 20 o superior)
```
(No abras `index.html` con doble clic: los módulos y el service worker necesitan un servidor.)

## Publicar
Sube la carpeta completa a Cloudflare Pages, Netlify o Vercel. No hay comando de build; el directorio de salida es la raíz (`/`). Necesita HTTPS, que estos servicios dan por defecto.

## Instalar en el celular
Abre la URL publicada: en Android, menú ⋮ > "Instalar app"; en iPhone, Compartir > "Añadir a pantalla de inicio".

## Al publicar una versión nueva
Cambia `V` en `sw.js` (por ejemplo `carioca-v49`) para renovar la caché, sube la versión visible en `index.html` (etiqueta "Versión" del menú) y en `package.json`, y si agregas archivos a `src/`, inclúyelos en `FILES`.

## Tamaño de la mesa
El menú principal elige cuántos rivales hay (1 a 4, por defecto 2). Siempre se juega con 2 mazos y 4 comodines (108 cartas) y 12 cartas por jugador; el que reparte rota con la ronda y el primero en jugar es el siguiente. Todo el estado usa `G.n` (jugadores en la mesa) y el asiento 0 es siempre el jugador.

## Guardado
La partida se guarda automáticamente en este dispositivo (también durante el turno de los bots) y se puede continuar desde el menú principal. Si el guardado está dañado, se descarta y se empieza una partida nueva.

## Ritmo de los bots
El bot juega cuando termina de "pensar", y cuánto tarda depende de lo difícil que sea su decisión (`effort()` en `src/bots.js`): las jugadas rutinarias salen en 1,5 a 3 s, las que implican bajarse o dudar sobre el descarte tardan algo más, y 1 de cada 5 turnos, al azar, el bot "duda" y espera el máximo. El máximo se elige en el menú de puntaje (7, 10, 15 o 20 s; por defecto 7 s). Con 7 s la espera media ronda los 3,5 s.

## Consumo de batería (móvil)
Al diseñar animaciones ten presente que, mientras algo se anima, el teléfono redibuja la pantalla completa en cada refresco (hasta 120 veces por segundo en un iPhone Pro). Por eso:
- Nada de `filter: blur()`, `mix-blend-mode` ni animar `box-shadow`, `width` o `background` en bucle; anima solo `transform` y `opacity`.
- Las animaciones continuas usan `steps()` (por ejemplo, las barras de tiempo avanzan 4 veces por segundo) o son finitas.
- Las luces de fondo solo se mueven en el menú: con la clase `ingame` en `<body>` quedan quietas.
- El reloj del turno (`setInterval`) solo funciona mientras hay un turno con tiempo límite.

## Multijugador en línea
Una sala admite de 2 a 5 asientos; las personas que entren juegan y los asientos libres los ocupan bots (siempre hay al menos una persona, así que como máximo hay 4 bots). El servidor (`worker/`) tiene el mazo y todas las manos y valida cada jugada con `src/game.js`; a cada jugador solo le envía su mano. Cada turno de una persona tiene un límite que elige el anfitrión (sin límite, 30, 45, 60 —por defecto— o 90 s): si se agota, el servidor roba del mazo y descarta por ella, y tras dos turnos agotados seguidos pasa a «ausente» (juega un bot por ella con una pausa corta) hasta que vuelva a jugar. Lo mismo ocurre si se desconecta; con el mismo navegador vuelve a entrar con su token. Si sale a propósito, un bot toma su asiento.

**Publicar el servidor (una sola vez)**
1. Cuenta gratuita en Cloudflare, con un subdominio `workers.dev` activado.
2. Crear un token de API con la plantilla «Editar Cloudflare Workers» y copiar el ID de cuenta.
3. En GitHub: Settings → Secrets

# Ball Knowledge
Co-op online sports-betting game set in a dive bar. Pick a sport, get a hidden real season, and bet your way through its last 10 games to the title. Cheat with the mob if you dare.

Run: `npm install && npm start` -> http://localhost:3000 (share the 4-letter room code; 1-6 players).
Dev: `BK_SPEED=10 npm start` divides every timer by 10 (full game in about a minute).

## How a game works
- **10-ish real games per season**, ending in the title game. A new game opens for betting every 2 minutes (or 50s on Quick pace); the betting window is a visible countdown.
- When the window closes the game goes **on the TV** for ~3 minutes (70s on Quick): a simulated highlights recap that always lands on the true final score. Bets pay out when it ends.
- **Markets**: moneyline, spread, total points. Lines are generated from team records (not historical lines). Team stats, form this season, series status and your crew's picks are in the betting UI.
- **Win condition**: put a moneyline bet on the champion of the title game. Crew wins if at least half the players do.
- **Bar**: buy drinks. Drunk confidence = gut-feeling hints on each game (more accurate as you get drunker, until you are wasted and they turn to nonsense). It wears off.
- **Mob (Uncle Sal)**: loans and game fixes (flips the real result, adds to your tab). Conflicting fixes cancel. At the end the mob collects; shortfalls bring the hitmen - pay, wire money, win cash, or fight them in the room.
- **Arcade (no more farming)**: darts, bowling and cornhole pay only when you beat an NPC's posted score in a **challenge** (stake from the bar's board; win streaks raise the stakes, caps apply). Practice mode pays nothing. Plus a 3D roulette wheel whose ball lands on the server's number.
- **Pool**: full 2D-physics pool table (your 4 solids vs an NPC's 4 stripes + the 8-ball). Pick Rookie or Shark, stake cash, win to double up.
- **Quota**: Uncle Sal sets crew net-worth checkpoints through the season. Miss one and his collectors shake you down (pay, fight, or forfeit cash). Hit the final quota for bonus tickets.
- **Chaos**: random bar events (happy hour, bar fight you can bet on, blackout, big tipper) and per-player bounties keep things moving.
- **Pro Shop**: earn tickets (finishing games, crew wins, quotas, bounties) and open crates for ~50 wearable items (helmets, jerseys, golf clubs, and more) in four rarities. Cosmetics are visible to the whole crew. Saved in browser localStorage.

## Controls
WASD move, mouse look, E interact, C crew/wire money, Esc releases the mouse / closes menus.

## Bottles
Grab 3 bottles at the bar (station near the stools, `E - Grab bottles`), throw with **F** or **right-click**. Bottles arc, spin and shatter on anything (glass-break sound + shards). A bottle that hits another player or an NPC knocks them out for 5 seconds (flat on their back / slumped if seated, stars overhead); the victim's controls lock and the camera drops to the floor. After waking there is 3 s of immunity. Flight is simulated on every client from the thrower's origin/velocity; only the thrower reports hits and the server accepts a hit only if the thrower really threw a bottle in the last 4 s (rate limited, one hit per throw).

## Sound & voice
- **Sound is fully synthesized in the browser** (`public/audio.js`, no audio files): ~55 effects, a spatial crowd/room ambience, and four procedural jukebox songs (E at the jukebox cycles them). Impacts exist for pool (cue, balls, cushions, pockets, break), darts (throw, board, bull), bowling (release, rolling rumble, pin hits, strikes, gutters), cornhole (throw, thud, hole), roulette (wheel whir, pocket ticks, drop), plus UI, drinks, footsteps, sitting, bar events (happy hour horn, blackout, fights), mob knocks/stings and crowd reactions to scoring plays on the TV. Sounds with a world position are 3D (HRTF) and follow the camera.
- **Voice chat** (`public/voice.js`): peer-to-peer WebRTC mesh (max 6 players); the server only relays signaling (`type:'rtc'`). Remote voices come out of their avatar's position, so you hear people where they stand (or "Whole bar" in settings). Join with the speaker button (bottom-right) or **O**; **hold V** to talk (or Open mic), **M** mutes. A green mic floats over whoever is speaking.
- Settings (volumes, mic mode, range, song) persist in `localStorage` (`bk_audio_v1`).
- **Deployment note:** browsers only allow the microphone on https (Railway is) or localhost. STUN is Google's public server; players behind strict NATs/corporate networks may need a TURN relay: set `TURN_URL` (comma-separated), `TURN_USER`, `TURN_PASS` on the server and `/ice.json` will hand it to clients.

## Files
- `seasons.js` - season data (real results). `server.js` - authoritative game state over WebSocket.
- **Look**: chunky faceted cartoon cast (Bub, the bartender, six regulars, Uncle Sal, hitmen, a crowd), dive-bar set with beams, windows, neon, chalkboard menu, ambient stylized sports broadcasts on the TVs, a live bar behind the title screen, bloom + color grade, and a four-stage drunk look.
- `public/` - client: `client.js` (2D UI), `world.js` (3D loop), `bar.js` (environment + NPCs), `tv.js`, `roulette.js`, `games.js`, `pool.js`, `cosmetics.js`, `people.js` (characters + hands), `textures.js`, `fx.js` (bloom + drunk shader). Three.js is vendored in `public/vendor/`.

## Characters (Blender pipeline)
The ten cast members are authored in Blender from the reference pack and exported as `public/models/*.glb`; the game loads them at startup (`public/people.js`) and falls back to the old procedural people for any custom variant a model cannot express (`?models=0` forces the fallback).
- Source: `blender/lib.py` (primitives, export, render), `blender/chars.py` (generic person builder), `blender/specs.py` (the 10 characters), `blender/textures.py` (jersey/floral/pinstripe prints).
- Rebuild: `pip install bpy` (Blender as a Python module), then `python3 blender/build.py [names]`. Output: GLBs

NermalYT/StreamLite.desc: Free AI noise removal for your mic, 3D game audio and headphone EQ - for Windows and Linux
NermalYT/StreamLite.readme:
# StreamLite

**A clean mic, 3D game audio and better-sounding headphones - free, for Windows and Linux.**

StreamLite sits between your microphone and Discord, OBS, Zoom, TeamSpeak or your game and removes keyboard clicks,
fans, PC hum, traffic and room noise with AI. It also turns games' 7.1 surround into 3D sound for your headphones,
corrects your headphones to sound neutral, and switches headphone profiles for games, music and voice chat on its own.

**[Download](https://github.com/NermalYT/StreamLite/releases/latest)** ·
**[Manual](https://nermalyt.github.io/StreamLite/)** ·
**[Report a bug](https://github.com/NermalYT/StreamLite/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml)** ·
[Credits](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)

![StreamLite's 3D audio page with the sound cube](docs/img/windows-3d.png)

## What it does

- **Clean microphone.** AI noise removal with RNNoise (light) or DeepFilterNet 3 (studio quality, runs on your
  graphics card on Windows). Includes a noise gate, auto level, compressor, de-esser and EQ. Apps pick **StreamLite Mic**
  as their microphone.
- **3D game audio.** Games' 7.1 surround becomes 3D sound on any headphones, using real measured heads (SADIE II).
  True 360° placement, footstep boost and a loud-sound tamer. A live **sound cube** shows where sounds come from on
  three floors (below, ear level, above). Right-drag the cube to look at it from any side.
- **Headphone correction.** "Find my headphones" looks up your model among thousands of AutoEq measurements and
  flattens it.
- **Automatic profiles.** Each game gets its own headphone EQ. **Music** applies while Spotify plays, **Chat** applies
  while Discord, Zoom, Teams, TeamSpeak, Mumble or another chat app is open, and **Movies & videos** applies otherwise.
- **AI camera (Windows 11).** A "StreamLite Camera" virtual webcam with background blur, AI green screen, face tracking
  and auto light.
- **Low VRAM.** On graphics cards with little video memory, one switch keeps all the AI (DeepFilterNet + camera) under
  250 MB of video memory at the same speed.
- **Any headset, any mic.**
  - USB, Bluetooth and analog headsets, audio interfaces and array mics all work.
  - Auto picks the mic input that carries your voice.
  - Each headset keeps its own correction.
  - Plug in or unplug devices and StreamLite follows.
- **Takes care of itself.** It installs the free drivers it needs on Windows, updates itself when it starts, and has a
  **Report a bug** button.

## Install

| System | Download | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows 10/11** (64-bit) | `StreamLite-<version>-x64.msi` | Double-click it. Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC": click **More info → Run anyway** (StreamLite isn't code-signed yet). |
| Windows, no install | `StreamLite-<version>-win-x64-portable.zip` | Unzip anywhere and run `StreamLite.exe`. |
| **Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin** | `streamlite_<version>_amd64.deb` | `sudo apt install ./streamlite_<version>_amd64.deb` |
| **Fedora, Nobara** | `streamlite-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./streamlite-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| **openSUSE** | `streamlite-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm` | `sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./streamlite-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| **Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS, CachyOS** | `PKGBUILD` | Put it in an empty folder, then run `makepkg -si` |
| **Any Linux** (one file) | `StreamLite-<version>-x86_64.AppImage` | `chmod +x StreamLite-*.AppImage` and run it |
| **Any Linux** (no root) | `streamlite-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Unpack it and run `./install.sh`, or use the one-liner below |

One-line install for any Linux distro, for your user only (no password):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NermalYT/StreamLite/main/packaging/linux/get.sh | sh
```

Linux needs PipeWire (with `pipewire-pulse`) or PulseAudio, which every mainstream desktop has. The packages pull in
everything else.

## Quick start

1. Start StreamLite and pick **your microphone** on the Microphone page.
   - On Windows, click **Install VB-CABLE (free)** if StreamLite asks for it. It's the virtual cable your clean mic
     travels through.
2. In Discord, go to *Settings → Voice & Video* and set **Input Device** to **StreamLite Mic**. Set Discord's own
   noise suppression to **None** so your voice isn't cleaned twice. OBS, Zoom, TeamSpeak and games work the same way.
3. Optional:
   - **Headphones → Find my headphones** corrects your headphones.
   - **3D Audio** gives games 3D sound. Set the game's audio output to 7.1 / surround.

The [manual](https://nermalyt.github.io/StreamLite/) covers everything else, with fixes for common problems.

## Bugs and ideas

Use **Report a bug** in StreamLite. It's in the sidebar, under Settings, and in the tray menu. It opens the
[bug form](https://github.com/NermalYT/StreamLite/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) with your version and system
already filled in. You need a free GitHub account. Ideas are welcome
[here](https://github.com/NermalYT/StreamLite/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml).

## Building it yourself

- **Windows:** run `.\build.ps1`. It uses the C# compiler that ships with Windows, so no SDK is needed. Then:
  - `.\install.ps1` installs it for your user.
  - `.\packaging\windows\build-msi.ps1` builds the MSI and the zip. This needs the .NET SDK and WiX 5.
  - `.\test\all.ps1` runs the offline tests.
- **Linux:** run `bash packaging/linux/build-linux.sh`. It needs the .NET 8 SDK. It builds the tarball, .deb,
  AppImage and PKGBUILD, plus the .rpm if `rpmbuild` is installed. After that:
  - `linux/publish/streamlite --selftest` checks the audio path.

Pushing a version tag (`v2.1.0`) makes GitHub Actions do the following:

- Build everything and run the tests.
- Install each Linux package on Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, openSUSE and Arch.
- Publish the release with `SHA256SUMS.txt`, which the updater checks.

## Credits

StreamLite is built on the work of a lot of generous people:

- RNNoise (Xiph.Org, Mozilla)
- DeepFilte

commits.msg:
3.1.1: mic to cable with one safety margin (6.6 ms instead of 9.5-10 ms), late packets filled in

- The cable's lead is the only margin: the cable writer takes all real sound after each packet and
  fills in only when the cable would play past what's written; the mic ring keeps just what its
  interpolator needs (ExternalSteer).
- Late packets are filled in by repeating the voice's last pitch period (seam-corrected start,
  crossfaded resume, skipping what was covered minus up to 1 ms), not faded to silence; short
  fill-ins don't count as gaps or raise the buffer. Learned mic floors from earlier versions reset.
- Drift steered from the cable's lead with a PI controller (integral learns the clocks' difference,
  slowed during fill-ins), remembered per mic.
- Packets the mic's driver loses (position jumps) are filled in too (PacketConcealer).
- status.txt: late packets filled in, lost packets, cable fill-in trace and learned clock drift.
- docs/driver-plan.md: what a StreamLite audio driver would gain and what signing it takes.
- Tests: ConcealRingTest (old vs new, 4 clock offsets, cable jumps), PlcTest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3.1.0: Direct to headphones (exclusive output + StreamLite's own app mixer)

- Opt-in, asked once after installing/updating (DirectAudioDialog), toggle in 3D audio > Output.
- Headphones in exclusive mode at their smallest period (3 ms on the QCC dongle), falls back to the
  normal output with the reason in Health; headphone EQ runs in StreamLite (APO skips exclusive).
- AppMixer: voice chat/music/browsers play to a muted side output and are mixed in via Windows'
  per-app capture (process loopback), drift-corrected per app; the side output's mute is restored
  (saved at once, also after a crash).
- 3D delay readout measured (buffer + output queue): 21.9 -> 16.5 ms with Direct to headphones.
- DeepFilterNet on the CPU auto-picked from 12 threads (was 8) for budget CPUs.
- Tests: AppMixerTest; probes for per-app capture, pauses, muted outputs and exclusive takeover.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3.0.2: realtime noise removal handles noise starting after silence; DeepFilterNet's verdict

- A held-open word start that the noise remover still calls noise after 150 ms becomes the
  background (a fan switching on or a mic unmuted was passed through with every engine).
- DeepFilterNet realtime: a pause is when RNNoise or DeepFilterNet hears no voice and the voice
  band hasn't risen 3 dB since DeepFilterNet listened; late frames don't update its gains.
- NsRealtimeTest: noise starting after silence (fan, white) for every engine.
- Linux self-test prints late frames, buffer and any fallback for DeepFilterNet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3.0.2: realtime noise removal (2.7 ms), zero-allocation audio paths, faster 3D

- Realtime noise removal: a 2.7 ms WOLA filter steered by RNNoise / Classic / DeepFilterNet
  gains (on by default); noise removal off adds no delay.
- No allocations on the mic, extra-mic, 3D, DeepFilterNet and camera paths (AllocTest).
- 3D: 1.3 ms renderer hop, prebuilt per-layout filters (stereo/7.1 switch 0.55 ms), resume grace.
- Mic capture polls for packets when the driver's signal is late; timing in status/health logs.
- PerfTest 3.0.2 baselines: mic 6.1 ms, 3D 11.9 ms, 0 dropouts on all tiers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3.0.1: lower mic and game latency, faded gaps, learned buffer floors per mic, Health warns only for real problems, health.log

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3.0.0: performance test across hardware tiers with release baselines; camera without effects when the CPU can't run them

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Auto EQ with overlapping apps: priority order, why-this-EQ, two-check switching, same loudness for every profile

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Setup export/import: name-only devices, no ids or paths, preview with per-part switches and device remap, exact undo

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Game spatial audio: show what the game sends, warn about Windows spatial sound, 7.1 game path in the listening test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Personalize 3D: blind listening test of head models and cue sharpening vs no 3D, saved per headphones

Personal3D renders two footsteps at a spot (new TestSignal point mode) with a variant - or panned left/right
for 'no 3D' - all at the same loudness, plays them on the headphones, scores answers with front/back and
up/down mix-ups; round 2 tunes cue sharpening on the winning head. AppCore keeps the result per headphones
(PersonalHeads) and applies it when switching to them. Personal3DTest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Voice comparison: compare noise engines on the same recording at matched loudness; keep the sample

VoiceTest: EngineOverride for the test chain only (Use this one applies it), loudness matching to the
recording's speech loudness (Match, +-15 dB, eases in), the recording saved as voice-sample.wav and reloaded.
Compare row in the voice test card. VoiceCompareTest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

One-click setup check with fixes; after-update check; --setup-check

SetupCheck: drivers, APO on the headphones, physical mic (privacy, silence), virtual mic end to end
(1 kHz test tone via AudioEngine.TestTone recorded back from StreamLite - In, only when nobody records),
its Windows volume, headphones end to end (quiet tone into the game device, loopback of the headphones),
Windows defaults, which device Discord / OBS record from (AudioSessions.All), camera. Health page card
with a fix button per problem; after an update a silent check shows an in-window note on failures.
Live on this PC: 10 OK, 1 warning (StreamLite - In at volume 76), Discord/OBS not running.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Health page: live latency, dropouts, buffers, noise engine in use, CPU/RAM/VRAM, plain-language log

HealthMonitor samples once a second (AppCore) and notes every fallback / recovery in plain words
(shared-mode mic and why, direct cable path failed, dropouts and buffer growth, DeepFilterNet resting or
falling back, extra mics / outputs dropping out, camera errors, sustained high CPU). VRAM from the
GPU Process Memory counters. status.txt has a resources line (live: CPU 0.5%, RAM 90 MB, VRAM 147 MB).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Outputs in sync: per-device delay, mic-timed clicks, line up; self-paced rendering fix

GameAudioEngine: DelayLine per output (saved per device in OutputDelayMs), clicks injected into one
output's ring (or all) through its real path; idle rendering now wakes every 2 ms and renders block by
block (20-40 ms bursts let the output rings run dry - also affected the footsteps test without game sound).
OutputSyncMeter times clicks from AudioEngine.RawTap; OutputSyncDialog measures / lines up / test clicks.
OutputSyncTest offline; SyncLive on QCC + Realtek: clicks only on their output, 100 ms delay = 99 ms shift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Multi-mic calibration: measured bleed, suggested volumes, bleed-aware auto mix

Calibrate... (Microphones list) records quiet + each person in turn through MicMixer.PowerTap;
MicCalibration measures voice, noise and bleed per mic and predicts doubling before/after.
MicMixer subtracts the expected bleed (held over ~40 ms for the added mics' latency).
MicCalibrationTest: bleed -4/-6 dB measured, doubling +12 -> -21 dB, both talking kept >= 37%.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

2.7.0: hotkeys for any setting, in-app update prompt, settings recovery

- Hotkeys page: numbered bindings (action, target, key) for 26 actions - mute any mic or all, push to
  talk / push to mute, mic chain toggles, noise remover / voice style, 3D on/off / preset / test,
  headphone profile / Auto EQ, mute any output, camera background / tracking / light / mirror, show
  window. Keys, combos, single modifiers and middle/back/forward mouse buttons via low-level hooks on
  their own thread (never swallowed, except while recording a key). Smooth (~5 ms) mutes in the mic
  engine and per mic in MicMixer; output mutes use the endpoint mute. Small click-through toast.

MightyTMZ/magnus_bot.readme:
# magnus_bot

Two SO-101 follower arms that play **White** in a physical chess game against a human, cooperating
through a handoff pad under a state-machine orchestrator. Scope today: controller, IK, planning,
orchestration. Computer vision is an interface stub only; there is no frontend/backend.

> **Status: M0 (scaffold).** Sim and planning work end to end; IK, live motion, reachability and
> vision are stubs for later milestones. **No command moves hardware without `--live`, in-session
> operator approval, and `measured: true`.** See `CLAUDE.md` and `HANDOVER.md`.

## Quick start

```bash
uv venv --python 3.13 .venv
uv pip install --python .venv -e ".[dev]"      # core + dev tools (NOT lerobot; see below)
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest                 # 47 tests
.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check .
magnus-bot info                                # config + arm placements
magnus-bot demo-move --uci e2e4                # build a sim motion program for one move
```

`lerobot` is **not** a core dependency — the sim, planner and tests import without it. For live
hardware, install the `hardware` extra inside LeRobot's own environment (see `HANDOVER.md`).

## How it works

A chess move (UCI) is decomposed into physical **piece transfers** (captures remove the victim
first; castling moves king then rook; en passant removes the pawn behind the destination;
promotion swaps a stashed queen). Each transfer is **assigned** to an arm using a reachability
map: one arm that reaches both ends does it alone, otherwise the two arms **hand off** over a
shared pad. Each transfer expands into the pick/place primitive (hover → descend → grip → lift →
traverse → descend → release → retract). A pure **state machine** sequences the game loop.

## Layout

`geometry/` frames & squares · `kinematics/` IK & reach · `motion/` safety, primitives,
trajectory · `hardware/` `Arm` + `SimArm` + `LeRobotArm` · `planning/` decompose/assign/handoff ·
`orchestration/` state machine + executor · `sources/` engines & input · `vision/` camera stubs.
Docs: `docs/frames.md`, `docs/state_machine.md`, `docs/joint_conventions.md`.

Js23321/Dashduel.readme:
# DASHDUEL — movement-first arena shooter

Fast first-person duels in colourful low-poly block arenas (Three.js / WebGL). Inspired by the quick, competitive
feel of Roblox-style arena shooters. The code, characters, weapons, UI and name are original; the weapon numbers follow Roblox
RIVALS, and the **Arena** map's layout is converted from the public-domain (CC0) "Rivals Arena Map" 3D-print model on
Printables (a copy of a layout from the Roblox game RIVALS, so keep that in mind before publishing the game widely). The other
five maps and the **3D lobby** are original designs made in Blender for this game.

**Movement and positioning beat aim**: the two guns are hitscan with **zero recoil, zero spread, zero bullet travel
time, no bullet drop and no camera shake**. Slide, bunny hop, air strafe, wall run, double jump and grenade-boost to
out-play the AI.

No installation and no build step (Three.js r159 is bundled in `vendor/`). The only feature that needs a server is
**Online 1v1**; everything else works offline.

---

## Run it in Chrome

**Easiest:** open `index.html` in Chrome (double-click it, or in ChromeOS open it from the Files app, or drag it
onto a Chrome window). That's it.

**Optional – tiny local server** (only if your setup blocks `file://` pages):

```bash
# in this folder
python -m http.server 8000      # then open http://localhost:8000
# or:  npx serve .
```

Pick a mode, pick a map, press **Start**. The mouse locks to the game (Pointer Lock). **Esc** releases it and pauses.

**Every Duel / Online round starts with a 3 second countdown with both fighters locked in their own spawn.** After that,
**winning or losing a Duel or Deathmatch never pauses the game or frees your mouse, and you are never frozen:** after
beating the opponent you keep full control (move, jump, slide, switch weapons) while a small summary card shows and the
next round / match starts by itself. (Prefer the old results screen? *Settings → Mouse & ADS → Results screen after matches*.)

### Chromebook / browser-safety notes
* **You always run (there is no sprint key); `Shift` slides, and so does `C`.** `Ctrl+W` closes a tab and `Ctrl+1…8` switches
  browser tabs (Chrome reserves those; no web page can block them), so the game needs no Ctrl: the **mouse wheel** and **`F`**
  (previous weapon) switch weapons without it, and *Settings → Graphics → Fullscreen* additionally asks Chrome to deliver those combos to the game.
* Gameplay keys never scroll the page, and **nothing is intercepted outside a running game**. Leaving or closing the
  tab mid-match shows a "Leave site?" confirmation.
* Losing focus (Alt-Tab, another tab, DevTools) pauses the game, releases the mouse, clears every held key and mutes
  sound, so nothing can get "stuck".
* Both **fullscreen and windowed** play work (pause menu → *Fullscreen*, or `F11`).
* Weak hardware? *Settings → Graphics → Quality: **Potato*** (the cheapest look: 40% resolution, no shadows, particles, outlines, clouds, reflections or interface animations; about 3-7× the frame rate of Medium in my software-rendering test) or *Low* (the first run auto-picks a preset from your device), or set
  **Target frame rate: 30 FPS**. The game also watches its own frame times and, if it can't hold the frame rate, removes
  expensive visuals one step at a time (particles → resolution → shadows → outlines and clouds).

---

## Game modes

| Mode | What you do |
|------|-------------|
| **Online 1v1** | **A real match against another player.** Press *Online 1v1*, wait in the queue, and you are paired with whoever else is searching. First to **5 rounds**, 150 health each, every round starts with a **3 second countdown** during which both players are locked in their own spawn. See *Online 1v1* below. |
| **Duel** | 1v1 against an AI. Each round ends on an elimination, then everything resets automatically (sides alternate). First to **3 / 5 / 7** round wins. 75 s round limit: most health wins. Maps: Arena, Bridge, Crossroads, Docks, Station, Backrooms. |
| **Deathmatch** | Free-for-all against 1–7 AI opponents (easy / normal / hard). First to **10 / 15 / 25** eliminations within 5 minutes. ~1 s respawns, regenerating health. |
| **Time Trial** | Race through glowing checkpoint rings on the **Gauntlet**. Splits compare with your best; falling respawns you at the last checkpoint (`Q`). |
| **Practice** | Free play on every map with target dummies (also from the lobby's practice range). The **Yard** has a shooting range, slide hills, wall-run fields, launch pads, a bunny-hop lane and stairs. `E` sets a spawn point, `Q` returns to it, `T` resets. |

**Everyone — you and every bot — has 150 health and no shield.** Opponents' weapons are never announced: not in the
round-start text, not on the death screen, not in the kill feed.

Personal bests, win streaks, accuracy, top speeds and eliminations are saved in your browser (*Records*).

### Maps (the active pool; every one is modelled in Blender, see *Maps and the lobby* below)
| # | Map | Size | Idea |
|---|-----|------|------|
| 1 | **Arena** | compact (28 x 44 m, 10 m walls) | a walled rectangle of white panelled concrete in the style of the RIVALS Arena: a long **ramp up to a high ledge** on each side wall (the pocket under each ledge is a covered corridor), a **catwalk** at ledge height bridging the middle over a low plinth, **turned slabs** and a tall bar on the diagonal, low blocks, and a **hollowed gate** (arch + windows, blue / red) that hides each team's spawn pad from the middle. A second **ramp at each spawn end** leads onto the ledge, and each team has six spawn points that rotate between rounds. 180-degree symmetric, so neither spawn has an advantage |
| 2 | **Bridge** | medium (80 x 60 m) | a city crossing: a raised bridge deck (ramps at both ends, stairs in the middle) over an avenue and a street, a **yellow bus stopped on the bridge** as the landmark, parked cars, jersey barriers, planters, buildings with windows around. Routes: avenue

# Protoa

A family of learning apps under one orb. The first is a German course for English speakers aiming for spoken B1.

## Run it

Requires Node 22.9 or newer.

```sh
npm run setup          # install server dependencies
cp .env.example .env   # then add your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
npm run dev            # http://localhost:8787/deutsch/
```

Without an API key the app still runs; the AI features (answer checking, corrections, Sprechen, lesson writing, exam marking) are turned off.

`npm test` runs the server tests. See `CLAUDE.md` for how the code is organised.

# Wonder Royale: online

Top-down battle royale for 2–6 players per room. Node + Express + Socket.IO server runs the real game rules;
the browser client keeps all the original rendering, art and UI.

```
client/   index.html, game.js (original game + net layer), config.js   (static files)
server/   index.js (Express + Socket.IO), src/rooms.js (rooms), src/sim.js (match host), game/sim-core.js (game rules)
src/      source of truth that tools/build.js bundles into client/game.js and server/game/sim-core.js
```
After editing anything in `src/`, run `npm run build`.

## Run locally
```
npm install --prefix server     # or: npm install   (root package.json lists the same deps)
npm start                       # http://localhost:3000  (serves client/ too)
```
Open it in two browser tabs and press the big **SOLO** button in both: you land in a public lobby of real players only (no bots) and the match starts by itself 30 s after the 2nd player arrives (10 s once 6 are in).
While the lobby counts down, players stand on a big green **waiting field** (no obstacles), walk around, see each other, and play two mini games run by the server: **Coin Rush** (collect coins) and **kick the ball into a goal**. The countdown is a small pill at the top. Left click punches (also hits the ball), **Enter** opens a chat box and the message floats over your character. When the timer ends everyone drops into the real map.
Friends-only rooms: **Play with friends** → Create room → the other tab joins with the 5-letter code → host presses Start.

### Admin (pause / resume / Start instantly)
Set a variable `ADMIN_KEY` on the server (Railway → Variables, any long secret). In a lobby press **Admin login** and type that key (the browser remembers it). The admin sees **Pause countdown / Resume countdown**, **Start instantly** (works even alone, for testing) and the map/storm/loot options. In friends rooms the host gets the same buttons without a key.

## Deploy on Railway
1. Push to GitHub:
   ```
   git init && git add . && git commit -m "Wonder Royale online"
   git branch -M main
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<you>/<repo>.git
   git push -u origin main
   ```
2. Railway → New Project → Deploy from GitHub repo → pick the repo. (Root `package.json` + `railway.json` are used: start = `npm start`, health check = `/health`.)
3. Variables: `ADMIN_KEY` = your secret admin key (needed for the admin buttons). `FRONTEND_URL` = your site's origin (e.g. `https://wonder-royale.up.railway.app`; comma-separate several). Leave unset to allow `*`. Do **not** set `PORT`; Railway provides it and the server binds `0.0.0.0`.
4. Settings → Networking → Generate Domain. Open it; `/health` should return `{"ok":true}`.
5. Optional, client hosted elsewhere: put the Railway URL in `client/config.js` (`server: 'https://…'`) or open the page with `?server=https://…`, and set `FRONTEND_URL` to that page's origin.
One instance only: rooms live in server memory, so don't scale replicas above 1.

## Railway checklist (all implemented)
`process.env.PORT` + `0.0.0.0` · `GET /health` 200 · CORS from `FRONTEND_URL` (`*` in dev) · client `transports:['polling','websocket']`, `reconnection:true` · reconnect restores the seat (code + token kept in sessionStorage; server holds the seat 20 s in lobby / 45 s in a match).

## Who owns what
| Server (authoritative) | Client |
|---|---|
| positions, velocity, plane/parachute phase, landing | draws everything; predicts own ground movement (server validates speed, corrects with a `c` flag) |
| hp, shield, alive, kills, placement, winner | HUD from snapshots |
| inventory, ammo, reload, selected slot, heal/use timers | shows `m` messages; sends `sel/use/reload/swap/drop/ammo` |
| bullets, hits, damage, melee, explosions | spawns cosmetic bullets/effects from `shot`/`hit` events |
| ground loot, crates, airdrops, trees, doors (open/closed) | applies `l+ l- l~ c c+ c- t d` events |
| storm/zone schedule, storm damage | draws zone from snapshot |
| rooms, host, roster, countdown, match clock, results | lobby/end UI |

Protocol: `room:create|solo|join|rejoin|leave|start|opts|ctl` and `admin:auth` (acks) · `in` 30 Hz input · `act` actions · server → `lobby`, `match:start`, `s` snapshot+events, `m` private state, `match:over`, `match:error`.

## Tests
`npm test` (33 room/match checks + 22 lobby/admin checks, in-memory Socket.IO stand-in) and `PLAYWRIGHT_PATH=… node server/test/browser.js` (38 checks, two real Chromium pages).
