# Pawnzi Scheme, starring Pawn Malone

A two-armed robot chess hustler. Pawn Malone sits behind a real chess board in
a hoodie, with a cartoon face on a tablet. It takes your play money, gives you
odds on the clock, talks trash the whole game, seals a prediction of your next
move, moves its own pieces with one robot arm and slams the clock with the
other. You can play it by hand or by voice. The same software also runs as a
robot-free chess table in the browser.

This is the team's entry for **Cal Hacks 13.0**: the event, the team, the task
list and the prize tracks are in [plan/cal-hacks.md](plan/cal-hacks.md).

**Created by Alexander Picon. Proprietary software: copyright Alexander
Picon, all rights reserved.** See [Ownership and license](#ownership-and-license).

> **Status.** The whole robot stack is built and reviewed in simulation, and
> the browser table is playable. The real arms, cameras and pedals wait for
> the humans' bring-up, Alex's safety reviews and the red team's clearance of
> the arm driver. No code here opens hardware on its own.

## Two products, one codebase

1. **The robot table.** The full visit with real arms, cameras, pedals and a
   DGT clock. Its software passes in simulation first; each physical step
   counts as done only when humans have run and recorded it.
2. **The browser table.** One command serves a chess table that only the
   local machine can reach: Human vs CPU against Moonshark or Stockfish, or
   CPU vs CPU with two virtual arms, switchable in one running server. It has
   live Stockfish analysis, clocks, hints, takebacks, PGN and FEN, an animated
   board, a Persona page where Pawn Malone talks, a Cameras page and a game
   journal. It never opens hardware.

## The experience

1. **The challenge.** Pawn Malone asks two quick questions, by tap or by
   voice: how good are you (beginner, decent, strong) and what do you want (a
   quick puzzle, a quick game, or a theme like knight tricks, a queen
   sacrifice or an endgame). Claude picks a real, verified mate-in-2 from the
   Lichess puzzle slice that the arm can reach, or sets up a quick game with a
   matched strength and clock odds, and introduces it in character.
2. **The stake and the hustle.** Play money on the table, odds on the clock,
   double or nothing.
3. **The sealed prediction.** A face-down card holds Pawn Malone's guess of
   your next move; it flips after you press the clock and proves it was
   sealed before you moved.
4. **The move.** You move by hand, or by voice (below). The big arm moves
   Pawn Malone's reply, the small arm slams the clock, and the face reacts.
5. **The finish.** Checkmate in about two minutes, and Claude explains the
   solution.

**Fallbacks.** If the camera misreads a move, a teammate types it in on the
house console. If the arms act up, the robot plays itself (CPU vs CPU) while
Pawn Malone commentates. The full experience is in
[plan/experience.md](plan/experience.md).

## Play modes and voice commands

| Mode | Who plays | The robot |
|---|---|---|
| **Hustle** (Mode 1) | You against Pawn Malone, with the stake, the hustle and the sealed card | Moves Pawn Malone's pieces; in voice mode also yours |
| **Hands** (Mode 2) | You play both sides, or two people play each other; Pawn Malone commentates | Is your hands: moves every piece you confirm |

**Voice mode** works in both modes, so someone with limited hand mobility can
play a real board game, with family and friends too:

1. **Say the move.** "Knight to f3", or loosely: "move my horse next to the
   king".
2. **Claude proposes one move.** Speech-to-text (Cartesia by default) gives
   the words; Claude turns them into one move; moonshark's rules accept it
   only if it is exactly one legal move. Ambiguous or illegal: it asks again.
3. **Confirm.** Say "yes" or tap the visitor pad; "no" cancels. You can also
   tap a move directly.
4. **The arm moves it**, through the same guard as every other move: both
   hand watchers clear, the dwell, fresh heartbeats.

Voice mode on the real arms is **simulation only until Alex signs the
voice-mode rule**. On the table a spoken "yes" is refused until the speaker's
echo time is measured (a tap confirms), and Pawn Malone's lines never contain
"yes" or "no". The rule is in
[plan/streams/voice-mode-safety.md](plan/streams/voice-mode-safety.md).

## What Claude does

Claude does real work, walled off from the moves, the board and the arms:

- **Picks the challenge** from verified puzzles and introduces it.
- **Writes live lines** in an operator-enabled lane, through a strict filter,
  with the authored line bank as the instant fallback. Safety and freeze lines
  always come from the bank.
- **Explains the solution** from the referee's line after a puzzle or game.
- **Understands loose voice phrasing** and proposes one move for you to
  confirm.

It never chooses Pawn Malone's move, reads the board, decides legality,
clocks or payouts, or commands an arm. Without Claude everything still works
from the bank and the default picks.

## Personality and gestures

Pawn Malone reacts to how good each move is, scored by Stockfish after every
move. He roasts the moves, never the person.

| Moment | Attitude | Small-arm gesture |
|---|---|---|
| You blunder | Trash talk: "You just hung your queen. I'll take that, thank you." | A slow clap or taunting wave |
| You play a great move | Rare, grudging respect: "...okay. Didn't see that one. Respect." | A respectful nod |
| He blunders | Cope: "That was a test. You passed. Barely." | A facepalm or shrug |
| He wins | Victory | A victory spin, then a clock slam |

Gestures are recorded once by hand, last 2 to 3 seconds, run only in open
air on Pawn Malone's side of the turn, and need Alex's review before they run
on the arm.

# Storybound

**Don't just read the fairy tale. Become part of it.**

Storybound is a third-person 3D fairy-tale adventure in the browser, built for HackTX 2026 (theme: Fairy Tale). A Gemini-powered storyteller writes the tale from what you do, and your real world plays along: your phone is the controller, a stick with a coloured ball is the wand, and a mug held up to the webcam becomes a weapon.

## How you play

- **Phone = joystick and sword.** Scan the QR code on the start screen. Drag to move, tap to act, swing the lime-taped phone to strike.
- **Wand = draw the shape the game asks for.** Draw it in the air in front of the webcam: ▲ meteor, ● nova, ■ wave, ★ chain lightning.
- **Reality Rift = scan a real object.** Gemini turns it into a relic that powers both your weapons; bosses take double damage from the element they fear.
- **Up to 3 players on 3 laptops,** each with their own phone and wand colour, seeing each other's heroes.

```
  Phones                       Browser: the game                cv_2 tracker (Python)
  /joystick page               Three.js + Rapier, :5173         webcam colour tracker
       |                          |            ^                    |
       | WebSocket                | HTTP       | WebSocket          | WebSocket
       v                          v            |                    |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | FastAPI backend, :8000                                                  |
  |   /ws/joystick/{room}   phones -> game                                  |
  |   /ws/cv/{room}         tracker <-> game (camera picture, wand, slash)  |
  |   /ws/presence/{room}   the other laptops' heroes                       |
  |   /api/provider/*   story beats, storybook   ----> Gemini (text)        |
  |   /api/artifact     photo -> relic           ----> Gemini (vision)      |
  |   /api/verify       photo shows "a book"?    ----> Gemini (vision)      |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Quick start

After the one-time [setup](#setup-from-a-fresh-clone), one command starts the backend, the game and the tracker, opens the game, and shows a QR code for your phone:

```bash
./scripts/demo.sh --tunnel --color red --name You          # macOS / Linux
```

```powershell
.\scripts\demo.ps1 -Tunnel -Color red -Name You            # Windows
```

`--tunnel` lets phones on any network connect through a Cloudflare tunnel (install `cloudflared` once: `brew install cloudflared`, or `winget install --id Cloudflare.cloudflared`); drop it if the phone is on the same Wi-Fi. If Windows blocks the script, run it as `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\demo.ps1 -Tunnel -Color red -Name You`. Scan the QR code, tap the phone to begin, hold the wand still, then draw.

## Features

**Two ways to play.** The default is a short **demo run**: Willow's briefing, one wave of six shadows, then Morwen the Frost Witch, then a result screen (tuned for roughly a minute of fighting per the code comments; not timed). `?story=full` plays the whole tale: the freeze challenge, a crossroads vote (castle or cave), pose seals, the riddle door, a boss on either route, and a personalised storybook. The demo run has no storyteller, vote, seals, riddle door or storybook, and Gemini is only called for a scan.

**Gemini storyteller (`?story=full`).** Each beat is written by Gemini (`gemini-3.8-flash`, structured output, 12 s timeout) from what you did; the engine owns the rules and Gemini only writes the words. Every call has a hand-written fallback, so a dead network or a missing key never stops a run.

**Reality Rift.** Press **X**, click **Scan**, or tap **Scan** on the phone. A small panel docks at the right and the game keeps running underneath. Hold a real object up and take the photo; Gemini returns a relic (name, element, ability, power, rarity), shown on a card framed around your own photo with the boss matchup, such as "Morwen is weak to fire · x2 damage". The relic's element infuses the wand, the F bolt and the sword, and its power (1-3) sets how hard wand spells hit. A boss takes **x2** from the element it fears and **x0.5** from the one it resists, for spells and slashes; a hit shows "Weak point!" or "Resisted". Relics are kept in an in-browser armory (up to 8). In the full story Gemini and the storybook mention the real object. With no camera, "Choose a photo"; with no Gemini, a stand-in relic (Moonlit Orb of light or Frostbound Blade of ice, at random).

| Boss | Route | Weak to (x2) | Resists (x0.5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Morwen the Frost Witch | castle (always, in the demo run) | fire | ice |
| Umbraxis the Shadow Wyrm | cave | light | shadow |

**Two weapons: sword and wand.** The sword is a three-hit combo. The wand casts the shape you draw, even before any scan: circle nova (2.2 s cooldown), triangle meteor (3 s), square wave (1.6 s), star chain lightning (1.8 s). In a fight the screen asks for one shape at a time ("▲ Draw a triangle · Meteor") and only that shape casts; another shape does nothing. The request moves on after a cast or 10 s. The wand needs 2 s between spells, and the tracker stops tracing whenever a spell could not be cast. A requested star is read leniently (96% of simulated stars accepted instead of 89%). `?runes=free` removes the requests.

**Phone control.** The start screen shows a QR code; the phone page needs no app. Drag moves, a tap does whatever Enter or E would, **Scan**, **Roll** and **Slash** are buttons. The backend gives each phone a player slot (up to three). Through `--tunnel` only the ph

wlc114514/clawd-pet.readme:
# clawd-pet

Claude Code 吉祥物 Clawd 的 Windows / macOS 桌宠。Windows 版是纯 C + Win32 API，单个 exe（约 150 KB），不依赖任何运行库，常驻 CPU 占用约 0.2%；macOS 版共用同一套状态机和像素画，外壳换成 Cocoa，产物是一个 Clawd.app。

> 粉丝作品，与 Anthropic 无关。Clawd 形象归 Anthropic 所有。

## 功能

- 站在任务栏上，眨眼、张望、走来走去、偶尔蹦一下
- 点它会跳并冒爱心（偶尔来个后空翻）；拖起来会举手乱蹬腿，甩出去能扔，撞墙会反弹；飞在空中时点它附近（不用正好点中）就能一把接住，接着再扔
- 5 分钟不碰电脑就趴下睡觉冒 zzz，你一动就醒
- 后空翻：闲着时偶尔自己翻一个，Claude Code 干完活庆祝时也可能翻；右键「一起玩 ▸ 后空翻」随时看（从托盘点就全体一起翻）
- 滑一下：快跑几步，然后蹲低身子张开手臂、扬着小尘土往前滑一大段，慢慢停住（太快撞上墙会撞晕）；闲着时偶尔自己滑，右键「一起玩 ▸ 滑一下」随时看
- Steam 弹窗（仅 Windows）：右下角弹出 Steam 通知时，离得最近的 Clawd 一路滑过去跳到弹窗上（再远也会赶在弹窗收起前到），弹窗要收起时在上面跳一下，跟着弹窗一起掉下去
- 偶尔（或者右键「爬上去」）从任务栏里变出一段楼梯（悬空石板 / 实心石砖 / 轮廓线，在「设置 ▸ 楼梯样式」里选），一格一格跳上去；到顶后楼梯塌掉，它就在半空那个高度上走来走去，还会从那里接着往上爬（最高到离屏幕顶端不远），过 1–3 分钟再一口气跳回任务栏
- 围墙：右键「放置围墙」，在屏幕上按住鼠标拖一下就砌出一面红砖墙（横着拖是横墙，竖着拖是竖墙）。墙会一直在，右键它可以拆掉这面或全部拆掉，重启后还在。Clawd 走路撞上墙会「啪」地贴上去、冒星星、往后弹一下，晕乎乎地坐一会儿再掉头走；被扔出去撞墙、跳起来撞到头顶的墙也一样。横墙上面能站：掉下来或扔上去会落在墙上走来走去，走到头就掉下去。楼梯不会穿墙
- 你打字时它坐到键盘前跟着敲（轮询按键状态，不装键盘钩子，不记录按了什么）；有好几只时只有第一只敲，其他的照常溜达
- 鼠标互动：不理鼠标 / 跟着鼠标走 / 怕鼠标（被逼到墙角会从鼠标头上跳过去）
- CPU 越忙跑得越快
- 电脑热了会流汗：读 Windows 的「热区域信息」性能计数器（不用管理员权限），75°C 起偶尔滴汗，85°C 起不再乱跑，身边搬出一台小风扇对着自己吹（敲键盘时也吹），降到 82°C 以下收起来；读不到温度的电脑按 CPU 占用超过 80% 流汗
- 番茄钟：在 Clawd 头顶弹出像素风小窗，用滚轮 / 拖动 / 方向键选专注（5–90 分钟）和休息（1–30 分钟）时长，记住上次的选择
- 喝水提醒，用中文气泡提示
- 「设置 ▸ 功能开关」里可以把用不上的番茄钟、喝水提醒从菜单里藏起来，也可以关掉爬楼梯、打乱桌面图标和自动检查更新
- 最多同时 6 只；送走一只时它会随机来一段告别戏（吓一跳 / 发抖 / 大哭 😭 / 乱跑），然后从任务栏掉下去，其他 Clawd 会被吓得往后蹦
- 配饰：每只 Clawd 出生时随机戴上几件——头上（圆顶礼帽 / 小皇冠 / 毛线帽 / 头戴耳机）、脸上（单片眼镜 / 圆框眼镜 / 墨镜）、嘴上（八字胡 / 一字胡 / 大浓胡 / 山羊胡）、脖子上（围巾 / 蝴蝶结）、手上（咖啡 / 星巴克 / 薯片 / 手表），每个部位最多一件。右键它选「换装…」打开换装窗口：左边是它穿戴后的样子，右边每件配饰都画出来，点一下穿上、再点脱下，还能随机搭配或全部脱掉。戴着耳机打字会跟着点头，叠罗汉时会踩在帽子顶上

## 下载

在 [Releases](https://github.com/wlc114514/clawd-pet/releases/latest) 里：

- **Windows**：下载 `clawd.exe` 直接运行
- **macOS**（11 以上，M 系列和 Intel 都行）：下载 `Clawd-mac.zip`，解压后把 `Clawd.app` 拖进「应用程序」。app 没有苹果开发者签名，第一次打开会被拦：右键 ▸ 打开；较新的 macOS 上要去「系统设置 ▸ 隐私与安全性」点「仍要打开」

## 编译

### Windows

需要 [w64devkit](https://github.com/skeeto/w64devkit)（便携 gcc）。`build.bat` 会先找 PATH 里的 gcc，找不到就用 `%USERPROFILE%\w64devkit\bin`。

```bat
build.bat
```

产物是根目录的 `clawd.exe`。编译前先退出正在运行的桌宠，否则 exe 被占用无法覆盖。

### macOS

需要 Xcode 命令行工具（`xcode-select --install`），没有别的依赖。

```sh
cd mac
make        # 产物是 mac/build/Clawd.app
make run    # 编译并启动
```

`src/pet.c`（状态机、物理）和 `src/render.c`（像素画）两边共用，平台相关的部分分别在 `src/platform_win.c` 和 `mac/plat_mac.m` 里，所以两个平台的行为是一致的。

## 联动 Claude Code

在 `~/.claude/settings.json` 里加上下面的 hooks（把路径换成你的 `clawd.exe` 所在位置）。它们都是 `async`，不会拖慢 Claude。桌宠没在运行时，这些命令什么也不做。

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit":   [{ "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "C:\\path\\to\\clawd.exe", "args": ["--cc", "prompt"], "async": true }] }],
    "PostToolUse":        [{ "matcher": "*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "C:\\path\\to\\clawd.exe", "args": ["--cc", "tool"], "async": true }] }],
    "PostToolUseFailure": [{ "matcher": "*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "C:\\path\\to\\clawd.exe", "args": ["--cc", "tool"], "async": true }] }],

    "Stop":               [{ "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "C:\\path\\to\\clawd.exe", "args": ["--cc", "stop"], "async": true }] }],
    "SessionEnd":         [{ "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "C:\\path\\to\\clawd.exe", "args": ["--cc", "end"], "async": true }] }]

```

mac: never clobber or unlink the user's shell rc

Turning on the clawd command read ~/.zshrc with stringWithContentsOfFile,
which returns nil for a file that exists but isn't valid UTF-8; that was
treated as empty, so the whole rc was replaced by the PATH block. Leave
unreadable files alone, and write through symlinks (dotfile managers)
instead of replacing the link with a plain file.

Turning it off appended a newline to every line including the last empty
one, growing the file each time, and left the blank line put in front of
the block. Rejoin the kept lines as they were.

NazOnPL/roblox-masterguide.readme:
# Roblox Masterguide

Naz's knowledge base for everything around a Roblox game except the code: ideation, validation, design, monetization, packaging, launch, live ops and competitor research. Scripting, project setup and asset-upload rules live in [roblox-game-boilerplate](https://github.com/NazOnPL/roblox-game-boilerplate) (`AGENTS.md`), not here. Every folder is one topic you can hand to a new game on its own.

## How to use it on a new game

1. Copy `starter-kit/` into the new repo. It gives you `CLAUDE.md` and the five slash commands (`/validate-concept`, `/design-loop`, `/monetize`, `/launch-prep`, `/live-ops`).
2. Copy any topic folder you need into the repo's `docs/` (for example `05-monetization/`), and tell Claude to read it.

## Topics

| Folder | What's in it | Slash command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01-mindset/` | Producer mindset, the 5-year-old rule | none |
| `02-ideation-validation/` | Purple ocean, 80/20 twist, demand signals | `/validate-concept` |
| `03-packaging/` | Titles, thumbnails, icons, mobile CTR | none |
| `04-game-design-retention/` | Core loop, FTUE, juice, retention | `/design-loop` |
| `05-monetization/` | Dev products, passes, purchase pathways, pricing | `/monetize` |
| `06-launch-algorithm/` | Sponsored ads, beta, discovery algorithm | `/launch-prep` |
| `07-live-ops/` | Patches vs updates, metrics, team | `/live-ops` |
| `inspiration/` | Clips of cool systems, mechanics, UI and VFX, plus useful tools | none |
| `ideas/` | Your game ideas, each with its validation report and open questions | `/validate-concept` |
| `competitors/` | One file per game you playtested: what to steal | none |
| `playtests/` | Playtests of your own games: fix lists, ready-to-paste prompts, ideas | none |
| `inbox/` | Raw brain dumps waiting to be sorted | none |
| `skills/` | The kit's slash commands as 3 Claude skills (validate concept, design + monetize, launch + live ops) | none |
| `sources/` | Original master guide and kit zip, untouched | none |

Inside each topic: `guide.md` is the Tizzy RBLX material, `notes.md` is your own observations and rules, and `command-*.md` is the matching slash command.

## How brain dumps get filed

Dump anything in the chat. It gets saved to `inbox/` with the date, then sorted: game-specific observations go to `competitors/<game>.md`, general rules go to the topic's `notes.md`.

keberos/kh1-companion.desc: KH1 Final Mix second-screen companion for the AYN Thor (GameNative)
keberos/kh1-companion.readme:
Kingdom Hearts Final Mix on the top screen. Everything you'd look up on the bottom one.
For the AYN Thor and other dual-screen Android handhelds, with the game running in GameNative.

⬇ Download the latest beta · Install · What it shows · Performance tips · Questions

> **Beta.** It works end to end on the AYN Thor, and it's still being tested across a full playthrough. Your game and saves are never changed. ## What it shows Four tabs, all live from the save you have loaded, and only what the game's own data proves. Rooms you haven't been to stay "???" unless you ask.

Here: an EXP bar to your next level (the game hides it in the Status menu), the chests in the room you're in, and which other rooms still hold chests. Tap a chest to see where it is. A chest the walkthroughs agree needs something you don't have yet (Glide, a Trinity, a spell) is marked Later, and one they agree opens up after an event or on a later visit says so.
Map: every room in the world, where you are, and how many chests are left in each. The save points shown are the ones found so far, not every one.

Progress: every world you've found with its chests (a crown when they're all open), the 99 Dalmatians, postcards and Ansem's Reports.
Level: what Sora learns at each level for your Dive choices, your next ability and how much EXP until it. Tap a level for details.
First time or replay? Tap the eye at the top: Replay shows room names and chest contents up front. It also has optional pop-up notes for chests, level-ups and new worlds (off by default).
**It reads your save, so there's nothing to keep in sync.** Load any save on any device and it's up to date. Starting the companion partway through a playthrough is fine. **It looks like part of the game.** Deep-blue menus, silver frames and gold titles, all drawn for this project. ## What you need - An **AYN Thor**, or another Android handheld with a second screen - **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** with **KINGDOM HEARTS HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX** (Steam) installed and launching normally - About **five minutes** for setup Setup's pictures and the steps below were made with **GameNative 1.3.0** on an **AYN Thor** (Android 13), with KINGDOM HEARTS HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX from Steam (KH1 Final Mix 1.0.0.10). If you're on a different GameNative version, menu names and positions may differ. ## Install 1. **Download** `KH1-Companion-….apk` from the [latest release](../../releases) and open it to install. 2. **Open KH1 Companion.** A setup checklist walks you through everything, with pictures of each GameNative screen: - two Android permissions (one switch each), - in GameNative, copying two files into the game with **Import Files** (the app has them ready) and turning on **Enable mod loaders**, - starting the game once, after which setup ticks itself off. 3. **Open it with the game.** On Cocoon Shell, set **KH1 Companion** as Kingdom Hearts' companion app: launching the game from Cocoon then opens the companion on the bottom screen too. Without Cocoon, start the game and tap the **KH1 Companion** icon. Either way, the companion closes by itself when the game does. **Optional: start straight into the game.** Out of the box, GameNative opens the collection's menu and you pick KH1 there; quitting KH1 drops you back in that menu, and the companion closes within a minute. For a seamless KH1 experience, point GameNative straight at KH1: in GameNative open the game → ⚙ → **Edit container** → **General** → **Executable Path** → `KINGDOM HEARTS FINAL MIX.exe` → save. Setup's step 6 shows each screen. To go back, pick `KINGDOM HEARTS HD 1.5+2.5 Launcher.exe` the same way.

## Using it - **Tap the KH1 Companion icon** to open the companion (or let Cocoon open it with the game). It closes by itself as soon as the game exits. - **Close it any time** with the **×** at the top of the companion, or **Close** on its notification. - **Settings:** tap **×** on the companion → **Settings** (or **Settings** on its notification; on launchers with icon menus, long-press the icon). - **Nothing shows until a save is loaded**, so you never see leftovers from another save. ## Smoother play on the AYN Thor These settings have nothing to do with the companion (it uses next to nothing while the game runs), but they made KH1 itself play noticeably better on our Thor (GameNative 1.3.0), measured frame by frame: | Setting | Where | What it fixed | |---|---|---| | **Top screen at 120 Hz** | Thor display settings | Uneven frame pacing and input lag: frames reached the screen in about 6 ms instead of about 60 ms, with far fewer hitches. The game still runs at 60. | | **FEXCore Preset: Performance** | GameNative → the game → ⚙ → **Edit container** → **Emulation** | The frame-rate dips when turning the camera. The game's main thread was maxing out one CPU core; this preset lightens it. If you ever see glitches, set it back to *Intermediate*. | | **High Performance mode** | The Thor's per-app panel:

# Couch **Your gamepad, now a media remote for your Mac.** Lean back, thumbs on the pad. Works with IINA, YouTube and any player that listens to media keys. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/necromancerthedark/Couch?color=f4663f&label=release)](https://github.com/necromancerthedark/Couch/releases/latest) ![macOS 13+](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-13%2B-8e3a8e) ![Apple silicon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Apple%20silicon-arm64-555) ![Swift 5.9](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-5.9-f05138) [![CI](https://github.com/necromancerthedark/Couch/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/necromancerthedark/Couch/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [Controls](#-controls) · [Settings window](#-settings-window) · [App allowlist](#-app-allowlist) · [Install](#-install) · [Accessibility](#-first-run-accessibility) · [Tuning](#-tuning-without-a-rebuild) · [Troubleshooting](#-troubleshooting)
--- ## ✨ What it does - 🎮 **Fixed, sensible mapping.** Play/pause, seek, volume, next/prev, mute, fullscreen, brightness. No setup, no rebind screen. - 🎚️ **Analog scrubbing.** Hold a trigger to seek. Press deeper to scrub faster. - 🫥 **Lives in the menu bar.** A filled icon means the pad is live. An optional [Settings window](#-settings-window) shows more. - 🛡️ **Stays out of your games.** Couch acts only in apps you allow (IINA, browsers and more by default), so a game never receives its keys. - 🔌 **Reconnects by itself.** The pad sleeps when idle. Wake it with the Xbox button and Couch picks it back up. - 🚫 **No cursor control.** Keys and media keys only, by design. Built and tested with an Xbox-protocol pad (Cosmic Byte Blitz) on macOS 26. Input uses Apple's GameController framework, so other pads that macOS maps to an extended gamepad should work too. ## 🎮 Controls ``` LT scrub back RT scrub forward LB brightness − RB brightness + ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ Left stick ▲▼ player volume (Y) fullscreen │ │ [Menu] │ │ D-pad ▲ system vol + mute (X) previous (B) next│ │ ◄ seek back seek ► (A) play / pause │ │ ▼ system vol − │ │ Right stick: unmapped │ ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ``` The **Controller** tab of the [Settings window](#-settings-window) draws this live. | Pad input | Action | Sent as | |---|---|---| | **A** | Play / pause | media key | | **B** | Next track | media key | | **X** | Previous track | media key | | **Y** | Toggle fullscreen | `F` key (IINA, YouTube) | | **Menu** | Mute | media key | | **D-pad ◄ ►** | Seek back / forward | arrow keys | | **D-pad ▲ ▼** | System volume up / down, one notch per press | media key | | **Left stick ▲ ▼** | Player volume up / down. Hold to repeat, push further to go faster | arrow keys, repeating | | **LB / RB** | Brightness down / up | media key | | **LT / RT** | Hold to scrub back / forward | arrow keys, repeating | > Brightness controls the system display. It may do nothing on an external > monitor. ### The menu | Item | What it does | |---|---| | Controller line | Shows the connected pad, or "No controller". Adds "paused in " when the [allowlist](#-app-allowlist) is blocking the app in front | | **Allow ** | Appears only when Couch is paused in the frontmost app. One click adds it to the allowlist | | **Remote** switch | Turns the whole pad on or off without quitting | | **Launch at Login** switch | Starts Couch when you log in | | Check Accessibility… | Re-prompts for the permission | | **Settings…** (⌘,) | Opens the Settings window | | About Couch | Version and credits | ## 🪟 Settings window The menu bar stays the main interface. **Settings…** opens a companion window for the things a menu cannot show. A Dock icon appears while it is open and goes away when you close it. Nothing in it is required for Couch to work. | | | |---|---| | ![General](docs/screenshots/general.png) | ![Controller](docs/screenshots/controller.png) | | **General.** Remote and Launch at Login switches, Accessibility status with a fix button. | **Controller.** A drawn pad showing what every input does, lit up live as you press, plus battery and device details. | | ![Tuning](docs/screenshots/tuning.png) | ![Debug](docs/screenshots/debug.png) | | **Tuning.** Sliders for every setting with live preview bars. Applies instantly and saves to `config.json`. | **Debug.** Live event feed, log viewer, copyable diagnostics, and an action tester that fires each action without the pad. | ## 🛡️ App allowlist Couch reads the pad even when another app is in front, and sends system-wide keys. To keep that out of your games, it **acts only while an allowed app is frontmost** and stays silent everywhere else. No permission is needed for this. ![Apps](docs/screenshots/apps.png) - **Default list:** IINA, Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Arc, Brave, Edge, VLC, QuickTime Player, Music, TV and Spotify. - **Add an app:** with it in front, choose **Allow ** in the Couch menu-bar menu, or use **Settings → Apps** (*Add running app…*, *Add app…*, remove, reset to defaults). - **Everywhere mode:** the Apps tab can turn the filter off, which restores the old behaviour. The **Remote** switch still turns everything off. - **Limits:** a video playing in an app that is *not* in front cannot be controlled. Browser web apps (PWAs) have their own entry and must be added separately. ## 📦 Install 1. Download `Couch-v.zip` (not the "Source code" archives) from the [latest release](https://github.com/necromancerthedark/Couch/releases/latest) and unzip it. 2. Move `Couch.app` to `/

# MeNIN

**A live voice poetry battle, judged out loud by Homer.** MeNIN trains your voice the way the Greeks did, like a sport: Homer teaches you to improvise poetry out loud, you spar with him, you battle other poets live, you debate the way Socrates did, and then you play Greek games with your friends. Most AI talks for you. MeNIN makes you talk. One big screen, with your iPhone as the mic and the controller.

μῆνιν (*mēnin*, "MAY-nin") means **rage**. It's the first word of the Iliad.

**Try it: https://play.206.189.237.157.sslip.io** (open it on a laptop, choose Homer, and "Host a battle" makes it the arena; https://play.206.189.237.157.sslip.io/homer goes straight in) · **iPhone app:** https://testflight.apple.com/join/r9KCHkhc (live once Apple approves the beta; submitted Sun 3:27 AM) · **Video:** https://youtu.be/gvGEeuahLdE (2:41) · **Devpost:** [Devpost link] · **Figma:** [stage log deck](https://www.figma.com/slides/oYPLd3JeIjhnkNyt75qfOm), [design file](https://www.figma.com/design/qyaXnV3HbIUPIfYVbyqKwv) · prototypes: [first open → practice](https://www.figma.com/proto/qyaXnV3HbIUPIfYVbyqKwv?node-id=15-102&starting-point-node-id=15%3A102), [a full battle](https://www.figma.com/proto/qyaXnV3HbIUPIfYVbyqKwv?node-id=15-364&starting-point-node-id=15%3A364)

Built at Cal Hacks 13.0 by Matus, Sunya and Paul, with a team of Claude Code sessions. Original score by Paul. (See Credits.)

## What it is

One screen is the arena: our website at https://play.206.189.237.157.sslip.io, open in any laptop browser. Every player's iPhone is their mic and their private cards.

- **The poetry battle** (the main event). Homer writes a fresh theme every round and coins each poet a fresh epithet. Your phone shows three of Homer's phrases, stock phrases that fit the theme and the beat, the way Homer himself improvised. They're optional: "Stuck? Use one of Homer's phrases. It scores Craft." There's no metronome: the beat is how Homer trains you, and in battle you spit free. 3, 2, 1, SPEAK, and you get one window with a countdown ring, into a hands-free mic. Go quiet for about two and a half seconds, and he whispers you a phrase that fits. Within seconds of your last word, he judges you out loud on Image, Answer and Craft, out of 100, and quotes your best line. At the end, he stitches everyone's lines into one song and crowns a champion.
- **The Socratic debate**, hosted by Socrates in his own voice. You argue a side you didn't choose, with a hand of rhetorical moves, on 22 real dilemmas from Homer's world and Greek thought, like Achilles' own choice: a long, forgotten life, or a short one, sung forever.
- **The discus**: swing your phone and lift your thumb to release. Homer calls the throw.
- **Talk to Homer**: say a verse, and Homer answers out loud in two sentences. He quotes you, gives you one fix and scores it.
- **The Stadion**: pump your arms with the phone like a sprinter; everyone races at once on the screen.
- **Pygmachia** (boxing, beta): your phone is your fist; the server resolves every punch. **Toxeia** (archery, beta): the laptop's webcam tracks your bow arm and your draw, and your own phone looses the arrow.
- **Bard mode**: six short lessons (the beat, the formula, the epithet, the turn, the answer, the boast). Lesson one opens with the first line of the Iliad, whose first word in Greek is *mēnin*, our name. **Practice mode**: spar with Homer.
- *Experimental:* no install needed. A judge or friend can play from their own phone's browser at `https://play.206.189.237.157.sslip.io/join/CODE?web=1` → "Play in your browser" (poetry and Talk to Homer only).

**Who it's for:** spoken-word and slam poets, who practice alone between weekly open mics with no one to tell them whether their beat landed. Battling friends, and the Greek games after, are why a room opens it again.

## How it works

```
iPhone (player)                         website in a browser (arena)
  mic → on-device syllable onsets ──────► beat lane hits (lessons)
  mic → Cartesia ink-2 STT (keyterms) ──► live transcript
  loudness + pitch, 20 Hz ──┐
                            ▼
                     SpacetimeDB (rooms, turns, scores, private cards)
                            ▲
  Agent service (Python, FastAPI, DigitalOcean)
    stress scanner (CMU dictionary) → Beat (lessons)
    Claude → Image, Answer, Craft (out of 100), the verdict, the song
    Moss → the three phrases that fit the theme
    backstop: a turn left in judging 6 s → judged straight from SpacetimeDB
    Cartesia token minting ──────────────► Cartesia TTS (Homer's voice) on the arena
```

Four deployables: the iOS app (`ios/`), the website (`homer/web/`, static files served from our droplet), the SpacetimeDB module (`spacetime/`) and the agent service (`homer/`).

## Cartesia: ears and voice

Voice is the whole game: you play by speaking, and Homer answers out loud.

| Feature | How we use it |
| --- | --- |
| **ink-2 streaming STT** over WebSocket | The live transcript of every verse. We send **every phrase Homer dealt the poet, plus the theme, as keyterms**, so rare phrases like "rose-fingered Dawn" and "the wine-dark sea" survive the noise. |
| **sonic-3.6 TTS**, voice Carl ("Steady Storyteller") | Homer: entrances, verdicts, the freeze whisper, lessons and the stitched song |
| **Short-lived access tokens** | Our server mints a token, and the phone streams straight to Cartesia. No audio passes through our server, and the API key never leaves it. |

**Measured:**

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Word error rate, a drum at full volume (0 dB) as test noise, **with keyterms** | **3%** |
| Same, **without keyterms** | 20% |
| Final transcript after the end of speech | 62–81 ms |
| Homer's first audio, from the arena laptop on Wi-Fi | 78–90 ms |

**How we measured** (receipt: [`docs/voice-wer/`](docs/voice-wer/), with the scripts and the raw output, Fri Oct 23): a four-line verse spoken by a synthetic voice (macOS `say`), mixed digitally with a 90 BPM drum loop at

laminar-web: streamline background, physical pour game, enforced type

Streamline field
  src/StreamField.tsx mounts a fixed <svg> behind the whole console: one
  sine along x from -600..1800 in <defs>, ~22 near-parallel <use> copies
  translated down the viewBox with amp 4..11 (largest mid-height) and
  phase (i*11) mod 420 so lines never cross. Each copy drifts via
  stroke-dashoffset over 3..4.2 s and goes quiet under
  prefers-reduced-motion. A top mask fades it out beneath the shell so
  the brand row and tabs stay clean. .console wraps content at z-index 1;
  cards keep --panel so text never sits on a line.

Beat the robot
  Replaces the old linear tilt + per-degree flow with a critically
  damped spring on tilt (ω=5, substep ω·h<0.45) and the spec's flow
  model: q = k·max(0, θ−θ0)^1.5·sqrt(remaining/full), capped at
  3 mL/s, scaled so q=1.6 mL/s at θ0+20° with a full vial. The hidden
  start angle θ0 is drawn once per round in [26, 44]°. Flight is a FIFO
  with τ=0.28 s; after release the flow trickles with τ=0.18 s instead
  of cutting to zero. The round ends 0.7 s after q<0.005 and θ<2°.
  Rendering: one SVG for both figures. The vial rotates about its lip
  (transform-origin at the mouth), the liquid inside is a rect in a
  counter-rotating group clipped to the vial shape, so its surface
  stays horizontal while the vial tips. The stream is a cubic path
  from the lip to the beaker surface, width scaling with sqrt(q),
  dashoffset animated by q. The beaker surface wobbles while
  pouring, decaying with τ=0.5 s after. One requestAnimationFrame
  loop; it pauses when the tab is hidden.

Type is three roles
  --sans / --mono / --display tokens on :root (keeps the --f-*
  aliases that older components still read). body font-size 15px,
  buttons/inputs/selects/textareas inherit, so no UA default leaks in.
  .t-body (15/1.45, 13.5 inside tables), .t-title (16/1.35 600),
  .t-label (mono 11px 600 .15em uppercase), .t-num (mono 13.5 tabular,
  17 in stat cells), .t-figure (Unbounded 800 -.05em). Swept inline
  styles in Builder, Chat, Data and Console for stray font-family or
  letter-spacing and routed them through the roles. console.html
  preloads the Google Fonts stylesheet.

Arm3D
  Canvas background --paper, hemisphere light 1.15 (warmer ground),
  key light 2.6, grid lines muted to paper tones, fog removed. Arm
  shell overridden to 0x262C30, joints to 0x0E1113, gripper fingers
  (gripper_left/gripper_right links) to 0x7F8A90. The in-world lime

Burger-Nice/tuner.readme:
# Tuner

A fast, ad-free IPTV player for Xtream Codes and M3U playlists. Live TV with a guide, movies, series, favorites and continue-watching. Nothing locked, nothing phoning home.

## Get it

Each device has its own download, built for that device only:

| Device | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Windows PC | [Tuner-Setup.exe](https://github.com/Burger-Nice/tuner/releases/latest/download/Tuner-Setup.exe) |
| Google TV / Android TV | [Tuner-TV.apk](https://github.com/Burger-Nice/tuner/releases/latest/download/Tuner-TV.apk) (see below) |
| iPhone | AltStore source (see below) |

They share the same insides (sign-in, guide, NBA scores), but the TV app always uses the TV layout and the PC and phone apps never do.

### Windows

Download [**Tuner-Setup.exe**](https://github.com/Burger-Nice/tuner/releases/latest/download/Tuner-Setup.exe) and run it. After that, Tuner updates itself: new versions download in the background and install when you restart it. Windows may warn that the app is from an unknown publisher, because it isn't code-signed: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

Then sign in with the server address, username and password from your provider. If your provider gave you one long link with `get.php?username=…&password=…` in it, paste the whole link into **Server address** and the other fields fill in.

### Google TV / Android TV

1. On the TV, install **Downloader** (by AFTVnews) from the Play Store.
2. Turn on installs from it: **Settings → Apps → Security & restrictions → Unknown sources → Downloader** (on some TVs: **Settings → System → About**, click **Android TV OS build** 7 times to unlock developer options first).
3. Open Downloader and enter `https://github.com/Burger-Nice/tuner/releases/latest/download/Tuner-TV.apk`, then **Install**.

Tuner then appears on the home screen. It updates itself: when a new version is out it pops up **Update** (or go to **Account → Check for updates**), downloads it and asks the TV to install it. The first time, the TV asks you to allow Tuner to install apps: turn it on, press Back, then **Update** again. If an update ever gets stuck, enter the Downloader link above again: it installs over the top and keeps your login.

The TV app opens on a Home screen (Google TV / Netflix style): the NBA games, then your channels, recently watched, your list and what's new. The menu on the left opens when you move into it. The guide previews whatever channel you're on, and **OK** watches it. The on-screen keyboard only comes up when you press **OK** on a search or text box.

On the TV every channel plays in the built-in ExoPlayer engine at the TV's full resolution, 4K and HDR included. The channel banner shows the picture quality (e.g. *4K HDR*) and **CC** when there are subtitles.

| In the TV player | Live TV | Movies and episodes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **↑ / ↓**, channel buttons | Change channel | ↑ shows the controls, ↓ options: subtitles, audio, picture size |
| **← / →** | Options: box score, sync the score, channels, subtitles, audio, picture size | Back / forward 10 s |
| **OK** | The channel list (on an NBA game: the score and box score at the side, ←/→ switch team, OK closes) | Pause / controls |
| **Hold OK** | Last channel | |
| Number keys | Jump to a channel | |
| **Back** | Back to the guide | Back to the details |

**Black bars** above and below a movie are normal: most films are wider than a TV, and the player shows the whole picture. **Picture size → Zoom** fills the screen instead (trimming the sides), and **Stretch** fills it by stretching; Tuner remembers your choice.

**Judder on slow pans** in films comes from playing 24 frames a second on a 60 Hz screen. In a movie, press ↓ and pick **Match frame rate**: it switches the TV to a matching refresh rate while it plays (off by default, since many TVs blank for a moment while they switch).

Subtitles work when the movie, episode or channel carries them (most MKV and MP4 files do, and many channels have closed captions). Tuner remembers your choice: pick a language once and it's used from then on; pick **Off** and they stay off. Teletext subtitles, used by some European broadcasters, aren't supported.

**Sync the score to your stream:** IPTV runs behind the real game, so Tuner can hold the score back to match. Right as you see a basket on the TV, press **←/→**, choose **Sync the score to this stream** and pick that basket from the list. Tuner works out the exact delay from ESPN's play-by-play times.

### iPhone

Tuner installs through **AltStore** (free Apple ID; AltStore re-signs it every few days in the background while your phone is on home Wi-Fi and AltServer runs on your PC). In AltStore, go to **Sources → +** and add `https://github.com/Burger-Nice/tuner/releases/latest/download/altstore-source.json`, then install Tuner. Updates show up in AltStore.

## Movies and series

Movies and series open sorted by **Popular**, with English titles first. The chips above the posters change the sort (Popular, Recently added, Top rated, Newest releases, A–Z), the language (English first, any, or just one), the genre, the picture quality (4K, Full HD) and subtitles; press OK on a chip and its choices slide in from the right.

**Popular** and **Top rated** use IMDb: Tuner downloads a small ratings file once a week (built from [IMDb's free datasets](https://developer.imdb.com/non-commercial-datasets/), for personal use) and matches your provider's titles to it by name and year. *Popular* ranks by how many people rated a title, leaning towards recent releases and anything your provider files under trending or top-10 style categories; *Top rated* uses IMDb's rating, held back until a title has enough votes. Posters and details show the IMDb score. Titles IMDb doesn't know fall back to your provider's rating. Rotten Tomatoes has no free source, so it isn't included. anthskti/claude-tyson.readme:
# Claude Tyson

A browser boxing game you play with your body. Your webcam tracks your head and hands, so
you throw real punches, raise your gloves and slip to dodge, against another player (PvP)
or an adaptive Claude sparring bot. A keyboard mode plays the same game without a camera.

**Play:** https://claude-tyson.vercel.app

**AirPod controllers:** [hosted companion setup and current integration status](docs/HOSTED_MOTION.md). The game stays hosted; optional native sensors and inference run locally.

Next.js and Three.js render the game in the browser. SpacetimeDB runs every match:
it decides which actions count, how much damage lands, stamina, KOs and results, and it
keeps player profiles. Computer vision runs entirely on the player's machine; only
classified actions (a punch, a dodge, which gloves are up) are sent to the server, never
webcam frames or landmark streams.

## How to play

Pick **Keyboard** or **Camera** on the menu, then **Fight adaptive bot** or **Find PvP match**.
Camera mode first walks you through a short calibration (step into frame, show your
stance, show your block) and remembers it on that machine.

| Defence | Beats | Beaten by |
|---|---|---|
| Block (both gloves up) · drains 4 stamina/s | either straight | either hook |
| Dodge (slip left/right) · 20 stamina | either straight, same-side hook | opposite hook (×1.5 damage) |

- A block needs **both** gloves up. One glove alone does not block.
- Left straight: 0.5 damage, 5 stamina. Right straight: 1.3, 12. Hooks: 1.0, 16.
- Stamina regenerates at 12/s while you are idle. Both fighters' health and stamina bars
  are shown at the top of the screen.
- A successful dodge opens a short counter window (×1.5 damage).

### Keyboard controls

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `A` / `D` (hold) | slip left / right |
| `S` (hold) | lean back |
| `W` (hold), or `Q` + `E` | raise both gloves (block) |
| `J` / `U` | left straight / left hook |
| `K` / `I` | right straight / right hook |
| `C` | recalibrate · `T` simulate losing tracking |

See [keyboard-cheat-sheet.md](keyboard-cheat-sheet.md) for details.

### Camera input

Camera input is classified in the browser: MediaPipe pose and hand models run in two Web
Workers, and a TypeScript port of the cv-mvp punch/dodge detector turns their landmarks
into actions, which press the same controls as the keyboard. The first time you pick
Camera the page downloads about 22 MB (models and WASM), cached afterwards. Use a desktop
browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox), stand back so your head and both hands are in frame,
and allow camera access. The camera chip in the top bar shows tracking status and frame
rate (hover for timings); below 20 FPS the HUD warns that punches may not register.

The deprecated `cv-mvp` Python package is replaced by `motion/`. Camera-only play keeps the browser workers. AirPods + camera uses the downloaded Mac companion for IMU punches and pose-only dodges.

## Architecture

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/app/` | Next.js page |
| `src/game/` | Three.js scene, HUD, SpacetimeDB client (`net/`) |
| `src/game/cv/` | Camera input: `input.ts` (actions to controls), `browserCv.ts` (in-browser source), `airpods.ts` (authenticated companion source), `guard.ts` (block calibration), `cameraFeed.ts` (preview) |
| `src/game/cv/local/` | In-browser CV: MediaPipe workers and the detector port, with parity fixtures from cv-mvp |
| `spacetimedb/src/` | Schema, reducers, authoritative combat, bot, profiles |
| `engine/`, `input/` | Pure combat/input utilities used by the standalone arena |
| `dev/` | Standalone local arena (not the online game) |
| `assets/mediapipe/` | MediaPipe models, copied into `public/cv/` at build time |
| `AGENTS.md` | Project scope, architecture boundaries, and engineering guidance |
| `CONTRACTS.md` | Shared design contract for actions and combat shapes |
| `schema-diagram.md` | Conceptual SpacetimeDB data model and client/server pipeline |

The client may animate immediately, but the server decides accepted actions, damage,
health, KO and results. The adaptive bot adjusts bounded tactics only, never damage, hit
outcomes or the winner.

## Run locally

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh) and the [SpacetimeDB CLI](https://spacetimedb.com/install).
From the repository root, install the frontend dependencies once:

```sh
bun install
```

Start the local SpacetimeDB server in one terminal, then publish the module from the
repository root in another:

```sh
spacetime start
spacetime publish --anonymous --server local --module-path spacetimedb claude-tyson
```

In a third terminal, start the frontend:

```sh
bun run dev
```

This script generates the local CV assets, then runs `next dev` with Bun's `--bun` runtime
for lower startup and request latency. Open http://localhost:3001. The module bundles
files inside `spacetimedb/`; `spacetimedb/src/rules.ts` is the live rule set. Do not run
`sync-engine.sh` for now: `engine/rules.ts` is an older design and the script would
overwrite the server's rules with it. After changing the module schema, regenerate the
client bindings:

```sh
spacetime generate --lang typescript --out-dir src/game/module_bindings --module-path spacetimedb
```

The client defaults to `ws://localhost:3000` and database `claude-tyson`; set
`NEXT_PUBLIC_STDB_HOST` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_STDB_DB` in `.env.local` to change them (see
`.env.example`). `bun run dev` and `bun run build` first run `scripts/cv-assets.ts`, which
copies the MediaPipe WASM and hash-checked models into `public/cv/` (generated, gitignored).

Debug URL parameters: `?input=camera|keyboard|airpods`,
`?cvVideo=/clip.mp4` (play a same-origin clip as the camera), `?cvDelegate=GPU|CPU|mixed`.

## Tests

```sh
bun run test
```

Runs the engine, input and CV tests (including frame-by-frame parity between the
TypeScript detector and the Python one) and the SpacetimeDB module tests. After changing
the detector on either side, regenerate the parity fixtures from the `cv-mvp` branch:

realworldbuilder/makgorakombat.readme:
# MAK'GORA KOMBAT

BLOOD. HONOR. FATALITY.

A one-on-one fighting game played with World of Warcraft characters, in your browser, drawn from the game files already on your computer. No account, no server: drop your World of Warcraft folder on the page and the fighters, their gear and their animations are read from your own install and never leave your machine.

Play: https://realworldbuilder.github.io/makgorakombat/

The welcome page, for sharing: https://realworldbuilder.github.io/makgorakombat/welcome/ (`welcome/`, built to the landing-page-design skill).

## How it plays

1. Drag your `World of Warcraft` folder onto the page (it is in `Applications` on a Mac). Chrome on a Mac is what it is made for. A folder that holds more than one game (retail beside WoW Forever, say) asks **which world** to fight in; **E** on the champion screen switches to the other.
2. **CHOOSE YOUR CHAMPION.** Every race the game lets you create is on the grid, in the game's own portraits; your own characters, as captured by the [Mogshot addon](https://github.com/realworldbuilder/mogshot/tree/main/addon/Mogshot), are in the row above with their real gear; above those, the **LEGENDS**: Tyrande, Thrall, Sylvanas, Malfurion, Illidan, Varian, Cairne and Vol'jin, drawn exactly as the game draws them (the NPC's own gear, face and painted body), as far as your install has them. For now the ring is the legends' alone; add `?all` to the address (https://realworldbuilder.github.io/makgorakombat/?all) for every race and your own characters. Both players' cursors are on the grid at once. Resting on a tile summons that champion full size on your side; choosing makes them roar.
3. The **VS** screen: pick the ground. The stages are real places in the game world, read from the open folder's map files and raised around the fighters while they wait: Gurubashi Arena's pit, the ring of totems in the Valley of Trials, the Crossroads, the Valley of Heroes, Goldshire's lawn, Sentinel Hill, the gardens of Darnassus, Thunder Bluff's rise, and on a retail install Dalaran and the gate of Icecrown. The strip shows the stages the open install has maps for; past them are the game's loading screens, flat pictures behind the ring, for installs that lack a map.
4. Best of three rounds, sixty seconds each. Take the other champion's health to nothing and they are dazed: **FINISH THE MAK'GORA!** You have four seconds. Enter your class's **fatality** sequence (it is shown on your side of the screen) and the execution plays; an ability that lands without it is the plain finisher; either is **DISHONOR!** A swing, or the clock, is a mere **K.O.** A round won untouched is **HONOR RESTORED**.

### Editions

Each game in the folder is its own edition of the ring, because each one's files hold different champions and different ground. CHOOSE YOUR CHAMPION is dressed as that game's login screen: the edition's name under our logo, one of its loading screens behind the champions, its title music, its colours (`src/game/edition.ts`, every picture and track read from the install by file id). The games' official logos are not used.

| | Midnight Edition (retail, `wow` 12.x) | Forever Edition (WoW Forever, `wowf` 1.60, and its beta) | Classic Edition (`wow_classic_era` and the other classic clients) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legends | Tyrande, Thrall, Malfurion, Illidan, Varian, Cairne, Vol'jin, in their newest looks with their artifacts | Tyrande, Thrall, Sylvanas, Cairne, Vol'jin, in their first looks with the weapons the old files name | as Forever, as far as the files have them |
| Races and classes | 31 races (every allied race, the Dracthyr, Earthen and Haranir), 13 classes | the eight 2004 races and the two Skyborne, the nine 2004 classes | the 2004 races and classes |
| Stages | the five on the rebuilt world | all six, the Valley of Heroes too (Cataclysm rebuilt it on retail) | all six up to Wrath Classic; the rebuilt world from Cataclysm Classic on |
| Login screen | the Assault on Quel'Danas screen, Midnight's main title, void violet | its inked Kalimdor screen, *Legends of Azeroth*, bronze and teal | the 2004 continent screens, *Legends of Azeroth* |
| Spells | newer visuals, mostly particles the renderer leaves to `fx2d.ts` | the old spell models (Lightning Bolt's ball, Wrath's orb) | the old spell models |

![The two editions of one folder](docs/edition-choose.png)
![Midnight Edition](docs/edition-midnight.png)
![Forever Edition](docs/edition-forever.png)

### The fight is World of Warcraft's

Hold the attack key and your champion **auto-attacks on the weapon's swing timer** whenever the other is in reach: every 1.5 s with a one-hander or bare hands, 2.4 s with a two-hander, and a bow, gun or crossbow shoots every 2.0 s from anywhere on the stage (three quarters of the game's timers, so the ring keeps moving). A tap queues one swing. Every blow is rolled twice, as the game rolls it. First on the hit table: **miss**, **dodge** (the Dodge animation), **parry** (only from the front, and the parrier's next ability is a sure crit), **block** (a shield takes 40 % off), **crit** (double for a blow, half again for a spell) or a plain hit. Then in its damage range, like a weapon's 70 to 131: a two-hander strays 30 % either side of its average, a one-hander 25 %, a melee ability 15 %, a spell 8 %. No two swings need land alike, and the tooltips give the range ("Strikes the target for 14 to 19 damage"). Spells cannot be dodged or parried; a bolt in flight can still be jumped over.

The fighters stand as far apart as their bodies need, read from each model: a gnome can stand closer than a human, and Cairne, hunched forward over his hooves, stands well off. Walking into the other fighter stops at their body rather than shoving them across the ring, and reach grows with size as the game's combat reach does, so a big fighter and whoever faces him still hit from where they stand.

Each class has **three abilities** on the action bar beside the auto-attack, on a 1.0 s g

MostafaRLotfi/pokedex-tracker.readme:
# Pokédex Tracker

Free, single-page completion trackers for the main series Pokémon games. Each game gets a story-ordered Pokédex route, plus tabs for its endgame goals. No account and no install.

**▶ Use it here:** https://mostafarlotfi.github.io/pokedex-tracker/

![The Let's Go Pokédex route with Route 1 & 2 partly checked off, the game bar at the top and the save code bar at the bottom](docs/screenshot.png)

## Games

| Game | Tracker | Tabs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! / Let's Go, Eevee! | [Open](https://mostafarlotfi.github.io/pokedex-tracker/letsgo/) | Pokédex route · Grand Master (all 153 Master Trainers) |
| Pokémon Legends: Z-A (+ Mega Dimension DLC) | [Open](https://mostafarlotfi.github.io/pokedex-tracker/za/) | Pokédex route (232 Lumiose + 132 Hyperspace, with a Wild Zone view) · Mega Stones (all 92) |

| Pokémon Brilliant Diamond & Shining Pearl | [Open](https://mostafarlotfi.github.io/pokedex-tracker/bdsp/) | Pokédex route (Sinnoh 151 and National 493, with the Grand Underground and an area view) · Ramanas Park legendaries |

## Features

For Legends: Z-A it's the Mega Stones, sortable by Pokémon or grouped by where you get them. For Ultra Sun & Ultra Moon it's the 100 Totem Stickers, grouped by island and area, with the Totem-size Pokémon rewards. For Sun & Moon it's the 95 Zygarde Cells and 5 Cores, grouped by island and area. For Omega Ruby & Alpha Sapphire it's every catchable legendary, with what each Mirage spot needs, and all 46 Mega Stones. For X & Y it's the 27 Mega Stones you can find in the games. For Black 2 & White 2 it's every catchable legendary, with how to unlock each one. For Black & White it's the Unova legendaries. For Hear

smasimar/loi-tools.desc: Minimap overlay and free third-person camera for Castlevania: Lament of Innocence on PCSX2 (over PINE)
smasimar/loi-tools.readme:
# loi-tools

Quality-of-life tools for **Castlevania: Lament of Innocence** (NTSC-U, SLUS-20733 v1.01) running
in [PCSX2](https://pcsx2.net), in one script:

- **Minimap overlay**: the game's own map, always on screen, with your position and facing.
  No need to open the map menu.
- **Free third-person camera**: orbit the camera around Leon with the right stick.

Both work from outside the emulator. They read and write the game's memory over PCSX2's PINE
interface, so nothing is installed into PCSX2 or the game.

## Requirements

- Windows, PCSX2 2.x, and the NTSC-U release of LoI (SLUS-20733, CRC 28270F7D) as a disc image.
- Python 3.10 or newer.
- PCSX2 → Settings → Advanced → **Enable PINE** (slot 28011).
- For the minimap, run the game windowed or borderless fullscreen. Exclusive fullscreen hides overlays.

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Running

Start the game in PCSX2, then:

```
python loi_tools.py
```

Both tools start. The minimap appears while PCSX2 is the active window, and the camera takes
over as soon as you're in gameplay. **Ctrl+C** in the console quits and puts the game's original
camera back.

PCSX2 serves one PINE client at a time, so close other PINE tools first.

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--no-camera` / `--no-minimap` | run only one of the two |
| `--start-off` | start with the game's original camera (R3 switches to the free camera) |
| `--distance`, `--lift`, `--focal`, `--sens` | set a camera value and save it to `config.json` |
| `--invert-x`, `--invert-y`, `--smoothing 14` | camera options for this run |
| `--slot N` | PINE slot, if not 28011 |
| `--verbose` | log what the camera does |

## Minimap

On first run, the maps are extracted from your LoI disc image into `data/gamemap/`. The ISO is
found through PCSX2's game folders; set `"iso_path"` in `config.json` if it isn't. Only the map
data is kept, not the disc.

It shows the floor you're on, drawn like the in-game map. Explored rooms are blue, save and warp
rooms are red, unexplored rooms are dimmed, and your current room is outlined in yellow. A red
arrow shows your position and facing. The map's markers are drawn too: yellow discs for sub-weapon
pickups, red bars for locked doors (gone once the room behind is explored), purple arrows at exits
to another floor, and the "S" start point. Floors and areas switch automatically, also inside rooms that
span two floors, and the overlay hides while a menu, the shop or the map screen is open, and in
rooms the in-game map doesn't cover (like the final boss arena). The line
under the map shows the area, room and floor (e.g. `area 8 room 16 2F`, named like the in-game map).

**Hotkeys** (hold **Ctrl+Shift**):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| M | show / hide |
| Z | whole floor / zoomed in on you |
| + / − (or ↑ / ↓) | bigger / smaller |
| C (or ← / →) | move to another corner of the game picture |
| O | cycle opacity |

## Camera

The right stick orbits the camera around Leon. **R3** switches between the free camera and the
game's own camera.

While the tool runs, neither the right stick nor R3 opens the item/equipment quick menu, because
both belong to the camera. On the map screen and in the Start menu it still scrolls as usual, and
while you hold L1 (Orb menu) or L2 (Relic menu) it picks from the menu while the camera holds still.
Opening the map or a menu doesn't lose the camera's angle. After a cutscene or a door, the camera
swings round behind Leon.

**Hotkeys** (numpad, while PCSX2 is the active window):

| Keys | Adjusts |
|---|---|
| 4 / 6 | turn sensitivity, −/+ 0.1× |
| 8 / 2 | distance, closer / farther by 50 |
| 7 / 1 | angle (camera height above Leon), up / down by 25 |
| 9 / 3 | field of view, wider / narrower |
| 5 | reset to defaults |

## Settings and data

Hotkey changes are saved immediately to **`config.json`**, which has a `minimap` and a `camera`
section.

`data/` holds the extracted maps and a few files the minimap learns as you play. Both
`config.json` and `data/` stay local (git-ignored).

| Minimap setting | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `corner` | `top-right` | `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-right`, `bottom-left` |
| `anchor` | `image` | `image`: the game picture inside PCSX2's black bars, `view`: the whole view |
| `size`, `margin` | 0.32, 0 | width and edge gap, as fractions of the picture width |
| `opacity` | 0.85 | |
| `zoom`, `zoom_factor` | false, 2.5 | zoomed-in minimap centred on you |
| `aspect` | 4/3 | game picture aspect (PCSX2's "Auto 4:3/3:2" shows LoI at 4:3) |
| `hide_when_unfocused` | true | hide while another window is in front |
| `show_status` | true | area / room / floor line under the map |
| `explored` | `game` | `game`: the game's explored flags, `visited`: rooms the overlay saw you in, `all` |
| `show_unexplored` | true | draw unexplored rooms dimmed instead of hiding them |
| `iso_path` | none | your LoI disc image, if PCSX2's game folders don't have it |
| `trace` | false | debugging: log every drawn frame's position data |

## Helper tools

Optional, in `tools/`. Close `loi_tools.py` first, since they need the PINE connection.

- `python tools/pine_info.py`: checks the PCSX2 connection and whether your game version is supported.
- `python tools/extract_maps.py [iso]`: re-extracts the maps into `data/gamemap/`.
- `python tools/restore_game.py`: puts the original camera and controls back if `loi_tools.py` was
  killed without its normal Ctrl+C clean-up (console window closed, crash).

## How it works

The wiki explains both tools, with the memory addresses each one uses:

# BagVerse — Phase 1 prototype (gameplay + world)

Browser metaverse hub on Solana. This build covers **third-person gameplay and The Bag Square world**.
The blockchain layer (stateful skins, billboard leases, RWA escrow) comes next and has hooks ready.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm run build        # static build in dist/ (deploy anywhere: Vercel, Netlify, S3, IPFS)
```

**Graphics quality & crash safety:** three tiers, cycled with the **GFX** button in the HUD (the choice is remembered).
- **HIGH:** CSM shadows, AO, GI, LYGIA surfaces, 90k grass, up to 1.5× pixel ratio.
- **MEDIUM:** a single shadow map, no AO, 40k grass, 1× pixel ratio.
- **LOW:** no shadows, bloom, AO or surface layer; 14k grass, 8 NPCs. This is the default on phones.
- **Resolution cap:** internal resolution is capped by total pixel count, so 4K and high-DPI screens don't blow up GPU memory.
- **Shader pre-compile:** all shaders compile in parallel during loading (`compileAsync`), not in one burst on the first frame.
- **Recovery:**
  - A lost WebGL context shows a "graphics reset" screen and reloads one tier lower.
  - A session that ends without closing cleanly (tab crash) makes the next load start one tier lower, with a chat note.
  - A session that stays under ~22 fps sheds effects live and saves the lower tier.
- **Testing:** `tools/crashtest.mjs` exercises the crash-flag and context-loss paths.

URL flags: `?q=high|medium|low` (force a tier), `?low` (same as `q=low`), `?noao`, `?nocsm` (single shadow map), `?nogi` (no scene-captured GI), `?nograss`, `?nosurf` (no procedural surface layer), `?look=day|sunset|night`, `?autostart`.

**Global illumination & shadows:**
- **Scene-captured GI.** After loading (and on every Day/Sunset/Night switch), `Look.captureGI()` renders the lit district into a cubemap from the plaza.
  - The cubemap is pre-filtered (PMREM) into `scene.environment`, so glass, metal and wet surfaces reflect the real buildings and neon.
  - It's also projected into a spherical-harmonics `LightProbe`, giving soft coloured bounce light: warm from sunlit facades, magenta and cyan from the signage at night.
  - The flat hemisphere fill is reduced once the probe is live.
- **Cascaded shadow maps** (3 cascades out to 260 m). Towers cast crisp shadows near the player and long shadows across the district, without the blur of one huge shadow map.

**Procedural surfaces (LYGIA):** shaders use the [LYGIA](https://lygia.xyz) shader library via `#include "lygia/generative/fbm.glsl"` and similar includes.
- **Build-time resolve.** `tools/vite-lygia.js` is a small Vite plugin. It resolves those includes from the `lygia` npm package and inlines each file once, the same way `lygia.xyz/resolve.esm.js` does at runtime. It needs no network, so it works offline and on hosts that block third-party fetches.
- **Surface layer.** `src/shaders/surface.glsl` is injected by `src/surface.js` into every world `MeshStandardMaterial`.
  - Materials get a profile by name: facade, ground, metal, roof, foliage or paint.
  - Each profile adds world-space detail on top of the baked textures: tonal patches, rain streaks, street grime at the base of buildings, worn and patched asphalt with tar seams and hairline cracks, oil stains, rust and smudges on metal, and per-tree colour drift on foliage.
  - It also adds a procedural bump that fades with distance.
  - Puddles go glossy and reflect the captured neon. Wetness is driven by the Look preset: dry by day, soaked at night.
- **Off switch.** `?nosurf` turns the layer off. `__bagverse.surfaceUniforms.uSurfAmt` blends it live.
- **Grass noise.** The grass vertex shader (`src/shaders/grass.vert.glsl`) also uses LYGIA simplex noise.
- **Licence.** LYGIA is dual-licensed: Prosperity 3.0.0 (free non-commercial, 30-day commercial trial) or the paid LYGIA Patron licence for commercial use. See `LICENSES/lygia.md`. BagVerse is commercial, so get a Patron licence before launch, or swap the few noise functions used for MIT-licensed ones.

**Grass:** `src/grass.js` draws up to 90k GPU-instanced blades on a grid that follows the camera, masked to the park lawns with paths cut out.
- Each blade gets its own height, lean and colour, with dry patches.
- Wind combines rolling gusts with small flutter.
- Lighting follows the active Look preset, and blades fade out with distance.
- It costs one draw call and is skipped entirely when no lawn is nearby.
- Edit the `zones` and `holes` in `main.js` to grow grass elsewhere.

**Look (Fortnite-style):** `src/look.js` drives the stylised rendering.
- **Tone mapping:** Khronos PBR Neutral instead of ACES, so saturated colours stay saturated.
- **Light:** a strong warm sun as a 3/4 key light over the default camera's shoulder, at 55° so streets between the towers stay sunlit. Soft cascaded shadows.
- **Shade:** a bright, near-neutral fill (hemisphere + scene-captured GI) keeps shaded areas readable. The GI capture is desaturated per preset (`giChroma`: day 0.12, sunset 0.3, night 0.35), because the plaza's cyan floor neon was tinting all the bounce light blue-green. The grade lifts shadows slightly warm-neutral, so they never go black.
- **Materials:** a stylise curve lifts near-black albedos (asphalt, dark metal, roofs) into the mid-tones.
- **Atmosphere and effects:** a bright saturated sky with crisp clouds and light AO. Bloom only catches real emissives, and a NaN guard runs ahead of it so one bad pixel can't black out the frame.
- **Presets:** press **N** or use the HUD button to cycle Day, Sunset and Night. Each rebalances sun, sky, fog, neon, surface grime, wetness and grade.

**Controls** — WASD / arrows move · Shift walk · Space jump · click or drag to look · wheel zoom ·
E interact · 1 wave · 2 dance · G emotes · I inventory · M map (click a district to fast-travel) · Enter chat.
Mobile: left joystick, drag right side to look, JUMP and E buttons.

asawisemansaid/stonetop-campaign-docs.readme:
# Stonetop Campaign Docs

**GM only.** Set up October 21, 2026. This folder keeps a copy of every doc in the Stonetop rpg Project, plus the table tools and older files that live outside it.

## How it's kept

- **This folder is a Git repository** (October 24), backed up to a private GitHub repo, asawisemansaid/stonetop-campaign-docs. Every change is a snapshot that can be reviewed and undone.
- **1_Project_Docs is a mirror of the Project.** Same docs, same file names. Whenever Claude creates or edits a Project doc, it saves the copy to the GitHub repo in the same chat, and Obsidian brings it here: when Obsidian starts, and every 10 minutes while it's open. That works even when this computer is off; the copy lands the next time Obsidian opens. A new Project doc lands here too.
- **The Project is the source of truth.** If you edit a file in 1_Project_Docs by hand, Obsidian saves it to the repo within 10 minutes, but still tell Claude, so the Project copy catches up instead of overwriting your change.
- **Retiring a doc.** When a doc leaves the Project, its last copy goes to 4_Retired with the date in its name. Claude does the move in the repo.
- **No dates in folder names,** so nothing goes stale. Dates appear only on retired files.
- **Obsidian:** this folder is the vault "Campaign Docs." Its Git plugin pulls on startup and saves (commits and pushes) every 10 minutes. Don't rename or move files in Obsidian; ask Claude, who does it in the repo and the Project together. Calendarium is installed, with no calendar yet.
- **Git settings files:** .gitattributes keeps every text file on Unix line endings on every computer, so this folder, the Project, and the repo match byte for byte. .gitignore keeps Obsidian's window layout, cache, and plugin code out of the history. Tool_Setup_Plan.md has the rest.
- **Backups of this folder** sit next to it, in Desktop\Stonetop\Stonetop: *Campaign Docs backup 2026-10-24 before Git and Obsidian.zip* (all 34 files, before any Git or Obsidian changes).

## What's here

### 1_Project_Docs: the live docs

- **Stonetop_Campaign_Overview.md:** lore, threats, secrets, open questions, action items, and the current episode's decisions.
- **Stonetop_Cast.md:** every PC and NPC, one short entry each, plus the follower blocks.
- **Episode_3_Run_Sheet.md:** prep for the current episode, and the source for the GM screen.
- **Back_Pocket.md:** built or pitched material that isn't scheduled for any episode.
- **Episode_1_Record.md, Episode_2_Record.md:** what was played, with each episode's decisions at the end. Episode 1's is still a stub.
- **GM_Insights_and_Techniques.md:** notes from Jeremy Strandberg's two actual-play series.
- **Portraits.md:** the NPC profile pictures for Amsel: the rules, the credits, and what's left (October 22).
- **Tool_Setup_Plan.md:** the plan for Git, Obsidian, Tome, and the prep check-ins, with progress (October 23 and 24). It retires once setup is done.

### 2_Table_Tools

- **Project_Instructions_full.txt:** the Project's custom instructions, ready to paste into the Project settings.
- **NotesBot_Custom_Prompt.txt:** NotesBot's custom prompt (October 20).
- **Stonetop_GM_Screen_Episode2.html:** the GM screen as of October 19. It opens in any browser, and its checkboxes save only in the browser you open it in. The live screen is a Claude artifact, rebuilt for Episode 3 at the same link.
- **Scripts:** the scripts Claude uses to rebuild Episode 3 in Tome from the run sheet, to make the hub notes and links for Obsidian (October 24), and to write Lore pages, including the October 25 powers-and-places rollout. The README inside explains them.

### 3_Amsel_Reference

The July files made for Amsel Suite: bestiary, concepts and eras, factions and groups, landmarks and regions, named characters (gods, mythic figures, and singular entities), places of interest, and settlement profiles. They use @ tags. Where they cover the same people or events as 1_Project_Docs, the Project docs are newer and win.

- **og templates.lorekit:** your Lore templates as exported October 21, before the Stonetop templates. Structure only, no page content.
- **Stonetop Characters.lorekit:** the Stonetop PC and Stonetop NPC templates (October 21). Import it in Lore from the three-dot menu at the top left (Import Templates). Its template names don't match any of yours, so nothing gets overwritten.
- **Stonetop Powers and Places.lorekit:** the Stonetop Power, Place, Settlement, and Group templates (October 25). They're already in Stonetop.lore, written in directly on October 25, so don't import this kit, or Lore will have two of each. It stays here as a record. Every power, place, settlement, and group page moved to them the same day (Tool_Setup_Plan.md has the rollout).
- **Your Lore and Tome files** live in Documents\Stonetop game, not here. Stonetop.lore is the live Lore file. Stonetop.tome holds the Episode 3 pilot, built from the run sheet (October 24): prep only, and rebuilt from the run sheet whenever it changes, so edits made in Tome don't last. The backups beside them, newest first:
  - Stonetop.backup-2026-10-25-before-hiding-unused-templates.lore: before the twelve stock templates that never had a page were hidden (October 25).
  - Stonetop.backup-2026-10-25-before-hiding-templates.lore: before the ten old templates with no pages were hidden (October 25).
  - Stonetop.backup-2026-10-25-before-rollout.lore and Stonetop.backup-2026-10-25-before-rollout.tome: before every power, place, settlement, and group page moved to the new templates, and before Tome was rebuilt to link the new pages (October 25).
  - Stonetop.backup-2026-10-25-before-powers-and-places.lore: before the four new templates, the Powers box on the character templates, and the test pages for Ghlast-Ehun and the Weeping Stone (October 25).
  - Stonetop.backup-2026-10-24-before-episode-3.tome: the Tome file before Episode 3 went in, with the test pages and Greg's formatting sample (October 24).

kromossomom-debug/decky-xbox-dashboard.readme:
A Decky Loader plugin that turns SteamOS Game Mode into the Xbox Series X|S dashboard.
A home screen built around the game's art, LB / RB tabs on top, “My games & apps”, Guide-style menus and Xbox colors across all of Steam.

--- ## ✨ Preview

My games & apps: filters on the side, square tile grid System: shortcuts as cards, like on Xbox


Game page (press Y on any tile): Play, pin, Deck compatibility, HowLongToBeat, achievements and shortcuts

Layout previews at the Steam Deck's resolution (1280×800), shown with Steam in Portuguese. ## 📦 Install

# Jonli Fizika

Fizika formulalarini jonli animatsiyalar orqali tushuntiruvchi interaktiv sayt. Har bir mavzuda parametrlarni oʻzgartirib, natijani darhol koʻrish mumkin.

- 145 ta mavzu, 14 boʻlim (kinematika, dinamika, statika, saqlanish qonunlari, tebranishlar, molekulyar fizika, termodinamika, elektrostatika, tok, magnetizm, optika, nisbiylik, kvant fizikasi, yadro fizikasi)
- Har bir boʻlim uchun erkin laboratoriya (🔬), jumladan Shryodinger tenglamasini yechadigan kvant laboratoriyasi
- Barcha mavzularda 3D koʻrinish (Three.js)
- ⚔️ Bellashuv: sunʼiy intellekt (3 daraja) yoki doʻst bilan bir qurilmada oʻynash. Oʻyinlar: viktorina, formulani top, joyiga qoʻy, tez hisob, toʻgʻri yoki notoʻgʻri, mavzuni top, xotira juftliklari, aralash (`#/jang` havolasi). Yangi: VS intro va 3‑2‑1 sanoq, 🔥 seriya (×1,5 / ×2), kuchaytirgichlar (50/50, ❄️ muzlatish, ×2 ochko), tortishuv chizigʻi, robot gaplari, yakunda statistika va XP
- 🛠️ «Modelni yig‘» oʻyini: detallarni sxemaga sudrab, shartni bajaring. 8 xil jumboq: aralash zanjir (umumiy qarshilik), parallel tarmoqlarda teng tok, richag muvozanati, yupqa linza bilan aniq tasvir, lazer va koʻzgular, P nuqtada E = 0, suv aralashtirish (issiqlik balansi), Guk qonuni boʻyicha prujinalar. Robot bilan poyga yoki doʻst bilan navbatma-navbat; vaqt tugasa toʻgʻri yechim koʻrsatiladi
- 🏅 Taraqqiyot: XP va unvonlar (🌱 Yangi boshlovchidan 🏅 Afsonagacha), 15 ta yutuq, har boʻlim boʻyicha progress, koʻrilgan mavzularda ✓ belgisi, profil oynasi
- 🔍 Tezkor qidiruv: Ctrl/⌘+K yoki `/` — mavzu, formula va buyruqlar
- ✨ Kun formulasi, 🎲 tasodifiy tajriba, 🎬 taqdimot rejimi (P tugmasi, toʻliq ekran)
- Uch til: oʻzbek, rus va ingliz (yuqori oʻng burchakdagi UZ / RU / EN tugmalari, tanlov eslab qolinadi; havola orqali `?lang=ru` yoki `?lang=en`)

## Ochish

`index.html` faylini brauzerda oching yoki GitHub Pages orqali joylang:
**Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from a branch → `main` / `(root)`**.

## Tuzilma

- `index.html` — tayyor sayt (GitHub Pages uchun)
- `jonli-fizika.html` — `build.sh` chiqargan bitta fayl
- `src/` — manba kodlar: `head.html`, `core.js`, `sim_*.js` (mavzular), `lab_*.js` (laboratoriyalar), `three3d*.js` (3D sahnalar), `ui.js`, `battle.js` va `battle_data.js` (bellashuv oʻyinlari va savollar banki), `extras.js` (XP, yutuqlar, qidiruv, taqdimot rejimi), `i18n.js` (til almashtirgich va tarjima mexanizmi), `i18n_dict.js` (rus va ingliz lugʻati)

## Qayta yigʻish

```sh
sh src/build.sh
```

Bu `src/` dagi modullarni birlashtirib `jonli-fizika.html` faylini yaratadi.
