YosuaSurianto/Worldrift.readme:
# WorldRift

WorldRift is a browser-based 3D endless runner set in a burning Borneo rainforest. A ranger escapes along a winding forest trail while an orangutan follows. Monad Testnet powers paid runs, revives and transferable premium cosmetic skins.

The project is a testnet demo. It does not establish trustworthy competition scores or support real-money rewards.

## Repository

| Folder | Responsibility | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web/` | Next.js app, 3D game, wallet UI, Shop, Vault, authentication and SQLite API | [Web README](web/README.md) |
| `contract/` | Solidity Arena and ERC-1155 Skins, Foundry tests, deployment scripts and ABIs | [Contract README](contract/README.md) |

The app imports generated ABIs from `contract/handoff/`. Keep both folders in the same repository layout.

## Quick start

Requirements: Node.js 24 or newer, npm, Git, a modern browser with WebGL, and an injected wallet for on-chain actions. Foundry is needed only for contract development and local chain tests.

```powershell
cd web
npm ci
Copy-Item .env.example .env
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. Use the same hostname consistently when signing in. Set `SITE_URL` to the actual public origin for production and restart after configuration changes. Public `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` changes require a new production build.

Leave both contract addresses empty for the labelled MOCK mode. For Monad Testnet, configure these public values in `web/.env`:

```dotenv
NEXT_PUBLIC_CHAIN_ID=10143
NEXT_PUBLIC_ARENA_ADDRESS=0x7476fD21A146271145156632D7d281BDeCEe5b10
NEXT_PUBLIC_SKINS_ADDRESS=0xcAFCC8042192133d0894854Da88bfc6461404fb6
```

Never commit `.env`, private keys, sessions or the SQLite database.

## Player flow

1. Open `/` and play free practice, or connect a wallet on Monad Testnet for paid play.
2. Sign in by reviewing and signing the server-issued message. Signing in costs no gas.
3. Open `/market` to browse skins. Premium purchases use a wallet transaction; standard purchases use Leaf Crystals stored by the backend.
4. Open `/vault` to inspect ownership. Premium ownership comes from ERC-1155 balances; standard ownership comes from SQLite.
5. Equip an owned skin after signing in, then return to the game. Premium models and standard color tints are selected from the server profile. Premium ownership is rechecked by the client and by the equip API.
6. During paid play, confirm each entry or revive in the wallet. A successful receipt is required before the game treats a payment as complete.

Desktop controls: A/D turn, W or Space jump, S slide. Touch controls: swipe left/right to turn, up to jump, down to slide. Paid runs cannot be paused.

## Skins and ownership

| Skin | Catalog ID | Storage | Appearance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Safari Ranger | `default` | Always available, not minted | Current default ranger |
| Cooperative Driver | `prem_2` | ERC-1155 token ID 2 | Imported Sopir Kopdes model |
| Plantation Foreman | `prem_3` | ERC-1155 token ID 3 | Imported Mandor Sawit model |
| Monad Sultan | `prem_4` | ERC-1155 token ID 4 | Imported Sultan Gmonad model |
| Standard Rangers 1 to 3 | `std_1` to `std_3` | Backend database | Placeholder tints |

Premium MON prices are read from the adapter. Standard prices are defined only in `web/src/game/skins.ts`. Crystals are credited only by server-validated runs. The browser game does not yet submit finished runs to that backend lifecycle, so a new account can legitimately have zero crystals.

A premium purchase mints one token directly to the purchasing wallet. No claim transaction is needed. A transferable token can leave that wallet, after which ownership checks fall back to the default appearance. Standard skins and the default skin are not NFTs.

## Public contracts

Network: Monad Testnet, chain ID `10143`, native currency `MON`.

| Contract | Address |
| --- | --- |
| WorldriftArena | `0x7476fD21A146271145156632D7d281BDeCEe5b10` |
| WorldriftSkins | `0xcAFCC8042192133d0894854Da88bfc6461404fb6` |

[View Arena](https://testnet.monadvision.com/address/0x7476fD21A146271145156632D7d281BDeCEe5b10) and [view Skins](https://testnet.monadvision.com/address/0xcAFCC8042192133d0894854Da88bfc6461404fb6).

The deployed demo was built from a patched copy: entry and each revive cost 1 MON. Checked-in contract source retains the original fee schedule. Read contract state before presenting or paying a fee. Source verification status is not established by this README.

## NFT metadata release requirement

A read-only check on 2026-10-24 confirmed ERC-1155 support, but the deployed Skins URI is still `https://worldrift.invalid/skins/{id}.json`. Ownership can exist on chain while wallet artwork is missing.

The app provides `/api/skins/metadata/{id}.json`, accepting the ERC-1155 64-digit lowercase hexadecimal token ID or decimal IDs 2, 3 and 4. It returns public names, preview images and GLB URLs. Deploy the app on a stable HTTPS origin, configure `SITE_URL`, verify metadata and image URLs publicly, then have the contract owner call `setURI` with that public endpoint. See the contract guide. Wallet NFT discovery and testnet display vary by wallet; do not promise automatic display.

## Verification

```powershell
cd web
npx tsc --noEmit -p .
npx eslint src
npm test
npm run build
```

Contract verification:

```powershell
cd contract
forge build
forge test -vvv
```

The web guide describes opt-in tests that deploy real contracts to a local Anvil, mint all three premium skins, verify balances and transfer events, equip them, and verify ownership loss after a transfer. Model tests exercise the real rig and gameplay clips without GPU rendering. These checks do not prove that a real wallet transaction succeeded on Monad Testnet.

## Operational boundaries

- SQLite requires persistent writable storage and backups. Do not place the database on an ephemeral deployment filesystem.
- In-memory rate limits and RPC caches are scoped to one server process. Multiple instances need shared

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The link stops pointer and key events natively so opening the shop does not

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(market): skin marketplace (reviewed) with server side crystal purchases and chain checked equip

Adds /market with premium skins (MON, read from the contract) and standard
skins (Leaf Crystals), the skin catalog, and the API: GET /api/skins,
POST /api/skins/buy and POST /api/skins/equip. The first draft was produced
outside this repo and reviewed here before committing.

Review findings, fixed:
- The chain read for premium ownership used one global rate bucket of ten
  reads per second, so a flood from any number of sessions made every player's
  catalog and equip requests fail, and the single public RPC with no retries
  was flaky on its own. Reads now go through a short cache, shared in-flight
  reads per wallet and a small concurrency gate (waiting instead of refusing),
  use the fallback RPCs, and failures are never cached.
- A premium skin is an ERC-1155 and can be transferred away after equipping;
  the catalog no longer reports it as equipped once the wallet stops owning it.

Verified in review: prices and ownership come only from the server catalog and
the chain, the purchase is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (balance check, ledger
debit and ownership row), the wallet comes only from the session, bodies are
strict zod schemas with a 256 byte cap, writes check Origin and are rate limited.

Tests: skin API security, purchase and equip rules, cache, concurrency and
failure handling of the chain reads, chain checked equip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(web3): make sign-in requests stateless so nobody can evict or block another wallet

Capping live nonces still let a flood push a victim's pending request out of
storage. The sign-in nonce is now a random value plus an HMAC over wallet, site
and issue time (secret kept in the database meta table), so the server
recognises its own requests without storing them. Issuing writes nothing, a
request is recorded only after its signature verifies (single use, primary key
enforced), and the signed text must match what the server would have issued, so
expiry cannot be extended and a nonce cannot move between wallets.

Rate limit keys for IPv6 clients now use the /64 prefix.

Tests: 5000 requests for a victim's address do not stop the victim, forged and
cross wallet nonces fail, expiry cannot be extended, /64 grouping.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(web3): sign-in requests can no longer be used to lock a wallet out

The nonce endpoint refused a wallet after 5 requests a minute, but anyone can
type anyone's address, so an attacker could fill that bucket and block the real
owner from signing in. The per-wallet refusal is gone. Abuse control stays on
the per-client ceiling and on signature attempts per issued message (an
attacker only holds messages they requested themselves), and storage is bounded
by capping live nonces and dropping the oldest instead of refusing new ones.

A per-wallet cap with eviction was considered and rejected: flooding a victim's
address could evict the nonce the victim is about to sign. Tests cover a flood
for another wallet not stopping its owner, and the bounded storage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(game): pay 1 MON to play and 1 MON to revive

Menu: "Play for 1 MON" pays the season entry fee with startRun and then runs.
"Connect wallet to play" and "Switch to Monad Testnet" appear when needed, and a
free practice run stays available for guests. After dying in a paid run a 3
second revive offer appears; paying calls instantRevive and only a confirmed
receipt brings the runner back, followed by a frozen 3-2-1 countdown and about
1.5 s of immunity. Pending, cancelled, slow network (retry by resume hash),
wrong network and not enough MON all have a visible state.

The contract clock does not stop, so a paid run cannot pause, ends by itself at
about 570 s, and ends if the tab is hidden for more than 5 s. HUD shows time
left, revives left and immunity. Space no longer starts a run when a wallet is
ready, so a stray key cannot trigger a payment.

Engine, store, screens and HUD changes are small and commented; the logic lives
in game/paid.ts. 15 engine level tests drive the whole flow on the mock adapter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(web3): fall back to other public Monad testnet RPCs

The first public RPC answered "requests limited to 15/sec" in practice, which
broke reads even for a single player. Reads now fall back to the Monad
Foundation and Ankr endpoints listed in the Monad docs (an explicit RPC URL
still wins), used by wagmi and by the server chain client.

Tests: the Anvil end to end tests follow the flat revive fee of the patched
deployment and tolerate Anvil's lagging safe block; the testnet read test uses
the same transport.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(web3): address security review findings in rate limiting and run settlement

- x-forwarded-for: behind a trusted proxy use the entry added by the Nth proxy
  from the right (TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS, default 1), never the client controlled
  leftmost entry. Without TRUST_PROXY the header is ignored and production logs
  a warning.
- Shared bucket lockout: without an IP source all direct clients share one
  bucket, so the per-client limits are now generous ceilings and the real
  brakes are per wallet (nonce) and per issued message (verify), which cannot be
  used to lock other players out.
- Run settlement race: a rejection can now only close a run that is still open,
  so a concurrent request that already settled it is never overwritten. A test
  covers an honest and a tampered finish racing.

Orimaster354/hackpsu-fall-2026.readme:
# Blindspot (HackPSU Fall 2026)

Blindspot is a social-deduction game, inspired by Among Us, played in a real room on four iPhones. Players walk to real task stations, do motion-based tasks, and try to find the impostor.

## MVP
- Host records a perimeter pose walk, then a sweep of JPEG frames with matching poses/intrinsics, and saves an ARWorldMap. The app does no geometry.
- The scan processor builds the room polygon and a 1 m tile grid from a perimeter pose walk. YOLOE detects wall Post-it notes and contextual wall features; Gemini chooses note observations as task candidates using nearby visual cues. Server geometry places stations on edge tiles and an emergency tile near the center; host reviews and edits. Perimeter/sweep endpoints and synthetic geometry acceptance are implemented; real ARKit sweep acceptance remains pending.
- Players see world-anchored AR icons: a question mark on task tiles and an EMERGENCY text icon on the meeting tile.
- Four phones join with a 4-letter room code. No QR codes.
- 1 impostor, 3 crew. Roles are private.
- Crew do tasks at stations: shake, hold-steady, rotate dial, gesture pattern, hammer.
- Impostor swipes to kill a player on the SAME tile (25 s cooldown).
- A dead player leaves their phone on the spot as the body, and may wander. Ghosts do not do tasks.
- Report or emergency meeting, 30 s vote, ejection, win check.
- One sabotage: lights out, fixed by holding a fix station.
- Fallback: if relocalization fails, a player taps their tile on a 2D map.

## Stack
- iOS: Swift, SwiftUI, ARKit (video, pose log, ARWorldMap, AR icons), Core Motion.
- Server: Node.js, `ws`, in-memory state (no database).
- AI: local YOLOE-26 Large detection (configurable checkpoint); Gemini task reasoning called only from the server. See `server/README.md` for detector setup and the live app-scan dashboard.

## Setup
1. iOS: open `Untitled Project 2.xcodeproj` on a Mac, set your signing team, run on a physical iPhone.
2. Server: `cd server && npm install && cp .env.example .env` (set `GEMINI_API_KEY`), then `npm start`. It listens on port 8080.
3. Network: join all phones to one phone hotspot, run the server on a laptop on it, and enter the laptop's LAN IP in the app's settings.

## Docs
- `docs/architecture.md`: modules, models, protocol.
- `docs/tasks.md`: ordered checklist with owners.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`: rules for coding agents.

katielarissamartin-source/pebble-island.readme:
# Pebble Island

Learning app for Ivy and Hayden, with a grown-ups' dashboard (Audrey's Hub). Plain JavaScript web app (PWA), hosted on Vercel, cloud sync on Supabase.

Live: https://pebble-island.vercel.app

## Rules for anyone editing (Claude, ChatGPT, people)
- Work on a branch, open a pull request, merge to `main`. Vercel deploys `main`.
- Bump the `CACHE` name in `sw.js` whenever an existing file changes (the service worker is cache-first). Use a number higher than the one on `main`.
- Add new files to the `CORE` list in `sw.js` and a script tag in `index.html`. Keep edits to those two files to the lines needed.
- Prefer a new file over editing a shared one.
- Do not commit the family code, the hub password or any child data.
- Test on a preview deployment before merging.

ducvd89/Bloodborne-android-rebuild-tool.readme:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later -->
# Bloodborne Android Rebuild Tool

The [Bloodborne Android port](https://github.com/ducvd89/Bloodborne-Android) runs the game only as **native ARM64 code**: the game's x86-64 code is recompiled ahead of
time from **your own** copy of the game, once, into a file (`libbbaot.so`). This tool does that recompiling. You can run it in two places:

- **on the phone**, inside the app (Bloodborne Android **2.1.0 Beta** or newer): no PC needed;
- **on a PC** (Windows, Linux, or a Mac with Apple Silicon), from your PKG files or an already extracted game, and copy the result to the phone.

> **Version 1.2.0** writes native code with **ABI version 2**. It needs the app **2.1.0 Beta or newer**, and app 2.1.0 needs a library from tool 1.2.0. Libraries built by
> tool 1.1.0 or older (ABI 1) are refused by the app and must be rebuilt: they contain a bug that can stop the game with `guest trap (0x800d0b, 0x287188a)`.
> Tested on an AYN Thor (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2).

## Why you build it yourself

The recompiled code is a translation of the game's own program, so it belongs to the game's
copyright holders and can never be downloaded from here or anywhere else. The tool only works on a
game you own: it reads your PKG files or game folder and writes the result for your phone. Nothing from
the game is in this repository (no PKG, no executable, no extracted file, no recompiled library,
ever), and nothing is uploaded: everything runs on your own device. The files the tool writes come from
your game: keep them for yourself and **never share them**.

## Two ways to get the native code

| | **A. On the phone** (in the app) | **B. On a PC** (this tool) |
|---|---|---|
| **You need** | Bloodborne Android **2.1.0 Beta** or newer, with the game installed in it. | The tool, and either the PKG files or an extracted game (see below). Then a copy to the phone. |
| **Time** | About **6 minutes** on a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 with the **charger connected**; the phone gets hot. | A few minutes on a PC (2.5 minutes on a 24-thread PC); more for unpacking PKGs. |
| **Resources** | About **4 GB of free RAM** and **1 GB of free storage** while it works. | 8 GB of free RAM, about 3 GB of disk (plus the PKG size). |
| **Result** | The app uses it by itself. | An `aot` folder (about 125 MB) to copy next to `eboot.bin` on the phone. |

### A. On the phone

When the app has no native code for its version it shows **Native code needed**: choose **Build on this phone** (later rebuilds: menu > **Native CPU** > **Rebuild on this phone**), and keep the app open with the charger connected until it is done. The app shows a progress bar and an estimate of the time
left. The phone gets warm and slows down if it overheats: take it out of its case and do not use it for other things. If the app is stopped or the phone restarts, start the build again:
the parts that were finished are kept. The tool inside the app is the same program as the PC tool (the same compiler, the same output: the library is the same file byte for byte).

### B. On a PC

You build the native code on a PC from your own game files and copy it to the phone. Pick the way that matches the files you have:

| | **B1. From PKG files** | **B2. From an extracted game** |
|---|---|---|
| **You have** | The base game PKG and the 1.09 update PKG (fake PKGs, the same files the app's "Install from PKG" uses), together in one folder with nothing else in it. | A game folder with the 1.09 update merged in: `eboot.bin`, `sce_module/`, `sce_sys/` and the rest (for example the folder the app's "Install from PKG" made, or a dump you extracted yourself). |
| **The tool writes** | The whole game folder (`CUSA03173`) with `aot/` inside, and a README.txt. | Only `aot/` (`libbbaot.so`, `libbbaot.json`). Your game folder is never changed. |
| **You copy to the phone** | The game folder (a large copy). | The `aot/` folder (about 125 MB), next to `eboot.bin` in the game folder there. |
| **Time** | 15-30 minutes, mostly unpacking and copying. | A few minutes. |

**Game already on the phone?** Build from whichever files you still have on the PC, then copy only the `aot/` folder next to `eboot.bin` on the phone.

#### What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| **Game files** | B1 or B2 above: Bloodborne **1.09** with the original `eboot.bin` (pre-patched 60 FPS eboots are refused). Tested with **CUSA03173**; other releases of 1.09 should work but are untested. |
| **PC** | Windows 10 (1903+) / 11, 64-bit, or Linux with glibc 2.35+ (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36, Arch or newer): a processor with AVX2 (Intel 2013+ or any AMD Ryzen). Or a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14.4+. |
| **Memory / disk** | 8 GB free RAM (16 GB+ is faster). Free disk space: about 3 GB, plus the size of the base game PKG for B1. |
| **Phone** | The Bloodborne Android app **2.1.0 Beta or newer**. |

#### Step 1: Get the tool

Download it from the [latest release](https://github.com/ducvd89/Bloodborne-android-rebuild-tool/releases/latest) (or build it from source, see
[Building from source](#building-from-source)); check the file against its `.sha256`:

- **Windows:** `bb-recomp-windows-x86_64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and double-click `bb-recomp.exe`. If Windows
  SmartScreen warns that the app is unknown, click **More info → Run anyway** (the tool is not signed with a
  paid certificate).
- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** `bb-recomp-macos-arm64.zip`. Unzip it and move **Bloodborne Android Rebuild Tool** to Applications.
  The app is not notarized: the first time, **right-click it → Open → Open** (or run
  `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Bloodborne Android Rebuild Tool.app"`). Intel Macs are not supported.
  Built from the [`macos`](https://github.com/ducvd89/Bloodborne-android-rebuild-tool/tree/macos) branch, which also has its build instructions.
- **Linux:** `Bloodborne-Android-Rebuild-Tool-x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable
  (`chmod +x Bloodborne-Android-Rebuild-Tool-x8

- arm64/build.sh aarch64|x86_64: cross build (x86-64 LLVM 23.1.3 clang/lld, LLVM-23.1.3-Linux-ARM64 libraries, Ubuntu jammy arm64 sysroot, static
  zlib/zstd), command line only, BB_RECOMP_BUNDLED (in-process LLD); the x86_64 mode builds the same sources for the PC baseline.
- bbrecomp.cmake: FEXCore's defines follow the host (ARCHITECTURE_arm64 + preserve_all for an AArch64 host; the x86-64 debug host is unchanged);
  libc.a/libm.a linked whole and first on AArch64 (BB_RECOMP_EARLY_LIBS_DIR): static glibc reaches its GOT with R_AARCH64_LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15
  (32 KB) and LLD does not range-check it, so with ~4400 GOT slots from the PIC LLVM libraries the binary died in __libc_start_main.
- fetch-sysroot.py --arch arm64: C library, libstdc++ and libgcc only.
- compile: --every N now also applies to --so/--obj/--emit-ll/--plan-only (uniform sample of functions); it was census-only.
- arm64/run-on-device.sh + device-run-one.sh: adb script that pushes the binary and inputs to /data/local/tmp/bbr and times --plan-only and the
  1/17 sample (--jobs 8 and 4) on the phone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

lowering: every unit of a granular function declines a probe, also one without cases

A granular unit with no cases (its code starts with a trap, so it has no GuestOpcode boundary) went straight into its entry block when the
runtime's GranularEntry probed it (_pad1 = 1, rip = target) and ran its own code, e.g. a `cli` -> "guest trap". The flag check is now emitted
for such units too (resume entries or granular): _pad1 != 0 -> return with the flag still set. Self-test case in --granular-selftest; docs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

jumptable: an unbounded table scan stops at the next table; vector moves are flag-safe between cmp and ja

A table whose bound was not found was scanned up to the first entry outside the function, which ran into the next table (three adjacent
tables in one function: 12 entries read against the wrong base, mid-instruction targets 0x18 early, bogus units). The read now also stops
at the next `lea base, [rip+T]` target above the table and at the end of the function.

The scheduler also puts a vector move between the cmp and its ja (`cmp r15d, 5 ; vmovss xmm1, [..] ; ja`): VMOV*/MOVAP*/MOVUP*/MOVDQ*/MOVSS
are flag-safe now, so that bound is found and the table resolves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Lowering: units carry null_pointer_is_valid (a store to address 0 after a call was deleted as UB)

The game stores to address 0 on purpose after a panic (`call <print>; movl $0xdeadba, 0x0`,
Dantelion2 DL_PANIC). LLVM treats an access through a constant null pointer as undefined
behaviour unless the function has null_pointer_is_valid, so at -O1 it deleted the store and
the call-return block before it; the rip check after the call then folded to "returned
elsewhere", a normal return became an unwind, and the player's game stopped with
"native code is missing an entry at +0x20b56d2" (kind=unwind) instead of the panic text
and a fault. Seen on the Thor at +0x20b55b0 / +0x20df920; the unit's call-return block was
valid in the lifter's IR, the loss happened in LLVM.

Every unit now has the attribute (all guest pointers are plain host pointers; any address
may fault at run time, as on the PS4). Cost on the whole image: +4.2 KB of 119.9 MB of code.

Tests: bb-recomp-asmtest --null-selftest (a call followed by a store to constant 0, a store
through a register that is 0, a load from constant 0: the unit must run the block and fault
there; fails without the attribute at -O1), case 3 of run_recomp_device_regressions.sh on
the real +0x20b55b0. Existing self-tests, run_aot_entries_check.sh and the FEX ASM suite
(1755/1760 as before) pass. Players must rebuild libbbaot.so to get the fix.

# Hear Me Out ⚖️ **The party game that turns "idk, where do you want to go?" into an actual plan.** Play it at **https://hear-me-out-jose.vercel.app**. Play with friends you already have, or use **Find my people** to meet new people nearby. The AI host (the Judge) finds **real places nearby** that fit the whole group: budget, diet, distance and open hours. Each player is assigned a place to **defend, usually not their own favorite**, with a style to argue in and real facts to use. Pitches last up to 30 seconds. While they play, listeners react, lean toward a place on a **live sway meter**, and object, and the Judge **fact-checks claims** against the venue data ("OBJECTION SUSTAINED: closes at 10 PM, not 2am!"). Everyone votes privately, and the winner becomes **the plan**: a time that works for everyone, an invite, a poster, a calendar event and RSVPs you can share to Instagram or Facebook. ![Home](docs/screenshots/home.jpg) | TV: tonight's contestants | TV: a pitch, the Judge's ruling and the live sway | | --- | --- | | ![Finalists](docs/screenshots/finalists.jpg) | ![Playback](docs/screenshots/playback.jpg) | | Phone: approve your tags | Phone: your case file | Phone: the plan | | --- | --- | --- | | ![Approve tags](docs/screenshots/approve-tags.jpg) | ![Case file](docs/screenshots/case-file.jpg) | ![Plan on a phone](docs/screenshots/plan-phone.jpg) | | TV: the verdict | TV: the plan | | --- | --- | | ![Results](docs/screenshots/results.jpg) | ![Plan](docs/screenshots/plan.jpg) | *Screenshots are from a live game on the deployed site: real Google Maps places in Hayes Valley, San Francisco, with live Muse and Apify calls.* ## A round 1. **Lobby.** The TV shows a 4-letter room code and players join from their phones (up to 8, and the host can add bots). The host picks Food, Activity or Movie and a place, which starts the live venue search right away. 2. **Your vibe.** Each player sets a budget, how far they'll travel, when they're free tonight, any dietary needs and a few vibe chips. Then comes the Muse step, and they can optionally link their own public Instagram, TikTok or Facebook page. Muse Spark drafts interest tags with a reason for each, and **you approve every tag before anyone sees it**. 3. **Hot takes.** A personalized either/or question for each player while real venues are scraped and curated. 4. **Finalists.** Two to four real places that pass everyone's hard constraints, each with a photo, rating, price, travel time, hours and a fit line per person. 5. **Secret ballot, then case files.** Everyone privately picks a favorite. Then each player gets a place to defend, usually not their pick, with a style to argue in and three facts from the real venue data. Extra players become co-counsel. 6. **Pitches.** Record up to 30 seconds (captioned by Muse Voice Transcribe) or type a pitch (read aloud by the browser). During playback, listeners react (Funny, Good point, Not convinced), privately lean toward a place, and can object. The TV shows only the anonymous sway totals and who is most persuasive right now. The Judge rules on claims about hours, ratings, reviews and price, and checks diet claims against dishes on the venue's own website. 7. **Vote and verdict.** One private vote each, for the place and not the person. The verdict shows the winner, ties broken by group fit, plus **Most Persuasive** (who swung the most people) and **Best Line**. 8. **The plan.** The earliest slot everyone can make, nudged away from the busiest hours using Google's popular times. It comes with invite copy, a fit line for each person, a Muse Image cover, RSVPs (I'm in, Maybe, Can't), a `.ics` file and a Google Calendar link, Maps directions, icebreakers for the table, and sharing to Instagram or Facebook. ## Find my people (strangers mode) ![Find my people](docs/screenshots/meet.jpg) Pick an occasion, an area, a first name and a little person, then build your vibe like above. The queue puts **3 or 4 people who share the most approved tags** into a host-less room, and the whole game runs on their phones. Public meetups are 18+, use first names only, meet at public venues, and show the exact address only after you RSVP. Three "I'm in"s confirm a meetup, every player can be blocked or reported, and two groups that pick the same place can vote to **merge tables**. There are also open public lobbies to host or browse from the home page. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Browsers["Browsers (one SpacetimeDB identity per tab)"] TV["TV /host/:code"] P1["Phone /play/:code"] P2["Phone /play/:code"] end subgraph STDB["SpacetimeDB module (TypeScript): the live world state"] R["Reducers: rooms, phases, votes, tallies,
assignments, time slots, matching, merges"] T[("Tables: room, player, option, pitch, vote,
plan, rsvp, menu_proof, media (audio + posters), …")] PV[("Private: prevote, lean, profile_draft, ai_job, venue_cache,
lobby_match → my_* views, room_sway totals, admin views")] S["Schedule tables: phase deadlines, janitor"] E["Event table: reactions"] end subgraph ORCH["Judge worker (Node): a SpacetimeDB client, hosted as a Vercel daemon"] J["Claims ai_jobs via admin_jobs view
→ finish_* reducers"] F["Fixtures + offline fallbacks"] end Muse["Meta Muse
Spark · Voice Transcribe · Image"] Apify["Apify
Google Maps · Website Content Crawler · vibe-profiler"] Browsers <-- "subscriptions + reducer calls (WebSocket)" --> STDB ORCH <-- "subscriptions + reducer calls (admin identity)" --> STDB J --> Muse J --> Apify J -.-> F ``` **Deterministic logic lives in reducers:** the phase machine on schedule tables, joining, vote tallying and tie-breaks, who defends what, availability intersection and slot choice, lobby and queue matching, merge offers, RSVPs and authorization. **Fuzzy and external work lives in the Judge worker.** A reducer inserts an `ai_job`, the worker claims it through an admin-only vi

# Saltmarrow Deep

A gothic roguelike that runs in the browser and installs as an offline app.

Play: https://alemeno-00.github.io/saltmarrow/

## Android app

Download the APK: https://github.com/Alemeno-00/Saltmarrow/releases/latest/download/SaltmarrowDeep.apk

The app shell loads the game from GitHub Pages, so game updates arrive automatically. The APK only needs rebuilding when `android-app/` changes (GitHub Actions does this on push).

## Mac app

Download: https://github.com/alemeno-00/Saltmarrow/releases/download/mac/SaltmarrowDeep.dmg

DabDavis/socom2-decomp.desc: Matching decompilation of SOCOM II: U.S. Navy SEALs (PS2, SCUS-97275 r0001) - Metrowerks CodeWarrior PS2 3.0b52, verified byte-for-byte
DabDavis/socom2-decomp.readme:
# `decomp/` — matching decomp of SOCOM II (SCUS-97275 r0001)

**4,503 functions byte-exact** (2026-10-25, 11.16 % of the map's bytes): **1,352 hand-written** --
zlib 1.1.4 in MAIN (the calibration), the boot loader's overlay decode, the engine's zMath, ZAnim
(the command handlers, CZAnimMain/Set/Anim), zdb (CNode, CWorld and its save/load, the asset
manager, intersections), CCamera, the input classes, the sound system (989snd.c and zsnd), the
game states and app camera, the mission and network game, the entities and the compass, the HUD
and the C2D 2D-graphics family -- and **3,151 generated**, m2c's drafts that are byte-exact as
they stand (`src/auto/`, counted apart; see "The generated tier"). Every open function is
diagnosed in its source. Canary: `./test_scdecomp.py`.

This is the start of a function-by-function, byte-exact decomp of the game, built the way
`~/claude-eqoa/decomp` (github.com/DabDavis/eqoa-decomp) is: offline Python tooling, a
hand-kept symbol map, every function verified against the shipped bytes **and** every call
and data reference resolved to the address the shipped code uses.

```bash
./test_scdecomp.py                    # the canary: run first, it refuses a wrong disc
./sccheck.py                          # build src/ and score every function (rc 1 on a regression)
./sccheck.py --wrong -f GetWeapon     # with the instruction diff of each mismatch
./scd.py show 0x307520                # disassemble a target function, callees named
./scdiff.py src/engine/quat.cpp MakeZRot__5CQuatFf     # one function, one TU
./tools/identify.py SRC.c ... --rename                 # name a known-source TU's functions
./tools/callnames.py --rename                          # name callees off matched call sites
```

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `scdecomp.py` | the image (MAIN + the two MWo3 overlays, digests pinned), ELF reading, the map, disassembly |
| `scdiff.py` | the compiler driver (wibo + mwccps2) and the differ: masks the object's own relocation fields, then **resolves every relocation** — calls by map address, `%hi/%lo` pairs by value, string literals by text, switch tables by target |
| `sccheck.py` | builds `src/`, scores every function, holds `src/MATCHED.txt` (keyed by address, so a rename is not a regression; a regression is rc 1); an inline function's out-of-line copy that misses and whose map address lies outside its unit is `elsewhere` (the linked copy is another unit's) |
| `scd.py` | `show` / `list` / `where` / `census` |
| `test_scdecomp.py` | the canary: each check paired with a negative control that proves it can fail |
| `tools/decrypt_overlays.py` | your disc -> the two decrypted overlays (the target) |
| `tools/seed_symbols.py` | the sweep that seeded `symbols.txt` |
| `tools/identify.py` | compile a known-source TU, find each function in the image, verify, rename |
| `tools/callnames.py` | name placeholders off byte-exact functions' own call sites (eqcallnames.py) |
| `tools/m2c.py` | a target function as m2c-ready assembly (labels, callees by map name, `%hi/%lo` as `data_<VA>`), and m2c's draft |
| `tools/perm.py` | the permuter: reorders `// PERM_BEGIN/END` lines and `// PERM_DECL` names until a function matches |
| `tools/automatch.py` | compiles m2c's draft of every small function as it stands; `--emit` writes the hits to `src/auto/`; `--stale` redoes the drafts a rename left behind; a template-named row is drafted under its placeholder and renamed in the object (`/* sc: as=OLD NEW */`); a miss is redrafted with its callees' prototypes, then as C++ |
| `tools/sigs.py` | a function's parameters for m2c: the mangled name's list, or the argument registers live at its entry (backward dataflow over its blocks) |
| `tools/cxx.py` | C++ declarations that mangle back to a Metrowerks name, for drafts that must make member and virtual calls |
| `tools/s1names.py` | SOCOM 1's function names, out of the May 2002 demo's symbols and relocations |
| `tools/s1data.py` | SOCOM 1's global data names, through the functions s1names paired |
| `tools/dwarf1.py` | the demo's Metrowerks DWARF 1: units, signatures, class layouts, enums; `func` (one function's parameters, locals, blocks, source lines); `header` (compilable C++ declarations of a type and all it embeds, offsets annotated, holes -- MW's vtable pointer -- padded) |
| `tools/beta_tu.py` | which source file a function was in, out of the press beta's asserts |
| `tools/rename.py` | rename map rows by hand, keeping the note, refusing a taken name, listing the source still using the old one |
| `tools/s1units.py` | SOCOM II's translation units: its static initialisers against SOCOM 1's named `__sinit_<file>`s |
| `tools/unitscan.py` | where one hand-written unit could be two: its pinned and inlined pairs, the target's own calls, every cut that separates the first and none of the second |
| `tools/s1vtables.py` | virtual functions named slot by slot: SOCOM II's vtables found by their RTTI's class-name string, aligned with the demo's `__vt__` tables; `--holdout` measures it on names the map already has |
| `tools/try.py` | compile one unit with one textual substitution at a time and score one symbol, in a scratch copy of `src/` |
| `tools/scperm.py` | the permuter: EQOA's tree-sitter mutations of one function, MW-compiled and alignment-scored (needs `.venv`) |
| `symbols.txt` | **the map** — `0xADDR SIZE name  # note`, kept by hand from here on |
| `data.txt` | the map of global data, the same format and namespace |
| `src/` | the reconstructed source; `MATCHED.txt` (the baseline), `ABSENT.txt` (dead-stripped) |

kachaj96/Project-3D-iso-game.readme:
# Project 3D Iso Game (working title)

An isometric tactical adventure RPG for Android, inspired by the feel of Dofus with a darker atmosphere. 2D illustrated art despite the repo name. Built in Godot 4.7 with Claude Code.

Status: **Milestone 0, setup.** No game code yet.

## Documents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [docs/RESEARCH.md](docs/RESEARCH.md) | Tool research, chosen stack, hardware, sources |
| [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Technical architecture and the rules that keep co-op cheap later |
| [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) | Milestones with goals, learning, testing and exit criteria |
| [docs/GDD.md](docs/GDD.md) | Living game design document |
| [docs/ART_PIPELINE.md](docs/ART_PIPELINE.md) | Art pipeline proposal, validated in Milestone 2 |
| [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md) | Prioritized backlog and First Playable scope |
| [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) | Record of technical and design decisions |
| [docs/RISKS.md](docs/RISKS.md) | Risks and known bugs |
| [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) | Repeatable testing checklist |
| [docs/WORKFLOW.md](docs/WORKFLOW.md) | How to work with Claude Code, plus the first prompts |
| [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) | Rules Claude Code follows in this repo |

## First steps (Milestone 0)

1. **Install on your PC:** Git, [Godot 4.7.x standard build](https://godotengine.org/download) (not .NET), Android Studio (used only for the Android SDK), JDK 17, Krita, Claude Code.
2. **Phone:** enable Developer options and USB debugging. Connect it by USB and accept the debugging prompt.
3. **Godot Android setup:** in Godot, Editor > Editor Settings > Export > Android, set the Android SDK path and the Java SDK path. Follow the [Exporting for Android](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/exporting_for_android.html) page for your exact Godot version.
4. **Create the project:** clone this repo, open Godot, create a new project **in the repo root folder** with the **Compatibility** renderer.
5. **Hello phone:** add a scene with a `ColorRect` and a `Label`, set it as main scene, add an Android export preset (Project > Export), then use the one-click deploy button (Android icon top right) to run it on the phone.
6. **Commit** `project.godot` and the scene.
7. **Run the three prompts** at the end of [docs/WORKFLOW.md](docs/WORKFLOW.md) in Claude Code, one at a time, verifying each.

Milestone 0 is done when the game runs on PC, runs on the phone, and CI produces an installable APK.

## Running checks locally

Set `GODOT_BIN` to the console build, for example `C:/Tools/Godot/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe`.

```bash
# Parse-check every GDScript file (fails on any error)
GODOT_BIN="$GODOT_BIN" tools/check_scripts.sh

# Run all gdUnit4 tests headless (exit code 0 = all passed)
"$GODOT_BIN" --headless --path . -s -d res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode
```

In the editor: open the gdUnit4 panel (bottom dock), select `tests/`, press the run button.

CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) runs the same checks on every push, then exports a debug APK and uploads it as an artifact. The Godot version is pinned in one variable (`GODOT_VERSION`) at the top of that file.

Knito58/Typestones.desc: Lettered smooth stone blocks for MC 26.3 Fabric
Knito58/Typestones.readme:
# Typestones

Fabric mod for Minecraft 26.3: smooth stone blocks that carry a letter on all six sides, in two dye
colors (letter and optional background). The Typewriter makes them from a typed line of text.

Work in progress. Planned for the first version:

- **Typestone blocks** with the character set of Billboard Engine (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, punctuation,
  Ä Ö Ü ä ö ü ß, ° · €). Top and bottom follow the placement direction, so text on floors and
  ceilings reads correctly. A broken block drops itself with letter and colors.
- **Typewriter**: takes smooth stone and dyes from inventories on any side, makes one block every
  5 ticks and puts it into the inventory at its back. Ghost slots for letter and background dye,
  buttons for A–Z, 0–9 and all characters, repeat up to 64 times. A space makes a plain block.
- No crafting recipes for the letter blocks, so recipe viewers stay clean.

## Font faces

Letters are generated, not drawn by hand. Each face in `fonts/` becomes a file of 16×16 ink
pixels, `src/main/resources/typestones/letters/<face>.txt`. The game draws each letter as a few flat
rectangles in the letter dye, so no textures are needed. A stone stores only a hash of its letter's
pixels.

- `fonts/classic.txt`: Billboard Engine's 5×7 dot-matrix font, as editable text (`#` = ink). This is
  the face the game uses for now.
- Any `.ttf` or `.otf` file put into `fonts/` becomes a face named after the file. The font must
  have every character of the set, otherwise the generator lists the missing ones and stops.

After changing a face, run `./gradlew generateGlyphs` and commit the letter files. A preview sheet of
each face lands in `build/glyph-preview/`. To try a font installed on the computer without copying it:

```
./gradlew generateGlyphs -Pfont=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf -Pface=dejavu_bold
```

Check the font's license before committing it or its letters. `./gradlew build` fails when the
committed letter files no longer match `fonts/`.

## Building and testing (Linux)

You need JDK 25 (`java -version` and `javac -version` must both say 25), git and IntelliJ IDEA.

1. In IntelliJ: **File → New → Project from Version Control**, URL `https://github.com/Knito58/typestones`.
2. Wait until the Gradle import finishes; the first time it downloads Minecraft and Fabric.
3. Gradle tool window: **Tasks → fabric → runClient**.

## Releasing

Pushing to the `release` branch builds the mod, creates a GitHub release from the newest
`CHANGELOG.md` section and uploads the jar to CurseForge. The upload needs the repository secret
`CURSEFORGE_TOKEN` and the project id in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (`CURSEFORGE_PROJECT_ID`).
*Actions → check CurseForge token → Run workflow* tests the token without uploading anything.

## How this mod is made

Typestones is written by Claude AI (Anthropic), code, textures and icon included. Konitor decides
what it does and tests it.

## License

MIT, see `LICENSE`.

CorbinPlayz/Side-hustle.readme:
# Side Hustle (formerly Duel Arena)

A first-person 3D loot shooter for two players. Everything runs on one Cloudflare Worker, with no other services:

- **Accounts, levels, leaderboard, admin approval** live in a Durable Object (SQLite) on Cloudflare.
- **Every match runs on the server.** Your browser sends inputs and draws what the server says. It does the 3D drawing only.
- **Nobody sees any page, script or image without an approved account.** The Worker checks the login before it serves any file. Only the sign-in page is public.
- **Only one admin.** The account whose user ID you put in `ADMIN_ID`.

## Deploy (about 10 minutes)

1. Install Node 20 or newer. In this folder run `npm install`.
2. Optional: set `SIGNUP_CODE` in `wrangler.toml` so only people you give the code to can request an account.
3. `npx wrangler login`, then `npx wrangler deploy`. Wrangler prints your site address.
4. Open the site, choose Create account and register yourself. The "waiting for approval" screen shows **your user ID**.
5. Put that number in `wrangler.toml` as `ADMIN_ID = "<your id>"` and run `npx wrangler deploy` again. That account is now approved and is the only admin. Nobody else can ever become admin, because admin is decided by that ID in the config and not by anything a visitor can do.
6. Everyone else registers, waits on the approval screen, and shows up in `/admin.html` under Waiting. Approve or block from there.

Alternatively, push this folder to GitHub and use Workers > Create > Import a repository in the Cloudflare dashboard (build command: none, deploy command: `npx wrangler deploy`).

Run it locally: `npx wrangler dev`.

## How it works

| Piece | File |
|---|---|
| Router, login gate, security headers, Durable Object classes | `worker/src/index.mjs` |
| Accounts, sessions, throttling, XP, leaderboard, admin rules | `worker/src/hubcore.mjs` |
| One room: seats, settings, 60 Hz simulation, snapshots, XP report | `worker/src/matchcore.mjs` |
| Game rules and world (shared by server and browser) | `public/js/sim.js`, `public/js/data.js` |
| 3D drawing, sound, UI | `public/js/render.js`, `game.js`, pages |

Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2 (100,000 rounds, per-user salt). Sessions are random tokens in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies, stored hashed. Five wrong passwords lock a username for ten minutes. XP is credited only by the server, only for matches of 45 seconds or more.

## Tests

`npm test` runs account rules, the router with a fake Cloudflare environment (login gate, admin-only, CSRF) and a full server-side match. `tests/browser/` has Playwright scripts that drive the real pages against the real match logic.

## Honest limits

- Built and tested without access to the real Cloudflare runtime or a real GPU. Run through the deploy steps and play a match with a friend before you rely on it.
- Rendering is in the browser, so approved players do receive the game's code and assets. Unapproved visitors do not.
- Accounts need approval, but one person could still make several accounts to farm XP if you approve them all.
- Durable Objects (SQLite) need a Cloudflare account; check Cloudflare's current pricing and free-plan limits for your expected traffic.

## Publishing the `public/` folder on GitHub Pages

Pages serves static files only, so on Pages you get the pages and demo mode (no login gate, no accounts, no online rooms). The Worker above is what provides those.

1. On GitHub choose New repository. The name becomes the address: `https://<your-username>.github.io/<repo-name>/`. Name it `<your-username>.github.io` instead to get the plain `https://<your-username>.github.io/`.
2. Upload the **contents of the `public/` folder** (index.html, css, js and so on) to the repo root, not the whole project.
3. Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Deploy from a branch > `main` and `/ (root)` > Save. It goes live in a minute or two.
4. All links in the site are relative, so the repository-name sub-path works without changes.

## The game so far (single player)

Open `world.html` (the front page redirects there). You start with nothing.

- **Earn:** pick things up off the ground (E): shells, driftwood, bottles, tin cans, berries, mushrooms, and rare pearls, old coins and glowcaps. Sell them at the market stall by the dock.
- **Grow:** buy a fishing rod ($110) or an axe ($170), a bigger bag, bait, boots. Fishing and logging are plain clicks, no minigames.
- **Spend it:** buy a house plot (about $850) and build on a snap grid (press 3; G turns snapping off). A boat to reach the next biome is the next goal.
- **Neighbours:** as the island earns money, NPC neighbours buy plots and move in. Each sale pushes land prices up harder than the last, and they buy goods too, which keeps market prices healthier. The number of neighbours is capped.
- **Landmarks:** a lighthouse you can climb, a shipwreck full of bottles, coins and pearls, a waterfall cave with crystals and glowcaps, and a village with its own market (pays more for logs and forage, less for fish). Press Tab to see where they are.
- **Characters:** press C to make your character (hair, hat, eyes, teeth, outfit). Neighbours and villagers use the same character model with NPC-only outfits.
- **Prices:** move slowly and predictably, with a town news line explaining events like a fish festival. Selling a lot of one thing drops its price.
- **Autosave:** progress saves every 8 seconds, when you switch tabs, and when you close the page (in this browser for now; account saves come with the Cloudflare version).

davideverettreed/stex-rifle-squad.readme:
# STEX: Rifle Squad

*Sand Table Exercise: Rifle Squad* (STEX) is real-time squad tactics in the browser. You command a 13-man Marine rifle squad
(squad leader and three four-man fire teams) against an enemy squad, using fire
and maneuver on a 2 × 2 km map (four 1 km grid squares) seen straight down.
The map grows with the echelon: platoon actions will use 4 × 4 km.

The battlefield is a printed 1:25,000-style map sheet on a planning table, in
the standard colors of US military topographic maps (FM 3-25.26): black for
man-made features and the grid, red-brown for contours (5 m, index every 25 m)
and elevations, blue for water, green for vegetation, red for the paved road.
It has a full collar: title, grid values, legend, graphic scale and
declination diagram. Each map is generated: rolling hills with 60–110 m of
relief, streams in gullies and ponds, fields with hedgerows and stone walls,
orchards, vineyards, woods, a paved road, dirt tracks, named villages and
farms. The sheet is drawn at three levels of detail as you zoom.

Zoomed out, each fire team (then the squad) is one square counter with the
standard unit symbol. Zoomed in, men are round game pieces printed with the billet symbols from the Marine rifle squad
organization figure: squad leader, fire team leader, automatic rifleman,
grenadier, rifleman. Status chits sit on the pieces (posture, suppressed or
pinned, wounded, no ammunition). Orders are drawn as overlay graphics in the
doctrinal colors: blue friendly, red enemy, black for targets.

## Play

Open `dist/index.html` in a browser. It is a single file with no install, and it
works with mouse or touch.

## Website and Android app

`docs/` is the website, built for GitHub Pages at **stex-riflesquad.com**: the
game at the root of the site, installable as an app on Android and desktop, and
playable offline after the first visit. It is live at
https://stex-riflesquad.com. Every push to `main` that updates `docs/`
publishes a new version.

How it was set up, for reference:

1. **DNS at Namecheap.** Domain List → stex-riflesquad.com → Manage →
   Advanced DNS. Delete the parking records Namecheap adds (the CNAME for
   `www` pointing to parkingpage.namecheap.com and the URL Redirect record for
   `@`). Then add:

   | Type | Host | Value |
   |---|---|---|
   | A Record | @ | 185.199.108.153 |
   | A Record | @ | 185.199.109.153 |
   | A Record | @ | 185.199.110.153 |
   | A Record | @ | 185.199.111.153 |
   | CNAME Record | www | davideverettreed.github.io. |

2. **GitHub Pages.** In the repository, Settings → Pages. Set Source to
   *Deploy from a branch*, branch **main**, folder **/docs**, and Save. The
   custom domain field should read `stex-riflesquad.com` (from `docs/CNAME`).
3. When GitHub shows the DNS check has passed (DNS can take up to a day; often
   minutes), tick **Enforce HTTPS**.
4. Recommended: verify the domain under your GitHub account's Settings →
   Pages → Add a domain. GitHub gives a TXT record to add at Namecheap; this
   stops anyone else from pointing a GitHub site at your domain.

To install on Android, open https://stex-riflesquad.com in Chrome and choose
**Install app** (or **Add to Home screen**) from the menu.

## Troop leading: the order and the plan

Each mission opens with a five-paragraph order beside the map:

- **Orientation**: your position, the reported enemy, the ground between, key terrain.
- **Situation**: the enemy in a SALUTE report (deliberately incomplete) and its
  capabilities as DRAW-D, with the most likely course marked; friendly forces; time available.
- **Mission**: one generated mission statement with task, place and purpose.
- **Execution**: the planning board. Place control measures on the map (checkpoint,
  objective, support-by-fire position, assault position, phase line, CCP, route,
  fighting position with a sector of fire, limit of advance, rally point, release
  point, target reference point) and write
  the scheme of maneuver as lines: trigger, unit, task, place. Triggers: at step-off,
  after or with the line above, on a red, green or white star cluster, at H+ minutes,
  on contact. **Draft a plan** gives a hasty attack (or, in a meeting engagement, a
  hasty defense) to start from.
- **Admin & Logistics**: the loadout, the CCP.
- **Command & Signal**: the signals and the succession of command.

The clock runs while you plan, at 4× speed: the one-third, two-thirds rule. In an
attack the enemy digs in over the time available; in a meeting engagement he keeps
coming. Planning past your third leaves the fire teams less ready. **Step off** to
execute; the Tracker shows each line, fires signals, and lets you start a line now
or resume one halted short by contact. A direct order that moves most of a line's
men takes that line off the plan.

**The plan is graded at step-off**: objective, a task for every fire team, a base
of fire, control measures, signals, a CCP, and time discipline. The grade is the
squad's confidence: it sets morale, how fast the men shake off suppression, and how
quickly they answer the radio. Stepping off with no plan leaves the squad shaken.

**After step-off, orders go by radio**: "SL: 2nd FT, suppress TRP 1, over." The unit
answers and acts after a few seconds, longer under fire, without its team leader, or
with low confidence; a shaken unit under fire may answer "Say again, over."

**The after-action report grades the mission**: plan 25%, result 35%,
casualties 25%, time 15%.

## What is modeled

- Selection at three levels: one Marine, a fire team, or the squad.
- Orders: walk, rush, crawl, bounding overwatch, assault, posture, fire control
  (fire at will, return fire, hold), area suppression, 40mm, hand grenades,
  take cover, fall back, halt, face. Five formations for teams and the squad.
- Loadout by billet: weapon, magazines, 40mm rounds, grenades, with load weight
  affecting speed.
- Line of sight over terrain height, walls, buildings, woods, orchards,
  vineyards and tall grass. Squads start

# PrintPitt — the onchain print shop on Monad

**Order a print from your phone, and two copy shops race for it onchain: the faster a shop finishes, the more it earns, and the rest flows back to you automatically.** Built for students and the copy kiosks around campus. Made at **Monad Blitz Jogja Vol. 2** (24 October 2026, Yogyakarta).

![PrintPitt](docs/printpitt.png)

> Demo video: **[ADD LINK]**

## Try it now

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Order from your phone (scan the QR on stage) | https://printpitt-app.vercel.app/pesan |
| Live board (projector) | https://printpitt-app.vercel.app/layar |
| Shop game (the two print shops) | https://printpitt-app.vercel.app/toko |
| Landing page | https://printpitt-landing.vercel.app (source: [`landing/`](landing/)) |
| Backend status (Railway) | testnet https://backend-production-2b31.up.railway.app/status · mainnet https://backend-mainnet-production-7835.up.railway.app/status |

**Contracts (v2.3), verified on Sourcify (exact match).** The app switches network with `?jaringan=mainnet` / `?jaringan=testnet` (badge in the bottom-left corner).

| Network | `FotokopiKilat` (escrow, claim race, decaying payout, refund, NFT receipt) | `TestIDRX` (tIDRX, Rupiah token with `permit`) | Deploy tx |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Monad Mainnet** (chain 143, block 116137717) | [`0x4b453b395eEa830C5CB208551A0326f6cd976f12`](https://monadvision.com/address/0x4b453b395eEa830C5CB208551A0326f6cd976f12) | [`0xEf3369C083B137C0FB3Fa9424990726d424ac205`](https://monadvision.com/address/0xEf3369C083B137C0FB3Fa9424990726d424ac205) | [`0xa1b1d9dd…4144019f`](https://monadvision.com/tx/0xa1b1d9dd4a85037ef24ec8156a623c81f8b5c5d9afb8890ec9c4ebaa4144019f) |
| **Monad Testnet** (chain 10143, block 73752547) | [`0x24b045E3B4155232F81c709dF3DD43595a5C5101`](https://testnet.monadvision.com/address/0x24b045E3B4155232F81c709dF3DD43595a5C5101) | [`0xcCf26C3b02a610fB87327f41a13384aF8ff57F45`](https://testnet.monadvision.com/address/0xcCf26C3b02a610fB87327f41a13384aF8ff57F45) | [`0x06746ec0…04e9e70f`](https://testnet.monadvision.com/tx/0x06746ec0ab0110ef87b5e6f6d05f5b8c3760b3e695062c41392c0f7204e9e70f) |

Real IDRX integration (proof only, not used by the demo app): `FotokopiKilat` on mainnet with real IDRX [`0x18Bc5bcC660cf2B9cE3cd51a404aFe1a0cBD3C22`](https://monadvision.com/address/0x18Bc5bcC660cf2B9cE3cd51a404aFe1a0cBD3C22) at [`0x1F8061d653896fF48EbFDD3Fee7C0684E2995f77`](https://monadvision.com/address/0x1F8061d653896fF48EbFDD3Fee7C0684E2995f77) (IDRX has no `permit`; the app falls back to a one-time `approve`).

On mainnet, judges pay nothing: one **judge code** on `/pesan` gives 1 MON for gas and a Rp20.000 tIDRX voucher. Example order transaction: **[ADD after demo]**.

**Run it locally (3 steps):**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/PrintPitt/frontend.git && cd frontend/web
npm install && cp .env.example .env.local   # testnet values: see "Moving to Monad testnet" in web/README.md
npm run dev                                  # open http://localhost:5173/pesan
```

It works if `/pesan` shows a Rupiah balance after "top up", and your order then appears on `/layar`.

## How it works (onchain flow)

1. **Order and pay.** The customer picks a job on `/pesan` (fixed-price jobs, or upload a real document priced per page by `hargaUntuk`) and pays in Rupiah (tIDRX). Uploaded files are stored encrypted by the backend; only the customer and the winning shop can download them, and they are deleted when the order is final. No gas needed: the customer signs an EIP-712 order plus an EIP-2612 `permit`, and our relayer submits it. The money sits in the contract's escrow, not with any shop.
2. **Race.** Shops within 1.5 km of the customer's rough location (3 km for Toko Pro) see the order and call `claim`. The first transaction in a block wins. The other shop gets "taken by Shop X".
3. **Work.** The winning shop completes each step (`completeStep`): copy → print → laminate. Its pay drops every second:
   `payout = price × (timeLimit − workTime) / timeLimit`, `refund = price − payout`.
4. **Ready and hand over.** The shop marks the order ready (payout is fixed at that moment). Funds are released when the shop scans the customer's secret QR at pickup.
5. **Too late?** `expire` refunds 100% automatically. A keeper calls it, no admin needed.
6. **Dispute.** While the order is ready, the customer can `komplain`. Funds are held until the operator decides; if nobody decides in time, `tutupSengketa` splits it 50/50.
7. **Receipt.** The customer gets an onchain SVG NFT receipt with the job, the order text, the shop and the work time.

Revenue model (live since contract v2.1): 3% platform fee on the shop's payout for completed orders, sent to the treasury (the customer's refund is never cut), Rp200 relayer fee per gasless order, and a "Toko Pro" subscription (Rp50,000 / 30 days, order radius 3 km instead of 1.5 km).

## Why Monad

- **~0.4 s blocks and ~0.8 s finality** (Monad docs). A claim race is decided in one block, so "who was first" is fair and instant.
- **Per-second pay only makes sense on a fast chain.** On a slow chain the order is stale before it confirms.
- **Low fees and full EVM.** Foundry, OpenZeppelin, viem and Envio work as-is, so a gasless Rupiah flow costs the customer nothing.

## Architecture

| Repo | What it does |
|---|---|
| `frontend` (this repo) | `web/`: React + Vite app with `/pesan` (phone), `/layar` (projector), `/toko` + 3D game. `landing/`: landing page. `assets/figures/`: interactive machine figures |
| `contracts` | `FotokopiKilat` + `TestIDRX` (Foundry, OpenZeppelin), unit + invariant tests, package `@printpitt/shared` (ABI, addresses, helpers) |
| `backend` | Railway service: faucet, simulated Rupiah top-up, relayer (gasless orders), keeper (auto `expire`), order bot |
| `indexer` | Envio HyperIndex: orders, shops, sessions, leaderboard, top-ups (GraphQL) |

Claude Code Game Studios

Turn a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio.
49 agents. 74 skills. One coordinated AI team.

--- ## Why This Exists Building a game solo with AI is powerful — but a single chat session has no structure. No one stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping design docs, or writing spaghetti code. There's no QA pass, no design review, no one asking "does this actually fit the game's vision?" **Claude Code Game Studios** solves this by giving your AI session the structure of a real studio. Instead of one general-purpose assistant, you get 49 specialized agents organized into a studio hierarchy — directors who guard the vision, department leads who own their domains, and specialists who do the hands-on work. Each agent has defined responsibilities, escalation paths, and quality gates. The result: you still make every decision, but now you have a team that asks the right questions, catches mistakes early, and keeps your project organized from first brainstorm to launch. --- ## Table of Contents - [What's Included](#whats-included) - [Studio Hierarchy](#studio-hierarchy) - [Slash Commands](#slash-commands) - [Does it produce games, or documents?](#does-it-produce-games-or-documents) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Upgrading](#upgrading) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Design Philosophy](#design-philosophy) - [Customization](#customization) - [Platform Support](#platform-support) - [Community](#community) - [Supporting This Project](#supporting-this-project) - [License](#license) --- ## What's Included | Category | Count | Description | |----------|-------|-------------| | **Agents** | 49 | Specialized subagents across design, programming, art, audio, narrative, QA, and production | | **Skills** | 74 | Slash commands for every workflow phase (`/start`, `/design-system`, `/create-epics`, `/create-stories`, `/dev-story`, `/story-done`, etc.) | | **Hooks** | 15 | Automated validation on commits, pushes, asset changes, design-doc reads, writes and registries, session lifecycle, agent audit trail, and gap detection | | **Rules** | 14 | Path-scoped coding standards enforced when editing gameplay, engine, AI, UI, network code, scene and asset files, and more | | **Templates** | 62 | Document templates for GDDs, UX specs, ADRs, sprint plans, HUD design, accessibility, and more | ## Studio Hierarchy Agents are organized into three tiers, matching how real studios operate: ``` Tier 1 — Directors creative-director technical-director producer Tier 2 — Department Leads game-designer lead-programmer art-director audio-director narrative-director qa-lead release-manager localization-lead Tier 3 — Specialists gameplay-programmer engine-programmer ai-programmer network-programmer tools-programmer ui-programmer systems-designer level-designer economy-designer technical-artist sound-designer writer world-builder ux-designer prototyper performance-analyst devops-engineer analytics-engineer security-engineer qa-tester accessibility-specialist live-ops-designer community-manager ``` Each agent declares a model in its frontmatter: the three directors ask for Opus, `lead-programmer` and fifteen specialists name Sonnet, and the remaining thirty **inherit your session's model**. Treat the tiers as seniority of role, not as a billing plan — most of the studio runs on whatever model you are already using. ### Engine Specialists The template includes agent sets for all three major engines. Use the set that matches your project: | Engine | Lead Agent | Sub-Specialists | |--------|-----------|-----------------| | **Godot 4** | `godot-specialist` | GDScript, Shaders, GDExtension | | **Unity** | `unity-specialist` | DOTS/ECS, Shaders/VFX, Addressables, UI Toolkit | | **Unreal Engine 5** | `unreal-specialist` | GAS, Blueprints, Replication, UMG/CommonUI | ## Slash Commands Type `/` in Claude Code to access all 74 skills: **Onboarding & Navigation** `/start` `/help` `/project-stage-detect` `/setup-engine` `/adopt` `/settings` **Game Design** `/brainstorm` `/map-systems` `/design-system` `/quick-design` `/review-all-gdds` `/propagate-design-change` **Art & Assets** `/art-bible` `/asset-spec` `/asset-audit` **UX & Interface Design** `/ux-design` `/ux-review` **Architecture** `/create-architecture` `/architecture-decision` `/architecture-review` `/create-control-manifest` **Stories & Sprints** `/create-epics` `/create-stories` `/dev-story` `/sprint-plan` `/sprint-status` `/story-readiness` `/story-done` `/estimate` **Reviews & Analysis** `/design

Release 1.1.0 — one config file, and a process weight you choose

`project.yaml` at the repo root is now the single source of truth for a
project's configuration, replacing `production/stage.txt`,
`production/review-mode.txt` and `.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` (all
three still read as a fallback; nothing is force-deleted).

**`modes.rigor` — one question instead of six.** `minimal`, `standard` or
`full` fronts six knobs: `modes.workflow`, `docs.density`, `qa.level`,
`modes.story_granularity`, `modes.review_mode` and `team.size`. It defaults to
`minimal`, which is a change from 1.0's behaviour: the heavier tier was
measured costing several times more to reach working code without producing a
better result, and returning nothing when a fresh developer inherited the
project. Pin `modes.rigor: standard` to keep 1.0's process level.

Also in this release:

- `/settings` to view or change any setting, and `project.local.yaml` for
  per-developer preferences that should not be committed.
- `system_overrides` to hold one system to a higher standard than the rest of
  the project, and `testing.strict` to set per test type whether missing
  evidence blocks a story or warns.
- A story that changes anything the player sees is not closed until the game
  has been launched, observed, and a screenshot retained in
  `production/qa/evidence/`. A parse check is not a run. This holds at every
  rigor level, including `minimal`, where automated tests are waived but the
  look is not.
- The code root is engine-specific and enforced as such: Godot `src/`, Unity
  `Assets/`, Unreal `Source/<Module>/`. Two of the three will not build a
  project laid out any other way.
- Migration tooling for existing projects: `.claude/scripts/migrate-v1-config.sh`
  converts a 1.0 layout, non-destructively by default, with a report to review
  before `--finalize` deletes anything.
- Ask-before-write holds regardless of personal automation settings.

Upgrading from 1.0 or earlier: see UPGRADING.md. Full list of changes:
CHANGELOG.md.

Both SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks were extracting `.agent_name` from the

entire agent audit trail useless.

fallback for systems without jq. Log output format is unchanged so existing
audit logs remain valid.

dehanz13/racing-game-orbit-rush.readme:
# Orbit Rush

An arcade drive-and-collect game that runs entirely in the browser. Built with **React**, React Three Fiber, Three.js, postprocessing (bloom, vignette), Zustand and Vite. No 3D asset files, no audio files, no backend: every model is procedural geometry, every sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API, and all progress lives in `localStorage`.

## Play

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # production bundle in dist/
```

| Action | Keys (arrows scheme) | Keys (WASD scheme) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drive / steer | Arrow keys | W A S D |
| Fire Bolt (hold to lock on) | F | J |
| Shockwave | E | K |
| Overdrive | Shift | L |
| Jump | Space | Space |
| Restart run | R | R |
| Pause / exit | Esc | Esc |

Touch devices get an on-screen joystick and buttons automatically.

## How a run works

- **Sparks** are the heart of your score. Gold Sparks are worth ten. Every 10 Sparks grant 3 Bolts.
- **Beacons** (24 towers on a spiral around the start) add a permanent multiplier that grows with the Beacon number. Lighting one drops a Supply Crate and opens a **Relay Lane**: five gates to pass within 14 seconds for a Comet Core and a Hull/Shield upgrade.
- **Drones** chase and shoot you. From Stage 2 a **Titan** can appear; destroying it drops a Comet Core and a spare Shockwave.
- The world shifts through five **stages** (new palette, more Drones) as your Spark total crosses thresholds.
- A hidden **hype** meter rises with speed, drifting and air time, and decays constantly. It drives the Velocity factor.
- The run ends when the clock hits zero or your Hull is gone.

### Pulse Score

```
raw      = Sparks + 3 × Drones + 12 × Titans + 5 × Beacons
weighted = 0.4 × Velocity + 0.3 × Control + 0.2 × Flair + 0.1 × Reach   (each 0..1)
score    = round(raw × multiplier × (1 + weighted))
```

Each run's score is paid into XP; levels follow `150 × level^1.45` and ranks are title bands over levels.

## Project layout

```
src/
  config/game.ts    every tunable number + the LEX vocabulary (rename anything here)
  game/engine.ts    framework-free simulation: player, drones, pickups, beacons, scoring
  game/Scene.tsx    React Three Fiber race renderer (cameras, lights, loop)
  game/Showcase.tsx turntable scene behind the menu / garage / pilot screens
  game/render/      car model, lit grid floor + sky, pickups, drones, beacons, effects, post-processing
  game/audio.ts     synthesized sound bank + generative music
  game/input.ts     keyboard + touch input
  store/game.ts     Zustand store (profile, settings, results, local leaderboard)
  ui/               screens and modals
```
